The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, August 18, 1937    23677
Nipponese Army Ready
For General Campaign
Along Three Railways

OFFENSIVE SLATED
SUNDAY; DEFENSE
PLANS COMPLETED                7994/45
                               13 8 37

Hostilities Break Out On Ping-Sui Line, Japan
Forces Attack Nankow, Chinese Casualties
Heavy; Tracks Blown Up; City Bombed

Fighting Still Going On This Morning

JAPANESE forces in North China will launch a
general offensive on Sunday on three fronts along
the Peiping-Suiyuan Railway, Tientsin-Pukow Railway
and the Peiping-Hankow Railway, according to Nan-
king reports claimed to have been obtained from mili-
tary circles.
    The Chinese defensive measures along these railways, the
reports added, have already been completed. The 29th Army
units have been reinforced by divisions directly under the
control of the Military Affairs Commission.
                NANKOW ATTACKED
    Hostilities have already broken out along the Peiping-
Suiyuan and Tientsin-Pukow Railways. In a move to capture
Kalgan, Japanese forces attacked the Chinese positions on two
sides, at Nankow and at Tsalkoupao. The attack on Nankow

        TIENTSIN WANTS U.S. TROOPS
              (Reuter's Agency)
    TIENTSIN, Aug. 18.—A resolution opposing the
withdrawal of United States troops from Tientsin was
unanimously passed at a meeting today of the American
Chamber of Commerce.
    The Chamber decided to forward
the resolution to the Navy and War Departments in
Washington.

was said to be one of the bitterest battles fought since the
outbreak of the Lukouchiao Incident. Despite heavy losses
under Japanese gunfire, the Chinese forces are still in control
of the strategic points, the reports declared.
    The Japanese attack commenced yesterday morning when
600 soldiers exchanged fire with the Chinese defenders, includ-
ing units of the 89th Division under General Tang En-po.
The Japanese artillery soon joined and the Chinese were driven
back, blowing up the railway tracks and the bridges in the
course of the retreat. The Japanese attackers then confined
their activities to the shelling of the Chinese positions, using
howitzers and heavy field guns. An area of about two miles
around Nankow was turned into ruins. Fighting was still
going on early this morning with the Japanese continuing the
attack with 30 planes, as well as tanks and field guns. Chinese
and Japanese infantry were also seen moving in the area.

日军准备
沿三条铁路线
发动全面战役

进攻定于
周日；防御
计划已完成                7994/45
                               13 8 37

平绥线爆发战事，日军
进攻南口，中国军队伤亡
惨重；铁轨被炸毁；城市遭轰炸

今晨战斗仍在继续

据称从军方渠道获得的南京消息显示，华北日军将于周日沿北平-绥远铁路、天津-浦口铁路和北平-汉口铁路三条战线发动全面进攻。
    报道补充称，中国军队沿这些铁路线的防御措施已经完成。第29军部队已得到军事委员会直接管辖的各师的增援。
                南口遭袭
    平绥铁路和津浦铁路沿线已爆发战事。为夺取张家口，日军从两侧攻击中国军队阵地，一处位于南口，另一处位于岔道堡。对南口的攻击

        天津希望美军留驻
              （路透社）
    天津，8月18日。—在今日举行的美国商会会议上，一致通过了一项反对美军撤离天津的决议。
    商会决定将该决议递交给华盛顿的海军部和陆军部。

据称是自卢沟桥事变爆发以来最激烈的战斗之一。报道宣称，尽管在中国军队在日军炮火下遭受重大损失，但仍控制着战略要点。
    日军的进攻始于昨日上午，当时600名士兵与包括唐恩波将军麾下第89师部队在内的中国守军交火。日军炮兵随即加入战斗，中国军队被迫后撤，并在撤退过程中炸毁了铁路轨道和桥梁。随后，日军攻击者将其活动限制在使用榴弹炮和重型野战炮轰击中国军队阵地。南口周围约两英里的区域变成了一片废墟。今晨早些时候战斗仍在进行，日军继续动用30架飞机以及坦克和野战炮发动攻击。在该地区还观察到中日双方步兵在行动。

CLASH IN CHINGHAI
In Chinghai, along the Tientsin-Pukow Railway, a fresh
clash took place yesterday. The Japanese forces shelled the
Chinese positions at 10 o'clock yesterday morning and by 1
p.m., a Japanese cavalry unit more than 200 strong attacked
Wulichang, north of Chinghai. They are said to have been
surrounded by the Chinese defenders and the fighting was
still going on after dusk last night.
A fleet of Japanese bombers yesterday bombarded Machang,
also along the Tientsin-Pukow Railway. The damage was un-
known.

MINES TO BOTTLE UP YANGTZE
(Havas)
LONDON, Aug. 12.—News of the arrival of the Japanese
fleet in Shanghai yesterday created a profound impression
locally. It is feared that gunboats whose gauge permits pas-
sage up the Yangtze River might go as far as Nanking, thus
generalizing the whole Sino-Japanese conflict.
Naval experts consider, however, that this would be im-
possible if the Chinese laid a few mines in the river.

WU TEH-CHEN BLAMED
(Domei)
CANTON, Aug. 12.—Claiming that the anti-Japanese
movement was "spontaneous and provoked by the hostilities
in North China," Dr. Philip K. C. Tyau, Foreign Affairs Com-
missioner for Kwangsi and Kwangtung, yesterday informed
the Japanese authorities that he was unable to control the
movement, Domei learned today from Chinese sources.
The anti-Japanese sentiment, the Japanese officials here
said, is being fanned by Generals Wu Teh-chen and Yu Han-
mou, respectively Governor and Pacification Commissioner of
Kwangtung.
A charity hospital, managed by the Government-General
of Formosa, was stoned by Chinese ruffians yesterday.
The Japanese officials charged that Chinese policemen
are canvassing Chinese shops and urging the merchants to
sell no goods to the Japanese.

NANKOW STATION CAPTURED
(Reuter's Agency)
TOKYO, Aug. 12.—The capture of Nankow railway
station at 9.30 this morning is announced in a Japanese re-
port received here.

静海冲突
昨日，在津浦铁路沿线的静海，发生了新的冲突。日军于昨日上午10时炮击中国军队阵地，至下午1时，一支200余人的日本骑兵部队袭击了静海以北的吴里场。据说他们被中国守军包围，昨晚黄昏后战斗仍在继续。
昨日，一队日本轰炸机轰炸了同样位于津浦铁路沿线的马厂。损失情况不明。

水雷封锁长江
（哈瓦斯社）
伦敦，8月12日。—昨日日本舰队抵达上海的消息在当地引起了极大震动。人们担心，吃水深度允许驶入长江的炮舰可能会一直开到南京，从而使整个中日冲突普遍化。
然而，海军专家认为，如果中国在江中布设少量水雷，这种情况将不可能发生。

吴铁城受指责
（同盟社）
广州，8月12日。—据今日从中方消息人士处获悉，广西和广东外交专员刘朝琴博士昨日告知日本当局，反日运动是“自发的，由华北战事引发”，他无法控制该运动。
此间的日本官员称，反日情绪正由广东省政府主席吴铁城将军和绥靖主任余汉谋将军煽动。
昨日，一家由台湾总督府管理的慈善医院遭到中国暴徒的石块袭击。
日本官员指控中国警察正在走访中国商店，敦促商人不要向日本人出售商品。

南口车站被占领
（路透社）
东京，8月12日。—此处收到的一份日本报告宣布，今早9时30分占领了南口火车站。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, August 12, 1937

Nipponese Censor
Mails From China,
Propagandists Busy

A Shanghailander in Unzen writes that censorship on mail from China has been extremely heavy. Letters from Tientsin had been cut open, re-pasted, and delivered from 24 to 48 hours later than other mail.
“For a while, Shanghai newspapers were taboo,” says the writer. “But now they allow them in, after they are sufficiently stale not to excite us. We are so full of pro-Japanese propaganda I can’t imagine the true state of affairs.”
A Kobe correspondent reports intermittent receipt of papers.

日本审查
来自中国的邮件，
宣传人员忙碌

一位身在云仙的上海居民写道，对来自中国的邮件审查极其严格。来自天津的信件被拆开，重新粘贴，并比其他邮件晚24至48小时送达。
“有一段时间，上海报纸被列为禁忌，”作者说。“但现在他们允许进入，前提是报纸内容已经足够过时，不会激起我们的情绪。我们充斥着亲日宣传，我无法想象事态的真实情况。”
一位神户记者报告说，报纸间歇性收到。

南京的反日派
稳步走向
掌控局面

东京认为上海和首都局势
日益紧张；
“基督将军”的影响被视为占主导地位

全国各地中国领导人
忙于磋商

东京，8月11日。—据今晨在此收到的新闻报道，随着“对日战争派”在南京迅速壮大，上海和南京的局势每小时都在变得紧张。
报道断言，在军事委员会副委员长冯玉祥将军的领导下，并得到国民党内“年轻派系”的支持，“战争派”现在正压倒温和派。
据进一步声称，反日分子现已威胁要对以中央政治会议主席汪精卫先生和军政部长何应钦将军为首的温和派发动政变。政府消息人士今日下午乘飞机从牯岭抵达此处。黄将军将会晤行政院院长蒋介石总统及其他政府当局，讨论当前局势。—中央通讯社。
报道称，受“战争派”影响的中国“强人”蒋介石将军已“显然”决定与日本正面碰撞。—（同盟社。）

龙云将军
南京，8月11日。—云南省政府主席龙云将军于周一抵达此处，在他访问首都的第三天，即今日，进行了艰苦的一轮会议和会晤。
龙将军首次出席中央党部会议，在今日上午的例行会议上受到中央政治会议成员的热烈欢迎。
今早早些时候，龙将军受到国民政府主席林森先生的接见。
下午，这位云南主席会见了中央政治会议主席汪精卫先生，随后拜访了立法院院长孙科博士。—中央通讯社。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 11, 1937

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 2994/37
Date 12 8 37

WARNING AGAINST
RECRUITING

Prosecution Threatened by
Los Angeles Official

Los Angeles, Aug. 9.
A warning to Lieutenant General
Russell L. Hearn, once aide to Marshal
Chang Tso-lin of China, that "anyone
recruiting Americans for the Chinese
or any other foreign Army will be
prosecuted" was issued to-day by the
Assistant District Attorney, Mr. Hal
Hughes.
General Hearn's reported enlistment
of a Foreign Legion to aid China
against Japan was said to have
brought several thousand applications
from every section of the nation.

A Denial

Later to-day, however, General
Hearn denied reports that he had
been recruiting for the Chinese
Army and warned against the use
of his name by people soliciting
funds for the Chinese cause.
The Chinese Government mean-
while was reported to have con-
tracted for 50,000,000 gallons of
American aviation gasoline at an
estimated cost of $6,775,000 and to
be delivered at Shanghai "as soon
as possible."
A dozen large tankers, it was
estimated, would be required to
transport the reported order, the
largest in the history of the Cali-
fornia oil fields. Mr. Robert Allen,
president of the Pacific Petroleum
Corp., was reported to have arranged
the sale.—United Press.

S.I.
C A / R

警告禁止

洛杉矶官员威胁起诉

洛杉矶，8月9日。
助理地区检察官哈尔·休斯先生今日向曾担任中国张作霖元帅副官的拉塞尔·L·赫恩中将发出警告，称“任何为中国人或任何其他外国军队招募美国人的人都将被起诉”。
据悉，赫恩将军招募外籍军团以协助中国对抗日本的行动，已从全国各地引来数千份申请。

否认

然而，今日晚些时候，赫恩将军否认了他为中国军队招募人员的报道，并警告人们不要利用他的名字为中国的事业募集资金。
与此同时，据报道中国政府已签订合同，以估计6,775,000美元的价格购买50,000,000加仑的美国航空汽油，并“尽快”运抵上海。
据估计，运输这批据报道为加州油田历史上最大的订单需要十几艘大型油轮。据报道，太平洋石油公司总裁罗伯特·艾伦先生安排了此次销售。—合众社。

S.I.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, August 11, 1937. 23617

4/15
12 8 37

Shanghai Should Be Neutralized!
—An Editorial—

SHANGHAI NEUTRALITY became an ex-
tremely live issue in 1932, when from the
Chinese point of view there “wasn’t any such
animal.” On February 2 of that year we re-
marked under the heading, “De-Neutralizing
the Settlement”:

It is inevitable that the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council should come in for bitter Chinese
criticism because of the fact that Japanese
forces have used the International Settlement
as an operating base of military operations
against Chinese territory.

There is no use in blinking the facts.
From a moral standpoint the situation is in-
defensible. Supposedly neutral territory has
been turned over to Japanese marines engaged
in active warfare.

But we cannot subscribe to the view that
the Council has permitted this either through
ignorance of the significance of the move or
through willingness to take sides. It will be a
grave error if Chinese blame the Council for a
turn of events in which the Council was a
victim, not a conspirator.... The present hap-
penings have demonstrated conclusively that
while a united front by all internal defenders
may protect the Settlement against outside
aggression, the system heretofore prevailing is
inadequate to cope with a situation where one
or more of the defenders takes the rôle of
aggressor.

The direct parallel between the historic
situation of 1932 and the potential situation of
1937 is clear. On February 9 the then Mayor,
General Wu Te-chen, said in a formal note:

“I have the honor to inform you that with
reference to the failure of the Shanghai Muni-
cipal Council to restrain armed Japanese
forces in their use of the International Settle-
ment as a base of operations against Chinese
troops in Chinese territory or even permitting
such use to be made by armed Japanese forces, I
have on several occasions placed my emphatic
protest with the Shanghai Municipal Council
....I have the honor to state further that in
Chinese territory contiguous to the Inter-
national Settlement there are now large numbers
of troops which might be drawn into the area of
the signatories’ rights and interests. In order to
avoid any possible conflict between Chinese and
foreign troops, and in order to preserve the
neutrality of the International Settlement, I
have the honor to suggest that the Shanghai
Municipal Council take immediate steps to
declare the International Settlement a neutral
zone, and to request the Powers concerned to
send sufficient forces to maintain such neu-
trality.”

faction”, finding the source of this “legal
right” in “the unique political status of Shang-
hai as a municipality, which has no exact
counterpart in the whole world.”

But that was 1927. Five years later no one
was much inclined to throw his chest out over
the Council’s rights in this matter, for the
situation swept over the city and over the
Council like a tidal wave. As Mr. Ching-lin
Hsia puts it in reviewing Professor William C.
Johnstone’s “The Shanghai Problem” in the
current T’ien Hsia Monthly, “the theory of
neutrality which Mr. Justice Feetham had help-
ed the Council to defend collapsed like a house
of cards”, and Professor Johnstone is quoted
as remarking:

“To summarise, the policy of Settlement
protection and Settlement neutrality so care-
fully built up over a period of seventy-five
years has become wholly ineffectuous as a result
of the Japanese action in 1932. The safety of
the Shanghai foreign settlements has been par-
tially destroyed and to that extent their
status has been modified.”

Mr. Justice Feetham noted that “the
practice has been adopted of recognising the
neutrality of the Settlement and the Port of
Shanghai in times of international conflict,
both in the case of wars between China and
other Powers, and in the case of wars between
any of the different Powers....” (P. 4 Part II
Chapter II) but this was, as indicated, before
1932; and 1932 changed everything.

This newspaper at the time of the 1932
Sino-Japanese hostilities made as strong a
stand as possible to maintain the theory of
Shanghai neutrality. But the impossibility of
the situation at that very time forced with
irresistible logic upon us the conclusion that
neutralization must be something more than a
mere declaration by the Council; it must be
something backed by force. We pointed out
that unless the Powers were prepared to send
sufficient forces to maintain neutrality, the
declaration would be a mere scrap of paper.
We urged that the Powers should either send
forces or abandon the idea of neutrality alto-
gether. The Powers did neither. They sent a
few token forces, enough to protect their own
concessions perhaps, but not enough to main-
tain the neutrality of the whole Settlement.
And so the theory of neutrality collapsed.

Today, five years later, we are faced with
the same problem again. The situation is even
more critical than it was in 1932. The Japanese
are once more using the Settlement as a base
of operations against Chinese forces. The
Council is once more powerless to prevent it.
And once more we are told that the Settlement
is neutral. But what does this neutrality mean?
It means nothing unless it is backed by force.
Unless the Powers are prepared to send suffi-
cient forces to maintain neutrality, the decla-
ration will be a mere scrap of paper.

We urge the Powers to face the situation
squarely. Either send sufficient forces to main-
tain neutrality, or abandon the idea altogether.
There is no middle course. The half-measures
of 1932 led to disaster. Let us not repeat the
mistake.

Shanghai should be neutralized. But neu-
tralization without force is a mockery. It is
time the Powers realized this.

上海应当中立化！
——社论——

上海中立问题在1932年成为一个极其热门的话题，当时从中国人的角度来看，“根本没有这回事”。那年2月2日，我们在“去中立化的租界”标题下评论道：

由于日军利用国际租界作为对中国领土进行军事行动的作战基地，上海工部局不可避免地遭到了中国方面的严厉批评。

回避事实是无济于事的。从道德立场来看，这种局势是站不住脚的。本应中立的领土已被移交给正在从事积极作战的日本海军陆战队。

但是，我们不能认同这样的观点，即工部局之所以允许这种情况发生，要么是因为不了解此举的意义，要么是出于愿意选边站队。如果中国人指责工部局在这场事件中是共谋者而非受害者，那将是一个严重的错误……目前的事态已确凿地证明，虽然所有内部防御者的统一战线可以保护租界免受外部侵略，但此前盛行的制度不足以应对其中一个或多个防御者扮演侵略者角色的局面。

1932年的历史局势与1937年的潜在局势之间的直接平行关系是显而易见的。2月9日，时任市长吴铁城将军在一份正式照会中说：

“本人荣幸地通知阁下，鉴于上海工部局未能制止武装日军利用国际租界作为对中国领土上的中国军队进行作战的基地，甚至允许武装日军如此使用，本人已多次向上海工部局提出强烈抗议……本人进一步荣幸地声明，在与国际租界毗邻的中国领土上，现驻有大量部队，这些部队可能会被卷入签约国权利和利益的区域。为了避免中外军队之间可能发生任何冲突，并为了保持国际租界的中立，本人荣幸地建议上海工部局立即采取措施，宣布国际租界为中立区，并请求有关列强派遣足够的部队以维持此种中立。”

派系”，并在“上海作为一个市政当局的独特政治地位，这在全世界都没有确切的对应物”中找到了这种“合法权利”的来源。

但那是1927年。五年后，没有人太倾向于就工部局在此事上的权利夸夸其谈，因为局势像潮水般席卷了城市和工部局。正如夏清林（Ching-lin Hsia，音译）先生在当期《天下月刊》（T’ien Hsia Monthly）上回顾威廉·C·约翰斯顿（William C. Johnstone）教授的《上海问题》一书时所说，“费瑟姆法官（Mr. Justice Feetham）曾帮助工部局辩护的中立理论像纸牌屋一样崩塌了”，并引用约翰斯顿教授的话说：

“总之，经过七十五年精心建立的租界保护和租界中立政策，由于日本在1932年的行动，已变得完全无效。上海外国租界的安全已部分遭到破坏，其地位也在相应程度上发生了改变。”

费瑟姆法官指出，“在国际冲突时期，无论是中国与列强之间的战争，还是任何不同列强之间的战争，都采取了承认租界和上海港中立的做法……”（第二部分第二章第4页），但如前所述，这是在1932年之前；而1932年改变了一切。

在1932年中日敌对行动期间，本报尽最大努力维护上海中立理论。但当时局势的不可能性以不可抗拒的逻辑迫使我们得出这样一个结论：中立化必须不仅仅是工部局的一项声明；它必须有武力作为后盾。我们指出，除非列强准备派遣足够的部队来维持中立，否则该声明不过是一纸空文。我们敦促列强要么派遣部队，要么彻底放弃中立的想法。列强两者皆未做。他们只派遣了少量的象征性部队，或许足以保护他们自己的租界，但不足以维持整个租界的中立。于是，中立理论崩溃了。

今天，五年过去了，我们再次面临同样的问题。局势比1932年更加危急。日本人再次利用租界作为对中国军队进行作战的基地。工部局再次无力阻止。我们再次被告知租界是中立的。但这种中立意味着什么？除非有武力支持，否则它毫无意义。除非列强准备派遣足够的部队来维持中立，否则该声明不过是一纸空文。

我们敦促列强正视局势。要么派遣足够的部队来维持中立，要么彻底放弃这个想法。没有中间道路可走。1932年的折衷措施导致了灾难。让我们不要重蹈覆辙。

上海应当中立化。但没有武力的中立化是一种嘲弄。列强是时候认识到这一点了。

hope that in some way the old position of
Shanghai neutrality can be regained. There
seems to be no difference whatever of foreign
opinion in that respect, for foreigners living
in Shanghai do not want any war involving
Shanghai—a highly natural state of mind.
But after 1932, no one can take any lofty
moral position in the matter in view of
Occidental acquiescence in Japan's use of the
Settlement as military base.
In writing on this subject a few days ago
(August 6) we pointed out that the Settle-
ment authorities did not premeditatedly pick
sides in 1932. The whole affair was simply
one of those "just-happen" matters and if
blame was to be attached to the Settlement
authorities it lay chiefly in the failure to
assume and to make public any clear policy
of neutrality. Conscious of the Japanese par-
ticipation in Settlement defense and of Jap-
anese membership on the Shanghai Municipal
Council, the authorities felt an explicable but
unfortunate self-consciousness about dis-
associating themselves from their partners even
though those partners had assumed a role as
belligerents.
While we hope most sincerely that there
may be no war in or about Shanghai, it is not
too early to face the fact now that if hostili-
ties do break out, the Settlement will find
itself in precisely the predicament it did be-
fore save with the important alteration that,
as we said on August 6, it is an open secret
that the Chinese this time will not regard
Japanese-occupied territory north of the Creek
as having any such "unique" status as was
proclaimed in the Chairman's speech of 1927.
They will not, that is, unless there can be a
clear agreement in which both the Chinese
and Japanese will join.
We feel it is decidedly to the interest of
both parties so to join. There need be no
pointing the finger particularly at any nation-
ality in making a neutrality arrangement at
this time; such an agreement should include
the Americans, the British, and in fact every
nationality in any degree interested in Shang-
hai. The pact would afford protection to
Chinese lives and property here, shelter to
Chinese refugees; and safeguard the lives and
property of non-belligerent nationals of the
party in conflict with China, as well as the
rest of us.
Without it, Shanghai neutrality is deader
than the proverbial door-nail. With it, the
old-time fiction of Shanghai neutrality can be-
come a guaranteed fact. There should be no
delay in striving to achieve such an agreement
which would be durable, not merely for the
present emergency, but for all time that
Shanghai retains its international status.

目前的局势正在讨论中，希望以某种方式恢复上海中立的旧有地位。在这方面，外国舆论似乎没有任何分歧，因为居住在上海的外国人不想卷入任何涉及上海的战争——这是一种非常自然的心态。但在1932年之后，鉴于西方默许日本利用租界作为军事基地，任何人都不能在此事上采取高高在上的道德立场。

几天前（8月6日）在撰写关于此主题的文章时，我们指出，租界当局在1932年并没有预谋地选边站队。整件事 simply 是那些“碰巧发生”的事情之一，如果要归咎于租界当局，主要在于未能承担并公开任何明确的中立政策。当局意识到日本参与租界防御以及日本人在上海工部局中的成员身份，因此对于与其伙伴划清界限感到一种可以理解但不幸的自我意识，尽管这些伙伴已经承担了交战方的角色。

虽然我们最真诚地希望上海及其周边地区不会发生战争，但现在面对这样一个事实并不为时过早：如果敌对行动确实爆发，租界将发现自己处于与以前完全相同的困境中，只是有一个重要的变化，正如我们在8月6日所说，这是一个公开的秘密，即这次中国人不会认为苏州河以北被日本占领的领土拥有1927年主席讲话中所宣称的那种“独特”地位。也就是说，除非中日双方能达成一项明确的协议。

我们认为，双方加入这样的协议显然符合双方的利益。在制定此时的中立安排时，无需特别针对任何国籍指手画脚；此类协议应包括美国人、英国人，以及事实上任何与上海有不同程度利害关系的国籍。该条约将为在此的中国人的生命和财产提供保护，为中国难民提供庇护；并保障与中国冲突一方的非交战国国民的生命和财产，以及我们其余人的安全。

没有它，上海中立比谚语中的门钉死得更透。有了它，上海中立的老套虚构就能成为有保障的事实。不应拖延争取达成此类协议的努力，该协议不仅应适用于当前的紧急情况，而且应适用于上海保留其国际地位的所有时间。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 11, 1937    2,606

President Lin Sen Speaks
On Critical Situation

Says China Has Been Pushed To The Limit Of
Endurance And Responsibility Is Japan's;
Japanese Lives, Property Protected

NANKING, Aug. 10.—The significance of the policy of co-existence among the nations of the world was explained by President Lin Sen in his address at the weekly memorial service yesterday at National Government House.
Ever since the outbreak of the Lukouchiao Incident, President Lin said, the Government has consistently adhered to the policy of peace. Repeated arrangements for the simultaneously withdrawal of troops of both sides were made, but the truce was always broken by the Japanese.
Utilizing the time gained by the negotiations for peace, the Japanese brought up reinforcements and completed all preparations for the attack on the Chinese, resulting in the occupation of Peiping and Tientsin.
After the occupation of Tientsin, President Lin continued, the Japanese military systematically destroyed the institutions of learning and culture. They bombed the Nankai University and reduced it to ruins.
Recently, the Japanese have repeatedly made illegal flights over Chinese territory, and evacuated their nationals from China. All this shows that they are making active preparations for further aggressions against China.
The Chinese are seeking the preservation of their national existence. At the same time, they believe in peaceful co-existence with the rest of the world. China and Japan have the same culture and belong to the same race. They should co-operate with each other as far as possible and not try to destroy each other.
This idea, President Lin recalled, was also fully expounded by the late Party Leader, Dr. Sun Yat-sen, during his sojourn in Tokyo. But, unfortunately, it has not yet been comprehended by the Japanese.
Limit Of Endurance
Following the recent Japanese aggressions in North China, President Lin continued, China has been pushed to the limit of endurance. Should peace be abandoned, the responsibility will have to rest with Japan.
In coping with the national emergency, which is unprecedented in the history of China, the people must remain calm, go about their pursuits peacefully, maintain order, stabilize the currency, redouble their efforts for the increase of the national productivity and do the part assigned them in accordance with the directions and orders of the Government.
The people should refrain from panic and avoid credence of rumours which are systematically disseminated by the enemy.

（批：S / JR / C.D.S.Li / 6/8 / 8/16）

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年8月11日，星期三    2,606

林森总统就危急局势发表讲话

称中国已被逼至忍耐极限，责任在于日本；日本人的生命财产受保护

南京，8月10日电。——林森总统昨日在国民政府举行的每周纪念仪式上发表讲话，阐述了世界各国共存政策的意义。

林总统说，自卢沟桥事变爆发以来，政府一贯坚持和平政策。曾多次安排双方同时撤军，但停战协定总是被日本方面破坏。

日本利用和平谈判赢得的时间，调集援军并完成了对华攻击的所有准备，导致北平和天津被占领。

林总统继续说，占领天津后，日军系统地摧毁了教育和文化机构。他们轰炸了南开大学，将其夷为废墟。

最近，日本多次非法飞越中国领空，并从中国撤离其侨民。所有这些都表明，他们正在积极准备进一步侵略中国。

中国人正在寻求保存其民族生存。同时，他们相信与世界其他地区和平共存。中国和日本拥有相同的文化，属于同一种族。他们应尽可能相互合作，而不是试图互相毁灭。

林总统回忆说，已故党领袖孙中山博士在东京逗留期间也充分阐述了这一思想。但不幸的是，日本人尚未理解这一点。

忍耐极限

林总统继续说，继最近日本在华北的侵略之后，中国已被逼至忍耐的极限。如果放弃和平，责任将必须由日本承担。

在应对中国历史上前所未有的国家紧急状态时，人民必须保持冷静，安居乐业，维持秩序，稳定货币，加倍努力增加国家生产力，并按照政府的指示和命令履行各自 assigned 的职责。

人民应避免恐慌，避免相信敌人系统散布的谣言。

（批：S / JR / C.D.S.Li / 6/8 / 8/16）

Small Exodus
Begins From
Native City

Hurried Departures Made
Following Incident
At Hungjao

FRENCH LIKELY
TO CLOSE GATES

More Shops Moving Into
Foreign Areas From
Hongkew, Chapei

A miniature exodus from Nantao was underway yesterday.
For the past several weeks despite the fighting in the North and the big exodus from Chapei, the Native City, remained quiet. In fact, many of those who fled from Chapei and Hongkew moved into Nantao.
Late Monday night and early yesterday morning, the report went about that 10 Japanese warships had arrived from Yangtse ports. Some of the more timid residents whose nerves had been on edge during the past weeks of uncertainty started to move out.
This morning's papers carrying news about the Hungjao incident in which two Japanese and one Chinese were killed when the two members of the Japanese Landing Party attempted to go to Hungjao Airdrome added to the fears.
Throughout the day there was a small exodus from the Chinese city crossing over into the French Concession.
The number of loaded rickshas and carts, passing through the gates, however, was not large and was far below that of the Chapei flood of refugees last week.
Some Still Leaving Chapei
Although there was a movement from Nantao into the French Concession, there was also a smaller movement of people, apparently Chapei and Hongkew refugees, who continued to move with their belongings into Nantao.
Despite the new Hungjao incident, the Chapei and Hongkew exodus did not increase yesterday, except for a few cases during the early morning.

Many of the North Szechuen Road cabarets are closing earlier because of the lack of customers.
Adding to the fears of the people in Nantao was the display of barbed wire entanglements and barriers in the various French police stations. Numerous of these barriers were displayed in the courtyard at the police station on Avenue Edward VII next to the Chung Wai Bank.
Word was passed around the Nantao residents that in case of trouble the gates on the Frenchtown boundary would be closed and the barbed wire barriers thrown up, thus preventing them from entering the concession.
Most of those seen moving yesterday had but a few suitcases and bags with them. Unlike the Chapei exodus of the past week, there were few cartloads of household goods.
This indicated that most of them planned to return to their homes later if the latest incident is settled peaceably and were not moving their household effects until later if the situation worsens.

小规模撤离
始于
华界

虹桥事件后
人们匆忙离去

法租界可能
关闭大门

更多商店从
虹口、闸北迁入
外侨区域

昨天，南市出现了一次小规模的撤离潮。尽管北方战事不断，且此前有大量人口从闸北撤出，但在过去几周里，华界一直保持平静。事实上，许多从闸北和虹口逃难的人搬进了南市。
周一深夜至昨天清晨，有消息流传称10艘日本军舰已从长江各港口抵达。在过去几周的 uncertainty（不确定性）中神经一直紧绷的一些较为胆小的居民开始搬离。
今早的报纸刊登了关于虹桥事件的新闻，两名日本海军陆战队队员试图前往虹桥机场时，导致两名日本人和一名中国人死亡，这加剧了人们的恐惧。
整天都有少量人员从华界穿越进入法租界。
然而，穿过大门的满载人力车和手推车的数量并不多，远低于上周闸北难民潮的规模。
仍有人离开闸北
虽然有人从南市进入法租界，但也有一小部分人，显然是来自闸北和虹口的难民，继续带着财物搬入南市。
尽管发生了新的虹桥事件，但昨天闸北和虹口的撤离人数并未增加，仅在清晨有少数几例。

由于缺乏顾客，北四川路的许多歌舞厅都提前打烊。
加剧南市居民恐惧的是，各法国警察局展示了铁丝网障碍和路障。在爱德华七世大道（Avenue Edward VII）紧邻中伟银行（Chung Wai Bank）的警察局院子里，展示了许多此类路障。
南市居民间流传着这样的消息：一旦发生麻烦，法租界边界的大门将关闭，并竖起铁丝网障碍，从而阻止他们进入租界。
昨天看到的大多数搬迁者只携带了几个手提箱和包裹。与上周闸北的撤离不同，装载家用物品的手推车很少。
这表明，如果最新事件和平解决，他们大多数人计划稍后返回家园，并且只有在局势恶化时才会随后搬运家当。

Export Of Rice To
Manchuria Banned
Order Issued by Maritime
Customs Here
Control over shipment of food-
stuff, placed by the Government
authorities following the Lukouchiao
incident, was further tightened yes-
terday when the Shanghai Customs
in a notice, prohibited the export
of rice abroad and Manchuria in-
cluding Dairen.
The order yesterday followed
notices during the past month which
banned shipment of flour, wheat,
and bran from this city.
Officials of the Shanghai Dealers'
Association were of the opinion that
the Customs order will have an
effect in equalising the rising price
of rice in Shanghai.

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 11, 1937

Itagaki Arrives
NANKING, Aug. 10.—(Central).—
Heralding the commencement of
major hostilities in North China,
Major-General Itagaki, Chief of
Staff of the Kwantung Army, has
arrived in Tientsin, according to
information received here tonight.
His 5th Division is due to arrive in
North China within the next five
days.
Concentrating her major forces
along the Peiping-Suiyuan Railway
Japan will mobilise 14 divisions to
North China, eight of which have
already arrived. These "expedi-
tionary forces" will either be com-
manded by Gen. Terauchi, former
Minister of War, or Lt.-Gen. Koiso,
Commander of the Chosen Gar-
rison force.

南京，8月10日.—（中央社）.—据今晚在此收到的消息，关东军参谋长板垣少将已抵达天津，预示着华北大规模敌对行动的开始。他的第5师团预计将在未来五天内抵达华北。

THE EVENING POST & MERCURY - 11.8.37.    23621

Japanese Operations
Extending To Chahar;
Peace Still Debated

BOTH SIDES WAIT
GESTURE BY OTHER
FOR NEGOTIATIONS

Chinese Willing To Carry Out Terms Of Truce
Originally Signed On July 11 Following
First Brush At Marco Polo Bridge

NORTH SKIRMISHES CONTINUE

AS the Japanese military operations in Hopei gradually extend to Chahar where some 3000 Japanese soldiers launched an attack on Tsaikoupao, west of Kalgan, yesterday, a deadlock on the question of who shall suggest the settlement of the North China crisis by diplomatic negotiations is holding up the possible peaceful solution of the latest Sino-Japanese dispute.

Despite the reported announcement by the Tokyo Foreign Office that Japan would be satisfied if the truce agreements reached on July 11 and 19 were carried out and despite the fact that Nanking authorities are prepared to fulfill the agreement reached on July 11 which they have already approved, formal negotiations have not yet started. Mr. Shigeru Kawagoe, the Japanese Ambassador to China, is remaining in Shanghai.

Meanwhile, according to reports from Peiping, fresh clashes took place yesterday. The battle at Tientsinwan, a station near Kalgan on the Peiping-Suiyuan Railway, is still going on. The Japanese claim to have occupied the station but this has not been confirmed by Chinese sources.

At Tientsin, after the clash at Tsaikoupao, the Japanese troops advanced towards the city. It is reported that the Japanese have occupied the railway station and are now in control of the city. The Chinese troops have withdrawn to the outskirts.

In Shanghai, it is reported that the Japanese Consul-General has demanded that the Chinese authorities take immediate action to suppress all anti-Japanese activities. The Chinese authorities have promised to do so.

with Ambassador Kawagoe. Mr. Kao left for Nanking last night presumably to report on the results of his preliminary conversations. The Waihsiao official was also widely rumored to have made a secret trip to Tokyo but these reports could not be confirmed.

For the first time the outcome of the Lushan conference resulted in the Japanese occupation of a major portion of the Peiping-Tientsin area. The Ta Kung Pao, commenting on the situation, said that Japan's aim is to establish a buffer state in North China. Negotiations with Japan to settle the North China crisis are now being conducted by the Chinese government.

It is understood that a new proposal for the settlement of the North China crisis has been submitted by the Chinese government to the Japanese authorities. The proposal includes the withdrawal of Japanese troops from the occupied areas and the establishment of a joint commission to investigate the causes of the incident.

(1) the 29th Army shall tender apology to the Japanese Army, punish the responsible officers, and give an assurance to prevent further incidents of the kind;
(2) the Chinese troops at Lukouchiao and Langwanmiao be withdrawn and replaced by Peace Preservation Units; and
(3) the "Blue Shirt," communist and other anti-Japanese organisations be suppressed.

General Sung accepted the terms on July 19 and carried out the provisions for an official apology when he called on General Matsui that day. It was not until July 22 that the terms of the agreement were submitted to Nanking and approved.

Other Pact Not Recognised

In reference to the agreement of July 19, supposed to be signed by General Chang Shin-chung with the Japanese authorities, the Ta Kung Pao declared that the 29th Army has not formally recognised the accord. The agreement provided:
(1) Expulsion of elements who obstruct the friendly relations between China and Japan;
(2) Thorough suppression of communists, and
(3) suppression of anti-Japanese organs, public bodies and movements, and essentially the anti-Japanese education.

The Ta Kung Pao admitted that the Chinese government has not formally notified the Japanese of Nanking's approval of the July 11 truce, causing a misunderstanding among the Japanese that the government was obstructing the local negotiations.

Japan must take immediate action to approach the Chinese government for an agreement on the principles for settling the North China crisis, failing to do so will only prolong the conflict and make the situation more complicated. The Ta Kung Pao warned.

《晚邮报与水星报》 - 1937.8.11.    23621

日军作战
扩展至察哈尔；
和平仍在争论中

双方均等待
对方做出
谈判姿态

中方愿意执行
7月11日卢沟桥首次冲突后
最初签署的停战条款

北方小规模冲突持续

随着日军在河北的军事行动逐渐扩展至察哈尔，昨天约3000名日军进攻张家口以西的柴沟堡，而在谁应提议通过外交谈判解决华北危机的问题上陷入僵局，阻碍了最新中日争端的可能和平解决。

尽管东京外务省据报道宣布，如果执行7月11日和19日达成的停战协议，日本将感到满意，而且尽管南京当局准备履行其已批准的7月11日协议，但正式谈判尚未开始。日本驻华大使川越茂先生仍留在上海。

与此同时，据北平报道，昨天发生了新的冲突。平绥铁路上靠近张家口的天津湾站战斗仍在进行。日军声称已占领该站，但中方消息来源尚未证实。

在天津，柴沟堡冲突后，日军向市区推进。据报道，日军已占领火车站，目前控制着该市。中国军队已撤退至郊区。

在上海，据报道日本总领事要求中国当局立即采取行动镇压所有反日活动。中国当局已承诺这样做。

与川越大使在一起。高先生昨晚前往南京，据推测是汇报其初步会谈的结果。这位外交部官员还被广泛谣传曾秘密访问东京，但这些报告无法得到证实。

庐山会议的结果首次导致日军占领了平津地区的大部分。《大公报》评论局势时说，日本的目标是在华北建立一个缓冲国。中国政府正在与日本进行谈判以解决华北危机。

据悉，中国政府已向日本当局提交了一项解决华北危机的新提案。该提案包括日军从占领区撤军，并成立联合委员会调查事件起因。

(1) 第29军应向日军道歉，惩办负责军官，并保证防止此类事件再次发生；
(2) 撤出卢沟桥和宛平的中国军队，并由保安队接替；以及
(3) 镇压“蓝衣社”、共产党及其他反日组织。

宋哲元将军于7月19日接受了这些条款，并在当天拜访松井将军时执行了正式道歉的规定。直到7月22日，协议条款才提交给南京并获得批准。

其他协定未获承认

关于据称由张自忠将军与日本当局签署的7月19日协定，《大公报》宣称第29军并未正式承认该协定。该协定规定：
(1) 驱逐阻碍中日友好关系的分子；
(2) 彻底镇压共产党，以及
(3) 镇压反日机关、公共团体和运动，实质上是反日教育。

《大公报》承认，中国政府尚未正式通知日本南京已批准7月11日的停战协定，导致日本人误解政府正在阻碍地方谈判。

《大公报》警告说，日本必须立即采取行动与中国政府就解决华北危机的原则达成协议，否则只会延长冲突并使局势更加复杂。

Huge Exodus Resumed
Huge crowds of refugees poured into the International Settlement last night, following a radio broadcast by a Chinese station describing the Hungjao Road incident. Between 7 p.m. and 11 p.m. nearly six thousand Chinese passed over the Soochow Creek bridges, bringing their belongings into the Settlement area. Many showed signs of having hurriedly collected whatever they could carry most handily, and to have evacuated their homes in Chapei, Hongkew, and Yangtsepoo with the utmost haste.

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, AUGUST 8, 1937

GRATITUDE

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS.
Sir:—I am sure that many Russians residing in Shanghai felt as I did on Friday morning when they read the article in THE CHINA PRESS announcing that some 300 Russians had volunteered their services to Japan in the present crisis just as they did in 1932.
China was one of the few countries which opened its doors to Russian refugees at the time of the Revolution and thousands of them came to Shanghai in order to escape the Bolshevik rule. As a matter of fact leaving Russia at that time was a matter of life and death to many.
We have been given every opportunity to earn a living and to live in peace under the Chinese law, and countless Russians are at present in the employ of Chinese firms and I have never heard of any discrimination having been made against them.
And now, when China is facing the most serious crisis in her history some of these same Russians are offering their services to an enemy nation.
It brings to mind that song of some twenty years ago: "Don't Bite the Hand that's Feeding You."
I would like at this time to call the attention of Russians who have within the past few years come to China from Harbin, a move made after the occupation of Manchuria by Japanese. Russians living in the northern city at that time welcomed the Japanese with bread and salt, the highest tribute we can pay a foreigner. What happened? It was not long before Russians holding important positions were dismissed, and those who were able to obtain work were paid on the basis of a coolie. Not only that. Today the rule of the Japanese is so strong it is difficult for Russians of the younger generation to leave Harbin, the Japanese seeking to hold them for service which may be valuable in war time.
Actions of the Russians in Shanghai in 1932 was a blot on the escutcheon of those of us who are seeking to live in peace here and in harmony with the Chinese people.
While there are 300 said to be seeking to aid Japan, I am sure that the great majority of White Russians would be proud to take up arms in defence of China should their assistance be required.
I should appreciate your publishing this letter in the hope that it may dissuade that small corps of vagabonds from actually participating in a war against China.
Yours very truly,
S. V. H.

《字林西报》，1937年8月8日，星期日

感激之情

致《字林西报》编辑：
先生：——我相信，许多居住在上海的俄罗斯人，在周五早晨读到《字林西报》上刊登的文章时，心情与我相同。该文章宣称，约有300名俄罗斯人在当前危机中自愿为日本效力，正如他们在1932年所做的那样。
在革命时期，中国是为数不多的向俄罗斯难民敞开大门的国家之一，成千上万的俄罗斯人来到上海，以逃避布尔什维克的统治。事实上，当时离开俄罗斯对许多人来说事关生死。
我们获得了在中国法律下谋生和和平生活的一切机会，目前有无数的俄罗斯人受雇于中国公司，我从未听说过他们受到任何歧视。
而现在，当中国面临其历史上最严重的危机时，这些俄罗斯人中的一些人却主动向敌国提供服务。
这让人想起大约二十年前的那首歌：“不要咬喂你的手。”
在此，我想提请那些在过去几年从哈尔滨来到中国的俄罗斯人注意，这一举动是在日本占领满洲之后发生的。当时居住在那座北方城市的俄罗斯人用面包和盐欢迎日本人，这是我们能给予外国人的最高礼遇。结果如何？不久之后，担任重要职位的俄罗斯人被解职，而那些能够找到工作的人，其薪酬仅相当于苦力水平。不仅如此。如今日本的统治如此严密，年轻一代的俄罗斯人很难离开哈尔滨，日本人试图留住他们，以便在战时提供可能有价值的服务。
1932年上海俄罗斯人的行为，给我们这些寻求在此和平生活并与中国人民和谐相处的人的声誉抹了黑。
虽然据说有300人试图援助日本，但我确信，如果需要他们的协助，绝大多数白俄罗斯人会自豪地拿起武器保卫中国。
如蒙贵报刊登此信，以期劝阻那一小撮流浪汉实际参与对华战争，我将不胜感激。
您真诚的，
S. V. H.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年8月3日，星期二

外籍军团谣言再起；美国酒保入伍

在当前严峻局势下，所谓的外籍军团——或由外国雇佣兵组成、与中国军队并肩对抗日本的国际 brigade ——的传言再次在外侨社区流传，这为紧张气氛带来了一丝轻歌剧式的缓解。每当中国发生战争，无论是与日本人、蒙古人作战还是内部冲突，这类谣言就会浮现，但从未像今天这样持久，因为一场大规模战争已迫在眉睫。最 persistent 的谣言是，当地白俄罗斯社区中的热血青年正试图组建一支由俄罗斯前军人组成的部队，这些人是俄罗斯和西伯利亚多次艰苦战役的老兵，旨在为他们所收养的国家对抗日本。上海充斥着这类精锐的机枪手、炮兵、骑兵、前军官等，而在中国将军麾下服役的俄罗斯雇佣兵在该国近期历史中并不罕见，尤其是在满洲。保镖和看守认为自己特别适合这项工作，因为他们除了经验外，还具备实用的语言知识。
迄今为止，《晚邮报》注意到的唯一一名加入中国军队的外国雇佣兵的真实案例是“布莱基”·威尔斯（"Blackie" Wills），他在上海以一名体格健壮、词汇丰富的酒吧侍者而闻名。
据报道，“布莱基”曾在这里的“血巷”（Blood Alley）做酒保，后来去汉口从事同一职业，现在已从这座江畔大都市辞去调酒工作，成为随部队北上的机枪手，该部队经平汉铁路开往保定府。报道补充说，凭借过去在法国及其他地方担任机枪手的经验，他获得了中尉委任状。威尔斯几年前作为海员来到中国。目前无人知晓他确切身在何处，但推测可能在冀南某处。
然而，据多方消息来源报告，过去几天里，一些英语流利且显然拥有大量资金的中国代理人在市内四处活动，接触外国退伍老兵。今天来自洛杉矶的一则报道称，182名美国飞行员已加入中国服役，另有304人仅在洛杉矶地区就试图入伍，这促使美国地区检察官警告称，美国志愿者参与外国战争属于联邦犯罪行为。声称曾是张作霖将军前副官的拉塞尔·L·赫恩（Russel L. Hearn）中将目前在洛杉矶，据称与中国空军有关。伯特·霍尔（Bert Hall），美国雇佣兵、军火走私者和飞行员；独臂萨顿（One-Arm Sutton），爱尔兰冒险家，曾效力于张作霖；广州的科恩将军（General Cohen）；这些人以及另外数十人——英国人、德国人和俄罗斯人——构成了中国所谓外籍军团的灵感来源。此处需回顾的是，在1932年上海战事期间，这里也曾广泛流传关于此类组织的言论。

《字林西报》，1937年8月9日，星期一

美国人应征
为中国服役

中国大使馆否认
有任何关联

大规模购买飞机
的报道似不可能

华盛顿，8月8日电。
中国驻美大使馆发言人今日表示，中国官员与据报道的美国公民加入中国军队一事没有任何关联。然而，每天都有数十封来信，来自希望志愿为中国军队服役的人士。
内华达州参议员基·皮特曼（Key Pittman）在今天关于禁止举着标语牌者接近本国外国大使馆和公使馆的法案辩论过程中指出，身处中国“战区”的美国人正面临“绝望的境地”。他补充说，美国政府“一个月来一直努力促使日本政府和中国政府为我国国民提供安全通行保证，但迄今收效甚微。”——合众社。

赫尔先生的立场
针对东京发来的电讯称日本已获得保证，即不允许在美国境内为中国军队招募人员，国务卿科德尔·赫尔（Cordell Hull）先生今日表示，未就此事向美国提出任何交涉。他重申，美国将对所有国家平等执行涉及此类招募的任何法律。——合众社。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, AUGUST 9, 1937

FURTHER REFUGEES
REACH SHANGHAI
Japanese Families Among
Those Leaving

DISAPPOINTED HORDES
LEFT ON JETTIES

A large number of Chinese and
Japanese refugees passed through
Shanghai yesterday bound for, in the
case of the Chinese, Yangtsze river
and Chekiang ports, and, in the case
of the Japanese, Nagasaki, Kobe and
Yokohama. Besides, thousands came
into the International Settlement and
the French Concession from the
northern area, western Chapei and
Nantao, and by rail from points on
the Shanghai-Woosung Railway and
the Shanghai-Nanking Railway.
Steamers, under British and Chi-
nese flags, which left for Ningpo and
Hankow again carried capacity num-
bers of refugees. The ss. Tuck Wo,
of the Indo-China Steam Navigation
Company, was delayed for several
hours at Hunt's Wharf, Hongkew, and
left behind hundreds of refugees on
the wharf. Many families spread
their bedding on the ground and on
piles of stone on the jetty, waiting
for better luck on subsequent boats.
Food hawkers thronged the wharf to
supply the needs of the hundreds
camping there yesterday afternoon.
On other jetties other hundreds
waited.
Japanese families left in numbers
for their home country, some being
refugees from up the Yangtse River
and others being from the North
Szechuen Road district of Shanghai.
More Japanese are expected to arrive
from the Yangtse ports to-day, in-
cluding many Hankow refugees.
The exodus from Hongkew,
Chapei, Kashing Road, West Heng-
kew, Yangtzepoo, Kiangwan, and
the western "outside roads" area
continued heavily yesterday. It was
estimated that during the morning
hours alone more than 1,000 refugees
on an average passed over the
Soochow Creek bridges every hour.
A steady stream of vehicles was
observed in the afternoon.

《字林西报》，1937年8月9日，星期一

更多难民
抵达上海
离沪者中有
日本家庭

失望的人群
滞留码头

昨日，大批中国和难民经过上海前往各地，其中中国难民前往长江沿线及浙江港口，日本难民则前往长崎、神户和横滨。此外，成千上万的人从北部地区、闸北西部和南市，以及通过沪淞铁路和沪宁铁路沿线的站点，进入公共租界和法租界。
悬挂英国和中国旗帜、驶往宁波和汉口的轮船再次载满了难民。印度支那轮船公司的“德和”号（ss. Tuck Wo）在虹口亨氏码头（Hunt's Wharf）延误了数小时，将数百名难民留在了码头上。许多家庭将被褥铺在码头地面和石堆上，等待后续船只带来更好的运气。食品小贩涌向码头，以满足昨天下午在那里露营的数百人的需求。
在其他码头，又有数百人在等待。
日本家庭成群结队地返回祖国，其中一些是来自长江上游的难民，另一些则来自上海北四川路地区。预计今天将有更多日本人从长江各港口抵达，其中包括许多来自汉口的难民。
昨日，从虹口、闸北、嘉善路、西虹口、杨树浦、江湾以及西部“越界筑路”地区的撤离潮依然汹涌。据估计，仅上午时段，平均每小时就有超过1,000名难民穿过苏州河桥梁。下午观察到车辆川流不息。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, AUGUST 9, 1937
7994/5-

CONCENTRATION OF
CHINESE TROOPS

Japanese Report Movement
Along Hopei Borders

Tientsin, Aug. 8.
Heavy Chinese concentrations in southern Charhar and Shansi were reported in military intelligence dispatches reaching Japanese headquarters here to-day.
Spread along a north-westerly arc, following the Charhar border with Hopei and Jehol were said to be troops belonging to the 89th Division. Their main points of concentration were reported as Hwalai, on the Peiping-Suiyuan railway about fifty miles west of Nankow Pass, Yenking, on the Great Wall, and Yungning, closer to the Jehol frontier.
Further to the north at Lungkwan and Chihcheng were reported to be forces of the 84th Division, while the 143rd Division was said to be concentrated at Suanhua on the Peiping-Suiyuan railway and Kalgan.
These movements, Japanese military authorities here contended, constituted a violation of the agreement for the demilitarization of areas adjoining Manchoukuo, concluded between Gen. Chin Teh-chun, former mayor of Peiping, and Major Gen. Kenji Doihara, former chief of the special service division of the Kwantung Army.
The Fourth Central Army was further reported to be digging-in at Siahwayuan and Shacheng also on the Peiping-Suiyuan line between Kalgan and Nankow Pass.
The 21st Division of the Central Government's Army was reported to be moving from Tatung, in the north-eastern corner of Shansi, to Pingtichuan, along the Peiping-Suiyuan Railway in Suiyuan.
The division numbers 15,000 men. Pingtichuan gained fame earlier this year as the headquarters of Suiyuan forces battling with anti-Chinese Mongol units and irregulars.
The 77th Division was reported to be already in Suiyuan, while the 89th Central Division was said to be in Tatung.—Domei.

7994/5-

中国军队集结

日军报告河北边境的调动情况

天津，8月8日电。今日抵达驻此间日军总部的军事情报电文称，察哈尔南部和山西有大量中国军队集结。
据称，沿察哈尔与河北及热河边界呈西北向弧形分布的是第89师的部队。据报道，其主要集结点为位于北平绥远铁路、南口以西约五十英里处的怀来，长城上的延庆，以及更靠近热河边界的永宁。
在更北面的龙关和赤城，据报有第84师的部队，而第143师则据称集结于北平绥远铁路上的宣化和张家口。
驻此间的日本军方当局声称，这些行动违反了前北平市长秦德纯将军与前关东军特务机关长土肥原贤二少将之间达成的关于满洲国毗邻地区非军事化的协议。
另据报道，第四中央军正在张家口与南口之间的北平绥远铁路线上的下花园和沙城挖掘战壕。
据报，中央政府军的第21师正从山西北角的大同，沿绥远境内的北平绥远铁路向平地泉移动。
该师兵力为15,000人。今年早些时候，平地泉因作为绥远部队与反华蒙古部队及非正规军作战的总部而闻名。
据报道，第77师已抵达绥远，而中央军第89师据称在大同。——同盟社

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, August 10, 1937
23582
Exodus Slowing Down
Despite New Incident,
Brief Period Of Panic
7994/-
Police Continue To Maintain Close Hongkew
Watch; Paoantui Said Active; Japanese
Allege Nationals Stoned

Despite the excitement caused by the incident at the
Hungjao Airdrome yesterday evening, the exodus from the
Chapel, Hongkew, Wayside and Yangtzepoo areas decreased
during the past 24 hours. Only from 7 to 12 o'clock last night
was there any sign of an increase when people streamed into
the Sinza district in such numbers that it was impossible to
count them. Most of them were travelling light, either having
left in such panic that they for-
got their possessions or else hav-
ing sent out their goods earlier.
In the Hongkew area this
morning police were making their
rounds in patrols composed of one
foreign sergeant, one Chinese
sergeant and two Chinese con-
stables. Although no official
statement was made known, it is
believed that some S.M.P. Specials
were last night called out for
patrol duty in Hongkew.
Motorists Stopped
Hongkew and Wayside pawn-
shop owners were this morning
busily moving their valuables to
places of safety in the French
Concession and Settlement. Most
of the shops were refusing to take
new pledges, confining their busi-
ness to redemption of pawned
articles.
Motorists found it impossible to
pass beyond Klangwan Road last
night, being turned by steel-hel-
meted members of the Shanghai
City Police and Peace Preservation
Corps who carried mausers and
had bayonets fixed. Curfew passes
were being issued, only persons
armed with such permits being
allowed to pass this point.
Truce Said Violated
Alleging that Chinese regular
soldiers dressed in Peace Preserva-
tion Corps uniforms in order not
to violate the Shanghai truce
agreement have been holding
nightly maneuvers and building
fortifications at Klangwan, the
Japanese today gave indication
that following the incident at the
Hungjao Airdrome they may de-
mand the withdrawal of the Corps
from the Shanghai area if their
suspicions prove correct. The
activities of these disguised reg-
ulars are blamed by the Japanese
for the exodus from Chapel,
Klangwan, Hongkew and the
North Essechuen Road districts.
The Japanese hold that the
situation in Shanghai is now worse
than it was prior to the Sino-
Japanese hostilities in 1932 and
state that in addition to nightly
maneuvers at Klangwan, anti-
Japanese feeling is openly mani-
fest in Hongkew where Japanese
residents are frequently pelted
with stones. They are also find-
ing difficulties in obtaining food
supplies, it is alleged, and the
community now remains indoors
after dark.
Store-Managers Arrested
Two alleged store-managers are
being held by the Chinese auth-
orities, following their arrest early
this morning. It is understood
they were taken into custody in
connection with the alleged ston-
ing of Japanese nationals.
students in Japan, Mr. Chen
Chih-fu, left for Japan yesterday
morning to supervise the with-
drawal of students.
Japanese Ships Here
> Japanese men-of-war ar-
rived in port yesterday to add to
the already imposing display of
Japanese naval power, the vessels
being the flagship Yaeyama of the
Eleventh Torpedo Flotilla and the
gunboats Futami, Hozu, Toba,
Tsuga, Kuri, Seta, Kotaka and
Hira.
The Emergency Service for Sol-
diers of the Y.M.C.A.'s of China
has launched a campaign to raise
$120,000 for supporting three bases
to take care of wounded soldiers
and do other war work with the
Chinese armies. The drive for
funds is to be nation-wide with
general headquarters at the Na-
tional Committee Y.M.C.A. build-
ing, 131 Museum Road.
Chinese To Leave Japan
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs
is today reported to have decided
to send a fleet of six ships to
Japan to evacuate the Chinese
populace there in the event the
Sino-Japanese crisis develops into
a major conflict. The overseas
Chinese have already been in-
structed to concentrate in the
coastal ports.
The ships will be those belong-
ing to the China Merchants'
Steam Navigation Company.
Officials from the Waichiaopu
will accompany the ships to
Japan.
Japanese En Route
With the exception of Shang-
hai, the evacuation of Japanese
nationals from river ports in the
Yangtse Valley has been com-
pleted.
A party of Japanese in Kiu-
kiang, it is reported, yesterday
boarded a gunboat for Shanghai.
From Hankow some 1800 Japan-
ese nationals have been evacuat-
ed during the last few days.
It is learned that out of the
total Japanese population of 362
in Nanking, nearly all have left
for Shanghai those remaining
behind being a few employees of
the Domei News Agency and staff
members of the Japanese Con-
sulate-General. The Domei group
is reported to have moved from
the city to Hsiakwan, preparatory
to evacuation following the im-
minent closing down of the news
agency.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年8月10日，星期二
23582
尽管发生新事件，
短暂恐慌后，
外逃潮减缓
7994/-
警方继续严密监视虹口；据说保安团活动频繁；日方指控侨民遭石击

尽管昨晚虹桥机场事件引起了骚动，但在过去24小时内，从礼拜堂、虹口、韦斯特赛德（Wayside）和杨树浦地区的外逃人数有所减少。仅在昨晚7点至12点期间出现增加迹象，当时人群涌入闸北地区，数量之多无法统计。大多数人轻装简行，要么是因惊慌失措而忘记了携带财物，要么是早已将物品运出。
今天上午，在虹口地区，警察由一名外籍巡官、一名华籍巡官和两名华籍巡捕组成巡逻队进行巡视。虽然未发表官方声明，但据信昨晚一些工部局警务处特别巡捕（S.M.P. Specials）被召至虹口执行巡逻任务。
机动车受阻
今天上午，虹口和韦斯特赛德的当铺老板正忙着将贵重物品转移到法租界和公共租界的安全地点。大多数店铺拒绝接受新的典当，业务仅限于赎回已当物品。
昨晚，驾车者发现无法越过江湾路，因为被头戴钢盔、手持毛瑟枪并上着刺刀的上海市警察和保安团成员拦回。宵禁通行证正在发放，只有持有此类许可证的人才被允许通过该点。
称停战协定遭违反
日方今日暗示，继虹桥机场事件之后，如果其怀疑得到证实，他们可能会要求将该保安团撤出上海地区。日方指控，为了不违反上海停战协定，身穿保安团制服的中国正规军一直在江湾进行夜间演习并修筑工事。日方将这些伪装成正规军的活动的责任归咎于导致礼拜堂、江湾、虹口和北四川路地区居民外逃的原因。
日方认为，上海目前的局势比1932年中日敌对行动之前更糟，并称除了在江湾进行夜间演习外，反日情绪在虹口公开显现，日本居民经常遭到石击。据称，他们在获取食物供应方面也遇到困难，社区成员现在天黑后便待在室内。
商店经理被捕
两名涉嫌商店经理的人在今天清晨被捕后，正由中国当局拘留。据悉，他们因涉嫌参与石击日本侨民事件而被收押。
在日本的学生，陈志甫先生，昨天上午启程前往日本，以监督学生撤离工作。
日舰抵沪
> 日本军舰昨日抵达港口，增加了原本已令人瞩目的日本海军力量展示，这些船只包括第十一鱼雷艇队的旗舰“八重山”号，以及炮舰“二见”号、“保津”号、“鸟羽”号、“栂”号、“栗”号、“势多”号、“小鹰”号和“平户”号。
中国青年会军人紧急服务处发起了一项运动，旨在筹集12万美元，用于支持三个基地，以照顾伤兵并配合中国军队开展其他战时工作。这次募捐活动将在全国范围内进行，总指挥部设在博物馆路131号的全国青年会委员会大楼。
中国人将离开日本
据报道，外交部今日决定派遣一支由六艘船组成的舰队前往日本，以便在中日危机发展为重大冲突时撤离那里的中国民众。海外华人已接到指示，在沿海港口集中。
这些船只将属于轮船招商局。
外交部官员将随船前往日本。
日侨在途
除上海外，长江流域各河港的日本侨民撤离工作已完成。
据报道，九江的一批日本人昨天登上了一艘炮舰前往上海。
在过去几天里，约有1800名日本侨民已从汉口撤离。
获悉在南京总共362名日本人口中，几乎所有人都已前往上海，留下的少数人是同盟社通讯社的员工和日本总领事馆的工作人员。据报道，随着该通讯社即将关闭，同盟社小组已从市区移至下关，为撤离做准备。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, AUGUST 10, 1937

SHANGHAI'S ATTITUDE
Apart from the fact that many thousands of the Chinese population in Shanghai have precipitately fled their homes in Chinese-controlled territory and sought what they believe to be safer accommodation in the Settlement and Concession, there is a very welcome absence of what might be described as tension or alarm. From the police point of view, the behaviour of all sections of the community in these trying days of uncertainty as to the future of Sino-Japanese relations has been remarkably good and there seems to be a widespread realization of the fact that if Shanghai wishes to avoid anything comparable to the ruinous chaos which prevailed here in the early months of 1932 then it is entirely up to Shanghai people themselves to do so. It has been well pointed out that Shanghai is of international character and that in the event of the Sino-Japanese situation developing into the widely unhoped-for war this area ought to be strictly regarded on both sides as lying outside the territory over which any of that trial of strength would be waged. It is incumbent upon all—Chinese, Japanese and foreigners of all nationalities—to keep Shanghai not only inviolate against physical strife but also as free as possible of partisan ebullition and demonstration. Peace will be kept here only if good sense and judgment is shown, and the manner in which public behaviour has so far been controlled would seem to augur well for the future. The authorities of all areas are, we believe, doing all that lies within their power to check and discourage the growth of any movement which might be considered to lead to public display, and it is to be hoped that the non-official leaders of the communities will loyally co-operate with those authorities and lend no aid of any kind to misguided activities by patriotic bodies.
The calmness with which Shanghai is awaiting the outcome of Nanking's and Tokyo's efforts, and the spirit of co-operation which exists here has been well evidenced during the past week in the financial market. When the clouds of war darkened towards the end of last week there were not a few people who naturally wondered what the future of the Chinese dollar was going to be and there was a fair amount of foreign currency buying. It would be an exaggeration to say that there was a rush to sell dollars, but there was a good deal of coverage done along the lines of prudent insurance against the possibility of an early and precipitate drop. Many merchants wisely decided that it was better to stabilize their exchange commitments as far as they could now rather than take a risk over two or three months. And so there was a good deal of foreign currency buying, which the Central Bank was well able to take care of, thanks to the support it received from the foreign banks. The nature of that support was not in the way of actual funds—of which the Central Bank is adequately possessed—but in the co-operative avoidance of encouraging anything in the way of speculation or of indulging in it themselves. With the Central Bank placed as it is to-day it is a valuable thing to have the foreign banks in Shanghai co-operating to keep things stable, and it is symptomatic of the calm with which Shanghai views an admittedly serious situation that there is in the financial and monetary realm a working together to avoid difficulty. So long as the Central Bank continues to function as it is now doing there need be no fears regarding the maintenance of the exchange value of the dollar, though of course everybody knows that if there develops a large-scale and long-drawn-out war the financial resources of this country will be taxed to the utmost and the recently-created structure threatened. But that is looking ahead to the worst possibility—not a very profitable or reassuring thing to do at any time. At the moment, there is no need for panic and the manner in which all concerned are refusing to display that negative symptom deserves tribute.

G.J.Sih S.I

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年8月10日，星期二

上海的态度

除了上海成千上万的中国居民仓促逃离中国控制区的家园，寻求他们认为在租界和公租界内更安全的住所这一事实外，这里非常可喜地没有出现可以形容为紧张或恐慌的气氛。从警方的角度来看，在中日关系未来充满不确定性的这些艰难日子里，社会各界的表现 remarkably good（非常好），而且似乎普遍认识到这样一个事实：如果上海希望避免任何类似于1932年头几个月在这里盛行的毁灭性混乱的局面，那么这完全取决于上海人自己。有人很好地指出，上海具有国际性质，如果中日局势发展为人们普遍不希望看到的战争，那么双方都应严格视该地区为不属于任何实力较量所涉及的领土。所有人——中国人、日本人和所有国籍的外国人——都有责任保持上海不仅不受物理冲突的侵犯，而且尽可能免受党派激情和示威的影响。只有表现出理智和判断力，才能在这里维持和平，而迄今为止公众行为受到控制的方式似乎预示着良好的未来。我们相信，各地区的当局正在尽其所能遏制和劝阻任何可能导致公开示威的运动的增长，并希望社区的非官方领导人能忠实地与这些当局合作，不为爱国团体的误导活动提供任何援助。

上海冷静等待南京和东京努力的结果，以及这里存在的合作精神，在过去一周的金融市场中得到了很好的体现。当上周周末战争阴云密布时，自然有不少人想知道中国法币的未来会怎样，并且出现了相当数量的外币购买。如果说出现了抛售法币的狂潮那是夸张了，但为了防范早期和突然下跌的可能性，许多人进行了谨慎的对冲操作。许多商人明智地决定，最好现在就尽可能稳定他们的外汇承诺，而不是在两三个月内冒险。因此，出现了大量的外币购买，得益于外国银行的支持，中央银行完全能够应对。这种支持的性质并非实际资金——中央银行拥有充足的资金——而是合作避免鼓励任何形式的投机，或者自身不参与投机。鉴于中央银行目前的地位，上海的外国银行合作维持稳定是一件有价值的事情，而在金融和货币领域共同努力避免困难，也象征着上海以冷静的态度看待 admittedly serious（确实严重）的局势。只要中央银行继续像现在这样运作，就无需担心法币汇率的维持，当然，每个人都知道，如果爆发大规模且持久的战争，这个国家的财政资源将被榨取到极限，最近建立的体系将受到威胁。但那是展望最坏的可能性——这在任何时候都不是一件很有益或令人安心的事情。目前，没有恐慌的必要，所有相关方拒绝表现出这种负面症状的方式值得赞扬。

G.J.Sih S.I

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, AUGUST 9, 1937    23563

SHANGHAI'S ROLE

There is still ground for hoping that by some adroit adjustment of their respective views, the Chinese and Japanese Governments will be able to come to an agreement which averts the peril of a major conflict. Both sides are taking steps to prepare for the worst. The Japanese evacuation of Hankow is not to be regarded entirely in that light. It has been accomplished with admirable dignity and with evident co-operation from the local Chinese authorities. Although, obviously, it must put a large number of Japanese citizens to inconvenience and distress which it would have been hoped that they could be spared, it may be inspired by a desire to ease the situation rather than to aggravate it. The Japanese authorities, it is true, are relieved of an obligation which might prove burdensome in the event of hostilities. They may, however, also be given credit for a drastic action which reduces to a minimum in Hankow the danger of any untoward happening prejudicial to the search for a peaceful solution of the main issues elsewhere. Here in Shanghai they are largely covered by the international status of this city, and, in addition, they have established with the Chinese authorities a good contact to which they have made valuable contribution by adopting measures calculated to promote restraint and maintain satisfactory relationships. Responsible Chinese, headed by the new Mayor, have shown their sense of the wisdom of a mutual forbearance. Other communities will assuredly desire to assist in this essential task and to do all that lies in their power to encourage the preservation of an atmosphere appropriate to Shanghai's specially delicate position. The chief duty of every Shanghailander at this critical time is to remember that his or her civic status is for the nonce of major importance. National feelings cannot be dragooned or suppressed but they should be directed into such channels as are compatible with the basic internationality of this important city.

Shanghai can do much to facilitate a peaceful settlement. It cannot—and should not—do anything to precipitate bellicose sentiments on either. The chief responsibility for determining the unfortunate differences which have arisen between China and Japan rests on the shoulders of the Central Government at Nanking and the Japanese Government at Tokyo. Shanghailanders have a right to form and express their opinions thereon always remembering the limitations of their position and the international polity in which they live. The French Concession is under French, the International Settlement under International and the City Government of Shanghai under Chinese control. The neutrality of the Concession requires no elaboration. The International character of the Settlement involves elements of Japanese and Chinese direction which has to preserve with the other national elements a corporate neutrality, using that term in the non-technical sense. The position of the Chinese municipality is not much different, for the agreement of May 1932 which brought to an end the Sino-Japanese hostilities of that year imposed on the Chinese authorities certain obligations which they are understood to have recognized, for keeping the area round Shanghai free of military commitments. It is important, then, without entering into abstruse questions of international law, to remember that Shanghai as a whole is international in its composition and should be scrupulously preserved from direct participation in such military activities as may, unhappily, accrue, from the present crisis. In the event of the efforts of the peace-makers proving unsuccessful, Chinese will fellow-citizens. Each will do well to show tolerance of the other's point of view, especially as any contrary action would neither advance nor retard their respective causes and would certainly import into the situation here a complication which both countries would fain see avoided.

This prescription has been generally endorsed and the comparative quietness which has governed Shanghai's occasions during the last month does credit to Chinese and Japanese leaders alike. Now that the major issues under treatment at Nanking and Tokyo have developed in gravity it is natural that the predominantly Chinese population of Shanghai should feel the effects of certain patriotic appeals quite properly issued from the Central Government. It is highly important, however, that severe discrimination should be brought to bear on the manner in which response is forthcoming. What may be most creditable and, indeed, imperative in purely Chinese territory may, in the peculiar circumstances here, be open to valid criticism, as calculated to impair Shanghai's neutrality. Leaving out of account the domain of the City Government which may be expected to continue along the lines so sagely prescribed by its Mayor in the exercise of his authority under the National Government and with due regard to the obligations under the agreement of May 1932, already cited, it should at once be observed that in the International Settlement—as also in the French Concession—there can be no toleration of activities which connote direct participation in hostilities between China and Japan, either present or prospective. However correct may be the organization of "anti-aggression" associations outside Shanghai it cannot be attempted without involving belligerent responsibilities. In Shanghai, therefore, it is incompatible with the state of neutrality which all communities do desire to maintain here. To humanitarian efforts for red cross work, relief of war victims and the like, the same objection cannot be maintained. So long as there is a possibility that peace will prevail and that Tokyo and Nanking will eventually solve their difficulties without recourse to major hostilities, it is proper for Shanghai, with reasonable attention to international courtesy and fairness, to form and express opinions. Raging, tearing propaganda, from whatever side, should be eschewed, if only on the practical ground that it is least conducive to the common aim of restoring stability. If, unfortunately, peace should not prevail, Shanghai, in its own interests which, incidentally, are those of China as well as of Japan and other foreign powers, will then be well-advised to concentrate on the cultivation of neutrality and address itself to the problem of the conflict in an objective frame of mind. Whatever may be the outcome of the crisis, Shanghai cannot serve itself or the two principals to the dispute better than by adopting a rigid line of neutrality and so preserving its resources, both moral and material, for the beneficent work of reparation when the occasion comes.

上海的角色

仍有理由希望，中日两国政府若能巧妙地调整各自立场，便能达成协议，从而避免重大冲突的危险。双方均在采取步骤，为最坏的情况做准备。日本从汉口的撤侨行动不应完全从这个角度去看待。该行动以令人钦佩的庄重方式完成，并得到了当地中国当局的明显配合。尽管这显然给大量日本公民带来了本希望他们能免予承受的不便与痛苦，但其动机可能是为了缓和而非加剧局势。诚然，日本当局由此摆脱了一项在敌对行动爆发时可能证明是沉重负担的义务。然而，他们也应因这一果断行动而受到肯定，该行动将汉口任何可能妨碍在其他地方寻求和平解决主要问题的意外事件的风险降到了最低。在上海，他们在很大程度上受到本市国际地位的保护；此外，他们与中国当局建立了良好的联系，并通过采取旨在促进克制和维持满意关系的措施，为此做出了宝贵贡献。以新任市长为首的中国负责任人士，展现了相互克制的智慧。其他社群无疑也渴望协助完成这一重要任务，并尽其所能鼓励保持一种适合上海特殊敏感地位的 atmosphere（氛围）。在此关键时刻，每个上海居民的首要责任是记住，其市民身份目前具有至关重要的重要性。民族情感不能受到强制或压制，但应将其引导至与本重要城市基本国际性相容的渠道中。

上海能为促进和平解决做很多事。它不能——也不应——做任何会激起任何一方好战情绪的事。决定中日之间出现的不幸分歧的主要责任，在于南京的中央政府和东京的日本政府肩上。上海居民有权就此形成并表达意见，但须始终铭记其地位的局限性以及其所生活的国际政体。法租界受法国控制，公共租界受国际控制，上海市政府受中国控制。租界的中立性无需赘述。租界的国际性质涉及日本和中国方面的因素，它们必须与其他国家因素一起保持一种集体中立性，此处使用该词的非技术性含义。中国市政当局的处境并无太大不同，因为结束当年中日敌对行动的1932年5月协定，对中国当局施加了某些义务，据信他们已承认这些义务，即保持上海周边地区无军事部署。因此，重要的是，在不深入探讨复杂的国际法问题的情况下，要记住上海作为一个整体在其构成上是国际性的，应谨慎地使其免于直接参与可能不幸由当前危机引发的任何军事活动。如果和平努力证明不成功，中国人将是同胞公民。双方都最好表现出对对方观点的宽容，特别是因为任何相反的行动既不会促进也不会阻碍各自的事业，而且肯定会给这里的局势带来两国都希望能避免的复杂化。

这一主张已得到普遍认可，过去一个月上海场合中相对的平静，为中国和日本的领导人皆赢得了赞誉。既然南京和东京正在处理的主要问题事态日益严重，上海以中国人为主的人口感受到中央政府正当发出的某些爱国呼吁的影响，也是自然的。然而，极其重要的是，应对回应的方式加以严格的甄别。在纯中国领土上可能最值得称赞、甚至势在必行的行为，在此地的特殊情况下，可能会受到合理的批评，因为其被认为会损害上海的中立性。且不谈市政府的领域，预计其将继续沿着市长在国家政府授权下明智规定的路线行使权力，并适当顾及前述1932年5月协定下的义务，应立即指出的是，在公共租界——以及在法租界——不能容忍任何意味着直接或间接参与中日之间现有或潜在敌对行动的活动。无论上海以外的“反侵略”协会组织得多么正确，若不卷入交战责任，便无法在此进行。因此，这在所有社群都希望在此维持的中立状态下是不相容的。对于红十字会工作、战争受害者救济等人道主义努力，则不能持同样的反对意见。只要和平仍有可能占上风，且东京和南京最终能在不诉诸大规模敌对行动的情况下解决困难，上海在合理注意国际礼仪和公平的前提下，形成并表达意见是恰当的。无论来自哪一方的激烈、撕裂性的宣传都应避免，仅就实际而言，因为它最不利于恢复稳定这一共同目标。如果不幸和平未能占上风，上海出于自身利益——顺便提一下，这也是中国、日本及其他外国列强的利益——届时最好专注于培养中立性，并以客观的心态着手处理冲突问题。无论危机结果如何，上海若能采取严格的中立路线，从而保存其道德和物质资源，以便在时机到来时从事有益的修复工作，便是对自己以及争端双方最好的服务。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, AUGUST 10, 1937
7994/6—

1,000 Stitch Belts
To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—We read in the papers that
the Chinese are making every effort
to keep peace in Shanghai and that
the Japanese are also doing their
part.
On Sunday we went to the Hong-
kew market and were very surprised
to see crowds of little Japanese girls
stopping every Japanese woman who
was making purchases to put stitches
in their "1,000 stitch belts" which
they carried. Is this not war pro-
paganda? There is nothing to pre-
vent the Japanese children doing
this in their homes or schools, but
in a public place which is crowded
with Chinese, is this wise? Should
one of these children be hurt ac-
cidentally while interfering with the
sale of goods in the market there
would be another "incident." Should
not the Japanese authorities do some-
thing to stop this practice?
SENSIBLE.
Shanghai, Aug. 9.

理智者。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, AUGUST 10, 1937

CHINESE SOLDIERS
NEAR SHANGHAI

Nightly Manoeuvres Said
Being Held On The
Outskirts

VIOLATION OF THE 1932
TRUCE ALLEGED

TOKYO, Aug. 9.—Chinese regular soldiers, dressed in Peace Preservation Corps uniforms to abide by the terms of the Shanghai truce agreement, are now engaged in building fortifications at Kiangwan, outside Shanghai, the Navy Ministry was advised to-day by the office of the Naval Attache to the Japanese Embassy in China.

These "masqueraders," the report alleged, were engaged in nightly manoeuvres in the northern outskirts of Shanghai, an area demilitarized by the truce accord of 1932.

These activities, the dispatch went on, has caused Chinese to evacuate in large numbers from Chapei, Kiangwan, Hongkew and the North Szechuen Road districts. Indicative of the acute tension existing in the city, the residents of the Yangtzepoo district are also evacuating their homes for the first time in recent history.

Japanese residents living outside of the Settlement, the report said, are moving in. The Japanese community in Shanghai, the report added, are experiencing difficulty in obtaining foodstuffs because of the refusal of Chinese dealers to sell to Japanese nationals.

There were several instances of Japanese being pelted with rocks, the report said. Consequently, the Japanese community remains indoors after darkness. Most of the amusement centres in the Hongkew District were said by the report to have been closed.—Domei.

中国士兵
逼近上海

据称夜间演习
正在郊区举行

被指违反1932年
停战协定

东京，8月9日电。——据日本驻华大使馆海军武官办公室今日告知海军省，身穿保安队制服以遵守上海停战协定条款的中国正规军，目前正在上海郊外的江湾修建防御工事。

报告称，这些“伪装者”正在上海北部郊区进行夜间演习，该区域根据1932年的停战协定已非军事化。

电文接着称，这些活动已导致大量中国人从闸北、江湾、虹口和北四川路地区撤离。杨浦区居民也在近期历史上首次撤离家园，这表明城市中存在的紧张局势极为严峻。

报告称，居住在租界以外的日本居民正在迁入。报告补充说，由于中国商人拒绝向日本国民出售食品，上海的日本社群在获取食物方面遇到困难。

报告称，发生了几起日本人被石块投掷的事件。因此，日本社群在天黑后留在室内。据报告称，虹口区的大多数娱乐场所已关闭。——同盟社。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, AUGUST 10, 1937

Failure
Of Bank
In Crisis

Bond Speculation And
Heavy Withdrawals
Said Cause

Reported as another victim of
speculation in Government bonds,
the prices of which have suffered
violent fluctuations as a result of the
developments in North China, the
Shanghai Mercantile Bank, Ltd., of
100 Tientsin Road, closed its doors
yesterday with a reported indebted-
ness of about $1,000,000.

Established 12 years ago, the clos-
ed institution had a good footing
when it was first started with a
small capital of only $300,000. After
a few years the capital was increas-
ed by $200,000. Again in 1933 $250,-
000 was added to the capital. The
bank had been doing good business
since then and the annual turnover
was said to have amounted to nearly
$3,000,000.

At a meeting held on Sunday
night, the directors of the institution
decided to close the business. A
lawyer and an accountant have been
employed to handle the liquidation
procedure. Directors of the bank
will hold a meeting on August 30 to
discuss their position.

The recent losses sustained by the
bank were further aggravated by
the fact that during the past few
days many customers went to the
bank to withdraw their deposits.
The sum thus taken away amounted
to $300,000, it was stated.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年8月10日，星期二

银行在危机中
倒闭

据称原因为公债投机
及大量提款

上海商业储蓄银行有限公司（位于天津路100号）昨日关门，据报道负债约100万美元，成为华北事态发展导致价格剧烈波动的政府公债投机的又一受害者。

该机构成立于12年前，初创时资本仅为30万美元，基础良好。几年后，资本增加了20万美元。1933年，资本又增加了25万美元。此后银行业务良好，据称年营业额近300万美元。

在周日晚举行的会议上，该机构董事决定停止营业。已聘请一名律师和一名会计师处理清算程序。银行董事将于8月30日举行会议，讨论其处境。

过去几天许多客户前往银行提取存款，这一事实进一步加剧了银行最近的损失。据称，由此取走的金额达30万美元。

THE CHINA PRESS. TUESDAY, AUGUST 10, 1937.

Bank Hit By
Crisis, Decides
To Close Doors

Influenced by the tense situation
and slackening of business, the
Shanghai Mercantile Bank, Ltd.,
100 Tientsin Road, suspended tem-
porarily its public transactions as
from yesterday, according to resolu-
tion passed in an emergency meet-
ing of the board of directors and
stockholders held late Sunday
night.
The bank, which is one of the
members of the Shanghai Bankers'
Guild, has been conducting steady
and prosperous business within the
last few years until recently when
the current deposits department
became hard-hit by the crisis,
which is chiefly responsible for the
temporary closing.
It was also resolved at the
conference that a general meeting
of all shareholders of the bank will
be held on August 30 to discuss
measures for the carrying on of
public transactions within the short-
est period.
The Shanghai Mercantile Bank,
Ltd. was inaugurated right before
the world's economic depression.
In 1932 the bank was formally
opened for commerce and sav-
ings, with a capital of $300,000,
Chinese currency. In 1890 all its
stocks and bonds reached an
amount of $20,000, making a total
asset of half a million dollars. In
1933 it mounted to the $700,000th
mark.
Official notice concerning the
temporary closing of the bank was
made through Lawyer Wu Ling-
yun and Accountant Pan Hiu-lun

银行遭遇危机，决定停业

受局势紧张及商业萧条的影响，位于天津路100号的上海商业储蓄银行有限公司（Shanghai Mercantile Bank, Ltd.）根据周日深夜召开的董事会及股东紧急会议通过的决议，自昨日起暂时停止对外营业。

该行系上海银行业同业公会成员之一，在过去几年中业务一直稳健繁荣，直至近期其活期存款部受到危机的严重冲击，这也是导致此次暂时停业的主要原因。

会议还决议，将于8月30日召开全体股东大会，商讨如何在最短期限内恢复对外营业的措施。

上海商业储蓄银行有限公司是在世界经济大萧条前夕成立的。1932年，该行正式开业经营商业及储蓄业务，资本为法币30万元。1890年（原文如此），其所有股票和债券总额达到2万美元，总资产达50万美元。1933年，这一数字增至70万美元。

关于银行暂时停业的正式公告由吴凌云律师和潘希伦会计师发布

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, AUGUST 10, 1937

Boatloads Of Japanese Here
From Yangtze Ports

Nearly One Thousand Men, Women And Children
Reach Shanghai Yesterday; Story Told Of
How Hankow Was Hurriedly Evacuated

Escorted most of the way down
the Yangtze by five warships, the
s.s. Fengyang Maru arrived in port
yesterday morning bringing with
her hundreds of Japanese refugees
from Hankow and other up-river
towns.
The ship presented a pathetic
sight on her arrival, as every foot
of her deck space was crammed
with unhappy men, women and
children.
Yesterday afternoon, the refugees
held an extraordinary meeting
aboard the steamer and passed the
following resolution:
"We, the Japanese residents of
Hankow, have left our homes in ac-
cordance with the Government's
orders, leaving behind our private
and public property.
"We express hereby our hope that
the Government will continue to
protect Japan's vested rights and
interests in this country, doing away
with the anti-Japanese sentiment
pervading China."
Tears In Hankow
As the Fengyang Maru and the
Hsinyang Maru left Hankow on

Saturday, many a tear was shed by
the refugees who were leaving their
homes and possessions behind, a
Domei correspondent aboard the
Fengyang Maru reported.
When the ships steamed by the
Kiangyin ports, they were escorted
by destroyer Kuri, mine-layer Yae-
yama, and gunboats Seta, Hira and
Otaka. Searchlights blinked at the
forts and played on the sides of the
little fleet, but no foreign sound dis-
turbed the silence of the night.
Most of the refugees slept on the
deck. Forced to leave Hankow on
a 20-hour notice, the refugees had
few utensils with them and not in-
frequently people were seen by
the Domei correspondent eating out
of wash basins.
Over Nine Hundred
The Fengyang Maru brought
here 670 refugees, of whom 286
were women and children. The
Hsinyang Maru brought 336 pas-
sengers.
Rear Admiral Umataro Tanimoto,
Commander of the Eleventh Flot-
illa, also arrived here aboard his
flagship, the mine-layer Yaeyama.
With a passenger list of 36, 20
of whom were refugees from
Wuhu, the Jangyang Maru docked
at the O.S.K. wharf at 6 o'clock
yesterday morning. The party was
headed by Consul Keiji Okabe and
Mr. Masajiro Nishizawa, President
of the Wuhu Japanese Residents'
Corporation.
Also aboard the vessel were 11
refugees from Tayeh, one from
Nanking, one from Chinkiang, and
three Japanese students touring the
Yangtze valley.
Other Boats Arrive
Two hours later, the Julyang
Maru pulled in with 38 refugees
from Kiukiang, headed by Mr.
Daikyo Hayashi, chancellor of the
Consulate in the port, and Mr.
Kasuji Takahira, President of
the Kiukiang Japanese Residents'
Corporation.
Still later in the morning, the
s.s. Loyang Maru brought here 11
refugees from Nanking.
The total of refugees from the
Yangtze ports to reach Shanghai
yesterday was 991.

《上海泰晤士报》。1937年8月10日，星期二。

大批日本人从长江各港口抵沪

近一千名男女老幼昨日抵达上海；汉口紧急撤离的内幕得以披露

在五艘军舰的全程护航下，“凤阳丸”号轮船于昨晨抵港，载来了数百名来自汉口及其他上游城镇的日本难民。

该船抵达时景象凄惨，甲板上每一寸空间都挤满了神情悲苦的男女老幼。

昨日下午，难民们在轮船上召开了一次特别会议，并通过了以下决议：

“我们汉口的日本居民已遵照政府命令离开家园，留下了我们的私有和公共财产。

“我们在此表示希望，政府将继续保护日本在本国的既得权利和利益，消除弥漫于中国的反日情绪。”

汉口的泪水

据“凤阳丸”号上的一名同盟社记者报道，周六当“凤阳丸”号和“新阳丸”号离开汉口时，许多不得不留下家园和财产的难民流下了眼泪。

当船只驶过江阴港口时，它们由驱逐舰“栗”号、布雷舰“八重山”号以及炮舰“势多”号、“平户”号和“大鹰”号护航。探照灯向炮台闪烁，并照射在这支小型舰队的一侧，但没有任何外来的声响打破夜晚的寂静。

大多数难民睡在甲板上。由于接到通知后仅20小时便被迫离开汉口，难民们随身携带的用具很少，同盟社记者不时看到人们用脸盆吃饭。

超过九百人

“凤阳丸”号载来670名难民，其中妇女和儿童286人。“新阳丸”号载来336名乘客。

第十一水雷战队司令谷本马太郎少将也乘坐其旗舰布雷舰“八重山”号抵达此地。

“江阳丸”号（Jangyang Maru，音译）载有36名乘客，其中20人为来自芜湖的难民，于昨晨6时停靠在大阪商船会社码头。该团由领事冈部敬二和芜湖日本居留民团团长西泽正次郎率领。

船上还有11名来自大冶的难民，1名来自南京，1名来自镇江，以及3名在长江流域游览的日本学生。

其他船只抵达

两小时后，“九江丸”号（Julyang Maru，音译）驶入，载有38名来自九江的难民，由该港领事馆主事林大恭和九江日本居留民团团长高桥数治率领。

当天上午晚些时候，“洛阳丸”号轮船载来11名来自南京的难民。

昨日从长江各港口抵达上海的难民总数为991人。

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, AUGUST 9, 1937

Japanese Send Out Patrols,
Cause Excitement In Chapei

Chapei, gripped by scares during the past fortnight, was again thrown into a panic last night when some 20 armed patrols of the Japanese Naval Landing Party crossed the Woosung-Shanghai Railroad line and marched into the Chinese area.

The incident, which happened at 11 o'clock, prompted the Chinese police and Peace Preservation Corps authorities to take precautionary measures.

Normality, however, was restored to the area adjoining the railroad line by midnight when the Japanese patrols returned to their barracks on Klangwan Road.

The reason which prompted the Japanese naval authorities to send their men into the Chinese area was unknown last night. Chinese police authorities informed THE CHINA PRESS that such a procedure was unusual, as unless in the case of an emergency, the Japanese naval authorities recently have never dispatched armed men across the railroad line.

The district which formed the locale of last night's tense situation is near the Wanpang Creek, some 800 meters north of the railroad tracks. Armed Japanese bluejackets for about 30 minutes patrolled the bridges and the immediate vicinity of the creek.

As a result of the mysterious movement of the Japanese, Peace Preservation Corps and the Greater Shanghai police details were called out. Sentries were placed along Paoshan Road, Hsin Paoshing Road and in other Chapei streets.

The situation remained tense until shortly after midnight, when information was received that the Japanese had withdrawn their patrols.

Chinese residents of the area, who have been moving into the Settlement and the Concession during the past two weeks, again swelled the volume of the exodus as a result of the tense situation. Up to an early hour this morning, many residents were moving their belongings out of the area.

《字林西报》，1937年8月9日，星期一

日军派出巡逻队，引发闸北恐慌

在过去两周里一直处于惊恐之中的闸北，昨晚再次陷入恐慌，当时约20名武装的日本海军陆战队巡逻队员越过吴淞-上海铁路线，进入华界区域。

这起发生在11点钟的事件，促使中国警察和保安团当局采取预防措施。

然而，午夜时分，当日军巡逻队返回江湾路的兵营后，铁路沿线附近地区恢复了正常。

昨晚日本海军当局派遣人员进入华界区域的原因尚不清楚。中国警方当局告诉《字林西报》，此种做法并不寻常，因为除非发生紧急情况，日本海军当局最近从未派遣武装人员越过铁路线。

昨晚紧张局势发生的地区位于万鹏浜（Wanpang Creek，音译）附近，在铁轨以北约800米处。武装日本水兵在桥梁及浜口附近巡逻了约30分钟。

由于日军的神秘行动，保安团和大上海警察分队被召集出动。哨兵被部署在宝山路、新宝兴路以及闸北的其他街道上。

局势一直紧张，直到午夜过后不久，收到日军已撤回巡逻队的消息后才得以缓解。

该地区的中国居民在过去两周内一直搬入租界和法租界，由于局势紧张，外逃人数再次增加。直到今天清晨，许多居民仍在将财物搬出该地区。

S.I / DR

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, August 9, 1937 238200
War Looms As Japanese
Evacuate; Peace Hopes
Dim; Conflict Expected

JAPANESE TROOPS
OCCUPY PEIPING,
SHIPS DUE HERE
7994/5
10 8 37

“Our Enemy The Lawless Chinese Army,” States
Military; Kawagoe Abandoning Nanking Trip;
Japanese Heading North For Nankow Pass

Nanking Preparing For Air Raids

MAJOR hostilities on a wide front between Chinese
and Japanese forces will break out sometime this
week, observers in Tokyo, Shanghai and Nanking ex-
pected today.
The evacuation of the entire Yangtze Valley by
Japanese communities, and the virtual severence of
Sino-Japanese relations in the past few days, are taken
as the signposts pointing to the crisis, a large number of
reports from Japan and major Chinese centers indicate.

TROOPS ENTER PEIPING
Japanese troops entered Peiping yesterday, and today
China’s ancient capital was under complete Japanese military
occupation, Japanese reports here state. The military com-
mand made a lengthy statement there last night warning
against interfering with its “tactical operations.”
“Regardless of whether such parties are individuals or
organizations,” the announcement read, “violators of this
injunction shall be dealt with according to law, without
hesitation.”
“Our enemy,” it added, “is the lawless Chinese army.
To crush it constitutes a step towards the establishment of
lasting peace in East Asia.” In conclusion the statement
urged the people of Peiping to remain calm “living as
under a temporary feeling of concern.”

FLOTILLA COMING HERE
The Eleventh Torpedo Boat Flotilla of the Japanese
Navy is concentrating in Shanghai this week. Three vessels
are already here, and the vanguard of the evacuating naval
craft from the Yangtze arrived this morning, these being
the destroyers Tama...
The flagship ... the mine-layer Yaeyama, and
the gunboats Hii, Ataka, Toba, Futami, ... and
Kotaki are due to arrive soon.
The situation has been aggravated constantly since the
July 7 Lukouchiao Incident, and these have increased fears
of a grim and lengthy struggle.

S!

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1937年8月9日，星期一 238200
随着日本人撤离，战争阴云密布；和平希望渺茫；预计将爆发冲突

日军占领北平，
舰船即将抵沪
7994/5
10 8 37

军方称“我们的敌人是无法无天的中国军队”；川越茂放弃南京之行；日军向北挺进南口

南京准备应对空袭

东京、上海和南京的观察家今日预计，中日军队之间的大规模正面敌对行动将在本周内的某个时刻爆发。

日本侨民从整个长江流域撤离，以及过去几天中日关系的实际断绝，被视为指向危机的路标，来自日本和中国主要中心的大量报告表明了这一点。

部队进入北平

此处的日本报道称，日军昨日进入北平，今日中国古都已处于日军的完全军事占领之下。军方司令部昨晚在那里发表长篇声明，警告不得干扰其“战术行动”。

声明称：“无论此类方是个人还是组织”，“违反此禁令者将依法严惩，绝不姑息。”

声明补充道：“我们的敌人是无法无天的中国军队。粉碎它是建立东亚持久和平的一步。”最后，声明敦促北平人民保持冷静，“如同生活在暂时的忧虑之中一样”。

舰队驶来

日本海军第十一鱼雷艇战队本周正在上海集结。三艘舰船已经抵达，从长江撤离的海军舰艇的先头部队今晨抵达，它们是驱逐舰“玉”号……

旗舰……布雷舰“八重山”号，以及炮舰“比良”号、“安宅”号、“鸟羽”号、“二见”号……和“小鹰”号预计很快抵达。

自7月7日卢沟桥事变以来，局势不断恶化，这加剧了人们对一场残酷而漫长斗争的恐惧。
