page_data.en:
JAPAN FORCES MOBILIZED
Beyond this, Mr. Kawagoe had no public statement to make. He has been very busy since his arrival in conferences with Japanese officials at his Route Pichon residence.
Tokyo reports through Reuter state that convinced that the Western Powers will not in any way interfere, Japan, it appears, is mobilizing large forces to carry out “the drastic surgical operation needed fundamentally to remove the menace to ‘Manchukuo.’”

HANKOW SIGNS OF HURRIED DEPARTURE
(Reuter’s Agency)
HANKOW, Aug. 9.—A general feeling of relief has descended upon Hankow following the evacuation of the Japanese Concession here by Japanese armed forces as well as residents.
The last detachment of Japanese blue jackets left yesterday, completing the withdrawal, which was carried out smoothly and without a hitch.
A force of 60 Chinese police have now entered the Concession, in accordance with the request made by Japanese Consular officials, to safeguard Japanese interests and property.
The transfer of administration is only a temporary measure which, it is presumed, will be removed when the North China “incident” has been settled.

ONLY ONE ENTRANCE
For the time being there will be only one entrance to the Concession, and it will be open daily only from six in the morning until seven in the evening. All persons entering or leaving are liable to be searched.
The Japanese area presented a desolate and somewhat pathetic picture when Reuter’s correspondent toured the place.
There were signs everywhere of hurried departure, such as half-finished meals on tables, open and bare cupboards, and floors strewn with refuse. Many Japanese did not even bother to lock up the doors of their houses.
Meanwhile, foreigners living in outlying districts are returning to their homes, which they had previously evacuated.

CHIH LEAVES FOR TONGSHAN
(Domei)
TIENTSIN, Aug. 9.—Mr. Chih Tsung-mo, acting chairman of the East Hopei Autonomous Government, left at 8:20 o’clock this morning for Tongshan where the new seat of his administration will be located. He was accompanied by about 15 officials.

REFUGEES REACH MOJI
(Domei)
MOJI, Aug. 9.—Carrying 307 Japanese refugees from Shantung, the Osaka Shosen liner Taishan Maru arrived here from Tsingtao early today.
On the roofs of various Government buildings could also be seen hooded anti-aircraft machine guns.

CAMOUFLAGE WORK
Painters were feverishly engaged in obliterating landmarks by covering with neutral colors the roofs of various structures.
The Chinkiang and Kiangyin fortresses are also fully manned, with 15 aircraft assigned to defend the latter which is reported to be the best in China.
Anti-aircraft detachments are also understood to have been posted at Wusih.

NANKING FEVERISHLY PREPARING
(Domei)
NANKING, Aug. 9.—With the evacuation of Japanese residents in upper Yangtze ports regarded with apprehension by Chinese officialdom, the capital today rushed anti-aircraft defenses.
The wholesale withdrawal of Japanese from the interior of China, a step which was not taken even in the tense days of the Manchurian and Shanghai conflicts, is considered by Chinese here as an indication that the Japanese armed forces will subject Nanking to an aerial bombardment in case of widespread hostilities.

PLANES GATHERED
One hundred first-line aircraft, Domei learned, have been concentrated near Nanking in the last few days, many of the planes being recalled from concentration camps further north.
The hills around Nanking today formed a bristling ring of anti-aircraft guns. Particularly strongly guarded were Lion Hill, Purple Hill and the Blue Mountain range.

LOSS OF JAPANESE AIRCRAFT CARRIERS
page_data.zh:
日军动员
除此之外，川越茂先生未发表任何公开声明。自抵达以来，他一直在其毕勋路寓所与日本官员举行会谈，事务繁忙。
据路透社东京电称，日本确信西方列强不会进行任何形式的干涉，似乎正在动员大批部队，以实施“为从根本上消除对‘满洲国’的威胁而需进行的 drastic surgical operation（剧烈外科手术式行动）”。

汉口出现匆忙撤离迹象
（路透社）
汉口，8月9日——随着日本武装部队及侨民撤离此地的日本租界，一种普遍的如释重负之感笼罩了汉口。
最后一批日本水兵于昨日离开，完成了此次平稳且毫无阻碍的撤离行动。
应日本领事官员的要求，一支由60名中国警察组成的队伍现已进入租界，以保护日本的利益和财产。
行政权的移交仅为一项临时措施，预计待华北“事变”平息后，该措施即予撤销。

仅留一个入口
目前，租界仅保留一个入口，且每日仅在早晨六点至晚上七点期间开放。所有进出人员均可能受到搜查。
当路透社记者巡视该地区时，日本居留区呈现出一片荒凉且略带凄惨的景象。
到处可见匆忙撤离的痕迹，如桌上未吃完的饭菜、敞开且空无一物的橱柜，以及散落着垃圾的地板。许多日本人甚至懒得锁上房门。
与此同时，居住在郊区的外国人正返回他们此前已撤离的家园。

池宗墨前往唐山
（同盟社）
天津，8月9日——冀东自治政府代理主席池宗墨先生于今晨8时20分启程前往唐山，其行政机构的新址将设于此地。约有15名官员随行。

难民抵达门司
（同盟社）
门司，8月9日——载有307名来自山东的日本难民的大阪商船株式会社轮船“泰山丸”号，于今日清晨从青岛抵达此地。
在各政府建筑物的屋顶上，还可以看到带罩的高射机枪。

伪装工作
油漆工们正疯狂地用中性颜色覆盖各种建筑物的屋顶，以抹去地标特征。
镇江和江阴炮台也已全员部署，另有15架飞机被指派保卫后者，据报道该炮台是中国最好的。
据悉，高射炮分队也已部署于无锡。

南京加紧备战
（同盟社）
南京，8月9日——鉴于中国官方对长江上游港口日本侨民的撤离感到忧虑，首都今日紧急加强防空防御。
日本人大规模从中国内地撤离，这一步骤即使在满洲和上海冲突的紧张时期也未采取，在此间的中国人看来，这表明一旦爆发大规模敌对行动，日本武装部队将对南京实施空中轰炸。

飞机集结
据同盟社获悉，过去几天内，一百架一线飞机已集中在南京附近，其中许多飞机是从更北面的集中地调回的。
今日，南京周边的山丘形成了密集的高射炮环。狮子山、紫金山和蓝山山脉的防卫尤为严密。

日本航空母舰的损失

page_data.en:
TSINGTAO FOREIGNERS LEAVING
(Press Wireless)
TSINGTAO, Aug. 9.—Not only the Chinese, but the foreign visitors are hastening to depart from here as fast as steamer room becomes available. British subjects have received warning from the British Consul to be ready and leave, and Americans have been informed that in case of emergency they will be taken aboard an American cruiser. The boys at the Y.M.C.A. Camp will be removed to an American warship if there is necessity.

Nanking Stands Pat
According to an unconfirmed Nanking report, Mr. Kawagoe may leave for the Chinese capital tomorrow. It is understood that the Chinese government will not refuse to enter into negotiations with the Japanese ambassador but is standing pat on the four minimum conditions laid down by General Chiang Kai-shek in his momentous Kuling statement of last month.
Meanwhile, Chinese reports continue to insist that Japanese armed forces, having already occupied Peiping and Tientsin, are now heading for Nankow, the Great Wall pass along the Peiping-Suiyuan Railway. Japanese troops also are said to be arriving at Tsingtao, causing increased pessimism in Nanking circles over the prospects of a diplomatic solution of the North China situation.

Clash In North
A minor clash occurred between Chinghai and Liangwongchuan along the Tientsin-Pukow Railway near Tic..tsin yesterday. The clash, started at 5 p.m., ended two hours later with the Japanese forced to retreat to Tuliuchen, it is claimed.
The conference of highest military leaders in Nanking continued over the weekend and today with Generals Chiang Kai-shek and Pai Chung-hai holding the spotlight. Official sources claim that the leaders show a marked harmony of opinions during the discussions on the Sino-Japanese situation.
A rumor originating in Japanese quarters that a coup was staged in Nanking during which General Ho Ying-chin, the war minister, was detained and Mr. Wang Ching-wei, chairman of the Central Political Council, had been murdered by "young officers," drew a prompt and emphatic denial from official Chinese quarters.

Leaders Arrive
More army leaders are joining the Nanking talk. General Lung Yung, chairman of the Yunnan provincial government, was due to arrive in Nanking by air today while General Tsai Ting-kai, field commander of the now defunct 19th Route Army, is leaving for Nanking tonight. Generals Li Chi-sen, Chen Ming-chu and Chiang Kwang-nai, former leaders of the Fukien rebellion, are in Hongkong waiting for word to join the discussions.
Sixty armed Chinese policemen are now patrolling the Japanese Concession in Hankow for the first time in 36 years, since the concession was opened. Before their departure for Shanghai, the Japanese landing party members were alleged to have smashed all of the street lights Saturday night.

Streets Dark
When the Chinese policemen entered the Japanese Concession, most of the streets were absolutely dark, it is said. A deserted "red light" district was...

August 4, according to belated reports. Before they evacuated, they are alleged to have attempted to set fire to their office building after locking four of the Chinese employees in an upstairs room. The fire was promptly put out by Chinese police.

Japanese Call
(Kuo Min News Agency)
NANKING, Aug. 8.—Mr. S. Hidaka, Counsellor of the Japanese Embassy, called on Mr. Hsu Mo, Political Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs, at 3 p.m. yesterday. In the course of a 40-minutes interview, diplomatic affairs concerning the two countries were discussed.
Mr. Fukui, Japanese Consul-General, also called on Mr. Tung Tao-ning, section chief of the Department of Asiatic Affairs of the Ministry, at 5 p.m.

Wang Gives Report
(Kuo Min News Agency)
NANKING, Aug. 8.—Dr. Wang Chung-hui, Minister of Foreign Affairs, at a meeting with the Central Government leaders last night, gave a detailed report on the attitude of the various foreign powers regarding the North China situation. He also reported on the wholesale evacuation of Japanese nationals from various parts of the country.
General Chang Chun, former Minister of Foreign Affairs and at present Secretary-General of the Central Political Committee, conferred with Messrs. Hsu Mo and Chen Chieh, Political and Administrative Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs.
General Chiang Tso-pin, Minister of Interior, also conferred with Vice-Minister Chen Chieh concerning the coordination of work between the Ministries of Interior and Foreign Affairs.

Canton Women Act
(Kuo Min News Agency)
CANTON, Aug. 8.—The women of Kwangtung have decided to launch a savings campaign to secure $100,000 to augment the Government's war chest.
Madame Yu Han-mou, wife of the Commander-in-Chief of the 4th Route Army, is at the head of the campaign with 200 teams captained by women leaders in various walks of life.
Each member of this Savings Army is required to save at least one dollar a month for the fund which will be remitted to the front
page_data.zh:
青岛外国人撤离
（_press wireless_ / 新闻无线电）
青岛，8月9日——不仅中国人，外国访客也在只要有轮船舱位便尽快 hastening to depart（匆忙离开）。英国臣民已收到英国领事的警告，要求做好准备并撤离；美国人已获知，在紧急情况下他们将登上一艘美国巡洋舰。如有必要，青年会营地的男童将被转移至一艘美国军舰上。

南京坚持立场
据一则未经证实的南京消息称，川越茂先生可能于明日前往中国首都。据悉，中国政府不会拒绝与日本大使进行谈判，但在蒋介石将军上月发表的具有重大意义的庐山谈话中所提出的四项最低条件上，仍坚持不变。
与此同时，中方报道继续坚称，日本武装部队在已占领北平和天津后，正沿平绥铁路向长城关口南口进发。据说日军也抵达青岛，导致南京各界对通过外交手段解决华北局势的前景愈发悲观。

北方冲突
昨日，在天津附近的津浦铁路上，静海与梁王庄之间发生了一次小规模冲突。据称，冲突始于下午5时，两小时后结束，日军被迫撤退至独流镇。
南京最高军事领导人会议在周末及今日持续进行，蒋介石将军和白崇禧将军成为焦点。官方消息来源称，领导人在讨论中日局势期间表现出显著的意见一致。
源自日本方面的一则谣言称，南京发生政变，期间军政部长何应钦将军被扣押，中央政治委员会主席汪精卫先生被“青年军官”谋杀，对此中国官方方面迅速予以坚决否认。

领导人抵达
更多军队领导人加入南京会谈。云南省政府主席龙云将军预计今日乘飞机抵达南京，而现已解散的第十九路军野战司令蔡廷锴将军将于今晚启程前往南京。前福建事变领导人李济深、陈铭枢和蒋光鼐将军正在香港，等待参加讨论的通知。
六十名全副武装的中国警察目前正在汉口日本租界巡逻，这是自该租界开放36年来的首次。据称，日本登陆队成员在前往上海之前，于周六晚砸毁了所有路灯。

街道黑暗
据说，当中国警察进入日本租界时，大多数街道一片漆黑。一个荒凉的“红灯”区……

据迟发的报道，此事发生在8月4日。据称，他们在撤离前，曾试图在将四名中国雇员锁在楼上房间后，纵火焚烧其办公大楼。大火被中国警察迅速扑灭。

日本人的拜访
（国民新闻社）
南京，8月8日——日本大使馆参事日高信八郎先生于昨日下午3时拜访了外交部政务次长徐谟先生。在40分钟的会谈中，双方讨论了两国间的外交事务。
日本总领事福井先生也于下午5时拜访了外交部亚洲司司长董道宁先生。

王宠惠作报告
（国民新闻社）
南京，8月8日——外交部长王宠惠博士在昨晚与中央政府领导人的会议上，详细报告了各外国列强对华北局势的态度。他还报告了日本国民从全国各地大规模撤离的情况。
前外交部长、现任中央政治委员会秘书长张群将军，与外交部政务次长徐谟先生和陈介先生进行了会谈。
内政部长蒋作宾将军也就内政部与外交部的工作协调问题，与次长陈介先生进行了会谈。

广东妇女行动
（国民新闻社）
广州，8月8日——广东妇女决定发起一项储蓄运动，以筹集10万美元，充实政府的战争基金。
第四路军总司令余汉谋的夫人余太太主持该项运动，200个小组由来自各行各业的妇女领袖担任队长。
这支“储蓄大军”的每位成员每月至少需为基金储蓄一美元，该款项将汇往前线

page_data.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, August 9, 1937.

Chapei Exodus
Thins; Tension
Slowly Easing

Refugees Still Packing
Vessels And Trains
Leaving City

JAPANESE NAVY
DISPLAYS FORCE

North Communications
Maintained; Local
Japanese Calm

With the passing of the fateful 9th, Chapei and Hongkew residents breathed easier today and a marked falling off of the exodus was noted; most police districts not making reports. A steady but reduced stream of refugees continued to flow across Garden Bridge, however. Many Chinese believe that any adventure upon which the Japanese militarists embark must be launched on the 8th, 18th or 28th, hence it was to be expected that tension would be reduced today although shortly after midnight excitement was great along North Szechuen Road.

The Japanese made one brief display of military strength this morning when an armoured car with a marine manning the machine gun in the turret passed down North Szechuen Road behind a military motorcycle. After midnight yesterday no members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party were seen on the streets, but numerous Japanese male civilians were out and about, some of them touring Hongkew in a large limousine until near dawn.

Ships in Harbor

With the arrival of two Japanese destroyers from up-river this morning, there were today 11 foreign naval vessels in harbor. The Falmouth, British sloop, which arrived from the north yesterday, left this afternoon, however, to return to the British China Fleet in northern waters. There are now five Japanese warships here, and nine en route from up-river, forming the Eleventh Torpedo Boat Flotilla. The Tsuga and Kuri came in today to join the Idzumo, cruiser and flagship, the Ataka and Kataka, gunboats. The British cruiser Danae, and destroyers Defender and Duncan are here besides the Falmouth, all having arrived in the last few days. The US Sacramento is the only American naval vessel, the rest of the U.S. Asiatic Fleet being at Tsingtao and Chefoo. The flagship Augusta, and destroyers have returned to Tsingtao from the Vladivostok cruise.

Japanese Refugees

In order to accommodate about 1200 Japanese men, women and children who have evacuated inland ports along the Yangtse, the Nippon Yusen Kaisha will dispatch two of its express liners from Shanghai on August 12.

Of the two ships, the Shanghai Maru alone will proceed to Kobe, while the Nagasaki Maru will turn back at Nagasaki to arrive here on August 15 sailing again the following morning.

Meantime, the influx of Japanese refugees began in earnest with the arrival yesterday of the Jangyang Maru carrying 29 Japanese men from Wuhu.

More Arrive

Following closely behind came the Yuankiang Maru with 65 from Changsha, the Loyang Maru with 11 from Nanking and the Julyang Maru with 35 from Kiukiang.

All tied up at Pootung.

The bulk of refugees, however, reached her in two ships tying-up respectively at Hongkew mail wharf and the O.S.K. Wharf.

They were the Pengyang Maru and the Hsinyang Maru from Hankow.

Local Japanese were cautioned against believing and relaying rumors regarding the situation in warnings published in the local Japanese press yesterday by the consular police authorities.

Navy Patrols

The Japanese Naval Landing Party gave new life to dying rumors of trouble when a patrol of some 20 armed men crossed the Woosung-Shanghai Railway line shortly after 11 p.m. last night and marched into Chinese territory. Although the Japanese returned to their barracks by midnight, excitement among residents of Chapei and Hongkew was still at a high pitch long after midnight, crowds gathering along North Szechuen Road and discussing the state of affairs until this morning. The exodus usually slows up in the early morning hours, but it was increased early today as women and children left their homes north of Range Road and started the trek into the Settlement. No reason was given by the Japanese for their unusual action which brought about an increase in Chinese sentries along important Chapei streets.

The River Police and French Police have been called out on several occasions during the past few days to prevent frightened Chinese refugees from storming wharves and vessels in their frantic attempt to get away from a city which they no longer considered safe. Vessels capable of carrying 500 passengers have been crowded with 2000 people and delayed many hours in sailing. Vessels of the China Merchants' Steam Navigation Co. and the San Poh S.N. Co. will increase their scheduled trips between this city and Ningpo in an effort to handle the demands for passage. Transpacific lines with vessels running to South China are also experiencing heavy bookings. Hundreds of Chinese are still camping along the wharves and jetties awaiting accommodations.

Steamers Bound for Japan Yesterday were all filled with Japanese families and their belongings. Most of the refugees were from Yangtse ports evacuated by the Japanese, but a number of residents of the North Szechuen Road area were among those returning to the homeland. The exodus of Japanese nationals is expected to continue during the next week with all Nippon-bound vessels carrying capacity numbers of passengers.

Communications

Train and air communication between this city and North China remained curtailed today with the rain making Tsinan its terminal and the planes-Tsingtao. The Blue Express from Tsinan was to arrive this afternoon at the North Station, probably a few hours behind schedule. Yesterday's Blue Express from the north arrived at 5 p.m., some 10 hours behind schedule. The north-bound express will, however, leave on time at 12 p.m. tonight. The C.N.A.C. plane service to North still made Tsingtao the terminal today. A plane left this morning with two passengers and the same plane is expected to return here this afternoon. There was no scheduled flight between Taiyuan and Hongkong today by the Eurasia Aviation Corporation.

Stern punishment against rumor mongers and publishers of "special extras" containing sensational but fabricated news today was ordered by the Garrison Commander's Headquarters for Shanghai and Woosung Areas. The "traitors," rumor mongers and plotters will be arrested and sent to the military tribunal where severe sentences will await them, it is declared.

Many Throng Hangchow
(Kuo Min News Agency)
HANGCHOW, Aug. 8.—Refugees from Shanghai are flocking to this city. All trains on the Shanghai-Hangchow Railway are crowded to capacity; more than a thousand people arrived here from Shanghai by rail yesterday. Special quarters for the accommodation of the poorer folks have been prepared by the Red Swastika Society.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年8月9日，星期一。

闸北外逃
局势；紧张
缓慢缓解

难民仍挤满
船只与火车
离开本市

日本海军
展示武力

北方通讯
保持畅通；当地
日本人平静

随着命运攸关的9日过去，闸北和虹口的居民今天松了一口气，外逃人数显著减少；大多数警区未提交报告。然而，跨过外白渡桥的难民流虽然减少，但仍持续不断。许多中国人认为，日本军国主义者发动的任何冒险行动必定在8日、18日或28日发起，因此预计今天紧张局势会缓和，尽管午夜过后不久，北四川路沿线曾出现极大的骚动。

今天上午，日本方面短暂展示了一次军事力量，一辆装甲车在一辆军用摩托车后方沿北四川路驶过，炮塔内有一名陆战队士兵操作机枪。昨天午夜之后，街上未见日本海军陆战队队员，但有许多日本男性平民在外活动，其中一些人乘坐大型豪华轿车在虹口巡游，直至接近黎明。

港内船只

随着两艘日本驱逐舰今晨从上游抵达，今日港内有11艘外国海军舰艇。昨天从北方抵达的英国单桅战舰“法尔茅斯”号（HMS Falmouth）于今天下午离港，返回在中国北部水域的英国中国舰队。目前这里有五艘日本军舰，另有九艘从上游驶来，组成第十一鱼雷艇舰队。“椿”号（Tsuga）和“栗”号（Kuri）今天抵达，加入巡洋舰兼旗舰“出云”号（Idzumo）、炮舰“安宅”号（Ataka）和“加贺”号（Kataka，注：原文如此，可能指代有误或为特定译名）。除了“法尔茅斯”号外，英国巡洋舰“达娜厄”号（Danae）以及驱逐舰“防御者”号（Defender）和“邓肯”号（Duncan）也在此，均于最近几天抵达。美国“萨克拉门托”号（Sacramento）是唯一的美国海军舰艇，美国亚洲舰队的其余部分位于青岛和烟台。旗舰“奥古斯塔”号（Augusta）及驱逐舰已从符拉迪沃斯托克巡航返回青岛。

日本难民

为了安置约1200名从长江沿岸内陆港口撤离的日本男女老幼，日本邮船会社将于8月12日从上海派遣两艘特快邮轮。

在这两艘船中，只有“上海丸”将前往神户，而“长崎丸”将在长崎折返，于8月15日抵达此处，并于次日清晨再次起航。

与此同时，随着昨天载有29名日本男子从芜湖抵达的“江阳丸”（Jangyang Maru，音译）的到来，日本难民的涌入正式开始。

更多人抵达

紧随其后的是载有65名来自长沙人员的“元江丸”（Yuankiang Maru，音译）、载有11名来自南京人员的“洛阳丸”（Loyang Maru，音译）以及载有35名来自九江人员的“九江丸”（Julyang Maru，音译）。

全部停靠在浦东。

然而，大部分难民是通过两艘分别停靠在虹口邮政码头和大阪商船株式会社（O.S.K.）码头的船只抵达的。

它们是来自汉口的“彭阳丸”（Pengyang Maru，音译）和“新阳丸”（Hsinyang Maru，音译）。

领事警察当局昨天在当地日文报刊上发布警告，告诫当地日本人不要相信并传播有关局势的谣言。

海军巡逻

昨晚11点刚过，一支约20人的武装巡逻队越过吴淞-上海铁路线并进入中国领土，日本海军陆战队的这一举动使即将平息的麻烦谣言死灰复燃。尽管日本人于午夜前返回兵营，但午夜过后很久，闸北和虹口居民的兴奋情绪仍然高涨，人群聚集在北四川路沿线讨论事态，直至今天早晨。外逃通常在清晨时分减缓，但今天早些时候外逃人数增加，因为妇女和儿童离开了界路（Range Road，今海宁路）以北的家园，开始向租界跋涉。日本人对其引发闸北主要街道中国哨兵增加的异常行动未给出任何理由。

在过去几天里，水上警察和法国警察多次被召出，以防止惊恐的中国难民在疯狂试图离开这个他们不再认为安全的城市时冲击码头和船只。载客量为500人的船只挤进了2000人，导致航行延误数小时。招商局轮船公司和三北轮埠公司（San Poh S.N. Co.）将增加本市与宁波之间的定期班次，以应对客运需求。运营至华南的跨太平洋航线也面临大量预订。数百名中国人仍在码头和栈桥旁露营，等待舱位。

驶往日本的轮船昨天都载满了日本家庭及其财物。大多数难民来自日本人撤离的长江港口，但也有不少北四川路地区的居民 among those returning to the homeland（在返回祖国的人群中）。预计下周日本国民的外逃将继续，所有驶往日本的船只都将满载乘客。

通讯

今天本市与华北之间的火车和航空通讯仍然受限，雨水使得济南成为列车终点站，青岛成为飞机终点站。从济南开出的蓝皮快车预计今天下午抵达北站，可能晚点几小时。昨天从北方开来的蓝皮快车于下午5点抵达，晚点约10小时。然而，北行快车将于今晚12点准时发车。中国航空公司（C.N.A.C.）飞往北方的航班今天仍以青岛为终点站。一架载有两名乘客的飞机今晨起飞，预计同一架飞机将于今天下午返回此处。欧亚航空公司今天没有太原至香港的定期航班。

上海及吴淞地区卫戍司令部下令，对散布谣言者和出版包含耸人听闻但属捏造新闻的“号外”者予以严厉惩罚。宣称，“叛徒”、造谣者和阴谋策划者将被逮捕并送交军事法庭，等待他们的将是严厉的判决。

许多人涌向杭州
（国民新闻社）
杭州，8月8日电。——来自上海的难民正涌向本市。沪杭铁路的所有列车均拥挤不堪；昨天有一千多人乘火车从上海抵达此地。红卍字会已为安置贫困民众准备了专门的住所。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, MONDAY, AUGUST 2, 1937. 23402

MISCONCEPTIONS

Mr. Yotaro Sugimura, the new Japanese Ambassador at Paris, has told a French journalist that Japan's objective in North China is essentially economic. The statement is accurate. Its sincerity cannot be doubted. It accords with the general line which Japanese apologists are taking in the endeavour to explain away the present crisis. It is argued that the anxiety of Japan to establish economic co-operation with North China, for the consolidation of the bloc composed of Manchoukuo, Korea and Japan, is being accentuated by Chinese provocation. The recent adoption of the "new concept", the conciliatory speeches of Mr. Koki Hirota and, especially, his immediate predecessor, Mr. Naotake Sato, and the moderation of Japanese actions in China during the last twelve months or more are cited to convict China of unresponsiveness. It is alleged that, permitted to develop national unity and to journey far on the road to economic reconstruction, China has betrayed symptoms of over-confidence in her own ability and so has been careless in handling relations with Japan. In particular it is alleged that "anti-Japanese" elements have been encouraged or, at least, not restrained. In other words Japan's moderation has been mistaken for weakness and, therefore, the operations in the North are reluctantly undertaken by Japan in self-defence. It is with no thought of territorial ambition that Japanese forces have bolstered up the East Hopei autonomous régime which has made contribution to economic co-operation by acting as a clearing house for an extensive smuggling or "special trade" organization designed to correct the asperities of the Chinese tariff. Although—as is shown by General Kiyoshi Katsuki's prompt appointment of a successor to Mr. Yin Ju-keng as head of the East Hopei administration at Tungchow and by the creation of Peace Maintenance Commissions to govern the Peiping and Tientsin areas—Japanese control in Hopei is now a fait accompli, the contention is that the arrangement gives a beneficent framework to Sino-Japanese economic co-operation for the better government of North China.

This sort of argument would be more impressive if it were not vitiated by the actual facts of Japanese activities in North China and beyond since Sept. 1931. The short-lived "peace and order committees" created to give regional self-government just after the Mukden incident were commended in precisely the same terms as are now being applied to the "Peace Maintenance Commissions". It will be recalled that they failed because the compliance of the Chinese nominees invariably broke down before the provocative rigour of Japanese masterfulness. Judging from the names of the men chosen for the honour of executing Japanese orders in Peiping, Tientsin and Tushan, there is no reason to believe that their fate will be any different.

spot. It is to be feared, therefore, that the effort to refute the general impression that, who ever fired the first shot at Marco Polo Bridge, the Japanese military have assumed the rôle of aggressor cannot be successfully attempted by academic consolation on Tokyo's oratory. Conciliatory speeches have their merit, but they avail little if they be not reinforced by action. It is more pertinent perhaps to note that General Kiyoshi Katsuki has disdained to echo the moderation of his superiors at Tokyo and, coming to "chastise the outrageous Chinese", he has matched his actions with his words, with inconvenient bluntness. Blindness in Tokyo to the fact that commendation of the "new concept" in Sino-Japanese relations has been consistently undermined by the astounding tactlessness and, frequently, arrogance of Japanese military forces in various parts of China has led to a complete misconception of the present crisis by Japanese who, in no sense, can be accused of any other desire than to deal with China in a spirit of friendly equality. That is the tragedy of the situation. It has been accentuated by ill-conceived propaganda by which the most trivial incident has been magnified for home consumption in Japan for the purpose of maintaining the theory that "anti-Japanese" sentiments and activities are chief attributes of Chinese occasions.

The main difference between the Chinese and Japanese Governments has, in the meantime, been ignored. Both are ready for economic co-operation, but China desires to have the political situation in North China defined before precise steps are taken to fulfil that common need. Japan does not see the necessity for this clarification but would proceed at once to enter into business agreements without the intrusion of political issues. There may be good ground for either point of view, but it seems to the detached observer that Japan is not doing herself justice if she thinks that the Gordian knot can be cut by the sword. Whether the reports from Nanking of an impending large-scale movement to engage the Japanese forces in combat will be justified by the event, may be left out of account for the moment. Let it be assumed that they are incorrect and that Japan will be able to consolidate her régime in the North while the Government of China seeks by the best means in its power to reconcile its people to the new demonstration of aggression's capacity for domination of Chinese soil. Will it be seriously argued that the prospect of establishing basically friendly relations between Japan and China has thereby been improved? If it be alleged that the Chinese Government has not been sufficiently alert to perceive the good intentions of Japan's more "moderate" policy and so has given a new handle for the Japanese militarists to discredit that policy, the question to be asked is whether a real diplomatic effort has been made to clear the air.

tent, have given colour to the argument that forbearance has been mistaken by them for weakness, but does a great nation like Japan, in devising its policy, shilly-shally on such frivolous pretexts? If a policy be seriously contemplated are not there means to see that such casual threats to its success are relegated to their proper obscurity. Whatever criticism there may be of Nanking for the failure to grasp the urgency of the crisis as it emerged on July 7, Japanese taxpayers on whom must now fall the burden of supporting a costly expeditionary force have reason to complain of the muddling of Sino-Japanese relations by their soldiers and statesmen. Not the least cause for complaint lies in the radical misconceptions of the situation forced upon them by official and semi-official pronouncements in Tokyo. Their diplomacy has not been given a free hand. It has been hamstrung by the militarists.

AMENDE HONORABLE

So extraordinary were the adventures of the young seaman, Sadao Miyazaki, that it is impossible not to sympathize with the authorities of the Japanese Landing Party in the predicament in which he placed them. Rear-Admiral Denshichi Okochi has made the amende honorable in a statement which by its frankness and courtesy disarms all criticism. The Shanghai Municipal Council and the City Government of Shanghai will no doubt recognize that to the full and appreciate the tribute paid by the Rear-Admiral to their prompt co-operation in the elucidation of the mystery which, for a short time, threatened to be an embarrassing incident at a time of exceptional strain. Miyazaki, apparently, was the victim of temptations which are often too accessible to the young service-man in Shanghai and was overcome by remorse. His inexperience and youth unfortunately led him to a desperate course of action which an older man would have probably eschewed. His conduct is obviously a matter solely for the consideration of his superior officers. Yet, as his escapade has become public property in a special degree, it may not be out of place to express the hope that whatever disciplinary action be necessary, he may eventually have the opportunity to retrieve his good name in the service, for, according to previous reports, his character and personality were favourably regarded until his sad lapse occurred.

误解

新任日本驻巴黎大使杉村洋太郎（Yotaro Sugimura）告诉一位法国记者，日本在华北的目标本质上是经济性的。这一说法是准确的。其诚意不容置疑。这与日本辩护者为解释当前危机所采取的总体路线一致。他们辩称，中国方面的挑衅加剧了日本急于与华北建立经济合作的焦虑，旨在巩固由满洲国、朝鲜和日本组成的集团。有人引用最近采纳的“新观念”、广田弘毅（Koki Hirota）先生的和解性演讲，尤其是其前任佐藤尚武（Naotake Sato）先生的演讲，以及过去一年多来日本在华行动的克制，以此证明中国方面缺乏回应。据称，中国被允许发展国家统一并在经济重建的道路上走得很远，却表现出对自身能力过度自信的迹象，因此在处理对日关系时粗心大意。特别是据称，“反日”分子受到鼓励，或者至少未受约束。换言之，日本的克制被误认为软弱，因此，日本不情愿地出于自卫在北方采取行动。日军支持冀东自治政权并非出于领土野心，该政权通过充当一个广泛的走私或“特殊贸易”组织的清算所，为纠正中国关税的严苛之处做出了贡献，从而促进了经济合作。尽管——正如香月清司（Kiyoshi Katsuki）将军迅速任命殷汝耕（Yin Ju-keng）的继任者担任通州冀东行政长官，以及成立治安维持会以治理北平和天津地区所示——日本在河北的控制已成为既成事实，但论点是，这种安排为中日经济合作提供了一个有益的框架，以更好地治理华北。

如果这种论点没有被1931年9月以来日本在华北及更远地区的实际活动事实所破坏，它可能会更具说服力。在沈阳事变后不久创建的、旨在给予区域自治的短命“治安委员会”，当时受到的赞扬与现在用于“治安维持会”的措辞完全相同。人们会记得，它们之所以失败，是因为中方提名人的顺从总是在日本主子挑衅性的严厉面前崩溃。从被选中在北平、天津和独山（Tushan，音译）执行日本命令的人员名单来看，没有理由相信他们的命运会有所不同。

spot. 因此，恐怕试图通过东京演说家的学术性安慰来驳斥这样一种普遍印象——无论谁在卢沟桥开了第一枪，日军都扮演了侵略者的角色——是无法成功的。和解性的演讲自有其价值，但如果得不到行动的加强，则收效甚微。也许更切中要害的是注意到，香月清司将军不屑于附和其在东京的上司们的克制态度，他在前来“惩罚猖獗的中国人”时，言行一致，直率得令人不便。东京无视这样一个事实，即对中国各地日军惊人的笨拙且经常是傲慢的行为的称赞，一直 undermining（削弱）着对中日关系“新观念”的推崇，这导致日本人完全误解了当前的危机，而这些日本人绝不会被指责怀有任何不同于以友好平等精神对待中国的愿望。这就是局势的悲剧所在。构思不当的宣传加剧了这一悲剧，其中最微不足道的事件也被放大以供日本国内消费，目的是维持这样一种理论，即“反日”情绪和活动是中国场合的主要特征。

与此同时，中日政府之间的主要分歧被忽视了。双方都愿意进行经济合作，但中国希望在采取确切步骤满足这一共同需求之前，先明确华北的政治局势。日本则认为没有必要进行这种澄清，而是希望在不介入政治问题的情况下立即达成商业协议。两种观点可能都有充分的理由，但在旁观者看来，如果日本认为可以用剑斩断戈耳狄俄斯之结（Gordian knot），那对她自己并不公平。至于南京方面关于即将大规模调动军队与日军交战的报道是否会成为现实，暂时可以不予考虑。假设这些报道是不正确的，并且日本能够在华北巩固其政权，而中国政府则尽其所能安抚民众，使其接受侵略者支配中国领土能力的新展示。难道能认真论证说，由此改善了在日中之间建立基本友好关系的前景吗？如果有人声称中国政府不够警觉，未能察觉日本较“温和”政策的善意，从而给了日本军国主义者新的口实来诋毁该政策，那么需要问的问题是，是否已做出真正的外交努力以消除误会。

tent, 确实为这样一种论点提供了依据，即他们的克制被误认为是软弱，但是像日本这样的大国，在制定政策时，会因为如此轻率的借口而犹豫不决吗？如果认真考虑一项政策，难道没有办法确保那些对其成功构成的随意威胁被归于其应有的默默无闻之中吗？无论人们对南京未能把握7月7日出现的危机的紧迫性有何批评，现在必须承担支持昂贵远征军负担的日本纳税人有理由抱怨其士兵和政治家搞乱了中日关系。最令他们抱怨的原因之一，正是东京官方和半官方声明强加给他们的对局势的根本性误解。他们的外交并未获得放手行事的空间。它被军国主义者束缚了手脚。

赔礼道歉

年轻水兵宫崎贞夫（Sadao Miyazaki）的经历如此非同寻常，以至于人们不禁同情日本海军陆战队当局因他而陷入的困境。大河内传七（Denshichi Okochi）少将在一份声明中进行了赔礼道歉（amende honorable），其坦率和礼貌使所有批评都失去了效力。上海公共租界工部局和上海市政府无疑会充分认识到这一点，并赞赏少将对他们在阐明这一谜团时的迅速合作所给予的赞誉，这一谜团曾在一段异常紧张的时期短暂地威胁要成为一起令人尴尬的事件。宫崎显然是受到了在上海年轻服役人员往往过于容易接触到的诱惑的受害者，并被悔恨所征服。他的缺乏经验和年轻不幸地导致他采取了一种绝望的行动路线，而年长者可能会避免这种做法。他的行为显然 solely（仅仅）是其上级军官考虑的事项。然而，由于他的丑闻在某种程度上已成为公众话题，表达这样的希望或许并非不合时宜：无论需要采取何种纪律行动，他最终应有机会在服务中挽回名誉，因为根据之前的报道，在他发生这一可悲的过失之前，他的品格和个性一直受到好评。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, AUGUST 7, 1937
25503

Red Cross Work
Organized On
National Basis

10 Mobile Units Being
Equipped To Take
Field Shortly

MORE MEDICAL
SUPPLIES NEEDED

250 Doctors Mobilized
Have To Direct
Hospital Work

Two hospitals, each capable of handling 1,000 wounded soldiers, and ten mobile units, each able to become a base hospital caring for 1,000 wounded men, are being organized by the Red Cross Society of China and other associations.

This large-scaled program which will furnish medical attention for some 12,000 soldiers was outlined yesterday to a CHINA PRESS reporter by Dr. F. C. Yen, Superintendent of the Red Cross Hospital, who is also the head of many medical projects in Shanghai, including the big Shanghai Medical Center.

Because of the large scale program, Dr. Yen emphasized the important part that the public can play in the work, especially in the contribution of much-needed medical supplies, especially cloth for bandages, cotton and gauze, and of money.

Medical Supplies Received

A Relief Association, including the Red Cross Society and other organizations, has been set up at 856 Sinsa Road to receive contributions and to supervise the organization of these various hospital units.

Five of the 10 hospital units have already been organized and one has already been sent to the war front.

The unit organized in Nanking has been dispatched to Paoting for service.

Three more have been organized in Shanghai and will be sent in a few days for duty at points on the Peiping-Hankow Railway. One organized by the National Medical Association in conjunction with the Red Cross Society will leave in a few days. Another, formed by the Bureau of Public Health of the City Government and National Tung Chi Medical College, is also ready to leave.

The fourth unit, to be stationed at Wuchang, is being formed by the National Medical College and the Red Cross Society.

A fifth unit, organized by Tung Chi and the City Bureau of Public Health, will be stationed at Tientsin.

250 Doctors To Be Mobilized

Each unit will have a staff of 25 persons, including doctors and nurses. Some 250 doctors will be mobilised in this entire program.

Much surgical supplies will be needed in this program, according to Dr. Yen. Contributions of cloth for bandages, cotton, and gauze will be greatly appreciated.

The materials contributed are being made into dressings by the members of the Chinese Women's Club and other volunteers every morning at the clubhouse. Other supplies, such as camp cots, flashlights, etc., are also greatly needed. Contributions can be made in either supplies or money to the Relief Association, 856 Sinsa Road.

An International Relief Committee to assist sufferers from the fighting in North China or elsewhere in the country has been formed in Shanghai, it was announced yesterday by the Chinese-Foreign Famine Relief Committee, 97 Jinkee Road.

Both Chinese and foreign authorities and organizations will co-operate in this organization.

红十字会工作
在全国基础上
组织起来

10个机动队正在
装备中，即将
开赴前线

急需更多
医疗物资

250名医生已动员
须指导
医院工作

中国红十字会及其他协会正在组织两家医院，每家可收治1,000名伤兵；以及十个机动队，每个机动队均可成为能照护1,000名伤员的基地医院。

红十字会医院院长颜福庆博士（Dr. F. C. Yen）昨日向《字林西报》记者概述了这一大规模计划，该计划将为约12,000名士兵提供医疗服务。颜博士也是上海许多医疗项目的负责人，包括大型上海医疗中心。

鉴于计划规模庞大，颜博士强调公众可以在这项工作中发挥重要作用，特别是捐赠急需的医疗物资，尤其是用于包扎的布料、棉花和纱布，以及捐款。

收到医疗物资

一个包括红十字会在内的救济协会已在信实路856号成立，以接收捐赠并监督各医院单位的组织工作。

十个医院单位中已有五个组建完毕，其中一个已派往战争前线。

在南京组建的单位已被派往保定服役。

另有三个单位在上海组建，将于数日后派往平汉铁路沿线各点执行任务。由中华医学会与红十字会联合组建的一个单位将于数日后出发。另一个由市政府卫生局和国立同济大学医学院组建的单位也已准备就绪，即将出发。

第四个单位将驻守武昌，正由国立医学院和红十字会组建。

第五个单位由同济大学和市卫生局组建，将驻守天津。

将动员250名医生

每个单位将配备25名工作人员，包括医生和护士。整个计划将动员约250名医生。

颜博士表示，该计划需要大量外科用品。非常感激捐赠用于包扎的布料、棉花和纱布。

每日上午，中国妇女俱乐部成员及其他志愿者在俱乐部会所将捐赠材料制成敷料。其他物资，如行军床、手电筒等，也急需。可向信实路856号的救济协会捐赠物资或现金。

中外义赈会昨日宣布，上海已成立一个国际救济委员会，以协助华北或国内其他地区战事的受难者。

中外的当局和组织将在该组织中合作。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, AUGUST 7, 1937

TO ASSIST WAR VICTIMS
Editor,
THE SHANGHAI TIMES
Sir,—A meeting was held last night in the office of the Chinese Foreign Famine Relief Committee, 97 Jinkee Road, to consider ways and means of assisting in the relief work on behalf of the victims of the fighting in North China.
The following delegates attended this meeting, representing the Chinese Red Cross Society, the Swastika Society, the United Charitable Societies of Shanghai, the Chinese Catholic Church, the China Philanthropic Institution, and the Chinese Foreign Famine Relief Committee.—Messrs. Sung Han-chang, Chou Fen-loh, Wong I-ding, Wong Han-tze, Feng Yang-san, Father R. Jacquinot, Chu Ning-kong, Hans Berents, Koo Chi-sun, Li Dih-sie, Loh Pah-hong and others. Mr. Sung Han-chang presided, and he and Mr. Koo Chi-sun welcomed the delegates and explained the object to the meeting. After a full discussion, on the motion of Father R. Jacquinot, it was unanimously agreed to form an organization called the International Relief Committee, Shanghai, and with the co-operation of both the Chinese and foreign authorities and representative bodies here, to take suitable steps to render assistance to the sufferers from the fighting in North China or elsewhere.
This is no more than a report of the initial meeting, but further reports will be given to the press as plans develop.
WM. E. SOUTER.
Shanghai, August 6, 1937.

先生，——昨晚在中外义赈会办公室（金神路97号）举行了一次会议，商讨如何协助开展救济工作，以帮助华北战事受害者。
以下代表出席了会议，他们分别代表中国红十字会、卍字会、上海慈善团体联合会、中国天主教会、华洋义赈会和中外义赈会：宋汉章先生、周芬洛先生（音译）、王以鼎先生（音译）、王汉兹先生（音译）、冯仰山先生（音译）、R. Jacquinot神父、朱宁公先生（音译）、Hans Berents先生、顾子馨先生、李迪希先生（音译）、罗柏洪先生（音译）等。宋汉章先生担任主席，他和顾子馨先生欢迎了各位代表，并向会议说明了宗旨。经过充分讨论，根据R. Jacquinot神父的提议，一致同意成立一个名为“上海国际救济委员会”的组织，并在中外当局及本地代表性团体的合作下，采取适当步骤，向华北或其他地区战事的受难者提供援助。
这仅是首次会议的报道，随着计划的推进，将进一步向新闻界发布报告。
WM. E. SOUTER.
上海，1937年8月6日。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, AUGUST 7, 1937

EVACUATION PLANS
FOR CHINESE IN
JAPAN PUSHED

NANKING, Aug. 6.—
(Central). — The Chinese
Government has reported-
ly decided to evacuate all
Chinese nationals from
Japan.
The decision was reached
recently after a joint meet-
ing of officials of the Min-
istries of Foreign Affairs,
Finance, Communications
and Overseas Affairs Com-
mission.
It is understood that the
China Merchants Steam
Navigation Company will
be instructed to dispatch
several of its large steam-
ers to Japan for the pur-
pose.
Concerned over the safe-
ty of the large number of
Chinese students in Japan,
Dr. Wang Shih-chieh, Min-
ister of Education, yester-
day called on Dr. Wang
Chung-hui, Minister of For-
eign Affairs, to discuss
measures for their with-
drawal.

《字林时报》，1937年8月7日，星期六

推动在华
日本侨民中的
中国人撤离计划

南京，8月6日.—
（中央社）.— 据报，中国
政府已决定撤离所有在
日本的中國国民。
这一决定是最近在外
交部、财政部、交通部
和侨务委员会官员联合
会议后作出的。
据悉，招商局轮船公司
将受命派遣其几艘大型
轮船前往日本，以执行
此任务。
出于对在日本的大量中
国学生安全的担忧，教
育部长王世杰博士昨日
拜访了外交部长王宠惠
博士，商讨他们的撤离
措施。

CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, AUGUST 7, 1937

3 More Provincial Chiefs
Join In Nanking Parleys

Ku Chu-lung, Ho Cheng-chun, Huang Shao-hsiung
Arrive In Capital; Liu, Lung Coming

NANKING, Aug. 6.—(Central).—
The number of high provincial
leaders now in Nanking to inter-
view Generalissimo Chiang Kai-
shek in connection with the na-
tional crisis was swelled by the ar-
rival today of Gens. Ku Chu-tung,
Ho Cheng-chun and Huang Shao-
hsiung.
Gen. Ku is Director of the
Generalissimo's Provisional Head-
quarters in Sian, Gen. Ho is Paci-
fication Commissioner of Hupeh,
and Gen. Huang is Hupeh Chair-
man.
The three regional leaders were
received by the Generalissimo
shortly after their arrival.
Gen. Ku, who came from Chung-
king, reported to the Generalissimo
on the reorganization of the Sze-
chwan and Sikong troops now in
progress, while 'Gens. Ho and
Huang reported on measures now
being taken to maintain public
peace and order in Hupeh.
Calls On Pai, Yen
Gen. Ho also called on Gen.
Feng Yu-hsiang Vice-chairman of
the Military Affairs Commission,
Gen. Yen Hsi-shan, Pacification
Commissioner for Shansi and Sui-
yuan, and Gen. Pai Chung-hsi,
Deputy Commander-in-Chief of
the Fifth Route Army in Kwangsi.
More army commanders from
other parts of China are expected
to arrive here within the next two
or three days. Gen. Liu Hsiang,
Pacification Commissioner for Sze-
chwan and Sikong, and Gen. Lung
Yun, Chairman of Yunnan, are
coming on Aug. 9 by plane.
A Hongkong message states that
Gen. Tsai Ting-kai, Commander of
the former 19th Route Army, left
the Colony this morning aboard
the Empress of Japan for Shang-
hai en route to Nanking.
Accompanied By Tan
Gen. Tsai is accompanied by
Lieut.-Gen. Tan Chi-hsiu, defender
of the Woosung Forts during the
Shanghai hostilities of 1932, and
Lieut.-Gen. Chen Kwang-han,
former divisional commander of
the same Army.
Others already here are Gen.
Pai Chung-hsi, Deputy Commander-
in-Chief of the Fifth Route Army.
Gen. Ho Chien, Chairman of
Hunan, Gen. Yen Hsi-shan, Paci-
fication Commission for Shansi
and Suiyuan and Gen. Yu Han-
mou, Pacification Commissioner for
Kwangtung.

Kwangsi Chairman Going
Gen. Huang Hsu-chu, Chairman
of the Kwangsi provincial govern-
ment, will come to Nanking next
Monday, Aug. 9, to confer with the
Central authorities and other pro-
vincial leaders on the national
crisis.
This is according to Mr. Wei
Jung-chang, Director of the Politi-
cal Training Department of the
Fifth Route Army, who arrived
here from Kweilin today.

Generalissimo Again Sees Pai
General Chiang Kai-shek, Presi-
dent of Yuan and Chair-
man of the Military Affairs
Commission, called on General Pai
Chung-hsi, Deputy Commander-in-
Chief of the Fifth Route Army, today
to have another lengthy talk
with him on the North China
situation.

Szechwan Chairman Leaving
CHENGTU, Aug. 6.—(Central).—
Gen. Liu Hsiang, Pacification Com-
missioner for Szechwan and Sikong,
who originally planned to leave on
August 9, has now decided to go to
Nanking tomorrow by plane.
Gen. Liu will be accompanied by
Mr. Teng Han-hsiang, Secretary-
General of the Szechwan provin-
cial government, and several other
subordinates.
Gen. Lung Yun, Chairman of
Yunnan, who at first planned to fly
to Nanking together with Gen.
Liu, will now leave for the capital
on Sunday, August 8, via Chengtu.

Plane To Fetch Lung
SIAN, Aug. 6.—(Central).—The
Eurasia Aviation Corporation's No.
31 plane, by order of Government
authorities, today left here for
Kunming to fetch Gen. Lung Yun,
Chairman of the Yunnan Provin-
cial Government, to Nanking to in-
terview the Central leaders.
Air service between Lanchow and
Suchow, operated by the Eurasia
Corporation, will be resumed next
week, the corporation's No. 20 plane
having arrived here from Chengtu
this morning to bring a number of
staff members to Suchow.

《字林西报》，1937年8月7日，星期六

又有3位省主席
加入南京会谈

顾祝同、何成濬、黄绍竑
抵达首都；刘、龙将至

南京，8月6日.—（中央社）.—
随着顾祝同将军、何成濬将军和黄绍竑将军今日抵达，目前在南京就国家危机事宜谒见蒋介石委员长的各省高级领导人数量增加。
顾将军是委员长西安行营主任，何将军是湖北绥靖主任，黄将军是湖北省主席。
这三位地方领袖抵达后不久即受到委员长接见。
从重庆前来的顾将军向委员长汇报了正在进行的川康部队整编情况，而何将军和黄将军则汇报了目前为维持湖北公共治安与秩序所采取的措施。
拜访白、阎
何将军还拜访了军事委员会副委员长冯玉祥将军、晋绥绥靖主任阎锡山将军以及广西第五路军副总司令白崇禧将军。
预计未来两三天内将有更多来自中国其他地区的军队指挥官抵达此处。川康绥靖主任刘湘将军和云南省主席龙云将军将于8月9日乘飞机前来。
香港消息称，前第十九路军指挥官蔡廷锴将军今晨乘坐“日本皇后号”离开殖民地前往上海，途中转往南京。
谭陪同
蔡将军由中将谭启秀陪同，谭曾是1932年上海战事中吴淞要塞的保卫者；同行的还有中将陈光汉，曾任该军师长。
其他已在此处的人包括：第五路军副总司令白崇禧将军。
湖南省主席何键将军、晋绥绥靖主任阎锡山将军以及广东绥靖主任余汉谋将军。

广西主席即将启程
广西省政府主席黄旭初将军将于下周一，即8月9日，前往南京，就国家危机问题与中央当局及其他省主席进行磋商。
这是第五路军政治训练部主任魏荣昌先生今日从桂林抵达此处时所说的。

委员长再次会见白
行政院院长兼军事委员会委员长蒋介石将军今日拜访了第五路军副总司令白崇禧将军，就华北局势与他进行了另一次长时间谈话。

四川主席即将离川
成都，8月6日.—（中央社）.— 原计划于8月9日出发的川康绥靖主任刘湘将军，现已决定明日乘飞机前往南京。
刘将军将由四川省政府秘书长邓汉祥先生及其他几名下属陪同。
起初计划与刘将军一同飞往南京的云南省主席龙云将军，现将经由成都于8月8日星期日前往首都。

飞机接龙云
西安，8月6日.—（中央社）.— 奉政府当局命令，欧亚航空公司第31号飞机今日从此处飞往昆明，接云南省政府主席龙云将军来南京谒见中央领导人。
由欧亚公司运营的兰州与苏州之间的航空服务将于下周恢复，该公司第20号飞机今晨从成都抵达此处，载送多名工作人员至苏州。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, AUGUST 7, 1937

Many Generals Returning
To Offer Their Services

General Hsiao Cheng-ying, Former Tientsin Mayor,
And General Wen Arrive; T. V. Soong Is Back
From Nanking; General Tsai Arriving

General Hsiao Cheng-ying, form-
er Mayor of Tientsin, who was re-
cently sent to Europe by the Gov-
ernment to study military develop-
ments, and who rushed back to
Shanghai yesterday by air in order
to offer his services to the Govern-
ment during the national crisis, fail-
ed to issue a written statement to
the press last night, being overcome
by sorrow over the death of one of
his best friends in the battle of Pei-
ping.
Immediately after his arrival here,
General Hsiao stated that he was
indignant about the situation in the
North and that after one or two
days' stay here, he would proceed
to the capital to offer his services
to the Government as a military
man. He promised to issue a writ-
ten statement, but failed to do so
last night as he received reports on
the death of General Chao Den-yu,
the late commander of the 132nd
Division of the 29th Route Army,
who lost his life in the battle of
Nanyuan, Peiping.
General Hsiao arrived together
with General Wen Ying-shing, form-
er Commissioner of the Bureau of
Public Safety in Shanghai, who ac-
companied Dr. H. H. Kung, as a
military attache of the Coronation
delegation to London. General Wen
also wants to offer his services to
the Government. He left last night
for Nanking. General Wen is one
of the few Chinese graduates of the
West Point Military Academy.
Mr. Soong Returns
Mr. T. V. Soong returned here
yesterday from a trip to Nanking,
where he had conferred with Gen-
eral Chiang Kai-shek and General
Pai Chung-hsi in connection with
financial matters during the extra-
ordinary period.
General Huang Chao-hsiung,
Governor of Hupeh, who arrived
here by air on Wednesday, left here
hurriedly yesterday morning for
Nanking, after learning of the seri-
ous situation in Hankow. In Nan-
king he will meet General Pai
Chung-hsi, his old friend.
Mr. Chao Lu, member of the
Standing Committee of the Central
Executive Committee, and General
Chiang Kwang-lai, former com-
mander-in-chief of the 19th Route
Army of the Chapei fame, are
scheduled to arrive here tomorrow
from Hongkong. General Tsai Ting-
kai, former field commander of the
same army, is delayed by illness.
They will all go to Nanking to offer
their services to the country.

《字林时报》，1937年8月7日，星期六

众多将军归来
效力国家

前天津市长萧振瀛将军
和温应星将军抵达；宋子文自
南京返回；蔡将军即将抵达

前天津市长萧振瀛将军近期由政府派往欧洲研究军事发展情况，为在国家危机期间向政府效力，他昨日乘飞机赶回上海。由于一位挚友在北平战役中阵亡，他悲痛不已，昨晚未能向新闻界发表书面声明。
萧将军抵达此处后立即表示，他对北方局势感到愤慨，在此停留一两天后，他将前往首都，以军人身份向政府效力。他曾承诺发表书面声明，但昨晚因收到第二十九军第一三二师师长赵登禹将军在北平南苑战役中牺牲的消息，未能履行承诺。
萧将军与前上海公安局局长温应星将军一同抵达，温将军曾作为加冕代表团武官陪同孔祥熙博士前往伦敦。温将军也希望向政府效力。他昨晚已前往南京。温将军是少数毕业于西点军校的中国毕业生之一。
宋先生返回
宋子文先生昨日从南京旅行返回此处，他在南京就非常时期的财政事务与蒋介石将军和白崇禧将军进行了磋商。
湖北省主席黄绍竑将军周三乘飞机抵达此处，在得知汉口局势严重后，于昨日上午匆忙离开此处前往南京。在南京，他将会见他的老朋友白崇禧将军。
中央执行委员会常务委员会委员赵棣华先生（音译）和前以闸北闻名的第十九路军前总指挥蒋光鼐将军，计划明日从香港抵达此处。该军前野战指挥官蔡廷锴将军因病延误。他们都将前往南京，为国家效力。

Hirota Hopes
Others To Join
Anti-Red Pact

TOKYO, Aug. 6.—(Domei)—
Foreign Minister Koki Hirota to-
day told the Diet he "hoped" to
"contact" Italy, France and Great
Britain on their possible adherence
to the German-Japanese Anti-
Comintern Pact.

The statement was made in reply
to a query put by Mr. Juso Miwa,
of the proletarian Social Masses
Party...as to whether or not the
accord could be "developed into
another Locarno Pact".

The Foreign Office, Mr. Hirota
said in reply to another question,
has received no reports regarding
the conclusion of an agreement
for the grant of a £20,000,000 loan
to China by Great Britain.

Urged by Mr. Miwa to "entrust
the diplomatic negotiations on the
settlement of the North China in-
cident to the custody of the people,"
Mr. Hirota said the Government
would carry on the negotiations
"with the assistance of the people
and in accordance with their de-
sires".

? 8 31

Attempt To Buy Foreign
Currency Causes Day Of
Rush In Shanghai Banks

Many Said Seeking To Exchange Chinese Money For
Foreign Banknotes; Financial Leaders Say That
Fears Are Largely Without Real Foundation

BELIEF EXPRESSED THAT GOVERNMENT
WILL MEET ALL ITS OBLIGATIONS

Many banks in Shanghai were facing a rather serious
problem yesterday as their halls were crowded with depositors
seeking to buy foreign currency. It was reported that there was
an especially heavy demand for American currency, and along
towards closing hour this had assumed such proportions that it
was impossible to supply the required banknotes.

A number of prominent local bankers were interviewed by
representatives of "The Shanghai Times" with regard to the
situation and asked to express their opinion. It was generally
thought that the majority of the buyers had been led to believe
that the Chinese dollar was no longer safe and were attempt-
ing to exchange their holdings as quickly as possible.

The consensus of opinion among
foreign financial leaders was to the
effect that such fears were uncall-
ed for and that the Chinese Gov-
ernment had given sufficient in-
dication that it would do every-
thing possible to meet all require-
ments. The officials of several big
foreign banks said that the insist-
ence upon cash was evidently
based on an unreasonable distrust
and indicated a lack of understand-
ing of the situation.

The Chinese banks in Shanghai
are said to be faced with an in-
creasing uncomfortable state of
affairs which has gradually been
taking hold since the outbreak of
hostilities in North China. One
well-known Chinese banking auth-
ority told "The Shanghai Times"
yesterday that big native banks
throughout the city were being call-
ed upon to close the accounts of
many of their depositors of long
standing.

Foreign Banks Assist

The general practice on the part
of those who have become alarmed
over the prospects of the future
seems to be to withdraw money
from the Chinese banks and head
straight for some foreign bank in
order to convert it into another
currency. This has naturally work-
ed an undue hardship on the Chin-
ese banks, and, realizing this, the
foreign banks are said to be doing
everything possible to alleviate the
tension.

One prominent Chinese banker
who was interviewed here yester-
day called attention to the fact that
most of the banks had not been re-
ceiving deposits to any great ex-
tent since the beginning of the
trouble in North China, and this,
in his estimation, was almost tant-
amount to an actual withdrawal of
cash.

All Chinese banks are said to be
doing their best to assist each other
through the period, and, as it was
pointed out by one informant, the
three official banks have shown a
willingness to co-operate with vari-
ous commercial banks, by accept-
ing certain mortgages and paying
for them in legal tender notes.

The thing which all foreign bank-
ers are inclined to stress is the
likelihood of a declaration of war,
many indicating that during the last
two days a feeling of greater optim-
ism has prevailed with regard to
this. Some called attention to the
substantial reserves which the
Chinese Government maintains
abroad to protect the dollar.

The question is whether China
would see fit to maintain these re-
serves if war were declared or use
them outright for purchases abroad.
There is no binding agreement
which would prevent the Govern-
ment from expending such funds
as it saw fit.

Matters Of Policy

If a major conflict does come,
such matters of policy will have to
be thrashed out about the round
tables of high finance, and, as it
was pointed out, China will have
to decide between damaging her
credits abroad or availing herself
of a sizeable war chest.

According to one foreign banker
interviewed here yesterday, the
Government financial experts had
given "informal" assurances that
there was no reason for alarm. A
comforting factor in the current
situation is the fact that the flight
of capital has been relatively slight
and has by no means been com-
parable to that which occurred in
1934-35.

试图购买外汇
导致上海银行出现
挤兑一日

许多人称寻求将中国货币兑换为外国纸币；金融领袖称恐惧 largely 缺乏实际基础

相信政府
将履行其所有义务

昨天，上海的许多银行面临着一个相当严重的问题，因为大厅里挤满了寻求购买外币的储户。据报道，对美元的需求特别巨大，临近收盘时，需求规模之大，以致无法供应所需的现钞。

《字林西报》记者采访了一些当地知名银行家，请他们就局势发表意见。普遍看法是，大多数买家被引导相信中国元不再安全，并正试图尽快兑换其持有的货币。

外国金融领袖们的普遍意见认为，这种恐惧是没有必要的，中国政府已给出充分迹象，表明它将尽一切可能满足所有需求。几家大型外资银行的官员表示，坚持提取现金显然是基于不合理的怀疑，表明对局势缺乏了解。

据说，上海的华资银行正面临着一种日益令人不安的局面，这种局面自华北战事爆发以来逐渐形成。一位知名的中国银行业权威人士昨天告诉《字林西报》，全市的大型本土银行正被要求结清许多长期储户的账户。

外资银行提供协助

那些因对未来前景感到恐慌的人的普遍做法似乎是从华资银行取款，然后直接前往某家外资银行将其兑换成另一种货币。这自然给华资银行带来了过度的困难，意识到这一点后，据说外资银行正在尽其所能缓解紧张局势。

昨天在此接受采访的一位著名华资银行家提请注意这样一个事实：自华北麻烦开始以来，大多数银行的存款接收量并未大幅增加，在他看来，这几乎等同于实际的现金提取。

据说所有华资银行都在这一时期尽力相互协助，正如一位消息人士指出的那样，三家官方银行表现出与各商业银行合作的意愿，接受某些抵押贷款并以法币票据支付。

所有外资银行家倾向于强调的一点是宣战的可能性，许多人指出，在过去两天里，对此的乐观情绪有所增强。一些人提请注意中国政府为维护币值而在海外维持的大量储备。

问题在于，如果宣战，中国是否会认为有必要维持这些储备，还是直接将其用于海外采购。没有任何具有约束力的协议会阻止政府按其认为合适的方式支出此类资金。

政策事项

如果发生重大冲突，此类政策问题必须在高层金融圈的圆桌会议上彻底解决，而且，正如所指出的那样，中国必须在损害其海外信用或利用可观的战备资金之间做出决定。

据昨天在此接受采访的一位外资银行家称，政府财政专家已给予“非正式”保证，称没有理由惊慌。当前局势中一个令人安心的因素是，资本外流相对较少，绝无法与1934-35年间发生的情况相比。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, August 6, 1937

Refugee Hordes
Pour Into City

Over 50,000 In Past
24 Hours Flee
Chapei

More than 50,000 refugees and their possessions from Chapei, Wayside, Yangtsepoo, Hongkew and the northern suburbs entered the Settlement and French Concession during the past 24 hours a steady stream of heavily laden trucks, rickshas, handcarta and even carrier coolies passing over the various bridges spanning Soochow Creek. The poorer refugees carried their possessions rolled up in blankets and travelled on foot, the women often with children strapped to their backs.

The municipal police report that 34,000 crossed the Garden Bridge during the 24 hours ending at 7 o'clock this morning, 8000 passed through the Louza district. 7000 through Sings, 4800 through West and 2300 through Dixwell. It is believed that those passing through West Hongkew and Dixwell districts passed over the Garden Bridge and were counted there again, so that 50,000 is a fair estimate for the total.

Many Can Be Absorbed

The housing problem is becoming acute in both the Settlement and French Concession, but there is no danger of the power of absorption of these areas being strained for some time to come. During the 1927 fighting around Shanghai close to 1,000,000 refugees were taken in and sheltered. The number in 1932 was not less. Godowns, alleys, camps, P.W.D. yards, empty houses and all available waste grounds were filled with refugees. It is estimated that today hundreds of thousands can be sheltered easily. About 100,000 have now left Chapei.

This influx constitutes a serious problem for the health department as well as police force. When overcrowding becomes serious the health department sends out squads to clean up alleyways and takes necessary prophylactic measures to prevent all epidemics.

The police are kept on the alert patrolling districts where refugees are concentrated in order to protect them from looters and others which prey on them. Gangs are robbing girls and stealing from refugees of poor people who have no means of protecting themselves in public or private life. The Municipal Police are doing their best to cope with the situation but the task is enormous.

《上海晚邮报及信使报》，1937年8月6日，星期五

难民潮
涌入城市

过去24小时内
超过5万人逃离
闸北

在过去24小时内，超过5万名来自闸北、曹家渡（Wayside）、杨树浦、虹口及北部郊区的难民及其财物进入租界和法租界，载重卡车、人力车、手推车甚至挑夫络绎不绝地穿过跨越苏州河的各座桥梁。较贫困的难民将财物卷在毯子里，步行前进，妇女们往往背着孩子。

据工部局警务处报告，在截至今天早上7点的24小时内，有34,000人穿过外白渡桥（Garden Bridge），8,000人通过老闸区（Louza district），7,000人通过新闸区（Sings，音译），4,800人通过西区（West），2,300人通过狄思威路区（Dixwell）。据信，那些通过西虹口和狄思威路区的人也穿过了外白渡桥，并在那里被再次计数，因此50,000人是总数的合理估计。

许多人可被吸纳

租界和法租界的住房问题正变得严峻，但在未来一段时间内，这些区域的吸纳能力不会有不堪重负的危险。在1927年上海周边的战斗中，近100万难民被接纳和安置。1932年的数量也不少于此时。仓库、弄堂、营地、工务局场地、空房以及所有可用的荒地都住满了难民。据估计，如今可以轻易安置数十万人。目前已有约10万人离开闸北。

这股涌入浪潮给卫生部门以及警察部队都构成了严重问题。当过度拥挤变得严重时，卫生部门会派出小队清理弄堂，并采取必要的预防措施以防止所有流行病的发生。

警察保持警戒，在难民集中的地区巡逻，以保护他们免受劫掠者和其他掠夺者的侵害。帮派抢劫女孩，并从那些在公共或私人生活中无力保护自己的贫困难民那里偷窃。工部局警务处正尽力应对这一局势，但任务极其艰巨。

THE CHINA PRESS, MONDAY, AUGUST 9, 1937

Tsai Ting-kai Warmly
Greeted On Return Here

Leader Of Old 19th Route Army Pledges
Self For Service Of Country

Returning to the city where he staged a gallant defense against the Japanese in 1932, General Tsai Ting-kai, former Commander of the 19th Route Army, stated that he is ready and willing to do his duty as a soldier during the present Sino-Japanese crisis.

Although General Tsai appeared to be as full of nervous energy as during his eventful stay in Shanghai five years ago, those who know him thought that he had aged considerably during the interval. Specks of white hair showed above his temple. His thin face was tanned.

General Tsai, who had been staying in Manila for sometime, decided to return to China following the outbreak of the fighting in North China. To pressmen yesterday the famed defender of Shanghai said that although he is not in active service at the present time, he wants to fulfill his duty as a soldier and as a citizen during the present crisis.

"I have always held that in the face of Japanese aggression, China should and must defend herself. At this time, I am the last person to change my belief and to escape from my duties. I am willing and ready to stand on the front lines and deal with the enemy," he told newsmen.

People Must Sacrifice

At this time, the Chinese people should maintain a calm attitude and do the duty along their own lines of pursuit, General Tsai explained. Like their Government leaders, the populace should follow the plans and orders of the highest military authorities of the country during the emergency, he said.

"People of every rank and profession must be united and ready for the supreme sacrifice in the fight for the existence and independence of the Chinese race. We must defend the country to the last man and last bullet. With that perseverance and courage, the final victory will be ours," he pointed out.

General Tsai recalled that during his defense of Shanghai in 1932, a number of Chinese were tempted by large sums of money to become guides of the Japanese soldiers and supply food and other things to the Nipponese troops. He warned that during a major war, this must not occur.

Coming on the Empress of Japan together with Gen. Tsai, in addition to several high officers of the Army, was Mr. Tsoo Lu, Chancellor of the Sun Yat-sen University in Canton and member of the Standing Committee of the Central Executive Committee.

The 19th Route Army officers who accompanied Gen. Tsai were Lieut.-Gen. Tan Chi-hsu, divisional commander and defender of the Woosung Forts during the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1932, Lieut.-Gen. Li Sheng-tsung, deputy divisional commander, and Lieut.-Gen. Yeh Shao-chuen, Director of the General Affairs Section.

In Foreign Suit

Two other divisional commanders of the Army, namely Lieut.-Gen. Shen Han-kwang, Commander of the 60th Division, and Lieut.-Gen. Chang Yen, Commander of the 49th Division, had already arrived in Shanghai a few days ago and were at the wharf today to greet their chief.

Dressed in grey foreign suit and in the best of health, Gen. Tsai was greeted at the wharf by a representative gathering of Chinese officials and friends, including Gen. Yang Hu, Garrison Commander of the Shanghai-Woosung Area, Gen. Tsai Ching-chun, Director of the Greater Shanghai Police Bureau, and representatives of Mayor O. K. Yui and Mr. T. V. Soong, member of the Standing Committee of the National Economic Council.

Interviewed shortly after arrival Gen. Tsai stated that he was going to Nanking to serve the National Government in the capacity of a retired army commander, now that the Central authorities were determined to resist further Japanese encroachments of Chinese territory.

Ready To Give Life

True to his policy that the best way to stop foreign aggression in China was armed resistance, Gen. Tsai said that he was ready to put down his life on the very first front-line of the battlefield.

All army men in China, whether in active service or retired, Gen. Tsai declared, should now come forward as one man to fight alien aggression shoulder to shoulder under the leadership of the nation's highest military command.

On the part of the people, Gen. Tsai continued, they should maintain an attitude of calm while discharging their respective duties in the rear.

The civilian point of view was expressed by Mr. Tsoo Lu when he declared that like everyone else he was fully in support of the two declarations made by Gen. Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Executive Yuan, regarding the North China situation.

《字林西报》，1937年8月9日，星期一

蔡廷锴返沪受到热烈欢迎

原十九路军领袖誓言为国效力

前第十九路军总指挥蔡廷锴将军回到了他在1932年英勇抗击日军的城市，他表示，在当前中日危机期间，他已准备好并愿意履行作为一名军人的职责。

尽管蔡将军看起来像五年前在上海度过那段多事之秋时一样充满神经质的活力，但了解他的人认为，在这段时间里他衰老了许多。他的鬓角露出了白发。他消瘦的脸庞晒得黝黑。

蔡将军此前在马尼拉停留了一段时间，在华北战事爆发后决定返回中国。昨天，这位著名的上海保卫者对记者表示，虽然他目前不在现役，但他希望在这场危机中履行作为一名军人和公民的职责。

“我一直认为，面对日本的侵略，中国应该而且必须自卫。在这个时候，我最不可能改变自己的信念并逃避自己的责任。我愿意并准备站在前线与敌人作战，”他告诉记者。

民众必须做出牺牲

蔡将军解释说，此时中国人民应保持冷静的态度，并在各自的职业领域内履行职责。他说，民众应像政府领导人一样，在紧急时期遵循国家最高军事当局的计划和命令。

“各行各业、各阶层人民必须团结起来，准备为中华民族的生存和独立做出最大的牺牲。我们必须战斗到最后一人、最后一颗子弹。凭借这种毅力和勇气，最终的胜利将属于我们，”他指出。

蔡将军回忆说，在1932年他保卫上海期间，一些中国人被巨额金钱所诱惑，成为日军的向导，并向日军提供食物和其他物资。他警告说，在大规模战争中，这种情况绝不能发生。

与蔡将军一同乘坐“日本皇后号”轮船抵达的，除了几位陆军高级军官外，还有广州中山大学校长、中央执行委员会常务委员邹鲁先生。

陪同蔡将军前来的第十九路军军官包括：中将谭启绪，他在1932年中日敌对行动期间担任师长并防守吴淞要塞；中将李盛宗，副师长；以及中将叶肇春，总务处处长。

身着西装

该军另外两位师长，即第六十师师长沈光汉中将和第四十九师师长张炎中将，已于数日前抵达上海，并于今日在码头迎接他们的长官。

蔡将军身穿灰色西装，健康状况极佳，在码头受到了中国官员和朋友代表团的欢迎，其中包括上海吴淞区卫戍司令杨虎将军、大上海警察局局长蔡劲军将军，以及市长俞鸿钧和全国经济委员会常务委员宋子文的代表。

抵达后不久接受采访时，蔡将军表示，既然中央当局已决心抵抗日本对中国领土的进一步侵蚀，他将前往南京，以退役陆军指挥官的身份为国民政府服务。

随时准备献出生命

蔡将军坚持其政策，即阻止外国在华侵略的最佳方式是武装抵抗，他说他随时准备在战场的最前线献出生命。

蔡将军宣称，中国的所有军人，无论是在役还是退役，现在都应该团结一致，在国家最高军事指挥部的领导下，并肩作战，抗击外来侵略。

蔡将军接着说，就民众而言，他们应在后方履行各自职责的同时保持冷静的态度。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, AUGUST 7, 1937

AMERICANS OFFER
SERVICES
Volunteers for China from
All Parts of U.S.A.
1,000 AVIATORS SAID TO
BE INCLUDED

Los Angeles, Aug. 5.
Persons close to Lieutenant Russell
L. Hearn, soldier of fortune and
former aide to Marshal Chang Tso-lin
in Manchuria, said to-day that the
organization of an American brigade
of aviators, infantrymen and artillery-
men to aid China against Japan had
exceeded expectations.
Seven thousand persons have al-
ready volunteered for service, the
informants said. Most of those
volunteering have been ex-service
men.
Applications from individuals and
groups are arriving from a score of
cities and towns, including New
York, Boston, Philadelphia, Cleve-
land, Newark, Los Angeles, San
Francisco, Seattle, Jacksonville and
Atlanta, they said. One Trenton, N.J.,
volunteer offered to bring fifty men
with him. A Boise, Ida., physician
offered to form a medical corps.
The brigade thus far is reported to
include 1,000 aviators. Some of the
volunteers have demanded salaries of
U.S. $500 monthly, while others
have asked even more.
The Brigade has not offered specific
pay, in order to avoid prohibition of
its activities under terms of the
Neutrality Act, which forbids "re-
cruiting for hire."
Reports received here said that
China had agreed to furnish equip-
ment and munitions. It was worthy
of note that Lieutenant Hearn for five
years was on the staff of the "Old
Marshal" and that he fled China
when Marshal Chang was assassinat-
ed in 1928. Thus far the Bureau
of Investigation of the Department
of Justice has remained silent as to
the activities of Hearn and the
Brigade.—United Press.

美国人提供服务
来自美国各地的援华志愿者
据悉包括1000名飞行员

洛杉矶，8月5日电。
接近冒险家、前满洲张作霖元帅副官拉塞尔·L·赫恩（Russell L. Hearn）中尉的人士今天表示，组建一支由飞行员、步兵和炮兵组成的美国旅以协助中国对抗日本的计划，其进展超出了预期。
消息人士称，已有七千人自愿服役。大多数志愿者是退伍军人。
他们说，来自纽约、波士顿、费城、克利夫兰、纽瓦克、洛杉矶、旧金山、西雅图、杰克逊维尔和亚特兰大等二十多个城镇的个人和团体的申请正源源而来。新泽西州特伦顿的一名志愿者提出愿意带领五十人同行。爱达荷州博伊西的一名医生提出愿意组建一个医疗队。
据报道，该旅目前包括1000名飞行员。一些志愿者要求月薪500美元，而其他人要求的甚至更多。
为了避免因违反禁止“有偿招募”的中立法条款而导致其活动被禁，该旅没有提供具体的薪酬。
此处收到的报告称，中国已同意提供装备和弹药。值得注意的是，赫恩中尉曾在“老帅”麾下任职五年，并在1928年张元帅遇刺时逃离中国。迄今为止，司法部调查局对赫恩及该旅的活动保持沉默。——合众社。

ment to Hearn's reported activities.
The populace here appeared con-
vinced that foreign nations would
remain aloof from any Sino-Japanese
conflict.—United Press.

Danger to Friendship

Los Angeles, Aug. 6.
The Japanese Consul, Mr. Tomokazu
Hori, to-day commented on the re-
ported American enlistments for
China by saying, "Thus far we have
had only rumours. I may ask the
District Attorney if that is enough or
if we need actual evidence of the
violation of the Neutrality Act. If
evidence is not required, I shall later
decide whether to request a Federal
investigation."
Mr. Hori said that from the military
standpoint seven thousand merce-
naries, the number reported to have
volunteered for service with the Chi-
nese armies, was insignificant, but the
enlistment might endanger Japanese-
American friendship, "It could create
ill will," Mr. Hori said, "and that is
important."—United Press.

German Advisers May Leave

Berlin, Aug. 7.
German military advisers to General
Chiang Kai-shek may shortly be
withdrawn, it is reported to-day. The
reason given is that their continued
presence might be regarded as an un-
friendly act by the Japanese.—Reuter.

《字林西报》，1937年8月8日，星期日

美国将执行现有征兵法律
日本针对援华行动采取行动

参议员提出要求

撤出驻天津第十五步兵团

华盛顿，8月6日电。
在日本外交官员就所谓招募美国人援助中国在预期的对日战争中一事与国务院举行会议后，国务卿科德尔·赫尔（Cordell Hull）先生今天告诉新闻界，美国将执行现有的反对为外国战争招募人员的法律。
据悉，日本大使馆参赞须磨弥吉郎（Yakichiro Suma）先生本周在与赫尔先生的谈话中，提请国务卿注意太平洋沿岸大规模招募的报道，但未提出正式抗议。
日本大使馆拒绝对此情况发表评论，但合众社获悉，加利福尼亚州的日本领事已调查了有关招募的报道，并在须磨先生采取行动之前向大使馆提供了信息。
值得注意的是，由于难以证明是在美国领土而非外国领土上进行的征募，因此因外国招募而被起诉的情况很少见。
民主党参议院党鞭J·汉密尔顿·刘易斯（J. Hamilton Lewis）参议员坚持要求美军撤出中国，今天提出了一项决议，要求战争部长哈里·H·伍丁（Harry H. Woodring）先生向参议院报告在天津保留美国第十五步兵团的任何理由。——合众社。

国会质询

东京，8月6日电。
尽管今天这里对美国冒险家拉塞尔·L·赫恩中将据报道为中国招募外籍军团的活动普遍兴趣不大，但几名国会议员就这些报道向外务大臣广田弘毅（Koki Hirota）先生提出了质询。
广田先生回答说，他了解到美国正在仔细防范此类行动。人们记得，驻华盛顿日本大使馆参赞须磨弥吉郎先生曾提请美国政府注意赫恩据报道的活动。
这里的民众似乎相信，外国将在任何中日冲突中保持超然态度。——合众社。

危及友谊

洛杉矶，8月6日电。
日本领事堀一和（Tomokazu Hori）先生今天就据报道的美国人为中国应征入伍一事评论道：“到目前为止，我们只有谣言。我可以询问地区检察官，这是否足够，或者我们是否需要违反中立法的实际证据。如果不需要证据，我稍后将决定是否请求联邦调查。”
堀先生说，从军事角度来看，七千名雇佣兵——据报道自愿在中国军队服役的人数——微不足道，但这种征募可能会危及日美友谊，“这可能会造成恶感，”堀先生说，“而这很重要。”——合众社。

德国顾问可能离开

柏林，8月7日电。
据报道，蒋介石将军的德国军事顾问可能很快被撤回。给出的理由是，他们的继续存在可能被日本人视为不友好行为。——路透社。

Japan Returns Hankow
Concession To China;
Troops, People Depart
CONSUL OFFICIALS SHA
ALONE REMAINING
IN TROUBLE SPOT 7994/c
Ships Loaded With Nipponese Ready To Leave;
400 Bound For Shanghai; 4 Gunboats, 1
Mine-Layer Cover Evacuation Move
TOKYO ORDERS WITHDRAWAL
(Reuter's Agency)
HANKOW, August 7.—Acting on instructions from
Tokyo, the Japanese Consul-General here has
ordered the evacuation of all Japanese armed forces as
well as civilians from Hankow by noon tomorrow.
Meanwhile arrangements have been completed for
the taking over of the Japanese Concession by the
Chinese authorities, who will in future administer and
police the area.
The only Japanese national who will remain in Hankow
after tomorrow will be the local Consular officials and others
who arrived here from other ports up-river during the past
ten days.
The Bund of the Japanese Concession is the scene of
considerable activity as a result of the evacuation order.
Japanese passenger steamers lying off the Concession are
completely full with Japanese civilians, including many wo-
men and children, who expect to sail some time today for
Shanghai en route to Japan.
400 BOUND HERE
No less than 400 Japanese women and children left the
port yesterday in a steamer bound for Shanghai.
Also lying off the Concession are five Japanese war-
ships—four river gunboats and one mine-layer.
Slight labor disturbances are feared when the Japanese
close their cotton mills, but the Chinese authorities have
promised to do their best to alleviate the situation.
All foreign residents living in the Japanese Concession
and its vicinity were warned yesterday to evacuate.
HANKOW REMAINS TENSE
(Domei)
HANKOW, Aug. 7.—After a night of acute tension, Ja-
panese residents today began an evacuation of their con-
cession here in earnest.
Four hundred women and children, as well as 100 men,
sailed on two Japanese ships for Shanghai this morning.
The remaining 400 men will sail downriver on the s.s. Yoyang
Maru tomorrow morning.
With Japanese women and children aboard the s.s.
Heinyang Maru and the s.s. Fengyang Maru, and men seeking
refuge on the N.K.K. hulk, the Japanese concession presented
a deserted appearance last night Japanese marines, ex-
service men pressed into a volunteer unit and consular police-
men manned sandbag and barbed wire barricades on the
boundary. Across the roads forming the boundary with
Chinese territory, were Chinese troops also manning bar-
ricades and concrete pill boxes.

东京下令撤退
（路透社）
汉口，8月7日电。——遵照东京指示，驻此地日本总领事已命令所有日本武装部队及平民于明日中午前从汉口撤离。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, AUGUST 8, 1937

AMERICANS NOT TO
LEAVE NANKING

Evacuation Story Is
Denied By Embassy
Second Secretary

NANKING. Aug. 7.—Rumours circulated to the effect that American nationals here will shortly be evacuated to Shanghai were denied by Mr. G. Atcheson, Jr., Second Secretary of the United States Embassy. No such steps have been contemplated, he said.

Mr. Shidaka, Counsellor of the Japanese Embassy, called on Mr. Hsu Mo, Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs, at the Waichiaopu at 3 o'clock this afternoon. "Political Affairs" were said to have been discussed during the 40-minute interview between two officials.

Two hours later, Mr. K. F. Kui, Second Secretary of the Japanese Embassy, interviewed Mr. Tung Tao-ning, sectional chief of the Asiatic Affairs Department of the Waichiaopu.

General Chang Chun, Secretary-General of the Central Political Council, had a 15-minute conversation with Mr. Hsu Mo, and Mr. Chen Chieh, Vice-Ministers of Foreign Affairs, at 5 o'clock this afternoon.

This morning, Gen. Chiang Tso-pin, Minister of Interior, discussed co-ordination work between the Home Ministry and the Waichiaopu with Mr. Chen Chieh. -- Central News.

美国人不会

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, AUGUST 8, 1937 235335
JAPANESE CONCESSION AT
HANKOW EVACUATED

All Civilians and Armed Force Out By Noon To-day:
Only Consular Staff Remain

CHINESE AUTHORITIES TO TAKE OVER

Move to Avert Any Outbreak of Incident: Departure
Does Not Mean Surrender of Concession

Hankow, Aug. 7.
THE Japanese Consul-General here announced to-day that, on instructions from the Government in Tokyo, all Japanese armed forces as well as civilians would be evacuated from Hankow by noon to-morrow.
Meanwhile, arrangements have been completed for the taking over of the Japanese Concession by the Chinese authorities, who will in future administer and police the area.
The only Japanese nationals who will remain in Hankow after to-morrow will be the local Consular officials and others who arrived here from other ports up-river during the past ten days.
The Bund of the Japanese Concession is the scene of considerable activity as a result of the evacuation order. Japanese passenger steamers lying off the Concession are completely full with Japanese civilians, including many women and children, who expect to sail some time to-day for Shanghai en route to Japan. No less than 400 Japanese women and children left the port yesterday in a steamer bound for Shanghai. Also lying off the Concession are five Japanese warships—four river gunboats and one mine-layer.
Slight labour disturbances are feared when the Japanese close their cotton mills, but the Chinese authorities have promised to do their best to alleviate the situation. All foreign residents living in the Japanese Concession and its vicinity were warned yesterday to evacuate.
Both the Chinese and Japanese authorities here have expressed a desire to avoid trouble, and the withdrawal of the Japanese will naturally help to prevent anything untoward occurring.
Although entry into the Japanese Concession has been barred, Reuter's correspondent was able to make a tour of the area this afternoon. He was stopped on the border by Japanese sentries with fixed bayonets, but was allowed to pass after they had been satisfied with his bona-fides. Everything in the Concession was quiet, but an air of activity prevailed as lorries laden with household goods sped to the wharves. Apart from house-moving vans, there was no traffic.
The tension of Sino-Japanese relations has been reflected here by the general slackening of business. All big contracts with Japanese firms have been cancelled, and, altogether, trade has suffered a severe setback.
—Reuter.

Civilian Evacuation Completed
Hankow, Aug. 7.
All civilian Japanese with the exception of Consular officials, left...

The evacuating Japanese sailed by the Shinyo Maru and the Yoyang Maru. The gunboat Seta will convoy the vessels to Shanghai.
The concession to-day presented a picture of feverish activity as the residents rushed their belongings to the warehouse of the Japanese Residents' Corporation for storage. Along the fringe of the Japanese settlement were marines, consular policemen and volunteers mounting a strong guard at the boundaries. Japanese private and public property will be left in the custody of the local Chinese authorities who will be requested to assume responsibility for its safe-keeping with a view to an eventual return to Japan after the present crisis is over.
The Japanese concession spent an anxious night as it was realized that Chinese troops in overwhelming numbers had the area surrounded on three sides. These Chinese forces, estimated at 10,000 men, this morning began cutting down trees along the boundary road. At the same time, another group moved into the adjoining former German Concession and mounted machine-guns on rooftops overlooking Japanese defence positions at street intersections.
The order to all residents to store their belongings in the warehouse of the Japanese Residents' Corporation, which was temporarily remanded last night, again went into effect this morning.—Domei.

The Official Explanation
The evacuation of the Japanese Concession in Hankow was ordered by the Foreign Office in a desire to prevent the outbreak of an incident that would aggravate the general situation, Domei was informed yesterday by Japanese official circles in Shanghai. The officials emphatically denied the reports that the Japanese Concession is being handed over to the Chinese authorities.
What really happened, they explained, was that the Chinese authorities were requested by the Japanese Consulate-General in Hankow to give assurances regarding the security of Japanese property in the Concession. The withdrawal of Japanese residents from Hankow, it was emphasized, is in no way different from the exodus of Japanese from Chungking, Soochow and Hangchow, each of which has a Japanese concession.
Orders to evacuate Hankow, Domei was informed, were issued because of the steadily growing tension. At the end of July the situation was further aggravated by the action of the Chinese Trade Guild in ordering a boycott of Japanese goods and a suspension of transactions with the Japanese. Fuel was added to the fire by the construction of defence works in Chinese streets bordering on the Concession by the "strongly anti-Japanese Chinese soldiers," the officials said. The anti-Japanese movement was also assiduously fanned by the City Tangpu and such anti-Japanese-bodies as the Society for the Encouragement of Resistance to the Enemy.
With tension growing every hour, the Concession was believed to be in danger of a sudden attack. Therefore, the officials said, on the evening of July 5, bluejackets were landed from the Eleventh Torpedo Flotilla and posted at positions facing the Chinese entrenchments.

"Non-Aggravation" Policy
In view of the seriousness of the situation, the Japanese acting Consul-General ordered all Japanese residents to evacuate the Concession, in accordance with the Japanese Government's policy of "non-aggravation" of the current crisis, the officials added. Japanese Consular authorities, Domei was informed, will remain in Hankow for the time being to negotiate on the protection of Japanese private and public property.
The officials recalled that the Nanking Government and the Chinese authorities in Hankow have been asked by the Japanese Embassy in China and the Consulate-General in the Yangtze port to give all possible assistance in carrying out the evacuation smoothly.

Wuhu Japanese Leave
Nanking, Aug. 7.
Japanese residents of Wuhu, numbering about 50 men, women and children, were evacuated to Shanghai by the Jang Yang Maru yesterday, the Japanese Embassy here was advised to-day.—Domei.

Trouble At Canton
Canton, Aug. 7.
With Chinese servants and other employees refusing to work, the evacuation of 160 Japanese women and children hit a snag here to-day. This situation compelled the Japanese Residents' Corporation to hire lighters to transport the household articles of the refugees.
Most of them will leave on the Fukken Maru sailing from here on August 10 and on the Tatsuta Maru leaving Hongkong on August 12.
Meantime, the activities of student orators and other agitators tended to increase the tension here. All vessels sailing for Hongkong as well as trains heading for the British colony are crowded to capacity with Chinese fleeing Canton.—Domei.

《字林西报》，1937年8月8日，星期日 235335
汉口日本租界
已撤离

所有平民及武装部队于今日中午前撤出：
仅留领事人员

中国当局将接管

此举旨在避免任何事件爆发：撤离并不意味着放弃租界

汉口，8月7日。
驻此地日本总领事今日宣布，遵照东京政府指示，所有日本武装部队及平民将于明日中午前从汉口撤离。
与此同时，中方当局接管日本租界的安排已完成，今后该区域将由中方行政并维持治安。
明日之后，留在汉口的唯一日本国民将是当地领事馆官员以及过去十天里从长江上游其他港口抵达此地的其他人。
由于撤离令，日本租界的外滩一带活动频繁。停泊在租界外的日本客轮上挤满了日本平民，其中包括许多妇女和儿童，他们预计将于今日某时启航前往上海，继而返回日本。昨日，不少于400名日本妇女和儿童乘一艘驶往上海的轮船离开港口。此外，停泊在租界外的还有五艘日本军舰——四艘内河炮艇和一艘布雷舰。
人们担心在日本人关闭棉纺厂时会出现轻微的劳工骚乱，但中国当局已承诺将尽力缓解局势。昨日，居住在日本租界及其附近的所有外籍居民被警告撤离。
此地中日双方当局均表示希望避免麻烦，日本的撤离自然有助于防止任何意外发生。
尽管进入日本租界已被禁止，但路透社记者仍于今天下午对该地区进行了巡视。他在边界处被持刺刀的日本哨兵拦下，但在对方确认其身份真实后获准通过。租界内一切平静，但随着装载家用物品的卡车疾驰向码头，一种忙碌的气氛弥漫开来。除了搬家货车外，没有其他交通车辆。
中日关系的紧张反映在这里商业活动的普遍放缓上。与日本公司的所有大额合同均已取消，总体而言，贸易遭受了严重挫折。
——路透社。

平民撤离完成
汉口，8月7日。
除领事官员外，所有日本平民已离开……

撤离的日本人是乘坐“SHINYO MARU”号和“YOYANG MARU”号离开的。“SETA”号炮艇将护送这些船只前往上海。
今天，随着居民们匆忙将财物送往日本居留民团仓库储存，租界呈现出一片狂热忙碌的景象。在日本定居点的边缘，海军陆战队员、领事警察和志愿者在边界处严密警戒。日本私人和公共财产将交由当地中国当局保管，并要求其承担保护责任，以便在当前危机结束后最终归还日本。
日本租界度过了一个焦虑的夜晚，因为人们意识到数量庞大的中国军队已从三面包围该地区。据估计这支中国军队有1万人，今晨开始砍伐边界道路沿线的树木。同时，另一支部队进入邻近的原德国租界，并在俯瞰街道交叉口日本防御阵地的屋顶上架设机枪。
要求所有居民将物品储存在日本居留民团仓库的命令，昨晚曾暂时暂缓执行，今晨再次生效。——同盟社。

官方解释
据上海日本官方人士昨日告知同盟社，汉口日本租界的撤离是外务省为防止爆发可能加剧总体局势的事件而下令的。官员们坚决否认了日本租界正在移交给中国当局的报道。
他们解释说，实际情况是，日本驻汉口总领事馆请求中国当局就保证租界内日本财产的安全作出承诺。他们强调，日本居民从汉口撤离与日本人从重庆、苏州和杭州（均设有日本租界）的出走并无不同。
据告知同盟社，下达撤离汉口的命令是因为紧张局势不断升级。7月底，中国同业公会下令抵制日货并停止与日本人的交易，使局势进一步恶化。官员们称，“强烈反日的中国士兵”在与租界接壤的中国街道上修筑防御工事，更是火上浇油。市党部以及“抗敌后援会”等反日团体也在竭力煽动反日运动。
随着紧张局势每小时都在加剧，人们认为租界面临突然袭击的危险。因此，官员们说，7月5日晚，第十一鱼雷艇支队的水兵登陆，并被部署在面向中国战壕的阵地上。

“不扩大”政策
官员们补充说，鉴于局势的严重性，日本代理总领事根据日本政府当前危机“不扩大”的政策，命令所有日本居民撤离租界。据告知同盟社，日本领事当局将暂时留在汉口，就保护日本私人和公共财产进行谈判。
官员们回顾说，日本驻华大使馆和长江口岸总领事馆已要求南京政府和汉口中国当局提供一切可能的协助，以顺利执行撤离行动。

芜湖日本人离开
南京，8月7日。
据日本大使馆今日获悉，芜湖约50名男女老少日本居民昨日由“JANG YANG MARU”号撤离至上海。——同盟社。

广州发生麻烦
广州，8月7日。
由于中国仆人和其他雇员拒绝工作，160名日本妇女和儿童的撤离今日在此受阻。这种情况迫使日本居留民团雇佣驳船来运输难民的家用物品。
大多数人将乘坐8月10日从此起航的“FUKKEN MARU”号和8月12日离开香港的“TATSUTA MARU”号离开。
与此同时，学生演说家和其他煽动者的活动倾向于加剧这里的紧张局势。所有驶往香港的船只以及开往英国殖民地的火车都挤满了逃离广州的中国人。——同盟社。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REGISTRY
7994/5
9 8 37

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, AUGUST 8, 1937

Flight From
North Areas
Slackening

Less Than 10,000 Pass
Over Boundary Lines
During Day

HONGKEW SHOPS
CLOSING DOWN

30 Stores Along North
Szechuen Road Move
Entire Stocks

The exodus of war-scared Chinese from the Chapel and Hongkew sections of the city slackened considerably yesterday from the record high of the previous days, with the police estimating that less than 10,000 refugees crossed into the Settlement yesterday.

The nature of the exodus changed yesterday with less people streaming into the Settlement and more wagons and pushcarts filled with household goods crossing the boundary.

This change indicates that the people, instead of fleeing with their portable goods, are now methodically moving their entire household effects into the Settlement in preparation for a long stay.

Hotel Of 120 Cots

The huge influx of people into the Settlement and Concession brought many unusual answers to the housing problem.

One enterprising old Chinese man with an empty lot on Boone and Chekiang Roads established yesterday afternoon an open-air "hotel" charging 50 cents a night for each camp cot. With approximately 120 cots on his lot, he looks forward to raking in quite a bit of money from the exodus.

The foreign and Russian boarding houses have opened their doors to the refugees, seeing in them a profitable source of income during the slack summer season when many of the regular paying guests were away on vacation. But even these are now completely filled with refugees.

Although many stores are closed in Chapel and Hongkew, the pawnshops are keeping open and are doing a rushing business taking in goods that refugees want to get off their hands temporarily.

But even the pawnshops have taken precautions against possible fighting and have moved their valuables to the French Concession and International Settlement for safe-keeping.

Although the exodus is slackening down, police officers are still continuing to direct traffic at the various points leading into the Settlement to keep the roads clear and prevent congestion.

Nippon Banknotes Scarce

Chinese "war fever" victims are not the only people moving out of the Chapel and Hongkew districts. The Japanese themselves are starting an exodus out of these areas but instead of crossing Soochow Creek, are going home to Japan.

This state of affairs has caused a scarcity of Japanese banknotes in the city and the official yen exchange rate went to Y103.75 for $100 yesterday. This was due, Japanese banks stated, to the growing exodus of Japanese from the city.

Many Japanese officers of the Municipal Police have sent their families home to Japan, while a great many Japanese businessmen have taken similar precautions.
