《字林西报》，1937年8月8日，星期日

从
北部地区
逃离之势
减缓

日间越过边界线者
不足一万人

虹口商店
停业

北四川路沿线
30家店铺
搬运全部存货

昨日，因战争恐慌而从本市老闸（Chapel）和虹口地区出逃的中国民众数量较前几日创下的纪录高峰大幅减少，警方估计昨日进入租界的难民不足一万人。

昨日出逃的性质发生了变化，涌入租界的人数减少，而装满家用物品的马车和手推车越过边界的数量增多。

这一变化表明，人们不再仅仅携带随身物品逃难，而是正有条不紊地将全部家当搬入租界，为长期滞留做准备。

设有120张床位的旅馆

大量人口涌入租界和法租界，给住房问题带来了许多不同寻常的应对方式。

一位有进取心的中国老者在布恩路（Boone Road，今塘沽路）与浙江路交界处的一块空地上，于昨日下午开设了一家露天“旅馆”，每张行军床每晚收费50美分。他的空地上约有120张床位，他指望从这次逃亡潮中大赚一笔。

外国人和俄罗斯人经营的寄宿公寓已向难民敞开大门，视其为夏季淡季的获利来源，此时许多常规付费客人外出度假。但即便这些住所现在也已完全被难民住满。

尽管老闸和虹口的许多商店已关闭，但典当行仍在营业，且生意兴隆，接收难民希望暂时脱手的物品。

但即使是典当行也采取了防范措施以应对可能的战斗，并将贵重物品移至法租界和国际租界妥善保管。

尽管出逃之势正在减缓，警察仍继续在各通往租界的路口指挥交通，以保持道路畅通并防止拥堵。

日本纸币稀缺

受中国“战争热”影响而撤离的并非只有中国人。日本人自己也开始从这些地区撤离，但他们不是越过苏州河，而是返回日本本土。

这种情况导致市内日本纸币短缺，昨日官方日元汇率涨至100美元兑换103.75日元。日本银行称，这是由于离开本市的日本人日益增多所致。

许多公共租界警务处的日本警官已将家人送回日本，而许多日本商人也采取了类似的预防措施。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, AUGUST 8, 1937    23J-37

Refugee Mob
Rushes River
Boat Kutwo

Police Called To Clear
Hundreds From Deck Of
Overcrowded Steamer

VESSEL HELD UP FOR
EIGHT HOURS

Disappointed Crowd Camps
On Wharf Waiting For
Arrival Of Tuckwo

Packed to the gunwales by hundreds of refugees determined to see the vessel sink under them before shifting, the Indo-China S. N. Company's river boat Kutwo was delayed eight hours at Hunt's Wharf yesterday until police had been rushed from Hongkew station to clear the decks of some thousand odd passengers more than the steamer is able to carry.

Due to being held up by the typhoon, the Kutwo arrived in Shanghai two days late to find all available accommodation booked up and a long waiting list of applicants for deck space or any odd nook and cranny capable of carrying a passenger.

When sailing time was reached yesterday, hundreds of Chinese refugees from Hongkew and Chapei areas, unprovided with tickets, staged a mad stampede and boarded the steamer with their own baggage, refusing to yield despite all pleas from the company's harried officials, and threats of police intervention.

Eventually the position became so serious that a call was put through to Hongkew Police Station and ...

most probably prove to be a much safer haven for refugees than the International Settlement or the French Concession.

The great influx of refugees from districts along the Shanghai-Nanking and the Shanghai-Hangchow Railways in the past few days has been causing a deep concern to the authorities. The All-Shanghai Committee for the Support of Resistance Against the Enemy, it was announced, has officially petitioned the Kiangsu and Chekiang Provincial authorities to check the exodus to Shanghai.

While thousands of people have kept flocking to Shanghai for the past few days, departing coastal and river steamers have also been doing a record business. All ships sailing for the South in the past few days and for the river ports, have been packed to overflowing, showing that a certain section of the public is of the opinion that perhaps Shanghai will not be the safest refuge in case of war.

200,000 Shift Home

Despite the large departures for the south and some of the river ports, the population of the Settlement and the French Concession is believed to have increased by almost 200,000 since the start of the exodus from the surrounding areas, this creating both a housing and a food supply problem.

Rents in various Chinese lodging houses have reached unbelievable figures, but refugees pay them, having no other alternatives. The food problem is being watched by authorities. The price of rice has again risen during the last few days, merchants mainly attributing it to the fact that the recent typhoons have greatly affected the producing districts, while allegations are being made in some quarters, that almost 4,000 bales of rice were sold recently to the "enemy."

Watch For Traitors

In order to cope with this alleged action of "traitors" a group of some 30 youths have organized a "Traitor Extermination Corps" with offices located in 93 Den Feng Alley, Avenue Road. The business of this corps is to investigate into the activities of the "traitors" and report to the proper quarter.

At a joint meeting held yesterday the Chinese Chamber of Commerce and the Shanghai General Labour Union decided to request the managements of factories to remove their plants to places of comparative safety, whenever possible, so as to be able to carry on production during any extraordinary period. It was also decided to petition banks to continue advancing funds to merchants and industrialists so as not to halt the progress of commerce.

The patriotic fervour among Chinese has reached even into S.M.C. schools it was revealed yesterday with the resignation from the S.M.C. Public School for Chinese of Y. Z. Sung, a teacher in Chin... for the purpose of enlisting

with the Chinese army as a private.
Fellow teachers are honouring their former colleague to-day at a little party.

Reports that a Chinese coppersmith employed by Andersen, Meyer and Company, had been tortured by Japanese Marines after having been held prisoner for two days were denied yesterday by the Japanese Naval Landing Party and strongly discounted by S.M.C. police investigating the report.

Sung Yung-chang, the coppersmith, disappeared two days ago and suddenly returned home yesterday with his mouth and the exterior of his stomach burned by what appeared to be acid.

Police called to his home by the man's wife were told by Sung that he had been arrested two days ago by Japanese Marines and had been taken to the Kiangwan Road barracks and imprisoned under suspicion that he was a Chinese plainclothesman.

According to Sung, he was questioned repeatedly and finally was ordered to drink sulphuric acid. This he refused but spilt some of the acid on his mouth and clothes. While a Japanese officer guarding him went for assistance, Sung recounted, he made his escape.

Police investigating the case pointed out that Sung disappeared immediately after he had collected his pay. He is a married man.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年8月8日    23J-37

难民群
涌向河边
“古土”号轮船

警方奉命清理
超载轮船甲板上
的数百人

船只
被阻八小时

失望的人群在码头露营
等待“德和”号（Tuckwo）的到来

昨天，印度支那轮船公司（Indo-China S. N. Company）的内河轮船“古土”号（Kutwo）在亨特码头（Hunt's Wharf）被延误了八个小时，直到从虹口警局调派的警察赶到，清除了甲板上比该轮运载能力多出约一千名的乘客，此前数百名决心在船移动前就挤上去、甚至不惜让船沉没的难民将船塞得满满当当，直至舷缘。

由于受台风阻碍，“古土”号抵沪晚了两天，发现所有可用舱位均已订满，还有一份长长的等候名单，申请者争相预订甲板空间或任何能容纳一名乘客的角落缝隙。

昨日到了开船时间，数百名来自虹口和闸北地区、没有车票的中国难民疯狂冲撞，带着自己的行李登上轮船，尽管公司疲惫不堪的官员再三恳求，并以警方干预相威胁，他们仍拒绝退让。

最终局势变得如此严重，以至于向虹口警察局发出了呼叫……

对于难民来说，这里很可能证明是比国际租界或法租界更安全的避难所。

过去几天，来自沪宁铁路和沪杭铁路沿线地区的难民大量涌入，已引起当局的深切关注。据悉，上海全市抗敌后援会已正式 petition（请愿）江苏和浙江省当局，制止向上海的逃亡潮。

虽然过去几天成千上万的人持续涌向上海，但离港的海轮和内河轮船业务也创下纪录。过去几天驶往南方及各内河港口的所有船只都拥挤不堪，这表明部分公众认为，万一发生战争，上海或许并非最安全的避难所。

20万人迁回故里

尽管有大量人员前往南方和一些内河港口，但据信，自周边地区开始出逃以来，租界和法租界的人口增加了近20万，这造成了住房和食品供应问题。

各中式客栈的租金已达到令人难以置信的水平，但难民别无选择，只能支付。当局正在关注食品问题。近日米价再次上涨，商人主要将其归因于近期台风对产区造成严重影响，同时也有方面指控称，近期有近4000包大米被出售给“敌人”。

监视汉奸

为了应对这种所谓的“汉奸”行为，约30名青年组织了一支“锄奸团”，办事处设在爱文义路（Avenue Road，今北京西路）登丰里93号。该团的职责是调查“汉奸”的活动并向有关部门报告。

在昨日举行的一次联席会议上，上海总商会和上海总工会决定请求工厂管理层在可能的情况下将厂房迁至相对安全的地方，以便在任何非常时期能够继续生产。会议还决定请愿银行继续向商人和工业家提供贷款，以免商业进程停滞。

据悉，中国人的爱国热情甚至蔓延到了工部局学校，昨日披露，工部局华童公学的一名教师Y. Z. Sung（宋永章？音译）辞职，目的是以列兵身份加入中国军队。同事们今日在一个小型聚会上向这位前同事致敬。

关于安德森·迈耶公司（Andersen, Meyer and Company）雇用的一名中国铜匠在被囚禁两天后遭日本海军陆战队酷刑折磨的报道，昨日遭到日本海军陆战队否认，负责调查此报告的工部局警察也强烈质疑该说法。

铜匠宋永昌（Sung Yung-chang，音译）两天前失踪，昨日突然回家，其嘴部和腹部外部被看似强酸的物质烧伤。

应其妻子召唤到家的警察听宋某说，他两天前被日本海军陆战队逮捕，并被带到江湾路兵营，因涉嫌是中国便衣侦探而被监禁。

据宋某称，他受到反复审问，最后被命令喝下硫酸。他拒绝了，但将一些硫酸洒在了嘴巴和衣服上。宋某叙述道，当看守他的日本军官去寻求援助时，他趁机逃脱。

调查此案的警察指出，宋某在领到薪水后立即失踪。他是一名已婚男子。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, AUGUST 7, 1937
23522

SCAREMONGERS
AMASS WEALTH
FROM GULLIBLE

Profiteers Keep Exodus at
Fever Pitch

FILL EMPTY HOUSES

“Mosquito Press” and
Transport Racket

SPECIAL TO THE “N.C.D.N.”

Thousands and thousands of dollars are daily flowing into the pockets of profiteers who are taking full advantage of the unsettled political conditions and who do their utmost to spread rumours of war to a gullible population.

“Remember 1932?” they say through countless agents. “Well, it is just about to start again. To-morrow you may hear the spatter of machine-guns and the boom of cannon. It would be the safest to move tonight. Now, we know of a nice place in such-and-such street....”

It is a well-organized racket, in which transportation and house-rental agencies work together. Having spread the rumours through scores of “mosquito papers” and thousands of paid scare-mongers, including transportation workers, they reap immediate profits and little can be done to bring them to justice as it is well-nigh impossible to trace the false reports.

Exodus Still Heavy

The exodus from Chapei, the North Szechuen Road area, Hongkew and West Hongkew, and the Kashing Road district continued yesterday on a large scale, being especially heavy in the afternoon. It was due, as on previous days, largely to the work of the profiteers, and the Chinese and Settlement police could do little to discourage it. A contributing factor, as far as the Kiangwan area was concerned, was machine-gun firing heard the previous evening in the vicinity of the Seekingjao Golf Course. This firing, which was practice shooting by the local Paotui, was audible for over an hour during the early evening. It was heavy for the most part and attracted considerable attention.

Previous operations of the Paocntui north of Shanghai, such as digging trenches and rifle pits, building machine-gun emplacements and depositing sand-bags, had been performed quietly, mostly after dark, and hence had given rise to little speculation as to their purpose. The presence of members of the Paocntui in the vicinity, itself, has not been obvious as the men have appeared largely in civilian clothes.

Irrespective of guarded activity, the exodus has been, and still is, tremendous owing to the machinations of the rumour-mongers. The demand for transportation has been so great that rates have skyrocketed, several times the usual amount being charged in many cases. Some of the smaller removal companies now have their lorries on the streets day and night. The effect of the presence of a van in a side-street or a lane is to create a feeling of insecurity among the neighbours, and the agents of the profiteers soon take advantage of this fact by inducing others to move. This house-to-house work...

House Rents Soar

The degree of panic is further reflected by the rents now being exacted. These are in most cases from 30 to 50 per cent. higher than before the scare. Half-empty terraces are being filled overnight and lodging-houses are crowded to their attics. The landlords and owners generally insist on advance payment of rent, sometimes for several months, and besides “key money” is exacted from the anxious new tenants. This bleeding is done by experts in the Settlement generally, south of the Soochow Creek, and in the French Concession. The most brazen profiteering is said to be that perpetrated in the Concession, where modest Chinese lodgings abound.

Some of the refugees come from points on the Shanghai-Woosung railway and the Shanghai-Nanking line and it is odd to observe refugees arriving by the latter line at the same time as others are leaving, in equally large numbers, for points on that railway. A similar situation obtains in the sphere of river travel, many families arriving from the nearer Yangtze ports as others depart for the same places.

There has been only a small exodus of Japanese residents of the Shanghai northern area to date and no official word has been given to Japanese subjects advising them to leave. The Japanese Landing Party, since the discovery of the missing Seaman Miyazaki, has maintained an extremely conservative attitude. There has been only the minimum of drills and no large-scale manoeuvres. Sentries and patrols do not wear steel-helmets, but only topees and cloth caps. Members of the Landing Party are freely given leave, as in ordinary times. A “parade” of tanks, armoured cars, lorries and other motor equipment in front of the Kiangwan Road barracks yesterday afternoon was routine, for the purpose of filling petrol tanks from the pump in front of the building.

No Food Profiteering

According to official information from the Public Health Department of the Settlement, there is no truth in reports which are being circulated of increased prices for foodstuffs at the Settlement markets. An inspection of all the principal municipal and private markets yesterday disclosed that there was a plentiful supply of all kinds of foodstuffs, with the exception of Japanese fish which did not arrive owing to... Supplies of Chinese fresh and salted fish, vegetables, fruits, eggs and all kinds of meats were plentiful and there was no increase in prices.

《字林西报》，1937年8月7日，星期六
23522

散布恐慌者
从轻信民众身上
大发横财

投机商使逃离潮
持续高烧不退

填满空置房屋

“蚊子报”与
运输勒索团伙

《字林西报》专电

成千上万美元正每日流入投机商的口袋，他们充分利用动荡的政治局势，并竭尽全力向轻信的民众散布战争谣言。

“还记得1932年吗？”他们通过无数代理人说道。“嗯，那一切即将重演。明天你可能就会听到机枪的哒哒声和大炮的轰鸣声。今晚搬家是最安全的。现在，我们知道在某条街有个好地方……”

这是一个组织严密的勒索团伙，运输公司和房屋租赁中介相互勾结。在通过数十家“蚊子报”和数千名受雇的散布恐慌者（包括运输工人）散播谣言后，他们迅速获取利润，而由于几乎无法追踪虚假报告的来源，很难将他们绳之以法。

逃离潮依然汹涌

昨日，从闸北、北四川路地区、虹口及西虹口，以及嘉善路地区的大规模逃离潮仍在继续，下午尤为严重。与前几天一样，这主要是由于投机商的推波助澜，华界警察和租界警察对此几乎无能为力。就江湾地区而言，一个促成因素是前一晚在沈家桥高尔夫球场附近听到的机枪射击声。这次射击是当地保团的实弹演习，在傍晚时分持续了一个多小时。射击声大部分时间都很密集，引起了相当大的关注。

此前上海北部保团的行动，如挖掘战壕和步枪掩体、建造机枪阵地以及堆放沙袋，都是悄悄进行的，大多在天黑之后，因此很少引起人们对其目的的猜测。保团成员出现在附近本身并不明显，因为这些人大都身着便服。

尽管行动谨慎，但由于造谣者的阴谋诡计，逃离潮一直并且仍然非常巨大。对运输的需求如此之大，以至于费率飙升，在许多情况下收取的费用是平常的数倍。一些较小的搬家公司现在日夜将卡车停在街上。一辆货车出现在小街或弄堂里，会在邻居中造成一种不安全感，投机商的代理人很快利用这一事实，诱使其他人也搬家。这种挨家挨户的工作……

房租飙升

恐慌的程度进一步反映在目前被索取的租金上。在大多数情况下，这些租金比恐慌发生前高出30%至50%。半空的联排房屋一夜之间被填满，寄宿公寓的阁楼也挤满了人。房东和业主通常坚持预收租金，有时甚至预收数月，此外还向焦虑的新租户索取“顶费”。这种盘剥行为通常由苏州河以南的公共租界以及法租界的行家所为。据说最肆无忌惮的投机行为发生在法租界，那里充斥着简陋的中式住所。

一些难民来自沪淞铁路和沪宁铁路沿线的站点，奇怪的是，观察到有人乘坐后者抵达的同时，也有同样多的人离开前往该铁路沿线的站点。内河航运领域也存在类似情况，许多家庭从较近的长江港口抵达，而另一些人则出发前往相同的地方。

迄今为止，上海北部地区的日本居民只有少量撤离，且官方未向日本臣民发布建议其离开的通告。自发现失踪水兵宫崎以来，日本海军陆战队一直保持极为克制的态度。仅进行了最低限度的操练，没有大规模演习。哨兵和巡逻队不戴钢盔，只戴热带盔和布帽。陆战队成员像平时一样自由获准休假。昨天下午，在江湾路兵营前出现的坦克、装甲车、卡车和其他机动装备的“列队”，只是例行公事，目的是从大楼前的油泵处加注汽油。

无食品投机行为

根据租界工务局卫生处的官方消息，有关租界市场食品价格上涨的报道纯属子虚乌有。昨日对所有主要的市政市场和私人市场进行检查后发现，除因……而未运抵的日本鱼外，各类食品供应充足。中国鲜鱼和咸鱼、蔬菜、水果、鸡蛋以及各种肉类的供应都很充足，价格也没有上涨。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, August 7 1937 23516

Big Chapei Exodus Largely
Due To Mob Psychology, Many
Have No Good Reason To Flee

Rumors Fly, Residents Seek Refuge In South
Foreign Areas; Eight Out Of Ten Households
Move Out; Many Remember 1932 Conflict

Endless Stream Flows Across Bridges

MOB psychology is playing an important part in the present exodus from the Chapei and other northern areas. The majority of the people who moved out today into the Settlement and Concession was of the poorer and illiterate class whose action was based on rumors and gossip rather than on sane judgment of the situation.

Most of them, who had learned a costly lesson during the local Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1932 when most of their worldly possessions were either lost or destroyed, started the new stampede when they saw Japanese bluejackets in Chapei after the disappearance of Miyazaki. When fresh war rumors pervaded the city even the stalwarts who had stood their ground joined in the flight.

Biggest Since 1932

The heavy exodus of the last few days is the biggest since the local hostilities in 1932. The stampede on the afternoon of January 27, 1932, was being re-enacted last night and this morning. Along North Szechuen Road, North Honan Road, Boundary Road, and North Chekiang Road, a continual stream of people, motor vans, rickshas, hand-trucks, and wheel-barrows poured into the Settlement and the Concession, just as five and a half years ago.

At some points in the districts north of Soochow Creek streets were so congested that normal traffic couldn't be maintained and people and vehicles had to wait several minutes before moving on and then only at a snail's pace. The streets most heavily taxed were North Szechuen Road, North Honan Road, Boundary Road, North Chekiang Road, Peking Road, and Yu Ya Ching Road.

Factories Move

NOT only private families moved into the settlements but factories and schools evacuated the Chapei area also. The National Chinan University in Chenju near the government radio station has officially ordered the students to evacuate and Fuh Tan University in Kiangwan has also likewise moved most of the school's property to its middle school at Siccawei. The City Government offices were, however, open as usual.

A survey of the situation in Chapei revealed that most of the houses and shops in the district are locked up and while many houses were still occupied all valuables and most of the furniture and personal effects have already been moved into the Settlement and the Concession. According to the shop-keepers in the district, "eight out of ten households have moved out of Chapei."

Swayed By Rumor

That most of the people who joined in the big stampede are totally ignorant of the situation and are swayed by gossip and rumors was revealed when several of them were interviewed by an Evening Post reporter. A typical case was that of an owner of a tailor shop who said that he is moving out because everybody else is moving. Asked if he had read any bad news in the papers he told the reporter that he doesn't read papers and he doesn't believe in newspapers, anyway. When the air is thick with war news and rumors he has to do something to save what he has before it's too late, he said.

The tailor stood a loss of over $1000 in 1932 when Chapei was demolished. In the present case he should have moved out long ago but he hoped for a better turn of events. But he moved his belongings last night. He was moving to a relative's home in the French Concession.

Leave By Ship

THERE are many who are taking steamers to Ningpo and other ports with their belongings while many others are leaving Shanghai by train for their native homes in Kiangsu and Chekiang. Several poor people with a bundle or two who haven't any place to go were sitting on the pavement on the Bund today without knowing what to do. The scenes last night resembled those of 1932 in more ways than one.

Most of the refugees did not know what to make of the situation. They neither advocated war or oppose it. They are so preoccupied with their own problems that they know nothing of national affairs. The instinct of self-preservation and the costly lesson they learned in 1932 cause them to evacuate the area which, in case of war in Shanghai, will again be the central stage of conflict between Chinese and Japanese.

With the exodus in full swing, sub-tenants are reaping big profits. Rents has greatly increased in the Settlement and the Concession. People anxious to find rooms have eagerly looking for "to let" signs throughout the day.
page_data.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年8月7日，星期六 23516

闸北大逃离主要
源于群体心理，许多人
并无充分理由逃亡

谣言纷飞，居民寻求
避难于南部外籍人居住区；
十户中有八户搬离；
许多人忆起1932年冲突

人流无尽穿过桥梁

群体心理在当前的闸北及其他北部地区逃离潮中起着重要作用。今日搬入租界和法租界的大多数人属于贫困且未受教育的阶层，他们的行动基于谣言和闲话，而非对局势的理性判断。

他们中的大多数人曾在1932年当地中日敌对行动中吸取了惨痛教训，当时他们的大部分财产要么丢失要么被毁，因此在宫崎失踪后看到闸北出现日本水兵时，便开始了新的恐慌性逃窜。当新的战争谣言弥漫全城时，即使是那些曾坚守阵地的坚定分子也加入了逃亡行列。

1932年以来规模最大

过去几天的严重逃离潮是自1932年当地敌对行动以来规模最大的一次。1932年1月27日下午的恐慌性逃窜情景昨晚和今晨正在重演。沿着北四川路、北河南路、界路（今天目东路）和北浙江路，人流、汽车货车、人力车、手推车和独轮车源源不断地涌入租界和法租界，正如五年半前那样。

在苏州河以北地区的一些路段，街道拥堵不堪，正常交通无法维持，人和车辆必须等待几分钟才能移动，而且只能以蜗牛般的速度前行。交通压力最大的街道是北四川路、北河南路、界路、北浙江路、北京路和虞洽卿路。

工厂搬迁

不仅私人家庭搬入租界，工厂和学校也从闸北地区撤离。位于政府电台附近陈家的国立暨南大学已正式命令学生撤离，位于江湾的复旦大学也已将学校的大部分财产迁至其位于徐家汇的中学。然而，市政府各部门照常办公。

对闸北局势的调查显示，该地区的大部分房屋和店铺都已锁门，虽然许多房屋仍有人居住，但所有贵重物品以及大部分家具和个人物品已被搬入租界和法租界。据该地区店主称，“十户中有八户已搬离闸北。”

受谣言左右

《晚邮报》记者采访了几位参与大恐慌性逃窜的人，揭示出他们对局势完全无知，受闲话和谣言左右。一个典型的案例是一位裁缝店老板，他说他搬走是因为其他人都在搬。当被问及是否在报纸上看到任何坏消息时，他告诉记者他不看报纸，而且反正他也不相信报纸。他说，当空气中弥漫着战争新闻和谣言时，他必须做点什么来挽救自己的财产，以免为时已晚。

这位裁缝在1932年闸北被毁时损失了超过1000美元。在目前的情况下，他本应早就搬走，但他希望局势会有好转。但他昨晚还是搬走了他的财物。他正搬往法租界的一位亲戚家。

乘船离开

有许多人带着财物乘轮船前往宁波和其他港口，而另许多人则乘火车离开上海，返回江苏和浙江的老家。今天，几个带着一两个包裹、无处可去的穷人坐在外滩的人行道上，不知所措。昨晚的景象在许多方面都让人联想到1932年。

大多数难民不知道该如何看待局势。他们既不主张战争，也不反对战争。他们如此专注于自己的问题，以至于对国家事务一无所知。自我保护的本能以及他们在1932年吸取的惨痛教训，促使他们撤离该地区，因为如果上海爆发战争，这里将再次成为中日冲突的中心舞台。

随着逃离潮的全面展开，二房东们正在赚取巨额利润。租界和法租界的租金大幅上涨。急于寻找房间的人们整天急切地寻找“出租”标志。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, August 7, 1937

More Refugees
Leaving Chapei
For Settlement

More Than 30,000 Pass
Across All Bridges
In 24 Hours

THOUSANDS FLOCK
ON BOARD SHIPS

Gangs Seizing Chance
To Victimize Many
Chapei Refugees

More than 30,000 refugees were counted entering the Settlement at various checking points within the past 24 hours, most of them bringing along all their possessions and indicating that they intended to remain for a while. Shopkeepers who in the past week or two had merely sent out the major part of their stock are now giving up their shops completely, bringing shelves, counters and other equipment along with them.

Indicating that Hongkew residents had other things on their minds than music, the only persons present at the band concert which was to have been held last Thursday night were two park attendants and two policemen assigned there for duty. The concert was cancelled.

Garden Bridge Crowded
Traffic continues heaviest over Garden Bridge, some 10,000 refugees having passed over this bridge yesterday. Most of them are headed for the French Concession and the most direct route is via this bridge. Cheaper housing accommodations are more plentiful in the Concession and the people also feel certain that no Japanese soldiers will be permitted to enter this area.

But not all refugees are satisfied to remain in the Shanghai area, some insisting on returning to their native districts by railway and steamer. One vessel is said to have been delayed more than 24 hours in sailing when 2000 refugees flocked on board although there were accommodations for only 500. The captain of another vessel which has Ichang for its destination had to request police assistance in keeping mobs of refugees from boarding his vessel which was tied up at the Old Nansao Wharf.

Racketeers Busy
Loafer elements have already started to take advantage of the misfortunes of their countrymen who feel themselves obliged to leave their homes in Chapei and northern areas. It is known that numerous refugees have lost part or all of their possessions to gangs operating carting service. Unless they accompany the carts, the refugees can never be sure that their goods will reach the address given to the carters.

The Japanese Naval Landing Party is said to have stopped sending patrols through the streets of Hongkew in order not to aggravate the situation. It is also reported that military exercises are being kept down to a minimum. In both Chapei and Nantao the police force has been augmented in order to cope with petty thievery and extortion which have a tendency to increase troubled times. Rumor mongers are also being hunted down.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年8月7日，星期六

更多难民
离开闸北
前往安置

24小时内
逾三万人通过
所有桥梁

数千人蜂拥
登上轮船

帮派趁机
侵害众多
闸北难民

在过去24小时内，在各检查点统计进入租界的难民超过30,000人，其中大多数人携带了全部家当，表明他们打算暂时停留。过去一两周仅将大部分存货运出的店主们，现在则完全放弃店铺，将货架、柜台和其他设备一并带走。

虹口居民的心思已不在音乐上，上周四晚原定举行的乐队音乐会，到场者仅有两名公园管理员和两名被派往该处执勤的警察。音乐会被取消。

外白渡桥拥挤
交通流量在外白渡桥依然最大，昨天约有10,000名难民通过此桥。他们大多前往法租界，而经由该桥是最直接的路线。法租界内较便宜的住房更为充足，而且人们也确信日本士兵不会被允许进入该区域。

但并非所有难民都满意留在上海地区，有些人坚持乘火车和轮船返回原籍。据说，当2,000名难民蜂拥登上一艘仅能容纳500人的船只时，该船的启航时间延误了24小时以上。另一艘目的地为宜昌的船只船长，不得不请求警方协助，以阻止成群的难民登上停靠在老南市码头的船只。

流氓滋事
游手好闲之徒已开始利用同胞的不幸，这些人感到被迫离开闸北及北部地区的家园。据悉，许多难民的部分或全部财物被经营搬运服务的帮派夺走。除非难民随车同行，否则他们无法确保货物能送达向搬运工指定的地址。

据称，日本海军陆战队已停止在虹口街道派遣巡逻队，以免加剧局势。另有报道说，军事演习已减至最低限度。在闸北和南市，警力均已增派，以应对在动荡时期倾向于增加的 petty thievery（小规模盗窃）和勒索行为。散布谣言者也在被追查中。

More Provincial
Leaders Leaving
For the Capital

Szechuen, Yunnan Chairmen
to Join Parleys

TWO GENERALS FLYING
BACK FROM U.S.A.

Chengtu, Aug. 5.
General Liu Hsiang, Chairman of
the Szechuen Provincial Government
and Pacification Commissioner for
Szechuen and Sikong, will fly to
Nanking on Aug. 9 in company with
General Lung Yun, Chairman of the
Yunnan Provincial Government, who
is expected to arrive here on Aug. 8.
While in Nanking General Liu, it
is understood, will make a report to
General Chiang Kai-shek on military
affairs in Szechuen and Sikong and
seek instructions from the latter re-
garding the current situation.
Much significance is being attached
to the imminent departure of Gen-
erals Liu and Lung for Nanking,
where many important conferences
have been held recently between the
Central authorities and many pro-
minent military leaders from other
parts of the country, including Gen-
eral Han Fu-chu, Chairman of Shan-
tung, General Yen Hsi-shan, Pacifica-
tion Commissioner for Shansi and
Suiyuan, General Ho Chien, Chair-
man of Hunan, General Yu Han-mou,
Pacification Commissioner for
Kwangtung, and General Pai Chung-
hsi, Deputy Commander-in-Chief of
the 5th Route Army.—Central News.

Fly From America

Manila, Aug. 5.
Continuing their dash back to
China in order to offer their services
to Nanking, two Chinese generals,
who crossed the Pacific in a Clipper
flying-boat, hopped off from here
this morning for Hongkong.
They are Major-General Wen
Ying-hsiang, former Commissioner of
the Public Safety Bureau in Shang-
hai, and General Hsiao Cheng-ying,
former Mayor of Tientsin, both of
whom decided to cut short their stay
in the United States as a result of
the North China crisis.
They were entertained to a dinner
last night by the Chinese Consul-
General here.
General Wen left China a few
months ago as one of the military
attaches connected with the Chinese
delegation to the Coronation of King
George.—Reuter.

更多省级
领袖离境
前往首都

四川、云南省主席
将参加会谈

两位将军
从美国飞回

成都，8月5日电。
四川省政府主席兼川康绥靖主任刘湘将军，将于8月9日飞往南京，同行的还有云南省政府主席龙云将军，预计龙云将于8月8日抵达此处。据悉，刘将军在南京期间，将就四川和西康的军事事务向蒋介石将军汇报，并就当前局势向后者的寻求指示。
刘、龙两位将军即将启程前往南京一事备受重视，近期中央当局与来自全国各地的许多著名军事领袖在南京举行了多次重要会议，其中包括山东省主席韩复榘将军、晋绥绥靖主任阎锡山将军、湖南省主席何键将军、广东绥靖主任余汉谋将军，以及第五路军副总司令白崇禧将军。——中央通讯社。

从美国起飞

马尼拉，8月5日电。
为了回国效力于南京政府，两位中国将军继续其匆忙返华之旅。他们乘坐泛美航空的“剪水鹱”式水上飞机跨越太平洋，今晨从这里起飞前往香港。
他们是前上海公安局局长温应星少将和前天津市市长萧振瀛将军，两人均因华北危机决定缩短在美国的停留时间。
昨晚，中国驻当地总领事设宴款待了他们。
温将军于几个月前离开中国，当时他是出席英王乔治加冕典礼的中国代表团中的武官之一。——路透社。

S. I.
OR
C G
6/8

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, AUGUST 6, 1937

OBJECTS TO U. S. FLIERS
* * * * * * * *
Japan To Protest To Washington Against
Yankee Airmen Joining China War Cause
* * * * * * * *
TOKYO, Aug. 5.—(Domei).—
Formal representations against the
reported plans of crack American
aviators to join the Chinese air
force will shortly be made to the
United States Government, Domei
learned today from authoritative
sources.

The demarche will call the atten-
tion of the American Government
to the unfavorable effect which such
plans, if materialized, would have
on the existing friendly relations
between Japan and the United
States.

Such project, Domei was informed
by Gaimusho officials, would not
only run counter to the American
representation made some time
ago for a peaceful settlement of
the North China incident, but would
also contravene the spirit of the
Neutrality Act.

Mr. Yakichiro Suma, Counsellor
of the Japanese Embassy in Wa-
shington, has already, according to
press reports, called on Mr. Stanley
Hornbeck, Chief of the Far Eastern
Affairs Division of the State De-
partment, to call the American
Government's attention to the
matter.

All metropolitan newspapers to-
day featured a report from Los
Angeles that Mr. Russell Hearn,
once an adviser to the late Mar-
shal Chang Tso-lin, Manchurian
warlord, is planning to organize a
party of 182 American pilots for
action in China.

The pilots, the report said, will
each be accompanied by a plane or
two, and would, on their arrival
in China, take charge of the Cen-
tral Government's air arm.

The papers recalled that during
the Shanghai hostilities of 1932 an
American aviator took part in mili-
tary engagements on the Chinese
side, "thus stimulating Japanese
sentiment".

S
DR

《大美晚报》，1937年8月6日，星期五

反对美国飞行员
* * * * * * * *
日本将就美国飞行员加入中国战事向华盛顿提出抗议
* * * * * * * *
东京，8月5日电。（同盟社）。——同盟社今日从权威渠道获悉，日本将不久就据报道的美国优秀飞行员计划加入中国空军一事，向美国政府提出正式交涉。

此次外交行动将提请美国政府注意，如果此类计划成为现实，将对日美之间现有的友好关系产生不利影响。

据外务省官员告知同盟社，此类计划不仅违背美国此前为和平解决华北事件所作出的表态，也将违反《中立法》的精神。

据新闻报道，日本驻华盛顿大使馆参赞须磨弥吉郎先生已经拜访了美国国务院远东事务司司长斯坦利·霍恩贝克先生，提请美国政府注意此事。

今天，各大都市报纸均重点报道了一则来自洛杉矶的消息，称曾任满洲军阀张作霖元帅顾问的拉塞尔·赫恩（Russell Hearn）先生，正计划组织一支由182名美国飞行员组成的队伍赴华参战。

报道称，每位飞行员将配备一两架飞机，抵达中国后，他们将接管中央政府的空军部队。

报纸回顾称，在1932年的上海战事中，曾有一名美国飞行员参与了中国方面的军事行动，“从而刺激了日本人的情绪”。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, AUGUST 6, 1937
50,000 Flock Into
Concessions From
Suburban Districts
Exodus From Northern Areas Reaches New
Peak Yesterday; Hongkew Pawnshops
Move Valuables To Frenchtown;
Yangtzepooi tes Departing

The population of the International Settlement south of Soochow Creek and the French Concession has increased by approximately 50,000 men, women and children during the past two days as a result of the heavy exodus from Chapei, Hongkew, Woosung, Kiangwan and even railway stations all along the line between here and Nanking, according to police estimate.

Featuring the exodus yesterday was the removal of all valuable jewelry by the pawnshops in Hongkew and Chapei into the areas across the creek and into the French Concession.

The flight of pawnshop diamonds, gold ornaments, watches and other valuable articles followed the action of the guild in advising all its members to take necessary precautions against the outbreak of Sino-Japanese trouble in Shanghai.

By nightfall yesterday, stores along the city's pawnshop row on Woosung Road had removed practically all their more precious valuables. Similar action was taken by pawnbrokers having shops in Chapei and other parts of Hongkew.

The removal of jewelry, however, is not likely to affect the regular transaction of pawnshop business in the two areas. Proprietors stated that their stores will remain open.

All day yesterday, with their household belongings piled high on trucks, wheelbarrows, ricshas, in the back seats of taxis and on hand carts, about 30,000 panic-stricken people crowded all roads leading into the Settlement from northern Chinese controlled areas throughout the day. Every bridge, every street was literally a continued traffic jam.

The Shanghai Municipal Police found it necessary to strengthen their traffic forces at all important street intersections and on Garden and Szechuen Road bridges. At the latter two points, traffic was next to impassable most of the day. Police on duty worked in shifts of four hours on and four hours off and when sundown arrived and the stream of movers commenced to thin out, every traffic officer was dog-tired.

Heaviest On Garden Bridge

Traffic was heaviest on Garden Road Bridge for the simple reason that the residents of the Yulin, Yangtzepoo, Wayside and Baikal Road districts joined in the exodus yesterday in a most determined manner. Broadway as far east as Muirhead Road was a mass of moving vehicles, headed west and loaded with household belongings.

In view of the present crop of rumors, there is little or no likelihood that there will be a slackening of the exodus today. Police officials expect it to become even worse, if anything.

Many of the families whose belongings were transported south of the creek yesterday are not residents of the Greater Shanghai area but are refugees from the interior who have been living in the suburban districts for some time. Thousands were forced to sleep out in the open.

Hongkew Population Gains

One of the strangest sights to be seen yesterday was in the Hongkew District itself. Houses vacated several days ago by Hongkew residents were filling up with yesterday's swarm of "war fever" victims. If a check could have been made last night, Hongkew's population would possibly have shown an increase rather than a decrease over its figure for two or three weeks ago.

the smaller landlords to hike rentals to as much as the traffic will bear.

Hotel and small lodging house owners have hiked their rates from 10 to 30 per cent. Sleeping space in hallways and corridors is being charged for at former room prices while room rents have doubled in some cases. Empty houses that could not be rented at any price during normal times are being let at exorbitant rates and terms are cash in advance.

Transport Companies Profit

The landlords are not the only ones reaping a harvest from the "war fever." Transportation companies, and ricsha, handcart and wheelbarrow coolies are also doing rather well for themselves.

Back of all this consternation, profiteering and unrest is a large crop of wild rumors, chief of which is a report that actual hostilities will commence in this area not later than August 8.

Visibly showing signs of a rough and uncomfortable passage down-river, 53 Japanese women and children who evacuated Yangtse ports arrived here yesterday noon in the s.s. Loyang Maru. The majority of these refugees are scheduled to sail for Japan in the s.s. Shanghai Maru at noon today.

These Japanese evacuated Chungking, Hankow and Wuhu.

For the past two days, the North Station has presented an unusual picture to the observer who could not find a spot in which he could stand still long enough without being jostled about to look at it. Special schedules are being run both on the Shanghai-Nanking and Shanghai-Hangchow lines and both incoming and outgoing trains are crowded.

Many Going To Interior

Shanghai Chinese are leaving for the interior with their luggage and bundles of clothing, apparently anxious to get far away from possible hostilities in this area. Chinese from the interior are coming to Shanghai to seek the safety of the Settlement and the Concession.

After the arrival of each train, luggage is piled high on the crowded station platform. More than 30,000 pieces were handled yesterday. After considerable time, it is eventually sorted out and loaded into ricshas, trucks and other conveyance for transportation to the Settlement.

Since the beginning of the exodus almost two weeks ago, it is estimated that more than 100,000 persons have entered the Settlement and Concession to establish temporary homes.

It is further calculated that approximately 20,000 residents of the city have departed by boat for river or coastal ports.

As a result of the increased number joining the trek to the Settlement and Concession, a serious housing problem has arisen. Every hotel and lodging house in both areas were packed two days ago and the thousands who crossed the boundaries yesterday were more or less up against it when it came to finding immediate shelter for the night.

《字林西报》，1937年8月6日，星期五
五万人从郊区涌入
租界
昨日北部地区外逃人数达到新
高峰；虹口当铺将贵重物品
转移至法租界；杨树浦居民
正在撤离

据警方估计，由于闸北、虹口、吴淞、江湾以及甚至从本地到南京沿线各火车站的大量人口外逃，在过去两天内，苏州河以南的国际公共租界及法租界的人口增加了约五万名男女老幼。

昨日外逃潮的一个显著特征是，虹口和闸北的所有当铺将其全部贵重珠宝转移至苏州河对岸地区及法租界。

当铺钻石、金饰、手表及其他贵重物品的转移，是继同业公会建议其所有成员采取必要预防措施以应对上海中日冲突爆发之后的行动。

截至昨晚夜幕降临，位于吴淞路本市“当铺街”沿线的店铺已几乎搬走了其所有更珍贵的财物。在闸北及虹口其他地区设有店铺的典当商也采取了类似行动。

然而，珠宝的转移不太可能影响这两个地区当铺业务的正常交易。店主们表示，他们的店铺将继续营业。

昨天一整天，约有3万名惊恐万状的人们，将家当高高堆在卡车、手推车、人力车、出租车后座以及独轮车上，整天拥挤在从中国控制区北部通往租界的各条道路上。每一座桥、每一条街道实际上都持续处于交通堵塞状态。

上海公共租界工部局警务处发现有必要在所有主要街道交叉口以及花园路和四川路桥加强交通警力。在后两个地点，全天大部分时间交通几乎无法通行。执勤警察实行四小时一班、轮换休息的制度，当日落时分搬迁人流开始稀疏时，每位交通警员都已精疲力竭。

花园桥最为拥堵

花园路桥的交通最为拥堵，原因很简单，因为玉林、杨树浦、韦斯特（Wayside，音译）和贝加尔路（Baikal Road，音译）地区的居民昨天以最坚决的方式加入了外逃行列。百老汇路向东直至缪尔黑德路（Muirhead Road，音译）挤满了向西行驶、装载着家当的移动车辆。

鉴于目前谣言四起，今天的外逃潮几乎没有或完全不可能减缓。警方官员预计，情况甚至可能变得更糟。

昨天其家当被运往苏州河以南的许多家庭并非大上海地区的居民，而是来自内地、已在郊区居住一段时间的难民。数千人被迫露宿户外。

虹口人口增加

昨天所见最奇特的景象之一出现在虹口区本身。几天前被虹口居民腾空房屋，昨天又住满了这群“战争恐慌”的受害者。如果昨晚能进行统计，虹口的人口数量相比两三个星期前可能显示为增加而非减少。

小房东们趁机将租金提高到市场所能承受的最高限度。

旅馆和小客栈老板已将房价提高了10%至30%。走廊和过道上的睡眠空间按以前的房间价格收费，而在某些情况下，房间租金翻了一番。在正常时期以任何价格都租不出去的空房，现在正以高昂的价格出租，且条件要求预付现金。

运输公司获利

并非只有房东从“战争恐慌”中收割利益。运输公司，以及人力车、独轮车和手推车苦力们也从中获益颇丰。

在这种惊慌、牟利和动荡的背后，是大量荒诞不经的谣言，其中主要的一则是报告称，实际敌对行动将于不晚于8月8日在本地区开始。

53名从长江港口撤离的日本妇女和儿童昨天中午乘坐“洛阳丸”号轮船抵达此处， visibly showing signs of a rough and uncomfortable passage down-river（明显显示出沿江而下旅途艰难不适的迹象）。这些难民中的大多数人计划于今天中午乘坐“上海丸”号轮船前往日本。

这些日本人是从重庆、汉口和芜湖撤离的。

在过去两天里，北站向观察者呈现出一幅不寻常的景象，观察者甚至找不到一个能站稳足够长时间而不被推搡的地方来观看这一景象。沪宁线和沪杭线均开行特别班次，进出列车均拥挤不堪。

许多人前往内地

上海华人正带着行李和成捆的衣物离开前往内地，显然急于远离本地区可能发生的敌对行动。而来自内地的华人则来到上海，寻求租界和法租界的安全庇护。

每列火车到达后，行李便高高堆在拥挤的站台上。昨天处理的行李超过3万件。经过相当长的时间，这些行李最终被分拣出来，装上人力车、卡车和其他交通工具，运往租界。

自近两周前外逃潮开始以来，估计已有超过10万人进入租界和法租界建立临时住所。

另据统计，约有2万名本市居民乘船前往沿江或沿海港口。

由于加入前往租界和法租界迁徙队伍的人数增加，出现了严重的住房问题。两天前，两个区域内的每家旅馆和客栈都已客满，昨天越过边界的那数千人在寻找当晚即时栖身之所时，或多或少都陷入了困境。

他们占据了有顶棚的弄堂、侧街以及已空置了一段时间的建筑群

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, AUGUST 6, 1937

CHAPEI EXODUS
The flight of Chinese residents from
Chapei has become much accelerated
during the past two days and the number
of refugees now in the settlement is very
considerable. The reason for this exodus
appears to be the rumour that there is
likely to be some fighting between the
Chinese and Japanese in the Chapei-
Kiangwan area in the near future. It
seems to us that any such clash can be
easily avoided if both the Chinese and
Japanese authorities sincerely desire it
and to the best of our knowledge they do.
Of course, there has been the usual crop
of foolish rumours which has tended to
increase the nervousness on both sides
and at least some of which have been put
round by persons hoping to derive some
benefit thereby. We feel that there
should be an understanding between the
Greater Shanghai City Government and
the Japanese civil and military authorities
that no conflict of any kind shall be start-
ed in the vicinity of this international
port and a very definite assurance on this
point given to the public. If that were
done, Shanghai would be spared a great
deal of anxiety and upset, the cost of
which falls so heavily on the poorer class
of Chinese. A plan to establish a number
of refugee camps in Shanghai has been
already decided upon and to-morrow
there will be a big meeting of Chinese
organizations to discuss the latest
developments in the situation and take
whatever measures may be deemed necess-
ary. But the point we would unfailingly
emphasize is that it is up to the public
authorities to ensure the public peace and
we are convinced that this is not imposs-
ible if the proper measures are taken in
time.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年8月6日，星期五

闸北外逃
过去两天，中国居民从闸北的逃离速度大大加快，目前租界内的难民数量相当庞大。此次外逃的原因似乎是谣传近期闸北-江湾地区可能发生中日战斗。在我们看来，如果中日当局真诚希望避免，任何此类冲突都很容易避免，而且据我们所知，他们确实有此意愿。当然，通常会出现一堆愚蠢的谣言，这往往加剧双方的紧张情绪，其中至少有一部分是由希望从中获利的人散布的。我们认为，大上海市政府与日本文武当局之间应达成谅解，即不在本国际港口附近发动任何形式的冲突，并向公众就此点给予非常明确的保证。如果做到这一点，上海将免除大量的焦虑和动荡，而这些代价沉重地落在中国较贫困阶层身上。在上海建立若干难民收容所的计划已经确定，明天将举行一次大型的中国组织会议，讨论局势的最新发展并采取任何被认为必要的措施。但我们要坚定不移强调的一点是，确保公共和平是公共当局的责任，我们相信，如果及时采取适当措施，这并非不可能。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, AUGUST 6, 1937
MR. HIROTA REVIVES ONE
OF "THREE POINTS"
Believes Co-operation Between China and Japan is
"Not Impossible" Against Communism
ARMED FORCE NOT ENOUGH IN IMPASSE
Disposition of 207,000 Chinese Troops Announced in
Communique of Tokyo War Office

Tokyo, Aug. 5.
REVIVING one of the three principles of his famous "Three-Point Programme", the Foreign Minister, Mr. Koki Hirota, to-day told the Diet that "the major point of our proposals to China consists of co-operation in joint defence against Communism". At least in this respect, he added, co-operation between the two nations is "not impossible."
The other two points of Mr. Hirota's programme, formulated in the Autumn of 1935 in collaboration with the Army, were suppression of the anti-Japanese movement in China and joint economic development of North China by China, Japan and Manchoukuo.
"I do not believe", the Foreign Minister told the Diet, "that the present Sino-Japanese impasse can be broken by armed force alone."

Side by side with military operations in North China, the Japanese Government is conducting diplomatic negotiations with Nanking to secure the latter's reconsideration of its stand, he added.
The Japanese Government, Mr. Hirota declared, wants to settle the North China incident on the spot, and "at the same time, effect a fundamental readjustment of the whole range of Sino-Japanese relations."
"Anti-Japanese sentiment in China", the Foreign Minister said, "is deeply rooted, and, therefore, it should be difficult to eradicate it. "But I believe that Sino-Japanese co-operation is possible if the radical elements, and especially the Communists, are effectively controlled."

Chinese Troop Movements
Continued converging of the Central Government's troops upon the Peiping-Tientsin area was reported to-day to the War Office. Chinese troops, the reports said, were advancing along the Tientsin-Pukow, Peiping-Hankow and Peiping-Suiyuan Railways.
The Japanese air force in North China, the reports said, has bombed several Chinese troops trains in Charhar and near Paotingfu in the past two days.
Commenting on the disposition of the Chinese troops, military observers here declared General Chiang Kai-shek is apparently striving to keep the Central Government's infantry and air force intact.
The troops placed in the first line of defence, they said, are those commanded by provincial war-lords or the Communist forces brought from the north-west.
General Chiang's "own" troops, it was pointed out, are held in the second line of defence, where they will not be directly involved in major hostilities should such break out.

40,000 Men
The troops massed along the Tientsin-Pukow Railway were reported to number 40,000 men, comprising the 25th Division and the 139th Division.

29th Army Reduced
The strength of the 29th Army, now having its positions at Machang, was reported to have been reduced from 80,000 to 20,000 men.
Badly battered in clashes at Nanyuan and Langfang, the units of the 37th and the 38th Divisions, which bore the brunt of the fighting, were said to be "tired and discouraged."

North of Yellow River
Military intelligence reports received here gave the following picture of the disposition of Chinese troops north of the Yellow River.
In Charhar.—Lieutenant-General Liu Ju-ming's 143rd Division, numbering about 15,000 men, stationed in the vicinity of Kalgan.
Between Hualai and Hsuanhua, on the Peiping-Suiyuan Railway, about 20,000 men belonging to the 84th and 85th Divisions, commanded respectively by Generals Kao Kwei-tzu and Wang Chu-lien.
In Hopei on the Tientsin-Pukow Railway, 10,000 men of General Chang Tzu-chung's 38th Division, which took part in the Tientsin hostilities on July 29-30.
On the Peiping-Hankow Railway.—20,000 men of General Feng Chih-an's 37th Division and the late General Chao Teng-yu's 132nd Division, stationed in the vicinity of Tingshing, 80 kilometres south of Lukouchiao, where they formerly had their positions.
At Paotingfu.—General Wan Fu-lin's 53rd Army, comprising the 29th, 116th and 130th Divisions and parts of the 10th Infantry and the 16th Cavalry Divisions, numbering in all 30,000 men.
North Honan.—30,000 men at Chengchow and the neighbouring areas, comprising General Sun Lien-chung's 2nd Army; General Sung Che-yuan's 29th Division; General Chi Feng-shan's 32nd Division and the Independent 46th Brigade.

Feverish expansion of aerodromes in Hainan, Shantung, Shuntei, Chochow and Chengting, Hopei, were also reported to be in progress.—Domei.

Army Prepared
Tokyo, Aug. 5.
In the course of a debate on the second supplementary budget in connection with North China, the Minister of War, General Sugiyama, told the Budget Committee of the House of Representatives to-day that it was problematical whether the Japanese troops in North China would be able to continue their present attitude in the Chinese Central Government troops.
The Japanese troops, said the Minister of War, were fully prepared to take "punitive measures" against the Central troops should they take the initiative.
General Sugiyama assured the Committee that the present budget would be enough to cover expenses for the time being, but the Government, he said, would be obliged to convoke an extra session of the Diet to seek approval of another supplementary budget if the situation further worsened.—Reuter.

Tientsin Relaxing
Tientsin, Aug. 4.
Normal conditions are steadily returning here. British auxiliaries were taken off patrol duty to-night, a partial tram service is being resumed to-morrow in the Chinese City, and railway officials are returning to the new administration building. Mail delivery in the Chinese City is also being resumed.
Accompanied by two Japanese and a representative of the Consular Body, M. Smirnoff, the Soviet Consul, to-day visited the Soviet Consulate to inspect the damage caused during the recent raid. Photographs were taken.—Reuter.

Lull In North China
Tokyo, Aug. 5
A comparative lull prevails in North China, but the mopping up of small parties of troops of the 29th Army is continuing, according to messages received here to-day. A Tientsin dispatch says that Japanese planes bombarded two Chinese troop-trains moving towards Peiping along the Peiping-Suiyuan Railway on August 4.
The Okasaki detachment, it adds, came into contact and routed about eighty Chinese troops near Liangsiang at about noon on August 4. No casualties were inflicted on the Japanese, but the Chinese troops are stated to have lost twenty men, thirty rifles and 200 hand-grenades.
The Nara detachment, states the Peiping correspondent of the "Asahi Shimbun," has come into contact with and annihilated 250 East Hopei militiamen believed to have participated in the recent massacre of Japanese and Koreans at Tungchow.

Policy Upheld
At an all-party conference held here to-day, it was decided that a joint resolution be submitted to the House of Representatives to-morrow upholding the Government's North China policy and urging it to seek "a fundamental solution to the China problem." —Reuter.

《字林西报》，1937年8月6日，星期五

广田弘毅重提“三点”中的一点
认为在反共问题上中日合作“并非不可能”
僵局之中仅靠武力尚嫌不足
东京陆军省公报公布20.7万中国军队的部署情况

东京，8月5日电。
外交大臣广田弘毅（Koki Hirota）今日向帝国议会发表讲话，重提其著名的“广田三原则”中的一项原则，称“我们对华提议的重点在于共同防共的合作”。他补充说，至少在这一方面，两国之间的合作是“并非不可能的”。
广田先生的方案中的另外两点，是于1935年秋季与陆军方面共同制定的，即镇压中国的排日运动，以及由中国、日本和满洲国共同开发华北经济。
外交大臣对帝国议会表示：“我不相信目前的日中僵局能单凭武力打破。”

他补充说，日本政府在进行华北军事行动的同时，正与南京进行外交谈判，以促使后者重新考虑其立场。
广田宣称，日本政府希望就地解决华北事件，并“同时，对日中关系的全盘格局进行根本性的调整”。
外交大臣称：“中国的排日情绪根深蒂固，因此难以根除。但我相信，如果能有效控制激进分子，特别是共产党人，中日合作是可能的。”

中国军队调动
据今日向陆军省报告，中央政府军队继续向平津地区集结。报告称，中国军队正沿津浦铁路、平汉铁路和平绥铁路推进。
报告称，过去两天，日本空军在华北轰炸了察哈尔及保定府附近的数列中国军车。
此间军事观察家评论中国军队部署时称，蒋介石将军显然正努力保持中央政府步兵和空军的完整。
他们说，部署在第一道防线的是由各省军阀指挥的部队或从西北调来的共产党部队。
指出，蒋介石的“嫡系”部队被部署在第二道防线，一旦爆发大规模敌对行动，他们将不会直接卷入。

4万人
据报道，集结在津浦铁路沿线的部队人数为4万人，包括第25师和第139师。

第29军减员
据报道，目前驻马厂的国民革命军第29军兵力已从8万人减至2万人。
据悉，在南苑和廊坊的冲突中遭受重创的第37师和第38师各部队（承担了战斗的主要压力）已“疲惫且士气低落”。

黄河以北
此处收到的军事情报报告提供了黄河以北中国军队部署的如下概况。
在察哈尔：刘汝明中将的第143师，约1.5万人，驻扎在张家口附近。
在北平至绥远铁路上，怀来与宣化之间，约有2万人，分属高桂滋将军和王长海将军分别指挥的第84师和第85师。
在河北津浦铁路上，有张自忠将军第38师的1万人，该部参加了7月29日至30日的天津战事。
在平汉铁路上：冯治安将军的第37师和已故赵登禹将军的第132师共2万人，驻扎在定兴附近，位于卢沟桥以南80公里处，他们此前曾在此驻防。
在保定府：万福麟将军的第53军，包括第29师、第116师和第130师，以及第10步兵师和第16骑兵师的部分部队，总计3万人。
豫北：在郑州及周边地区有3万人，包括孙连仲将军的第2军；宋哲元将军的第29师；吉星文将军的第32师以及独立第46旅。

另据报道，海南、山东、顺德、涿州和河北正定的机场正在加紧扩建。——同盟社

陆军已做好准备
东京，8月5日电。
在今日众议院预算委员会关于华北相关第二次补充预算案的辩论中，陆军大臣杉山元将军告诉委员会，日军在华北能否对中国中央政府军队维持目前的态度，尚成问题。
陆军大臣称，如果中央军采取主动，日军已做好充分准备对其采取“惩罚性措施”。
杉山将军向委员会保证，目前的预算足以支付暂时的开支，但他表示，如果局势进一步恶化，政府将不得不召开帝国议会特别会议，以求批准另一项补充预算案。——路透社

天津局势缓和
天津，8月4日电。
这里的正常秩序正在稳步恢复。英国辅助人员今晚撤出了巡逻任务，华界部分电车服务将于明天恢复，铁路官员正返回新的行政大楼。华界的邮件投递也在恢复中。
苏联领事斯米尔诺夫先生（M. Smirnoff）今天在日本人和领事团代表的陪同下，访问了苏联领事馆，视察最近袭击造成的损坏。现场拍摄了照片。——路透社

华北暂趋平静
东京，8月5日电。
根据今日收到的消息，华北地区相对平静，但仍在继续肃清第29军的小股部队。天津发来的电报称，8月4日，日本飞机轰炸了两列沿平绥铁路向北平移动的中国军车。
电报补充说，8月4日中午左右，冈崎支队在良乡附近与约八十名中国士兵接触并将其击溃。日军无伤亡，据称中国军队损失二十人、三十支步枪和二百枚手榴弹。
《朝日新闻》北平记者称，奈良支队已与被认为参与了近期通州屠杀日本人和朝鲜人的冀东保安队250人接触并将其歼灭。

政策获支持
在今日于此举行的各党派会议上，决定明日向众议院提交一项联合决议，支持政府的华北政策，并敦促其寻求“中国问题的根本解决”。——路透社

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, AUGUST 5, 1937

GEN. TSAI TING-KAI
WELCOMED

Big Canton Turnout for the
Former Shanghai Hero

Canton, Aug. 4.
An extremely warm welcome was accorded General Tsai Ting-kai, former commander of the 19th Route Army, on his arrival here this morning by steamer from Hongkong after many months' absence abroad.
A huge crowd, including General Wu Te-chen, Governor of Kwangtung, General Hsiang Han-ping, Deputy-Commander of the Fourth Route Army, and other officials, thronged the wharf to greet the soldier who became internationally famous for his stand against the Japanese during the Shanghai hostilities in 1932.
During his stay here General Tsai will visit his former subordinates and will call on the local authorities. Later, he is expected to offer his services to Nanking.—Reuter.

Off for Shanghai

After visiting Canton for one day, during which he called on the local military leaders and laid a wreath at the cemetery for soldiers of the 19th Route Army, General Tsai Ting-kai left for Hongkong to-night to catch the Empress of Japan for Shanghai, whence he intends to proceed to Nanking.
Interviewed by Reuter, General Tsai, who is now greyhaired, declared that he had decided to sink all personal differences and fight under a united banner for China should diplomatic exchanges fail and war break out. The Central Government, he added, had already organized its defence policy, and his trip to Nanking was for the purpose of offering his services to the Generalissimo. General Wu Te-chen, Governor of Kwangtung, and the highest military leaders in Canton thronged the smoke-room of the steamer to wish General Tsai bon voyage.—Reuter.

《字林西报》，1937年8月5日，星期四

蔡廷锴将军
受到欢迎

前上海英雄抵穗受到盛大欢迎

广州，8月4日电。
前第十九路军总指挥蔡廷锴将军在出国数月后，今晨乘船从香港抵达此处，受到了极其热烈的欢迎。
包括广东省主席吴铁城将军、第四路军副总司令香翰屏将军及其他官员在内的大量人群涌向码头，迎接这位因在1932年上海战事中抗日而闻名国际的军人。
蔡将军在此停留期间，将探望其旧部，并拜会地方当局。随后，预计他将向南京效力。——路透社

启程前往上海

在广州停留一天期间，蔡廷锴将军拜会了当地军事领导人，并在第十九路军烈士墓敬献花圈，随后今晚离开前往香港，以便搭乘“日本皇后号”轮船前往上海，他打算从那里前往南京。
蔡将军在接受路透社采访时宣称，这位如今已生华发的将军表示，如果外交交涉失败且战争爆发，他已决定放下所有个人分歧，在统一的旗帜下为中国而战。他补充说，中央政府已经制定了防御政策，他此次前往南京的目的是向委员长效力。广东省主席吴铁城将军和广州最高军事领导人挤满了轮船的吸烟室，为蔡将军送行。——路透社

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, AUGUST 5, 1937

General Pai Chung-hsi Confers with Generalissimo:
Nanking Prepares for Emergency

REINFORCEMENTS POUR INTO TIENTSIN

Japanese Continue to Report Concentration by the
Chinese Forces: Evacuation on All Sides

THE eagerly anticipated visit of General Pai Chung-hsi to
Nanking became reality yesterday, when the Kwangsi leader
stepped out of the special plane sent by General Chiang Kai-shek
to convey him to the capital. A Nanking report through Central
News stated that he had conferred with the Generalissimo last
night and it was believed that the North China situation was
discussed.
Reports continue to be received from Japanese sources of
Chinese preparations for defence against an impending Japanese
advance. It is further reported that there is a large concentration
of Chinese troops, Salt Guards, and Paoantui in Shantung province.
Chinese foresee an imminent battle at the Nankow Pass, where
it is said that 4,000 Japanese troops from Peiping and Kupeikou
are massing for an attack on Chinese positions in and around
Kalgan.
Evacuation continues on all sides. Japanese nationals are
leaving all interior Chinese cities; Chinese are removing from
Nanking and big coastal cities to interior points; and a huge exodus
of Chinese from the Chapei area marked yesterday in Shanghai.
Daventry's broadcast yesterday evening stated that London
had received a report that the headquarters of the so-called East
Hopei Autonomous Government had been moved from Tungchow
to Peiping. This was regarded as a sign that the Japanese have
assumed full control over the area.

白崇禧将军与委员长会谈：
南京准备应对紧急情况

援军涌入天津

日军继续报告中国军队集结：各方纷纷撤离

备受期待的白崇禧将军访问南京一事昨日成为现实，这位广西领袖走下了蒋介石将军派来接他前往首都的专机。据中央通讯社南京报道，他昨晚与委员长进行了会谈，据信讨论了华北局势。
来自日本方面的报告继续称，中国正在为抵御日军即将发动的进攻进行防御准备。另有报道称，山东省有大量中国军队、盐务缉私队和保安团集结。
中方预见南口即将发生战斗，据说来自北平和古北口的4000名日军正在集结，准备攻击张家口及其周边的中国阵地。
各方撤离仍在继续。日本侨民正离开中国内地所有城市；中国人正从南京和沿海大城市迁往内陆地区；昨天上海闸北地区出现了大量中国居民外逃的景象。
达文特里（Daventry）昨晚的广播称，伦敦收到报告称，所谓“冀东自治政府”总部已从通州迁至北平。这被视为日军已完全控制该地区的迹象。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, August 5, 1937

Ole Champs At His Bit,
Sniffing War Powder

AN OLD war-horse named Ole Olsson is champing on the
bit and sniffing the powder down Wayside way today.
An adventurer and soldier of fortune in many lands for many
years, he is now enthusiastic about the idea for a mixed
brigade of Swedes, Norwegians, Danes, Finns and Germans to
form the nucleus of a Foreign Legion to fight for Shanghai,
for China, or for anything that's offered.
Mr. Olsson lives at 58 Wayside Road. He is a Swede, and
he started seeing service in the Boer War back in 1899. He
continued to fight, bleed and darn near die until 1902, when
the Dutch and the English declared for peace.
Being a seaman and formerly in the Swedish Navy—that's
how he got to South Africa—it wasn't hard for him to shift
the scene of his activities to the Philippines, where he took
part in the Insurrection from 1904 to 1906, serving in the 7th
Cavalry stationed among the Moros in Mindanao. That
brought him to the Far East, and since then he has travelled
through much of Japan, Korea, Siberia, Manchuria and in-
terior China, mostly by foot-slogging. He has picked up
Chinese, Korean, Japanese, Norwegian, Danish and Spanish
besides his native Swedish and, of course, English.
Very interested in the revived stories of an International
Brigade, rumored to be about to be organized in Shanghai to
join the Chinese Army, Mr. Olsson is now hot for action. He
is particularly approving of Harry "Blackie" Wills of Detroit,
the American bar-tender of Shanghai who joined the Chinese
at Hankow and went north as a machine-gunner. He is also
interested in the rumor of a Russian volunteer detachment.
If there's going to be a war, says he, he wants to be in it.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年8月5日，星期四

奥勒·查普斯跃跃欲试，
嗅到战争火药味

一位名叫奥勒·奥尔森（Ole Olsson）的老兵正按捺不住、跃跃欲试，在韦赛德路（Wayside way）一带嗅到了战争的火药味。作为一名多年来在许多国家闯荡的冒险家和雇佣兵，他现在对组建一支由瑞典人、挪威人、丹麦人、芬兰人和德国人组成的混合旅的想法充满热情，以此作为外籍军团的核心，为上海、为中国、或为任何提供的目标而战。

奥尔森先生住在韦赛德路58号。他是瑞典人，早在1899年的布尔战争中就开始服役。他继续战斗、流血，几乎丧命，直到1902年荷兰人和英国人宣布和平为止。

由于他是一名海员，且曾在瑞典海军服役——这也是他前往南非的原因——他将活动场景转移到菲律宾并非难事。在1904年至1906年间，他参与了那里的起义，在驻扎于棉兰老岛摩洛人地区的第7骑兵团服役。这将他带到了远东，此后他徒步跋涉，游历了日本、朝鲜、西伯利亚、满洲和中国内地的广大地区。除了母语瑞典语和当然的英语之外，他还学会了中文、韩文、日文、挪威语、丹麦语和西班牙语。

奥尔森先生对有关国际旅复兴的故事非常感兴趣，据传该旅即将在上海组建以加入中国军队，他现在渴望行动。他特别赞赏来自底特律的哈里·“布莱基”·威尔斯（Harry "Blackie" Wills），这位上海的美国酒吧侍者已在汉口加入中国军队，并作为机枪手北上。他也对有关俄罗斯志愿分队的传闻感兴趣。他说，如果要有战争，他希望身处其中。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, AUGUST 5, 1937.

CHINESE ASKED TO
OFFER SERVICES

War-Time Preparations by
Public Organizations

ANTI-AIRCRAFT CORPS
ORGANIZED

A call to Chinese residents in
Shanghai for war-time service was
made by the All-Shanghai Associa-
tion for the Support of Armed Resist-
ance, organized by numerous public
bodies Every able-bodied Chinese
has been urged to register with the
Association at the Public Recreation
Ground, Nantao, without delay.
A set of seven measures has been
mapped out by the Association.
Aimed at the concentration of
strength, the measures call for the
organization of nine service corps,
namely, peace and order maintenance,
publicity, engineering, communica-
tions, transportation, first aid, fire-
prevention, burial and contributions-
canvassing.

All those who register with the
Association will be examined as to
their physical fitness. They will then
be enlisted in the corps which best
suit them. One of the rules govern-
ing the enrolment of citizens with
these corps is absolute obedience to
the commander.

In anticipation of Japanese air
raids, an anti-air corps has been
organized under the auspices of local
philanthropic organizations. The first
training class will be held to-day to
impart general anti-air knowledge to
the public.

Elaborate preparations are also
being made by the China First Aid
Association in view of the existing
tension.

According to a message from Nan-
king, Mr. Aw Boon-haw and his
brother had wired the Government,
offering to contribute $30,000 for the
care of wounded soldiers in the
north. The money was reported to
have been sent to the capital.

After two days' sharp rise, gold
prices declined yesterday. Gold
changed hands at $1,330. This drop-
ped to $1,250 when a Chinese bank
sold a large quantity of gold to be
delivered in a week's time. Later,
the price climbed back to $1,330,
which was about $70 to $80 lower
than that quoted the previous day.

The minimum prices fixed by the
Government prevailed in the Chinese
bond market yesterday. The 86
millions improved by about 85 cents.

呼吁华人
提供服务

公共团体的战时准备

组建防空队

由众多公共团体组织的“全上海支援武装抵抗协会”向上海华人居民发出战时服务号召。敦促每一位身体健全的华人立即前往南市公共体育场向该协会登记。

该协会制定了一套七项措施。旨在集中力量，这些措施要求组织九个服务队，即：维持治安、宣传、工程、通讯、运输、急救、防火、殡葬和募捐。

所有向协会登记的人员都将接受体格检查。随后，他们将被编入最适合他们的服务队。公民加入这些服务队的一项规则是绝对服从指挥官。

为防备日本空袭，在当地慈善组织的赞助下组建了一支防空队。今天将举办第一期培训班，向公众传授一般的防空知识。

鉴于目前的紧张局势，中国红十字会也在进行周密的准备。

据来自南京的消息称，胡文虎先生及其兄弟已致电政府，愿捐款3万元用于照顾北方伤兵。据报道，这笔款项已汇往首都。

金价在连续两天大幅上涨后，昨天下跌。黄金交易价格为1,330美元。当一家中国银行出售大量一周后交割的黄金时，价格跌至1,250美元。随后，价格回升至1,330美元，比前一天的报价低约70至80美元。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL C°
S. B. REGIS
No S. R. D. 7994/5
Date 6 8 37

Nanking Express
Brings Crowds

Refugees Flee Capital;
SMPmen Warned,
Say Japanese

When the Nanking Express pulled into Shanghai North Station yesterday afternoon it disgorged a huge crowd of people, foreign and Chinese, who had boarded it at Nanking that morning. The train had been scheduled to leave Nanking at 11 o'clock the night before but delayed all night in the Nanking Station while crowds waited patiently, sleeping on the platform. Two Japanese planes were believed sighted over the city after dawn.

Most of the 2000 Chinese were believed to have left Nanking as refugees, fearing a Japanese attack on the capital. They crowded into third and second class cars and when these were filled overflowed into first class, sleeping in the aisles.

A foreigner aboard the train reported that during the trip down to Shanghai he had sighted many heavily loaded troop trains and armoured trains on sidings and second tracks, some moving toward Nanking but most moving eastward.

Communications

With the exception of radio all communications to Tientsin and Peiping from Shanghai were at a standstill today. Trains still made tsinan the terminal while the C.N.A.C.'s regular service to North China was being maintained only as far as Tsingtao. The firm's plane which left here for the resort yesterday arrived here last night in spite of the storm while a plane left for Tsingtao on schedule this morning.

An Eurasia plane left Hongkong this morning for Taiyuan. According to the local office there is still no feeder service from Taiyuan to Peiping. Telegraphic communications to Tientsin and Peiping was disrupted today and although radio communication is open to the cities, the line was so congested that messages are not guaranteed prompt delivery.

Police Barred

Japanese and foreign members of the Shanghai Municipal Police have been warned against proceeding into Chinese-controlled areas because of possible complications such action might precipitate, Japan sources reported today.

The Council, the Japanese added, disclaims any responsibility for the consequences should any Japanese or foreign police disregard his order.

This warning was apparently issued by the Council...

日方称，已警告
工部局警员

昨天下午，当京沪快车驶入上海北站时，涌出了大量乘客，包括外国人和中国人，他们于当天早上在南京登车。该列车原定于前一天晚上11点离开南京，但在南京车站整夜延误，人群在站台上耐心等候，甚至睡在站台上。黎明后，有人相信在该市上空看到了两架日本飞机。

据信，2000名中国人中的大多数是作为难民离开南京的，他们担心日本会对首都发动攻击。他们挤进三等和二等车厢，当这些车厢满员后，又涌入一等车厢，睡在过道上。

车上的一名外国人报告说，在前往上海的途中，他看到侧线和第二条轨道上停着许多满载的军用列车和装甲列车，有些开往南京，但大多数向东行驶。

通讯

除无线电外，今天上海通往天津和北平的所有通讯均陷入停滞。火车仍以济南为终点站，而中国航空公司的定期华北航线仅维持到青岛。该公司昨天飞往避暑胜地的飞机尽管遭遇风暴，仍于昨晚抵达此处，而今天上午有一架飞机按计划飞往青岛。

一架欧亚航空公司的飞机今天上午从香港飞往太原。据当地办事处称，目前仍没有从太原到北平的支线服务。今天通往天津和北平的电报通讯中断，虽然与这些城市的无线电通讯畅通，但由于线路过于拥堵，无法保证消息及时送达。

警方受阻

据日方消息来源今天报道，上海工部局警务处的日本籍和外籍警员已被警告不要进入华人控制区，因为此类行动可能会引发复杂的局面。

日方补充说，工部局声明，如果有任何日本或外籍警员无视此命令，工部局不对后果承担任何责任。

这一警告显然由工部局发出……

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, AUGUST 3, 1937

FRENCH PROTEST TO
JAPANESE
Incident at Tientsin Bridge
Causes Friction

PARIS PAPERS PLEAD FOR
MODERATION

London, Aug. 2.
A dangerous tension between Japanese and French troops at the international bridge over the Peiho at Tientsin is reported by the papers here. According to despatches received from Tientsin, the Japanese demanded the right to cross the bridge, but this was refused by French troops, who placed tanks into position in order to offer armed resistance if necessary. The tension apparently originated in the alleged cutting off of telephonic communications between the French Concession and the French troops by the Japanese, who are also accused by the French of having fired last week on a group of French soldiers at the East Railway Station, one non-commissioned officer being wounded.
—Trans-Ocean.

French Protest
Paris, Aug. 2.
The French Ambassador in Tokyo has been instructed to lodge a protest with the Japanese government regarding alleged aggressions committed by the Japanese troops in Tientsin against French sentries and also regarding the interruption of telephonic communications between the French Concession and the arsenal.
The papers here add that the French Foreign Minister, M. Delbos, has already got into touch with the Japanese Ambassador, Mr. Sugimura, on this subject.—Trans-Ocean.

Incident Deplored
Paris, Aug. 2.
"The shedding of French blood is a serious occurrence and the Japanese authorities are conscious of it," declares to-day's issue of "Le Petit Journal," extreme rightist paper, concerning the incident at the East Station in Tientsin in which several French soldiers were injured in a clash with Japanese forces. "Such occurrences always happen in troubled periods and end by excuses and reparations."
On the other hand, the communist newspaper, "L'Humanité," affirms, "The criminal attempt against French soldiers at Tientsin is a very serious international incident, and France must do more than protest, as has already been done." The French Government must clearly state its policy concerning the Far East.
If France the Popular Front ought to condemn the aggression of which China is to-day a victim, the journal continues. "It is impossible that a country whose Premier Blum has deposited at Geneva a plan for the reinforcement of the Covenant of the League of Nations should cross its arms when Peking is bombarded and when French troops carrying out an international mission are attacked."

Caution Urged
Paris, Aug. 2.
A very cautious handling of the Far Eastern situation by France is advocated by the Radical Socialist paper "Republique" which at the same time demands that for reasons of foreign policy France must not oppose Japan.
Referring to the Franco-Japanese incident at Tientsin, which led to a French demarche in Tokyo, the paper demands that France should carefully avoid anything detrimental to her prestige in the Far East, since the Asiatic nations despised those losing their "face." The paper points towards the French Indo-Chinese Empire whose 30,000,000 inhabitants were controlled by a handful of soldiers, and hopes that the Tientsin incident will have no repercussions, especially since the French troops in China consisted mainly of Annamites. In settling the incident, the new Japanese Ambassador in Paris could prove that Japanese magnanimity understood French pride.—Trans-Ocean.

Japanese Regrets
Paris, Aug. 2.
According to a despatch from Shanghai, the commander of the Japanese troops in North China, General Katsuki, has expressed his regrets to the commander of the French garrison in Tientsin regarding the recent incident. General Katsuki assured the French commander that the Japanese troops would not interfere with the free communication between the French Concession and the arsenal.—Trans-Ocean.

《字林西报》，1937年8月3日，星期二

法国向日本
提出抗议
天津桥事件
引起摩擦

巴黎报纸呼吁
保持克制

伦敦，8月2日。
据此处报纸报道，在天津海河国际大桥上，日军与法军之间出现了危险的紧张局势。根据从天津收到的电报，日军要求通过桥梁的权利，但遭到法军拒绝，法军部署坦克，以便在必要时进行武装抵抗。这种紧张局势显然源于日军 allegedly 切断了法租界与法军之间的电话通讯，法方还指责日军上周在东火车站向一群法国士兵开枪，导致一名士官受伤。
——跨洋通讯社。

法国抗议
巴黎，8月2日。
驻东京法国大使已奉命就日军在天津 allegedly 对法国哨兵实施的侵略行为，以及法租界与兵工厂之间电话通讯中断一事，向日本政府提出抗议。
此处报纸补充说，法国外交部长德尔博斯先生（M. Delbos）已就此问题与日本大使杉村先生（Mr. Sugimura）取得联系。——跨洋通讯社。

谴责事件
巴黎，8月2日。
极右翼报纸《小日报》（Le Petit Journal）在今日刊文中谈及天津东站事件中几名法国士兵在与日军冲突中受伤一事时宣称：“法国人流血是一起严重事件，日本当局对此心知肚明。”“此类事件总是发生在动荡时期，最终以道歉和赔偿告终。”
另一方面，共产党报纸《人道报》（L'Humanité）断言：“在天津针对法国士兵的犯罪企图是一起非常严重的国际事件，法国必须做得不止于抗议，正如已经做过的那样。”法国政府必须明确阐明其远东政策。
该报继续写道，如果法国人民阵线应当谴责中国今日遭受的侵略，“一个国家，其总理布鲁姆已在日内瓦提交了一份加强国际联盟盟约的计划，却在北京遭受轰炸、执行国际任务的法国部队遭到攻击时袖手旁观，这是不可能的。”

呼吁谨慎
巴黎，8月2日。
激进社会党报纸《共和国报》（Republique）主张法国应非常谨慎地处理远东局势，同时要求出于外交政策原因，法国不得反对日本。
提及导致法国在东京采取外交行动的天津法日事件，该报要求法国仔细避免任何损害其在远东威望的行为，因为亚洲民族鄙视那些丢“面子”的人。该报指出拥有3000万居民、由少数士兵控制的法属印度支那帝国，并希望天津事件不会产生反响，尤其是因为在华法军主要由安南人组成。在解决该事件时，新任驻巴黎日本大使可以证明，日本的慷慨大度理解法国的骄傲。——跨洋通讯社。

日本表示遗憾
巴黎，8月2日。
据来自上海的电报称，华北日军指挥官香月清司将军（General Katsuki）就最近的事件向天津法国驻军指挥官表示了遗憾。香月将军向法国指挥官保证，日军不会干涉法租界与兵工厂之间的自由通讯。——跨洋通讯社。

North China Daily News - Tuesday, August 3, 1937.
22430

CHINESE TROOP MOVES TO
NORTH CONFIRMED

Occupation of Kalgan by Central Forces May Cause
New Complications: Japanese Alert

PEIPING, TIENTSIN NEARLY NORMAL

Reinforcements for Gen. Sung Reach Tsangchow:
Americans in Shantung Warned

FROM OUR OWN CORRESPONDENT

Nanking, Aug. 2.
MANY indications pointing to the possible expansion of Sino-Japanese hostilities reached Nanking to-day, these including the closing of several Japanese consulates up the Yangtze and the evacuation of Japanese nationals from several points in the interior. In anticipation of a possible air raid upon the capital, the police authorities in Nanking are making house to house visitations in order to instruct the population in air raid precautions.
Confirmation of the northward movement through Tsinanfu of Central Government troops, consisting mostly of Hunanese units, reached me from two independent foreign sources to-day. It is believed here that these forces are halting for the present at Tehchow.
Presumably in view of the possibility of hostilities being extended to Shantung, the American Consul at Tsinanfu has advised all American women and children in the interior of the province to proceed either to Tsinanfu or to Tsingtao.

Chinese official despatches stated that at 8 o'clock this morning six Japanese aeroplanes bombed the Chinese positions in the Nankow Park, near the Great Wall, north of Peiping. Half an hour later, a further ten machines brought machine-guns into action in addition to dropping a number of bombs.
Following the air raid, the despatches stated, a mixed Japanese force of infantry and cavalry made several assaults upon the Nankow positions, but these attacks were being successfully resisted by the Chinese defenders.

Tientsin, Aug. 2.
Hastening to support the Chinese forces, now reforming their lines at Machang, three trainloads of Central Government troops arrived at Tsangchow, 60 miles south of Tientsin, yesterday, according to information reaching Japanese military sources here to-day.
Japanese forces at Langfang, scene of a Sino-Japanese encounter last Monday, yesterday were reported to have concluded "mopping-up" operations slaying 30 plain-clothes Chinese snipers who were found in the former Chinese barracks there. Langfang is halfway between Tientsin and Peiping.
With conditions again peaceful Peiping was rapidly resuming its normal appearance to-day. Stores boarded-up for protection during last week's tension, had almost all reopened this morning.
With the exception of Chao yangmen, the gate leading to Tungchow, all city gates of Peiping were opened to permit the entry of farmers and others bringing much-needed fresh food into the old capital.
A Japanese detachment was in occupation at the Kwang'anmen, facing the road to Fengtai. British residents, who were evacuated to the Embassy compound last week, were permitted this morning to return to their homes within the city.

Central Troops At Kalgan
Injecting a new disturbing note into the North China situation, Central troops arrived in Kalgan last night from Shansi. The units were commended by Gen. Tang En-po.
Their arrival, Japanese military quarters here said, might force Lieut.-Gen. Liu Ju-ming, Chairman of the Chahar Provincial Government and a subordinate of Gen. Sung Cheh-yuan, Commander-in-Chief of the Twenty-Ninth Army, to throw in his lot with the Central Government.
Such action, it was pointed out, would inevitably lead to serious developments in the area.
Surrounded by Col. Kenji Suzuki's detachment, 3,200 soldiers of the Thirty-Ninth Brigade were disarmed at Peiyuan, six miles north of Peiping, at 8 o'clock last night, the headquarters of the Garrison here announced to-day. The Chinese unit was commanded by Major-Gen. Yuan Yuan-wu.
The arms seized included 3,200 rifles, eleven trench mortars, four field guns, 230 machine-guns and other types of weapons, and a large amount of ammunition, the communiqué claimed.
More than 2,000 Chinese corpses were found in Nanyuan, following the engagement of July 28, Japanese military officers here said. The Chinese authorities placed the casualties at 5,000. Some 100 Chinese soldiers were also captured at Nanyuan.
In addition to 1,000 horses, captured by the Japanese detachment at Nanyuan, also seized were two aeroplanes and four field guns.

Chinese Air Reconnaissance
Tientsin, Aug. 2.
Japanese aerial and land forces were on the alert here this morning following the reported sighting of a Chinese aeroplane engaged in a reconnaissance flight over Tientsin.

Special measures were hurriedly taken in view of persistent reports that the Chinese air force would attempt a bombardment of the Japanese Concession in Tientsin where the Japanese military headquarters are situated.
This operation is regarded as "possible, if not probable" by local Japanese military circles who claim having information in their possession that Chinese aircraft have begun moving north to various temporary bases in Shantung and southern Hopei.
Japanese aerial scouts to-day reported that Chinese Central troops were engaged in digging trenches in the vicinity of Paoting.
Bombing operations were conducted by Japanese squadrons all day yesterday upon Chinese concentrations in the Tientsin vicinity. Land troops also took part in these "mopping-up" operations.—Domei.

Japanese Planes Take Off
Nanking, Aug. 2.
Thirty Japanese planes took off from Tientsin for an unknown destination this morning. One of them appeared over Shihchiachuang to-day.
Although hostilities at the outskirts of Tientsin have ceased, martial law is still being rigidly enforced in the foreign concessions there.
The populace in Tientsin is facing an acute shortage of foodstuffs, and relief measures are eagerly awaited.
Chinese residents in the Japanese Concession and in the Hopei District, who had been lucky enough to have escaped death during the Japanese aerial bombardment during the past few days, have been forced to hoist Japanese flags, reports received here state.
Word has also been received here from Peiping that students and faculty members and their families at Tsinghua University have safely moved into the city.

《字林西报》——1937年8月3日，星期二。
22430

证实中国军队向北方调动

中央军占领张家口可能引发新 complications：日本方面保持警惕

北平、天津几乎恢复正常

宋哲元将军的援军抵达沧州：在山东的美国人受到警告

本报特约记者

南京，8月2日。
今日有多项迹象表明中日敌对行动可能扩大，这些迹象传至南京，其中包括关闭长江沿线的数个日本领事馆，以及从内地多处撤离日本侨民。为防备可能对首都进行的空袭，南京警方当局正在进行挨家挨户的走访，以指导民众采取防空预防措施。
我从两个独立的外国消息来源处获悉，证实中央政府军队（主要由湖南部队组成）正经济南府向北移动。据信，这些部队目前正停留在德州。
 presumably 鉴于敌对行动可能扩展至山东，驻济南府的美国领事已建议该省内地的所有美国妇女和儿童前往济南府或青岛。

中国官方电文称，今晨8时，六架日本飞机轰炸了北平以北、长城附近的南口阵地中国军队位置。半小时后，另有十架飞机在投掷多枚炸弹的同时，使用机枪进行扫射。
电文称，空袭之后，一支由步兵和骑兵组成的混合日军部队对南口阵地发动了数次突击，但这些攻击均被中国守军成功击退。

天津，8月2日。
据今日到达此处日本军方消息源的信息，为支援目前正在马厂重整防线的中国军队，三列火车的中央政府军队于昨日抵达位于天津以南60英里的沧州。
据报道，上周一日发生中日冲突现场的廊坊日军，昨日已完成“扫荡”行动，击毙了在该处前中国兵营内发现的30名便衣中国狙击手。廊坊位于天津与北平之间。
随着局势再次恢复平静，北平今日迅速恢复正常面貌。上周紧张局势期间为防护而 boarded-up 的商店，今晨几乎全部重新开业。
除通往通州的朝阳门外，北平所有城门均已开放，允许农民及其他人员将急需的新鲜食物运入这座古都。
一支日军分队占领了面向丰台道路的广安门。上周撤至使馆界内的英国居民，今晨获准返回其在城内的住所。

中央军抵达张家口
中央军昨夜从山西抵达张家口，给华北局势注入了新的不安因素。这些部队由汤恩伯将军指挥。
此处的日本军方人士称，他们的到来可能会迫使察哈尔省政府主席、第二十九军军长宋哲元将军的下属刘汝明中将，选择与中央政府站在一起。
有人指出，此举将不可避免地导致该地区局势严重恶化。
卫戍司令部今日宣布，昨晚8时，在北平以北六里的北苑，铃木健二大佐率领的分遣队包围并解除了第三十九旅3,200名士兵的武装。该中国部队由袁毓文少将指挥。
公报称，缴获的武器包括3,200支步枪、11门迫击炮、4门野战炮、230挺机枪及其他类型武器，以及大量弹药。
此处的日本军官称，在7月28日的战斗之后，在南苑发现了2,000多具中国士兵尸体。中国当局公布的伤亡人数为5,000人。在南苑还有约100名中国士兵被俘。
除了日军分遣队在南苑缴获的1,000匹马外，还缴获了两架飞机和四门野战炮。

中国空军侦察
天津，8月2日。
今晨，据报发现一架中国飞机在天津上空进行侦察飞行后，此处的日本空中和地面部队处于警戒状态。

鉴于持续有报告称中国空军将试图轰炸设有日本军事总部的天津日租界，当局匆忙采取了特别措施。
当地日本军方人士认为这一行动“有可能，甚至很可能”，他们声称掌握情报显示中国飞机已开始向北移动至山东和河北南部的各个临时基地。
日本空中侦察员今日报告称，中国中央军正在保定附近挖掘战壕。
昨日一整天，日本中队对天津附近的中国集结部队进行了轰炸行动。地面部队也参与了这些“扫荡”行动。——同盟社。

日本飞机起飞
南京，8月2日。
今晨，三十架日本飞机从天津起飞，前往未知目的地。其中一架今日出现在石家庄上空。
尽管天津郊区的敌对行动已经停止，但那里的外国租界仍在严格执行戒严令。
天津民众正面临严重的食品短缺，迫切等待救济措施。
此处收到的报告称，在过去几天的日本空袭中侥幸逃生的日租界和河北区中国居民，被迫悬挂日本国旗。
此外，此处还收到来自北平的消息，称清华大学的学生、教职员工及其家属已安全迁入城内。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, AUGUST 3, 1937
23429
Council Would Frown On
Forced Conscription Of
Troops Under New Order

Agreement Regarding Armed Forces In Area May
Be Called Up; No Action Taken Regarding
Volunteers; 30,000 Drilled Here

GROWING TIDE OF MILITARISM BOUND
TO HAVE ITS EFFECT UPON CITY

With a circular issued by the Nanking Government ordering the enforcement of universal military conscription, the whole question of the training of Chinese troops in the Shanghai area has taken on new interest, and, as it was ascertained here yesterday, may be brought into the limelight in the very near future.

During the course of an interview with a high official of the Shanghai Municipal Council, a representative of "The Shanghai Times" was informed that enforced conscription would probably be frowned on in the Settlement. Its practice would not be in accordance with the recognized procedure demanding that a Chinese cannot be removed forcibly from the foreign area without a court order.

It is obvious, however, that the growing tide of militarism in China must have its effect in Shanghai, and it is the belief of some who have studied the problem that it must be the object of an understanding between the powers that be in the Settlement and the Government before very long.

"The people should understand that military service is the duty of all citizens," reads an order from Nanking. "During this period of national emergency, we should adopt all means to strengthen the country. The people throughout the country should wake up and co-operate in its enforcement. Those who should render military service in accordance with the law should especially bestir themselves and enlist in the army with enthusiasm, so as to regenerate the nation."

A Political Basis

It was explained here yesterday that the question of conscription in the foreign areas of Shanghai or even in the Municipality of Greater Shanghai may without difficulty be related to the agreement of 1932 regarding the presence of Chinese armed forces within a certain distance from the city. If and when the matter is discussed by the authorities concerned, however, it will probably be decided upon a political rather than a legal basis.

The Shanghai Municipal Council is able to enforce many things that are vague from a legal standpoint through its control of the police, basing its right to do so upon a recognized custom. Large bodies of armed Chinese troops, for instance, have only been admitted to the Settlement on special occasions, such as important State funerals.

As one informant remarked, it would not be easy to write a legal treatise upon the rights of the Shanghai Municipal Council to keep conscription officers outside the Settlement gates. On the other hand, if a local native Chinese who did not wish to be conscripted could appeal to the police and would receive protection, sary to do so. It is understood that most of the volunteers have been drawn from the Chinese area, and those living within the foreign areas have given the authorities no reason to take action.

Report On Volunteers

As one official pointed out yesterday, the Shanghai Municipal Council itself maintains a sizable Chinese unit in the Shanghai Volunteer Corps and its members have long been respected for their efficiency and service to the community. Under these circumstances it would be difficult to prohibit the training of volunteers unless their presence in the Settlement or the Concession became a menace to peace and order.

According to an authoritative report obtained here yesterday by a representative of "The Shanghai Times," there are now 30,000 men in the Chinese area who have received military instruction in the Citizens Training Corps. At the present time 10,000 more are being drilled, and, upon graduation, these will be replaced by a similar number.

It is particularly important to note that the Chinese volunteers are kept in form after graduation, being fully armed and ready for mobilization at a moment's notice. During a crisis these men would automatically become a part of the national army and would receive the same pay as regular troops.

As volunteers the men supply their own uniforms and receive no pay. They must rise at an early hour every morning in order to show up on time at the training fields, where they are put through their paces for about one hour. At the end of a course lasting three months they are declared ready for service at a mass review.

Trains Now Enlisted

Most of the men who have been drilling on the training fields of the Municipality of Greater Shanghai are drawn from the lower middle class, being shop assistants, students or even skilled workers. There is now a tendency to recruit men from the higher brackets, and it has been reported that a unit of well-to-do business men has been taking a course in military training.

23429
工部局对新法令下的强制征兵持反对态度

关于该地区武装力量的协议可能被提及；对义勇军未采取行动；此处有30,000人受训

日益高涨的军国主义浪潮必将对城市产生影响

随着南京政府发布命令实施普遍兵役制，上海地区中国军队训练整个问题引起了新的关注，且据昨日在此处获悉，可能在不久的将来成为焦点。

在与上海公共租界工部局一位高级官员的访谈过程中，《上海泰晤士报》代表获悉，强制征兵在租界内可能会遭到反对。这种做法不符合公认的程序，即未经法院命令，不得强行将中国人从外国区域带走。

然而，显而易见的是，中国日益高涨的军国主义浪潮必然会对上海产生影响，一些研究过这一问题的人士认为，在不久将来，这必须成为租界当权者与政府之间达成谅解的目标。

南京的一道命令写道：“民众应明白，服兵役是所有公民的义务。在国家紧急时期，我们应采取一切手段加强国家力量。全国民众应觉醒并配合执行。依法应服兵役者尤应奋起，踊跃参军，以振兴国家。”

政治基础

昨日在此处解释称，上海外国区域甚至大上海市范围内的征兵问题，可以毫不困难地与1932年关于中国武装部队在城市一定距离内存在的协议联系起来。然而，如果有关当局讨论此事，可能会基于政治而非法律基础作出决定。

上海公共租界工部局能够通过其警察控制权，执行许多在法律立场上模糊不清的事项，其权利依据是公认的惯例。例如，大批中国武装部队仅在特殊场合，如重要的国葬时，才被允许进入租界。

正如一位消息人士所言，要撰写一篇关于上海公共租界工部局有权将征兵官员拒之租界门外的法律论文并不容易。另一方面，如果一名不愿被征召的本地华人可以向警方求助并获得保护，就有必要这样做。据悉，大多数义勇军来自中国区域，居住在外国区域内的人并未给当局提供采取行动的借口。

关于义勇军的报告

正如一位官员昨日指出的那样，上海公共租界工部局本身在上海义勇军（Shanghai Volunteer Corps）中维持着一支规模可观的中国分队，其成员长期以来因其效率和对社区的服务而受到尊重。在这种情况下，除非义勇军在租界或公廨内的存在成为对和平与秩序的威胁，否则很难禁止其训练。

根据《上海泰晤士报》代表昨日在此处获得的一份权威报告，目前中国区域有30,000人在市民训练团接受了军事指导。目前另有10,000人正在受训，毕业后，这些人将由同等数量的人员替换。

特别值得注意的是，中国义勇军在毕业后仍保持建制，全副武装，随时准备动员。在危机期间，这些人将自动成为国民军队的一部分，并获得与正规军相同的薪饷。

作为义勇军，这些人自备制服，不领取薪饷。他们必须每天清晨早起，以便准时出现在训练场，在那里接受约一小时的训练。在为期三个月的课程结束时，他们在大规模检阅中被宣布具备服役资格。

现在征募列车员

大多数在大上海市训练场受训的人来自中下层阶级，他们是店员、学生甚至是熟练工人。目前有一种从较高阶层招募人员的趋势，据报道，一个由富裕商人组成的单位正在参加军事训练课程。

据悉，市政府

青岛发生华人恐慌

许多人试图离城：
旅行社门庭若市

青岛，8月2日电。由于担心华北局势出现严重恶化，惊恐万状的中国人纷纷从青岛大规模撤离。据估计，仅昨天一天就有超过2万人离开该港口。据说中国官员及其家属正尽可能快地离开。与此同时，在中国旅行社（China Travel Service）办事处外，排起了长队，人们等待购买轮船或火车票。今天上午，火车站聚集了大量人群，等待搭乘中午的列车。自华北危机爆发以来，一直从山东其他港口集中到这里的日本家庭，也正被运回日本。——路透社。
