THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, AUGUST 3, 1937

Shanghai Reflects Air
Of Anxiety; Demands On
Shipping From Tsingtao

Jardine Ships Which Went Through Bombardment
At Tientsin Due To-day; More Vessels May
Be Needed To Evacuate Refugees

SCHOOLS AND HOSPITALS PREPARING TO
AID IN EXPECTED HOSTILITIES

A definite air of anxiety prevailed in Shanghai yesterday, reflecting the gloomy situation in North China and the exodus of vacationists from summer resorts in adjacent areas.

At Tsingtao residents and visitors are said to be making heavy demands on transportation facilities to Shanghai, and it is possible, though no decision has yet been reached, that the China Navigation Company and other lines may put on extra ships to serve the northern ports, exclusive of Taku and Tientsin.

To-day the Jardine ships, Taksang and Fausang, are expected in from Tientsin, where they were lying when the severe Japanese bombardment took place. Shrapnel fell on the decks of the ships, and the second officer of the Taksang had his hat knocked off by a fragment of shell.

The s.s. Yunnan is still standing by at Tientsin, ready to help in the evacuation of refugees if necessary. Two other ships are waiting at Chefoo for further orders. It is understood that Tientsin and Taku are both quiet, but there are no coolies to serve the loading and unloading of ships.

Plans For Boys Uncertain

News of the anxiety at Tsingtao may possibly change plans for many youngsters who were to leave this week for Camp Tsingtao and other recreation camps at the resort.

Y.M.C.A. officials said yesterday that they had not decided to change their plans, although it might be necessary to do so to-day. A large number of boys will leave by the s.s. Shuntien to-day unless orders are changed. There are at present 101 boys at Camp Tsingtao under the leadership of Mr. Harold Brown and other counsellors. Then there are the following youngsters who are returning to their homes here on Wednesday afternoon by the s.s. Shengking. Nicolas Bookhjadoff, George Kaitov, Igor Poliakoff, Arthur Krupolitz, Thomas Dunne, Samuel Wong, Willie Tsandia, Stanley Lau, Lee Shang, Paul Chung, Harold Thoren, Alistair Borden, Michael Malipko and George Munn.

The Red Cross Society in Shanghai is buying large quantities of medicines and bandages for wounded soldiers, who are said to be suffering greatly in Peiping and Tientsin. These supplies are also being sent to Paoting and Tsangchow.

Northern Banks Open

Shanghai banks have reported that their branches in Peiping and Tientsin are still open and the Government notes are still being accepted. There are reports, however, that Japanese currency is to be circulated shortly by the Bank of Chosen.

The train with passengers from Peiping arrived in the city yesterday at 1.45 p.m., six hours late, with 300 refugees from the Northern cities. Service is still being maintained to the North, but passengers for Peiping must stop at Tsinan to change trains for the old capital. The train for Tientsin stops at Tsauchow.

It has been reported that Japanese have formed an organization for purposes of transport in the event of trouble in Shanghai. They have allegedly secured 200 trucks and 100 motor cars and are seeking to hire 300 White Russian chauffeurs.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年8月3日，星期二

上海弥漫着焦虑气氛；
来自青岛的航运需求激增

曾在天津遭受炮击的怡和洋行船只今日抵达；可能需要更多船只疏散难民

学校和医院准备在预期的敌对行动中提供援助

昨天，上海弥漫着一种明确的焦虑气氛，这反映了华北的严峻局势以及邻近地区避暑胜地度假者的撤离。

据说在青岛，居民和游客对前往上海的交通工具提出了大量需求，尽管尚未做出决定，但中国航运公司（China Navigation Company）和其他航线可能会增加船只服务于北方港口（不包括大沽和天津）。

今天，怡和洋行的“大昌”轮（Taksang）和“福昌”轮（Fausang）预计将从天津抵达，日军进行猛烈炮击时，这两艘船正停泊在那里。弹片落在船甲板上，“大昌”轮的二副的帽子被一块炮弹碎片打飞。

“云南”号轮船（s.s. Yunnan）仍待命于天津，随时准备在必要时协助疏散难民。另有两艘船在烟台等待进一步指令。据悉，天津和大沽两地均平静，但没有苦力负责船只的装卸工作。

男孩们的计划尚不确定

青岛的焦虑消息可能会改变许多原定于本周前往青岛营地及其他度假村娱乐营地的年轻人的计划。

青年会（Y.M.C.A.）官员昨天表示，他们尚未决定改变计划，尽管今天可能有必要这样做。除非命令变更，否则大批男孩将于今天乘坐“顺天”轮（s.s. Shuntien）离开。目前，在哈罗德·布朗（Harold Brown）先生和其他辅导员的带领下，青岛营地有101名男孩。此外，以下年轻人将于周三下午乘坐“盛京”轮（s.s. Shengking）返回此间的家中：尼古拉斯·布克哈多夫（Nicolas Bookhjadoff）、乔治·凯托夫（George Kaitov）、伊戈尔·波利亚科夫（Igor Poliakoff）、阿瑟·克鲁波利茨（Arthur Krupolitz）、托马斯·邓恩（Thomas Dunne）、塞缪尔·王（Samuel Wong）、威利·赞迪亚（Willie Tsandia）、斯坦利·刘（Stanley Lau）、李尚（Lee Shang）、保罗·钟（Paul Chung）、哈罗德·索伦（Harold Thoren）、阿利斯泰尔·博登（Alistair Borden）、迈克尔·马利普科（Michael Malipko）和乔治·蒙恩（George Munn）。

上海红十字会正在购买大量药品和绷带，用于救治伤兵，据说北平和天津的伤兵痛苦不堪。这些物资也被送往保定和沧州。

北方银行开业

上海各银行报告称，其在北平和天津的分行仍然营业，政府法币仍在流通。然而，有报道称，朝鲜银行（Bank of Chosen）即将发行日元纸币。

载有来自北平乘客的列车昨天下午1点45分抵达本市，晚点六小时，车上载有300名来自北方城市的难民。通往北方的服务仍在维持，但前往北平的乘客必须在济南下车，换乘前往旧都的列车。前往天津的列车在曹州（音译，原文为Tsauchow，可能指沧州或德州，此处依原文音译）停靠。

据报道，日本人为防备上海发生事变，已成立一个运输组织。据称他们已 securing 200辆卡车和100辆汽车，并试图雇佣300名白俄司机。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, AUGUST 3, 1937

Rumors Cause
Large Exodus
From Chapei

Area, However, Quiet
Despite Undercur-
rent Of Tension

Rumors, which defied all efforts
at confirmation, yesterday caused a
heavy increase in the exodus of
Chinese residents from Chapei.
Up to a late hour last night, a
steady stream of trucks, ricshas and
handcarts, laden with household
goods and trunks was making its
way into the Settlement from the
Chinese areas.
The exodus, which dropped during
the end of last week to a negligible
extent, began to pick up shortly
after noon yesterday. As rumors of
impending trouble gained wider
currency, large groups of residents
started to joined the exodus.
Areas Quiet
Information gathered by THE
CHINA PRESS yesterday from respon-
sible sources failed to substantiate
any of the widely circulated reports.
Chapei and Hongkew were normal
and quiet last night, although an
undercurrent of tension stronger
than during the past week, seemed
to exist in the area.
Meantime, the Greater Shanghai
Association for the Support of De-
fense had yesterday launched its
campaign for a salvation fund. Ap-
peals were sent to various local or-
ganisations and individuals to con-
tribute.
According to the regulation an-
nounced by the campaign com-
mittee, the money collected in
the drive will be turned over
to the Military Affairs Commission.
The association will forward the
names of those making donations of
more than $2,000 to the Military
Affairs Commission. Decorations
will be given by the association to
those contributing $1,000. Those
contributing $5,000 will receive a
decoration from the City Govern-
ment of Greater Shanghai, while
those giving more than $1,000 will
receive official commendation from
the National Government.

《大美晚报》，1937年8月3日，星期二

谣言导致
闸北大量人口
外逃

然而，尽管暗流
涌动，该地区
保持平静

昨天，无法证实的谣言导致闸北中国居民外逃人数大幅增加。直到昨晚深夜，满载家具和箱子的卡车、人力车和手推车源源不断地从中国区域进入租界。

上周末外逃人数曾降至微不足道的程度，但昨天午后不久又开始增加。随着即将发生事变的谣言广泛传播，大批居民开始加入外逃行列。

地区平静

《大美晚报》昨天从可靠渠道收集的信息未能证实任何广泛流传的报告。昨晚闸北和虹口正常且平静，尽管该地区似乎存在比过去一周更强烈的紧张暗流。

与此同时，上海市民支持国防大会昨天发起了募集救国基金的运动。已向各地方组织和个人发出捐款呼吁。

根据运动委员会宣布的规定，募集到的款项将移交给军事委员会。该会将把捐款超过2,000美元者的名单报送军事委员会。该会将向捐款1,000美元者颁发勋章。捐款5,000美元者将获得大上海市政府颁发的勋章，而捐款超过1,000美元者将获得国民政府的官方嘉奖。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, AUGUST 3, 1937
2342¹

TRAFFIC TO NORTH
DISRUPTED

No Foodstuffs to be Sent to
Northern Ports

EXODUS FROM CHAPEI
INCREASES

Communications to Tientsin remained disrupted yesterday. The through express to the north only ran to as far as Tsinan, capital of Shantung, while the China National Aviation Corporation's plane flew to Tsingtao instead of Tientsin. The Eurasia's Hongkong-Peiping service has been curtailed, with Taiyuan as the terminus.

Chinese shipping service to the north was practically severed. According to a Chinese message, a group of Japanese vessels on the Shanghai-Nagasaki run have been commandeered by the Japanese Government. Other Japanese vessels for the North China service have likewise been ordered to transport troops.

According to a Chinese message from Tientsin, Chinese banks have reopened for business. The legal tender notes are circulated as usual. Japanese banknotes on the market have been greatly increased.

The Shanghai Cereal Hong Owners' Association in Nantao have issued a circular notice to members, requesting them to suspend any transactions they may have for foodstuffs with dealers in Tsingtao, Yingkow, and Dairen. The Association has organized a party of twenty persons to see that the notice is complied with and to report those members ignoring the notice.

Chinese insurance firms, other trade organizations and residents' associations held separate meetings yesterday when measures to meet any emergency were discussed.

According to a Chinese message from Washington, present indications in America are that the Neutrality Act will not be applied to the Sino-Japanese conflict.

Chapei Exodus

The continued evacuation of Chapei residents gained considerable size yesterday evening as new rumours of impending trouble spread through the Northern area.

It was mainly in Hongkew that the southward movement of families and their possessions attracted attention during the late afternoon and early evening. Many filled removal vans, motor-cars and rickshaws were seen proceeding towards the bridges over the Soochow Creek, destined for the southern part of the Settlement and for the French Concession. Many refugees entered the Settlement from Paoshan Road at North Honan Road, proceeded east to North Kiangse Road or west to North Shanse Road and finally reached the Soochow Creek at the various bridges. Owing to repairs, North Honan Road was not the favourite refugees' highway, as during previous evacuations.

The Hongkew district was generally quiet and most shops there were open for business. The Japanese Naval Landing Party stationed to patrol the area following the recent disturbances were seen patrolling the streets.

《字林西报》，1937年8月3日，星期二
2342¹

通往北方的
交通中断

不再向北方港口
运送食品

闸北外逃
人数增加

昨天，通往天津的交通依然中断。北上的直达特快列车只运行到山东省会济南，而中国航空公司的飞机飞往青岛而非天津。欧亚航空公司的香港-北平航线已缩短，以太原为终点站。

中国通往北方的航运服务实际上已断绝。据中方消息，一组在上海-长崎航线上运行的日本船只已被日本政府征用。其他服务于华北航线的日本船只也奉命运输军队。

据来自天津的中方消息，中国银行已重新开业。法币照常流通。市面上日元纸币的数量大幅增加。

南市上海米业同业公会向会员发出通函，要求他们暂停与青岛、营口和大连商人的任何食品交易。该会已组织一个二十人的小组，以确保通函得到遵守，并报告无视通函的会员。

中国保险公司、其他贸易组织和居民协会昨天分别举行会议，讨论应对任何紧急情况的措施。

据来自华盛顿的中方消息，美国目前的迹象表明，《中立法案》不会适用于中日冲突。

闸北外逃

随着新的关于即将发生事变的谣言在北部地区传播，闸北居民的持续撤离在昨天晚上规模显著扩大。

主要在虹口，家庭及其财产向南迁移的景象在下午晚些时候和傍晚初刻引起了关注。可以看到许多装满物品的搬家货车、汽车和人力车驶向苏州河上的桥梁，目的地是租界南部和法租界。许多难民从河南路北段的宝山路进入租界，向东行至江西北路或向西行至山西北路，最后通过各座桥梁到达苏州河。由于维修，河南北路不像以前撤离时那样成为难民的首选通道。

虹口区总体平静，大多数商店照常营业。在最近骚乱后派驻该地区巡逻的日本海军陆战队士兵被看到在街道上巡逻。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, August 5, 1937 23469
D7994/5-
Thousands Flee Chapei
To Foreign Districts;
War Rumors Blamed

REFUGEE HORDES
CROSSING BRIDGES
INTO SETTLEMENT

Traffic Southward Toward Safety Taking On New
Aspect As Chinese Begin Leaving Yangtzepoo;
Rumors Fly, Rents Soar; Bonds Slack

JAPANESE EVACUATING CANTON

THE frantic exodus of Chinese residents from the
northern districts of the city to places in the Settle-
ment and Concession south of Soochow Creek increased
to huge proportions last night and today, thousands of
people swarming out of Chapei with bag and baggage.
The rush was swelled by hundreds from Wayside and
Yangtzepoo districts, which hitherto have been comparatively
quiet. At press time this afternoon hordes were moving
across nearly all bridges over Soochow Creek, bound south.
Between 7 a.m. yesterday and 7 a.m. today approximately
16,000 Chinese left Chapei, according to Municipal Police esti-
mates this morning. Between 4 p.m. yesterday and 7 a.m.
today about 350 had moved out of Wayside, and this morning
scores more joined the parade from Yangtzepoo. Garden
Bridge, Chapoo, Szechuen, Kiangse, Shanse, Fokien, Che-
kiang, Yu Ya Ching, Wuchen, Tatung and Heng Foong Road
bridges were crowded with ricshas, wheelbarrows, and push-
carts, piled high with household goods that literally buried
their owners.

EQUALS 1932

This continual stream of humanity from Chinese ter-
ritory to the safety of the foreign areas equals, if not ex-
ceeds, the great exodus of Chinese from Chapei early in
1932 just prior and during the Sino-Japanese hostilities here.
The removal from northern and eastern Settlement
districts was a new aspect of the movement that has been
underway for almost two weeks. Traffic is extremely crowd-
ed in the Central District as a result. The refugees are
scattering everywhere through the Settlement and Concession,
centering chiefly in the Chinese hotels and lodging houses of
Peking and Yu Ya Ching Roads, but many are moving on
across into Nantao. Whereas the exodus formerly was con-
fined to men moving belongings to safety and then return-
ing home, the crowds now are swelled by women and chil-
dren, and obviously the refugees are moving to stay.

PATROLS WATCHFUL

There has, however, been little movement noted out of the
Hongkew district. Municipal Police are doing the best they
can to direct the crowds of refugees, and police patrols are
now composed of four men together where formerly they
patrolled singly in daytime.
The North Station presented an unusual scene today,
crowded with people and baggage. Special trains are run-
ning on the Shanghai-Nanking and Shanghai-Hangchow Rail-
ways to accommodate increasing traffic. Nanking Chinese are
arriving and Shanghai Chinese are departing. About 25,000
people move through the station a day, according to railway
officials; officials denied today that the number had swelled to
40,000 as reported this morning. Trains, however, are packed
with passengers, Chinese, and there is a greatly increased
demand for river boats and vehicles going down the coast and to
Ningpo.

MANY RUMORS

Shanghai is a city of rumors, and rumors alone are chiefly
credited for this state of affairs. Among the scores of stories
that drifted through Shanghai today, brought by Chapei re-
sidents and other elements were: (1) that China is to declare
war on Japan tomorrow, starting the campaign in North
China and in Shanghai and other cities where Japanese forces
are present; (2) that the Police Bureau has notified Chinese
residents in Chapei, especially those in the section adjoining
Wayside area, to move in three days, as Chinese will attack
that section in the event it is used as a Japanese military
base, and attacks on Hongkew will be aimed at the Japanese
Landing Party barracks; (3) that thousands of Chinese troops,
mostly in plainclothes, are in Chapei, Kiangwan, Woosung and
other areas, digging in during the night, and that General
Chang Fah-kwei of "Ironsides" fame is said to have establish-
ed headquarters in Sunkiang to direct operations; (4) that a
traitorous Chinese rice merchant supplying rice to Japanese
in preparation for the forces due to arrive from Japan was
caught in Wayside and the go-between was also seized, and
both shot on the spot; therefore Japanese are planning re-
prisals; (5) that Japanese are placing anti-aircraft guns in
Hongkew.

BONDS UNCHANGED

These rumors and many more are rife. The Japanese
are not slow to put forward their own rumors. One today
blamed the exodus on Paotanti activities in Chapei.
The Chinese government bond quotations remained un-
changed this morning with but a negligible amount of trans-
actions recorded. The only change took place during the
morning session at the China Merchants' Bond and Stock Ex-
change as compared to the quotations of yesterday was the
slight gain of 40 cents in the 96 Millions. At the closing
this noon, the quotation was $9.10.

FLIGHT FROM CANTON
(Reuter's Agency)

CANTON, Aug. 5.—An undercurrent of anxiety prevails
throughout the city as a result of the wildest stories concern-
ing the intentions of the Japanese regarding Canton.
Transportation to Hongkong has been packed during the
past few days, and foreign banks are very active because of
increased Chinese deposits of monies and jewelries.
A number of Japanese families evacuated last night on
official orders, while it is understood that certain Japanese
(Concluded from Page 1)
firms are arranging for foreign firms to take over their busi-
ness in the event of hostilities.
Meanwhile, large-scale military preparations are proceed-
ing.
The Government is reported to have chartered 200 launches,
allegedly for transport from upriver ports.

JAPANESE LOSSES IN NORTH CHINA
(Reuter's Agency)

TOKYO, August 5.—The Japanese forces in North China
lost 364 men killed and 869 wounded between July 7, the date
of the Lukouchiao incident, and August 4, according to an
announcement today by the War Office.

SMALL CHINESE FORCE SAID ROUTED
(Domei)

TIENTSIN, Aug. 5.—Japanese forces operating south of
Changhsintien, 20 miles from Peiping on the Peiping-Hankow
railway, yesterday noon defeated a Chinese unit of between
70 to 80 men outside Liangsiang, the Japanese headquarters
here announced this morning.
The Chinese left about 30 dead, 30 rifles and more than
300 hand-grenades behind them, the communique stated. The
Japanese forces did not suffer any casualties, according to the
announcement.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年8月5日，星期四 23469
D7994/5-

成千上万人逃离闸北
前往外国辖区；
归咎于战争谣言

难民潮
跨过桥梁
涌入租界

随着中国人开始离开杨树浦，向南通往安全地带的交通呈现出新面貌；谣言纷飞，租金飙升；公债交易清淡

日本人正在撤离广州

昨夜及今日，中国居民从本市北部地区向苏州河以南的公共租界和法租界各地的疯狂逃亡规模急剧扩大，成千上万的人带着全部家当涌出闸北。此前相对平静的越界筑路区和杨树浦地区也有数百人加入这股人流，使得逃亡潮进一步膨胀。截至今天下午发稿时，大批人群正穿过苏州河上的几乎所有桥梁，向南进发。据工部局警务处今晨估计，从昨天上午7时至今天上午7时，约有16,000名中国人离开闸北。从昨天下午4时至今天上午7时，约有350人搬离越界筑路区，而今天上午又有数十人加入从杨树浦撤出的行列。外白渡桥、乍浦路桥、四川路桥、江西路桥、山西路桥、福建路桥、浙江路桥、虞洽卿路桥、吴淞路桥、大同路桥和恒丰路桥上挤满了黄包车、独轮车和手推车，车上堆满的家什几乎将主人淹没。

堪比1932年

这种从中国领土持续不断流向外国辖区安全地带的人流，即便没有超过，也至少相当于1932年初中日在此发生敌对行动前后，中国人大举撤离闸北时的规模。从租界北部和东部地区迁出，是这场已持续近两周的迁移运动中出现的新动向。因此，中区交通极度拥挤。难民们散居在租界和法租界的各处，主要集中在北京路和虞洽卿路的中国旅馆和客栈，但许多人正继续迁入南市。此前的撤离仅限于男子将财物转移至安全处所后返回家中，而现在的队伍中增加了妇女和儿童，显然难民们是打算长期滞留。

巡逻队保持警惕

然而，虹口地区并未观察到明显的 outward movement（外出流动）。工部局警务处正尽力引导难民潮，警察巡逻队现在由四人一组组成，而以前白天是单人巡逻。
今天北站呈现出不寻常的景象，挤满了人和行李。为应对日益增长的交通量，沪宁铁路和沪杭铁路增开了特别列车。南京的中国人正在抵达，而上海的中国人正在离开。据铁路官员称，每天约有25,000人通过该站；官员们今天否认了今早报道的该数字已激增至40,000人的说法。然而，火车上挤满了中国乘客，且对沿海岸南下及前往宁波的轮船和车辆的需求大幅增加。

谣言四起

上海是一座充满谣言的城市，而这种局面主要归咎于谣言本身。在今天流传于上海的众多故事中，由闸北居民和其他人士带来的包括：(1) 中国将于明天对日本宣战，在华北以及上海和其他有日军驻扎的城市发起战役；(2) 警察局已通知闸北的中国居民，特别是毗邻越界筑路区地区的居民，在三天内搬离，因为如果该地区被用作日军军事基地，中方将发动攻击，且对虹口的攻击将针对日本海军陆战队兵营；(3) 数千名中国军队，大多身着便衣，已在闸北、江湾、吴淞及其他地区挖掘工事过夜，据说“铁军”名将张发奎将军已在松江设立总部指挥作战；(4) 一名向日本人供应大米以备战事、准备迎接从日本抵达的部队的奸商在越界筑路区被捕，中间人也被抓获，两人均被当场枪决；因此日本人正计划报复；(5) 日本人正在虹口部署高射炮。

公债价格不变

这些谣言以及其他许多谣言甚嚣尘上。日本人也不迟缓地散布他们自己的谣言。今天有一则谣言将逃亡潮归咎于闸北的保皇党活动。
今晨中国政府公债报价保持不变， recorded transactions（记录在案的交易）微乎其微。与昨日报价相比，唯一的变化发生在华商证券交易所的上午交易中，“九六公债”小幅上涨40分。中午收盘时，报价为9.10美元。

逃离广州
（路透社）

广州，8月5日电——由于有关日本人对广州意图的最荒谬传闻盛行，全市弥漫着一种焦虑的暗流。
过去几天，前往香港的交通线路拥挤不堪，外资银行非常活跃，因为中国人的存款和珠宝存入量增加。
昨晚，一些日本家庭奉官方命令撤离，同时据悉某些日本
（接第1版）
商社正在安排由外国公司接管其业务，以防发生敌对行动。
与此同时，大规模军事准备正在进行中。
据报道，政府已包租200艘小汽艇，据称用于从上游港口运输人员。

日军在华北的损失
（路透社）

东京，8月5日电——根据陆军省今天的公告，从7月7日卢沟桥事变发生之日至8月4日，日军在华北损失364人阵亡，869人受伤。

据称一小股中国部队被击溃
（同盟社）

天津，8月5日电——驻此间的日军总部今晨宣布，昨天中午，在北平至汉口铁路线上、距北平20英里的长辛店以南作战的日军，在良乡附近击败了一支由70至80人组成的中国部队。
公报称，中国人遗留下约30具尸体、30支步枪和300多枚手榴弹。公告称，日军未遭受任何伤亡。

43470

JAPANESE BANKS AID
(Domei)
TOYKO, Aug. 5.—Following the example set by Osaka institutions, member banks of the Tokyo Clearing House today waived the terms of fixed-term deposit contracts in the case of conscripted officers and men and their families.
Effective today, sums up to Y.1,000 may be drawn from fixed-deposit accounts even though the bank is not bound by contract to make such payments.
Similar steps will be taken by banks throughout the country to alleviate the financial strain caused by the enlistment of family wage-earners.

Tsai Coming Here
(Reuter's Agency)
CANTON, Aug. 4.—After visiting Canton for one day, during which he called on the local military leaders and laid a wreath at the cemetery for soldiers of the 19th Route Army, General Tsai Ting-kai left for Hongkong tonight to catch the Empress of Japan for Shanghai, whence he intends to proceed to Nanking.
Interviewed by Reuter, General Tsai, who is now greyhaired, declared that he had decided to sink all personal differences and fight under a united banner for China should diplomatic exchanges fail and war break out.
The Central Government, he added, had already organised its defense policy, and his trip to Nanking was for the purpose of offering his services to the Generalissimo.
General Wu Teh-chen, Governor of Kwangtung, and the highest military leaders in Canton throughed the smoke-room of the steamer to wish General Tsai bon voyage.

Inspect Troops
(Kuo Min News Agency)
KWEIHUA, Aug. 4.—Owing to the tense situation in eastern Suiyuan, Lieut.-General Chao Cheng-shou, Commander of the Shansi-Suiyuan Cavalry Forces left here for Tatung, northern Shansi, by rail on Monday night to inspect his troops.
A meeting of 200 civic leaders was convened yesterday by the Air-Defense Headquarters for Suiyuan when measures governing air-defense and completion of air-defense equipment were decided upon.

Air Defense Ordered
(Kuo Min News Agency)
HSUCHOW, Aug. 4.—In view of the geographical importance of Hsuchow and Haichow, northern Kiangsu, air-defense measures are being instituted by the local authorities to protect the public during the extraordinary period of emergency. Large-scale maneuvers will be staged in order to show the people what to do in case of enemy air raids.

Donations Received
(Kuo Min News Agency)
NANKING, Aug. 4.—A sum of $30,000 was received here yesterday by the Government from the millionaire brothers, Messrs. Hu Wen-hu and Hu Wen-pao, well-known overseas philanthropists, towards the fund for the relief of wounded soldiers and refugees in North China.

Air Lines Resumed
The service of the China National Aviation Corporation to different parts of the country was resumed today after a day's lay-off yesterday due to the typhoon. The firm's planes for Hankow, Tsingtao, and South China all left this morning on schedule. A C.N.A.C. plane left for Tsingtao, a Douglas DC2, with four passengers, which will come back to Shanghai this afternoon. Eurasia's plane left Taiyuan today for Hongkong on its regular schedule while a plane left Shanghai for Chengchow this morning to connect the Taiyuan-Hongkong line. Trains continued to make Tsinan the terminal. The incoming Blue Express from Tsinan arrive every day in the afternoon, about six hours behind the usual schedule.

Aid Fund Plans
The recently-organized All-Shanghai Association for the Support of Armed Resistance had already formed elaborate plans according to which every individual, business firm and public body in the city will be requested to contribute to an aid fund. Contributions will be payable in installments, employees pledging a certain amount from each month while employers make monthly, semi-annual or annual donations based on profits. The association is also calling for physically fit recruits for the formation of nine service corps, namely, peace and order maintenance, publicity, engineering, communications, transportation, first aid, fire prevention, burial and contributions canvassing.
Medical students from National Tungchi University and the National Medical College of Shanghai leave here today for the North to aid wounded soldiers and civilians. This group under the direction of the Red Cross Society of China is the first to be sent from this city. With it go large supplies of medicine and first-aid equipment while further orders for $100,000 worth of medicines are reported to have been placed. Additional funds for this type of work may be raised by the sale of patriotic stamps similar to the Christmas seals sold in America. Post offices throughout the country will be asked to handle these stamps. Patriotic badges are another possible source of funds.

Rents Rising
A real estate boom bringing about increase of rents has resulted in the Settlement and French Concession from the exodus of refugees from the Chapei and Hongkew areas caused by the continued trouble in North China. Living quarters are becoming increasingly difficult to find and houses long empty are again showing signs of life. Although reputable firms are against profiteering, some unscrupulous house owners have been increasing their rents. Those refugees who delayed their departure until the last day or two are finding particular trouble in getting settled in quarters at a reasonable rate.
Rent increases of from $5 to $20 a month are reported while landlords are also demanding two months' deposit, two months' rent in advance and the signing of one year lease. This action is the result of past experiences when refugees from the same areas returned to their own homes without notice, leaving the houses in a state of disrepair which robbed owners of profit. Storing space for household effects alone now costs from $25 to $30 while unfurnished rooms are going for about $30. Large families are crowding into single rooms.
A relief committee to study the housing problem and profiteering has been suggested. Besides the profiteering charge against them, some landlords are charged with deliberately spreading wild rumors in order to stimulate the exodus from Chapei and Hongkew. They are said to have had such success that foreign residents are also taking alarm and leaving their homes in those areas.

43470

日本银行提供援助
（同盟社）
东京，8月5日电。——继大阪各机构之后，东京票据交换所的成员银行今日宣布，针对被征召的官兵及其家属，免除定期存款合同的条款限制。
自今日起，即使银行依合同并无此付款义务，也可从定期存款账户中提取高达1,000日元的款项。
全国各地的银行也将采取类似措施，以缓解因家庭主要劳动力应征入伍而造成的经济压力。

蔡廷锴即将抵沪
（路透社）
广州，8月4日电。——蔡廷锴将军在广州停留一日，期间拜访了当地军事领导人，并在第十九路军烈士墓前敬献花圈后，于今晚启程前往香港，拟搭乘“日本皇后号”轮船前往上海，随后打算赴南京。
蔡廷锴将军在接受路透社采访时宣称，这位如今已生华发的将军表示，如果外交交涉失败且战争爆发，他决定摒弃所有个人分歧，在统一的旗帜下为中国而战。
他补充说，中央政府已经制定了防御政策，他此次前往南京的目的是向总司令效力。
广东省主席吴铁城将军及广州最高军事领导人在轮船的吸烟室为蔡将军送行，祝他一路顺风。

视察部队
（国民新闻社）
归绥，8月4日电。——鉴于绥远东部局势紧张，晋绥骑兵司令赵承绶中将于周一晚乘火车离开此地，前往山西北部的大同视察部队。
绥远防空司令部昨日召集了200名市民领袖开会，决定了有关防空及完成防空设备的措施。

下令防空
（国民新闻社）
徐州，8月4日电。——鉴于江苏北部徐州和海州的地理重要性，地方当局正在实施防空措施，以便在非常紧急时期保护公众。将举行大规模演习，向民众展示在遭遇敌机空袭时应如何应对。

收到捐款
（国民新闻社）
南京，8月4日电。——政府昨日在此收到著名海外慈善家、百万富翁胡文虎和胡文豹兄弟捐赠的3万美元，用于华北伤兵和难民救济基金。

航线恢复
由于昨日台风停航一天，中国航空公司的国内各地航班服务于今日恢复。该公司飞往汉口、青岛和华南的飞机均于今晨按时起飞。一架中航飞机飞往青岛，这是一架道格拉斯DC2型飞机，载有四名乘客，将于今天下午返回上海。欧亚航空公司的飞机今日按计划从太原飞往香港，同时一架飞机今晨从上海飞往郑州，以衔接太原-香港航线。火车继续以济南为终点站。从济南开来的蓝色特快列车每天下午抵达，比正常时间晚约六小时。

援助基金计划
新近成立的上海各界抗敌后援会已经制定了详尽的计划，根据该计划，将要求本市每个人、每家商号和每个公共团体向援助基金捐款。捐款将分期支付，雇员承诺每月捐出一定金额，而雇主则根据利润按月、半年或年度捐款。该会还号召身体健全者应征，组建九个服务队，即：维持治安、宣传、工程、通讯、运输、急救、防火、殡葬和募捐。
国立同济大学和上海国立医学院的医学生今日离开此地北上，援助伤兵和平民。这支队伍在中国红十字会的指导下，是从本市派出的第一批人员。随队携带了大量药品和急救设备，另有报道称已下达价值10万美元的药品订单。此类工作的额外资金可能通过出售爱国邮票来筹集，类似于美国销售的圣诞封缄标签。将要求全国各地的邮局处理这些邮票。爱国徽章是另一个可能的资金来源。

租金上涨
由于华北持续动荡，导致闸北和虹口地区的难民外流，公共租界和法租界出现了房地产繁荣，进而导致租金上涨。住房越来越难找，长期空置的房屋再次显现出有人居住的迹象。虽然信誉良好的公司反对牟取暴利，但一些无良房东一直在提高租金。那些直到最后一两天才推迟离开的难民发现，特别难以以合理的价格找到住所。
据报道，租金每月上涨5至20美元，同时房东还要求两个月的押金、两个月的预付租金，并签署一年期的租约。此举是过去经验的结果，当时来自同一地区的难民未经通知便返回自家，留下房屋失修的状态，使业主无法获利。仅存放家具的空间现在就需要25至30美元，而无家具的房间租金约为30美元。大家庭挤在单人间里。
有人建议成立一个救济委员会来研究住房问题和牟取暴利行为。除了被指控牟取暴利外，一些房东还被指控故意散布谣言，以刺激人们从闸北和虹口外逃。据说他们取得了如此大的成功，以至于外籍居民也感到恐慌，离开了这些地区的家园。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, AUGUST 5, 1937

City Officials Take
Lead In Organizing
Student First Aid Unit

Bureau Of Social Affairs Organizing Corps
To Assist Behind Lines; Red Cross
Society Also Makes Preparations

Shanghai's university and high school students will be organized by the Greater Shanghai Bureau of Social Affairs into a service corps to handle first aid, transport, publicity, and intelligence work if the North China hostilities should result in a major war.

Under the direction of Mr. Pan Kung-chan, Commissioner of Social Affairs, work to organize the corps is now in progress among all local schools where students are asked to join-up. Mr. Pan, according to information obtained here yesterday, will himself assume the post of Commander of the Student Service Corps.

Mr. Pan's project aims at centralizing and co-ordinating the various student aid associations which have been formed since the outbreak of the Lukouchiao incident.

Will Prevent Confusion

Educational authorities of the city felt that unless one well-organized body is established, the work of the independent students may conflict and overlap during the time of an emergency.

According to the plan revealed by the Bureau of Social Affairs, Service Corps will be organized with the various high schools, professional schools, evening schools, colleges and universities as units. Principals and presidents of the institutions will be named as directors. The administrative officers of the schools will form the members of the "general staff" of the various corps.

Discipline To Be Enforced

Students are to join the corps at their own volition, but once they have signed up they have to execute and obey the orders of the commanding officers of the corps as well as the military and civil officers of the district where the corps is sent for work. Discipline as strict as that in an army will be enforced among the student non-combatant servicemen.

To be included among the work of the student corps are publicity, defense, technical work, transportation, campaign for raising aid funds, and ambulance. Students engaged in the work will wear the uniforms of the different schools. The operating expenses for the

The Society has also announced plans for a nation-wide first aid training project to those who are interested. No fees or tuition will be charged. In addition to this a medical corps has been organised by the Society which will bring medical skill and material to the wounded.

In the meantime in co-operation with the National Health Administration in Nanking, the Red Cross Society recently announced the inauguration of an All-China First Aid Center, with its head office stationed in the Capital. A financial drive for the purpose of purchasing medical equipment is being made among local financial leaders.

According to a discussion conducted by Dr. J. Heng Liu, among medical men and local financiers at least $200,000 will be needed for first aid purposes. To this plan, Dr. Li Ting-an, Mr. Tu Yueh-sen, Mr. Y. M. Ch'ien and several others have concurred.

Aside from all these, the Red Cross Society is also organizing two batches of first aid corps to be sent to the Northern front, soon.

Reports were current several days ago that the headquarters of the Red Cross Society were to be transferred from Shanghai to Nanking. This, however, has been officially denied.

Red Cross To Aid

In order to meet the urgent demand in the North, the Red Cross Society of China, whose headquarters are located in Shanghai, have cabled to all its branches in North China to conduct actual first aid fieldwork in the war zone, according to a letter sent to The China Press yesterday.

市政官员带头
组织学生急救队

社会局组织服务队
在后方提供协助；红十字会
也在做准备

如果华北战事演变成大规模战争，大上海社会局将把上海的大学生和中学生组织成一个服务队，负责急救、运输、宣传和情报工作。

在社会局局长潘公展先生的指导下，目前在当地所有学校中正在进行组织服务队的工作，学生们被要求加入。据昨日在此获得的消息，潘先生将亲自担任学生服务队的队长。

潘先生的计划旨在集中和协调自卢沟桥事变爆发以来形成的各个学生援助协会。

防止混乱

市教育局认为，除非建立一个组织良好的机构，否则独立学生的各项工作在紧急时期可能会发生冲突和重叠。

根据社会局透露的计划，服务队将以各中学、职业学校、夜校、学院和大学为单位进行组织。各院校的校长将被任命为主任。学校的行政人员将组成各服务队“参谋部”的成员。

执行纪律

学生自愿加入服务队，但一旦报名，就必须执行并服从服务队指挥官以及服务队被派往工作地区的军政官员的命令。在学生非战斗服务人员中将执行如同军队般严格的纪律。

学生服务队的工作包括宣传、防御、技术工作、运输、募集援助基金运动和救护车服务。从事这些工作的学生将穿着各自学校的制服。服务队的

红十字会提供援助

为了满足华北的迫切需求，总部设在上海的中国红十字会已致电其在华北的所有分会，要求在战区开展实际的野外急救工作，这是根据昨日发给《字林西报》的一封信得知的。

Reports Reach Tokyo Of
Severance Declaration
Now Ready In Nanking

DEFENCE CONFERENCE ON FRIDAY

STEADY ENVELOPING OF PEIPING-

Vanguard Of Main Body Reported To Be Massed

Conference With The Generalissimo

Although there is still official silence in Nanking as to what decision, if any, the Government has come to regarding the use of National Government troops against the Japanese in North China, it is reported that General Chiang Kai-shek is calling an emergency national defence conference on Friday, to be attended by all military leaders, to decide on the disposition of troops in case of need.

Domei reports from Tokyo that, according to Nanking messages reaching the big newspapers there, a declaration of the severance of diplomatic relations with Japan, to be promulgated following its approval by the Central Political Council, has been drafted by the Legislative Yuan.

The reports add that a national defence programme, already approved by the Military Affairs Commission, will be considered by the military conference on Friday.

The Nanking Government was also reported to have decided to enforce nation-wide military conscription.

Troop Movements

Messages from Nanking, Peiping and Tsinan reported a steady enveloping of the Peiping-Tientsin area by Chinese troops in Chahar, Southern Hopei, Shansi and Shantung.

The main body of the Nanking Government's troops, estimated at 30 divisions, was reported to have been concentrated along the Peiping-Hankow Railway. The vanguard of this force was said to have been massed at Paotingfu, where strong defence works were reported to be under construction.

The vanguard of the Chinese troops fringing the Tientsin-Pukow Railway was said to have established its positions at Tsangchow and Machang.

the Local Authorities

Owing to precautionary measures adopted by the Chinese authorities in the Shanghai district, road traffic is being diverted and motorists are subject to examinations; according to information received by the "North-China Daily News" yesterday.

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, AUGUST 1, 1937.

General Chiang Believed To
Be In Precarious Spot

Japanese Newspaper Outlines Predicament Of The
Leader; Rallied Country Under Anti-Nippon
Banner And Now Unable To Stem Tide

Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek has been counselled by his two highest Chinese military advisors to resign after accepting "minimum Japanese demands" and thereby assume the responsibility for China's failure to "resist Japanese aggression."

This sensational report was carried by the Shanghai "Nippo," one of the three local Japanese newspapers, yesterday morning. This daily and the Shanghai "Mainichi" displayed prominently long special articles describing in detail the alleged conflicting political currents now flowing in Nanking as a result of the developments in North China.

General Ho Ying-chin, Chinese Minister of War, and General Cheng Chien, Chief of Staff, were the two officers named by the "Nippo" in its report.

Pointing out that a war with Japan at the present moment would have a disastrous effect on the unification and military readjustment programmes of the Nanking Administration, they are alleged to have opposed immediate hostilities.

Year's Preparation

As a result they have come into direct conflict with the younger and more radical element in the Chinese Army which favours the launching of a large-scale war at once.

In the opinion of General Ho and General Cheng, a year's preparation would be necessary for waging a successful war against Japan.

These views they are stated to have communicated to General Chiang a few days ago, according to the "Nippo."

Members of the first graduating class of the Whampoa military academy, the alma mater of China's Nationalist Army, were further reported by the "Nippo" as favouring war against Japan at once.

The "Mainichi," in a special Nanking despatch, described General Chiang as finding himself "in a dilemma of his own making."

After utilizing anti-Japanism as a rallying cry for his programme of unification, the Chinese generalissimo was alleged to find himself in a predicament because of the sudden turn taken by the situation in the North.

Job Seekers

Alleged to be jockeying into a commanding position in Nanking's affairs, by taking advantage of these "difficulties," were said to be General Feng Yu-hsiang, the "Christian general" and vice-chairman of the Military Affairs Commission; Mr. Sun Fo, son of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and president of the Legislative Yuan, and other members of the allegedly "pro-Soviet" faction.

In an effort not to become further involved in this "difficult situation," General Chiang, the "Mainichi's" correspondent predicted, would avoid direct diplomatic negotiations with Japan; but would energetically seek to secure foreign mediation.

This procedure, the writer pointed out, would save General Chiang from "losing face" and thus would avert a threat to his present position of virtual dictator.

相信蒋介石将军
处境危殆

日本报纸勾勒领袖困境；
曾举国团结于抗日旗帜下，如今却无法遏制潮流

蒋介石委员长在其两位最高中国军事顾问的建议下，在接受“日本最低限度要求”后辞职，从而为中国未能“抵抗日本侵略”承担责任。

这一耸人听闻的报道由上海三家本地日文报纸之一的《上海日报》（Nippo）于昨日上午刊登。该报与《上海每日新闻》（Mainichi）显著刊载长篇特稿，详细描述了据称因华北事态发展而在南京流动的相互冲突的政治潮流。

《上海日报》在报道中指名的两位军官是中国军政部长何应钦将军和参谋总长程潜将军。

据称，他们指出目前与日本开战将对南京政府的统一和军事调整计划产生灾难性影响，因此反对立即发生敌对行动。

一年的准备

结果是，他们与中国军队中主张立即发动大规模战争的年轻激进派发生了直接冲突。

据何将军和程将军认为，要对日成功作战，需要一年的准备时间。

据《上海日报》称，他们在几天前将这些观点传达给了蒋将军。

《上海日报》还报道说，作为中国国民党军队母校的黄埔军校第一期毕业生成员，也主张立即对日作战。

《每日新闻》在一篇南京专电中形容蒋将军发现自己处于“自作自受的困境”。

报道称，这位中国委员长在利用反日情绪作为其统一计划的号召力之后，由于北方局势的突然转变，发现自己陷入了困境。

求职谋位者

据说，冯玉祥将军（“基督将军”兼军事委员会副委员长）、孙中山先生之子、立法院院长孙科先生，以及其他据称属于“亲苏”派系的成员，正利用这些“困难”，试图在南京事务中谋取主导地位。

《每日新闻》的记者预测，为了避免进一步卷入这种“困难局面”，蒋将军将避免与日本进行直接的外交谈判；但会积极寻求外国调停。

作者指出，这种做法将使蒋将军免于“丢面子”，从而避免对其目前实际独裁者地位的威胁。

随着日本武装部队完全控制平津地区，以及据称在华北两个主要城市建立亲日政权，目前的注意力集中在南京的下一步行动上，这可能意味着中日战争，或者中国屈服于日本侵略，这将涉及巨大的“面子损失”并可能引发反政府情绪的爆发。

上海的一般中国公众确实抱有南京打算对日作战的观念，其直接目标是收复北平和天津，更遥远的最终目标是收复满洲“失地”。

热度上升

同盟社昨日报道蒋介石将军命令部队从保定向北推进，尽管这一消息被审查员扣留，但通过报纸简报和无线电广播广泛传播，使战争狂热达到新的高潮。

许多中国观察家，特别是那些敦促并希望进行抗日战争的人，将南京最近的行动解释为迈向……[文字模糊]……救国会领导人……[文字模糊]……今日在苏州；宣布逮捕郭沫若的命令，这位著名作家在流亡日本10年后于周二悄悄回到上海；解除对包括建议的战歌《打回老家去》在内的“救国”歌曲的禁令，随后这些歌曲在南京中央广播电台播出；以及据报道红军从陕西向绥远进军，这些都是列举出的“战争准备”措施。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, AUGUST 1, 1937

Truce Pact
Here Said
Violated

Demarches Reported To
Be Made By Powers
To Chinese

Alleged Chinese violations of the
terms of the Shanghai truce agree-
ment have been made the subject
of international representations to
the Chinese authorities, the Shang-
hai "Nippo" reported yesterday.

Objections have been offered, the
Japanese daily said, to the increase
of the Peace Preservation Corps
strength from 3,000 men at the close
of the Shanghai "war" to 6,000; the
reconstruction of the Woosung
forts, and the construction of tren-
ches in the vicinity of Chenju.

The equipment, including the par-
tial motorisation of the Peace Pre-
servation Corps, has also been un-
favourably commented upon as con-
stituting a violation of the spirit of
the armistice agreement, the "Nip-
po" said.

These démarches were made, the
daily asserted, at a meeting held by
the representatives of four Powers,
parties to the original truce agree-
ment, held at the French Consulate-
General on June 28.

Also present were Japanese and
Chinese delegates, the latter being
headed by the then acting Mayor,
Mr. O. K. Yui.

据称此处
停战协定
遭违反

据报道列强
向中国提出交涉

据上海《日报》昨日报道，据称中国违反上海停战协定条款的行为，已成为向中国当局提出国际交涉的主题。

这家日本日报称，已提出反对意见的事项包括：和平警察总队（Peace Preservation Corps）的人数从上海“战争”结束时的3,000人增加到6,000人；重建吴淞炮台；以及在真如附近挖掘战壕。

《日报》称，包括和平警察总队部分摩托化在内的装备配备，也被不利地评论为构成违反停战协定的精神。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, July 31, 1937

City Government
Forbids Parades

Delicateness Of North
Situation Prompts
Precautions

Acting on instructions from the
City Government of Greater
Shanghai, Mr. Pan Kung-chan,
commissioner of Social Affairs,
yesterday issued orders prohibiting
unauthorized meetings, parades
and demonstrations in view of the
delicate situation prevailing in
Shanghai as result of the tension
in North China.

Anti-Japanese demonstrations
in Shanghai at this time may lead
to mob activities and international
complications, it is feared. While
all precautions are being taken by
the Chinese authorities to main-
tain peace and order in Shanghai,
no martial law has been proclaim-
ed, it is ascertained today.

Patriotic activities continue
among the Chinese despite the
disappointment over the Chinese
evacuation of Peiping and Tien-
tsin. Anticipating fresh hostili-
ties on a larger scale in North
China and, eventually, other areas
various "war service corps" and
first-aid corps are being organiz-
ed by Chinese public bodies.

The Chinese government bond
market remained closed today and
the official reason given was that
the Chinese Bond and Stock
Exchange, the sole market for
bond transactions, requires a two-
day closure to practice with the
new style book-keeping.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年7月31日，星期六

市政府
禁止游行

华北局势
微妙促使
采取预防措施

大上海市政府指示，社会局局长潘公展先生昨日发布命令，鉴于华北紧张局势导致上海局势微妙，禁止未经授权的集会、游行和示威。

人们担心，此时上海的反日示威可能导致暴民活动和国际纠纷。虽然中国当局正在采取一切预防措施以维持上海的和平与秩序，但据今日查明，并未宣布戒严。

尽管对中国撤离北平和天津感到失望，中国人的爱国活动仍在继续。鉴于预期华北乃至其他地区最终会发生更大规模的敌对行动，各种“战时服务团”和急救队正由中国公共团体组织成立。

中国政府债券市场今日依然关闭，给出的官方理由是，作为债券交易唯一市场的中国证券交易所，需要关闭两天以练习新的式样簿记方法。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, AUGUST 1, 1937

Atrocities Intensify China's
Determination To Resist Japan

Wires Pouring In To
Support Gen. Chiang's
Stand

DESTRUCTION
STIRS RESENTMENT

Country Will Not Toler-
ate Bogus Regime
For Hopei Prov.

NANKING, July 31.—(Central).—
The Japanese bombardment of
Tientsin with its heavy toll of
human lives and property has in-
tensified China's grim determination
to resist to the bitter end, a survey
of influential opinion in Nanking
by the Central News Agency reveals
today.

Telegrams pouring into the capital
show that the entire nation is rally-
ing to the stand enunciated by
General Chiang Kai-shek that there
will be no turning back once the
hostilities have started.

High officials interviewed this
morning are all of the opinion that
comparative quietude in the last 24
hours constitutes but an ominous
lull before the storm.

They quote General Chiang's words
that "the only thing to do is to put
into operation the government's
comprehensive plan for leading the
entire nation in a struggle to the
bitter end."

Nation Indignant

A wave of indignation sweeps over
the entire country as the details
of the alleged Japanese atrocities
are received from the war area in
the North.

Wholesale destruction of Nankai
University and other cultural insti-
tutions is bitterly denounced in
Chinese newspapers this morning.
The South Campus, which was
shelled yesterday, is reported to be
a mass of ruins. The library, con-
taining rare volumes, is said to have
been set on fire yesterday by Japan-
ese troops.

Chinese civilian refugees have
crowded the stations at Tientsin in
their efforts to escape from the bom-
bardment. Many were killed and
wounded when the station was
shelled. It is reported that the Jap-
anese prevented the Red Cross am-
bulances from reaching the wounded.

Racked To Death

According to the reports all vic-
tims with hands tied behind their
backs were apparently hacked to
death. Two of them were decapitat-
ed.

Questioned concerning reports of
a movement afoot to organise a so-
called "self-governing" body in Pei-
ping, Chinese officials unhesitatingly
declared that the movement was but
a device employed by the Japanese
to camouflage their military rule.

"Our experience in Mukden and
East Hopei," one official remarked,
"has made us familiar with this
Japanese method for extending do-
mination over the Chinese territory.
No pseudo-autonomous bodies could
exist anywhere in China without
the presence of Japanese troops."

"It is out of question," he added,
"that North China would for a
single instant tolerate the creation
of a bogus regime in the Peiping and
Tientsin area."

Japanese Atrocities

TIENTSIN, July 31.—(Central).—
Eyewitness accounts of Japanese
atrocities in Tientsin continued to
flood the editorial rooms and news
offices here today.

At Tungku Hutung Japanese
soldiers were seen sprinkling
kerosene on Chinese homes, which
they subsequently set of fire. Then
without any warning they machine-
gunned the frightened people as the
latter rushed out from their burn-
ing houses.

On Yuhwa Road in the Chin-
ese area where the Headquarters of the
29th Army was located, Japanese
soldiers pursued their methodical
way of killing Chinese civilians.

Japanese machine-gunners brought
down from the roof-tops raked the
streets and made the target
of the innocent Japanese rifles and
machine guns.

Adding insult to injury Japan-
ese soldiers in many instances pre-
vented Chinese from burying their
dead. In one case a group of Chi-
nese who attempted to remove the
bodies of their relatives were shot
down by Japanese soldiers.

《字林西报》，1937年8月1日，星期日

暴行加剧中国抗日决心

电文纷至沓来
支持蒋介石将军之立场

破坏激起愤慨

国家不容忍河北省的伪政权

南京，7月31日.—（中央社）.— 中央通讯社今日对南京有影响力舆论的调查显示，日军轰炸天津造成巨大的人员伤亡和财产损失，这加剧了中国抗战到底的严峻决心。

涌向首都的电报显示，举国上下正团结在蒋介石将军所阐明的立场上，即战端一旦开启，便绝无退路。

今晨接受采访的高级官员均认为，过去24小时的相对平静不过是暴风雨前不祥的沉寂。

他们引用蒋介石将军的话说：“唯一要做的是实施政府领导全国进行殊死斗争的全面计划。”

举国愤慨

随着来自北方战区的所谓日军暴行细节传来，一股愤怒浪潮席卷全国。

今晨，中国报纸严厉谴责南开大学及其他文化机构遭到大规模破坏。据报道，昨日遭炮击的南校区已是一片废墟。据说，藏有珍本图书的图书馆于昨日被日军纵火焚烧。

中国平民难民为躲避轰炸，挤满了天津的各火车站。车站遭炮击时，许多人死伤。据报道，日军阻止红十字会救护车接近伤者。

折磨致死

据报告，所有双手被反绑在背后的受害者显然均被砍杀致死。其中两人被斩首。

当被问及有关在北平组织所谓“自治”机构的运动报道时，中国官员毫不犹豫地声明，该运动不过是日本人为掩盖其军事统治而使用的手段。

一位官员评论道：“我们在沈阳和冀东的经验，使我们熟悉了日本人这种扩展对中国领土统治的方法。没有日军的存在，中国任何地方都不可能存在伪自治机构。”

他补充说：“华北绝不会容忍在北平和天津地区建立伪政权，哪怕是一瞬间。”

日军暴行

天津，7月31日.—（中央社）.— 今日，关于日军在天津暴行的目击者叙述继续涌入这里的编辑室和新闻机构。

在佟家胡同，有人看见日本士兵在中国人的房屋上洒煤油，随后放火焚烧。然后，他们在没有任何警告的情况下，用机枪扫射从燃烧的房屋中冲出的惊恐人群。

在位于华界、第二十九军司令部所在的玉华路，日本士兵有条不紊地屠杀中国平民。

从屋顶撤下的日本机枪手扫射街道，使无辜百姓成为日本步枪和机枪的靶子。

日本士兵在许多情况下还阻止中国人埋葬死者，可谓雪上加霜。在一个案例中，一群试图移走亲属尸体的中国人被日本士兵开枪射杀。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, AUGUST 1, 1937

News Briefs
On North
China Crisis

26,543 Youths Conscripted
Altogether 26,543 out of a total
of 32,305 youths between the ages
of 20 and 25 have been enlisted in
Nanking under the Conscription
Act which is being enforced here.
According to figures from the
local conscription office, 2,779 per-
sons have been exempted from
ordinary conscription while 2,897
others have been allowed to post-
pone their enlistment to a later
date owing to various reasons says
Central News.

Wedding Ring Contributed
HANKOW, July 31.—(Central).—
A gold wedding ring and an earpick
have been received by the local
Association for the Support of
Armed Resistance against Japan as
contributions to the “war chest.”

Japanese Active In Tsingtao
TSINGTAO, July 31.—(Central).—
Japanese plain-clothes men, dis-
guised as Chinese, are reported to
be active here, attempting to spy
into Chinese military secrets,
against which the Chinese au-
thorities are taking precautionary
measures.
With the outbreak of Sino-
Japanese hostilities in the Tientsin-
Peiping area, another batch of over
100 Japanese residents have
evacuated various cities along the
Kiaotai Railway and arrived here.

Japanese Quit Hangchow
SHANGHAI, July 31.—(Domei).—
Alarmed by the events in North
China, 23 Japanese women and
children arrived here from Hang-
chow on Friday.
Included among them was Mrs.
Yuse Matsumura, the wife of the
Japanese Vice-consul at Hangchow,
and their three children.
The group was escorted by Chief
Masakichi Yamakita of the Hang-
chow Japanese Consular Police,
who returned to the Chekiang city
early yesterday morning.

Generals In Chengchow
CHENGCHOW, July 30.—(Kuo-
min).—General Hsu Tung-cheng,
Director of the Administrative
Office of the Military Affairs Com-
mission; General Hsiung Shih-hui,
Chairman of the Kiangsi Provincial
Government, and Lieut.-General
Hsiung Fu, Vice-Chief of the Gen-
eral Staff, arrived here from Nan-
king by airplane yesterday. They
subsequently entrained for Pao-
ting, provincial capital of Hopeh, to confer
with General Sung Che-yuan,
Chairman of the Hopeh-Chahar
Political Affairs Council and
Commander of the 29th Army, con-
cerning further resistance against
the Japanese.

Shanghai journalist, Mr. Wang
Yun-sheng of the Ta Kung Pao,
and Mr. Hu Yu-chih. The party
disbanded at 7 o’clock p.m.

Irregulars To Renew Attack
TAIYUAN, July 31.—(Central).—
“Manchukuo” and Mongol irregulars
are making plans for a renewed
attack on Suiyuan following the
dramatic turn in the Peiping-Tien-
tsin situation, according to messages
received here.
In view of the grave situation,
General Yen Hsi-shan, Pacification
Commissioner for Shansi and Sui-
yuan, has instructed his troops on
the front to take precautions against
any emergencies.

Envoys See Hsu Mo
NANKING, July 31.—(Kuomin).—
Sir Hughe Montgomery-Knatchbull
Hugessen, the British Ambassador,
called on Mr. Hsu Mo, Political
Vice-Minister of Foreign Affairs,
yesterday at 4 p.m. regarding the
Northern situation.
Dr. Oskar P. Trautmann, the
German Ambassador, also called on
Mr. Hsu Mo in the same connection.

Honda Calls In Nanking
NANKING, July 31.—(Kuomin).—
Commander T. Honda, Japanese
Naval Attache, called yesterday on
General Tsao Hao-sen, Political
Vice-Minister of War, and Admiral
Chen Shao-kuan, Minister of the
Navy.
In the course of the interviews,
Commander Honda said that the
Japanese Third Fleet regretted the
outbreak of hostilities between the
Chinese and Japanese troops in the
Peiping Tientsin area. Every effort
will be made to prevent the
incident from spreading to other
parts of the country, he said, but
in the latter eventuality the Japan-
ese Third Fleet cannot but adopt
all necessary measures.
He hoped that the Chinese au-
thorities will prevent the outbreak
of unfortunate incidents in Central
and South China.

《字林西报》，1937年8月1日，星期日

华北危机
新闻简报

征召青年26,543人
在此地实施的《兵役法》下，年龄在20至25岁之间的32,305名青年中，共有26,543人在南京应征入伍。据当地征兵办公室的数据，中央社称，2,779人被免除普通兵役，另有2,897人因各种原因获准推迟入伍日期。

捐赠结婚戒指
汉口，7月31日.—（中央社）.— 当地支援武装抗日协会收到一枚金结婚戒指和一个挖耳勺，作为对“战争基金”的捐款。

日人在青岛活动频繁
青岛，7月31日.—（中央社）.— 据报道，伪装成中国人的日本便衣人员在此地活动，企图刺探中国军事机密，中国当局正对此采取预防措施。
随着天津-北平地区中日敌对行动的爆发，另一批超过100名日本居民已从胶济铁路沿线各城市撤离并抵达此地。

日本人离开杭州
上海，7月31日.—（同盟社）.— 受华北事态惊吓，23名日本妇女和儿童于周五从杭州抵达此地。
其中包括日本驻杭州副领事松村勇介（Yuse Matsumura，音译）的夫人及其三个孩子。
该团体由杭州日本领事馆警察署长山kita正吉（Masakichi Yamakita，音译）护送，他于昨天清晨返回浙江这座城市。

将领们在郑州
郑州，7月30日.—（《国民日报》）.— 军事委员会办公厅主任徐庭瑶将军、江西省政府主席熊式辉将军以及参谋本部次长熊飞中将，昨日乘飞机从南京抵达此地。随后他们乘火车前往河北省会保定，与冀察政务委员会委员长兼第二十九军指挥官宋哲元将军会晤，商讨进一步抗日事宜。

《大公报》记者王芸生先生和胡愈之先生。该团于下午7时解散。

非正规军将重新发动进攻
太原，7月31日.—（中央社）.— 据此处收到的消息，随着北平-天津局势的戏剧性转变，“满洲国”和蒙古非正规军正计划重新进攻绥远。
鉴于局势严重，晋绥绥靖主任阎锡山将军已指示前线部队警惕任何紧急情况。

使节会见徐谟
南京，7月31日.—（《国民日报》）.— 英国大使许阁森爵士（Sir Hughe Montgomery-Knatchbull Hugessen）昨日下午4时就北方局势拜访了外交部政务次长徐谟先生。
德国大使陶德曼博士（Dr. Oskar P. Trautmann）也就同一事宜拜访了徐谟先生。

本田在南京拜会
南京，7月31日.—（《国民日报》）.— 日本海军武官本田少佐（Commander T. Honda）昨日拜访了军政部政务次长曹浩森将军和海军部长陈绍宽上将。
在会谈过程中，本田少佐表示，日本第三舰队对北平天津地区中日军队之间爆发敌对行动表示遗憾。他说，将尽一切努力防止事态蔓延到该国其他地区，但若发生后者情况，日本第三舰队不得不采取一切必要措施。
他希望中国当局能防止华中和华南地区发生不幸事件。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, AUGUST 1, 1937
23263

NO MASS MEETINGS,
PARADES ALLOWED

Precautionary Measures by
Chinese Authorities

SHANGHAI SITUATION
REMAINS QUIET

Mass meetings and processions have been prohibited by the Shanghai City Government. A circular order to this effect has been distributed among local public bodies and labour unions by the Bureau of Social Affairs.

This action is taken by the authorities to avoid any untoward incident when extreme tension prevails in the north. Special precautionary measures for the maintenance of peace and order are understood to have been taken by the Chinese Police and military organisations. Hongkew and the Northern area generally remained quiet yesterday, with a dwindling exodus of Chapel residents leaving their houses and shops for districts south of the Soochow Creek. In many cases it was only a matter of shifting the most valued possessions to safer ground and then return to the old residence. The evacuation was considerably smaller than on Friday, when it was not really large. Rickshaws again were the favourite means of removal.

Situation Discussed

Measures to meet any emergency were discussed by local civic leaders and bankers in separate gatherings. Mr. Sun Fo, President of the Legislative Yuan, invited local businessmen to his residence in Columbia Road on Friday, when their hearty support to the Government was encouraged and discussed. Local Chinese bankers also met and discussed the financial situation with Mr. T. V. Soong, Chairman of the Bank of China and member of the Standing Committee of the National Economic Commission. Mr. Hsu Kai, Vice-Minister of Finance, also arrived from Nanking. Measures for the stabilisation of the monetary and other markets were discussed.

In a telegram to its branch offices all over China, the Chinese Red Cross Association asks that immediate preparations be made for the organisation of first aid corps. The Red Swastika Association is maintaining four such corps in the north. Local charity organisations are planning to establish war refugee camps in the north.

A meeting of Chinese insurance firms is scheduled to take place tomorrow when opinions on the insurance policy will be solicited.

Communications Disrupted

Communications between Shanghai and Peiping have been severed, while those to Tientsin are partially disrupted. Aeroplanes to Tientsin now land at Tsingtao. The express train from the north arrived from Tangkuantsun, are station below Tientsin, yesterday morning, while the north-bound express is expected to make Chungchow as the terminus. Mails to the north are still accepted. Radio and telegraphic communications with Tientsin are open.

Employees Quit Work

More than 100 Chinese employees and domestic servants in local Japanese firms and homes have quit their service during the past few days, states a report to the "China Times." This voluntary withdrawal of the Chinese came in spite of Japanese offers to increase their salaries or otherwise improve their treatment.

As a result of the boycott, it is reported, the Japanese firms and homes concerned have been compelled to take White Russians into their employ.

Among the most publicized of these cases is one concerning Wang Ah-yu, a rickshaw puller employed by a Japanese family for more than 20 years, who finally left the service in accordance with "the dictates of his conscience."

《字林西报》，1937年8月1日，星期日
23263

禁止举行群众集会
和游行

中国当局的预防措施

上海局势
保持平静

上海市政府已禁止群众集会和游行。社会局已向当地公共团体和工会分发了一份以此为目的的通令。

当局采取这一行动是为了在北方紧张局势极度严峻之际避免任何意外事件。据悉，中国警察和军事组织已采取特别预防措施以维持和平与秩序。虹口及北部地区总体保持平静，离开住所和店铺前往苏州河以南地区的闸北居民外流逐渐减少。在许多情况下，这只是将最珍贵的财物转移到更安全的地方，然后返回原住处。此次撤离规模远小于周五，而周五的规模实际上也不大。黄包车再次成为搬迁的首选交通工具。

讨论局势

地方士绅领袖和银行家在各自的聚会中讨论了应对任何紧急情况的措施。立法院院长孙科先生于周五邀请当地商人到其哥伦比亚路寓所，鼓励并讨论他们对政府的大力支持。当地中国银行家也与中国银行董事长、国民经济委员会常务委员宋子文先生会面，讨论金融形势。财政部次长徐堪先生也从南京抵达。会议讨论了稳定货币及其他市场的措施。

中国红十字会在给其遍布中国的分支机构的电报中，要求立即准备组建急救队。红卍字会在北方维持着四个这样的队伍。当地慈善组织正计划在北方建立战时难民收容所。

定于明天召开中国保险公司会议，届时将征求对保险政策的意见。

通讯中断

上海与北平之间的通讯已中断，而与天津的通讯部分中断。飞往天津的飞机现在在青岛降落。北上的特快列车昨天早晨从天津下方的塘沽站抵达，而北行特快列车预计将以郑州为终点站。寄往北方的邮件仍然受理。与天津的无线电和电报通讯畅通。

雇员辞职

一份向《时事新报》提交的报告称，在过去几天里，当地日本公司和家庭中的100多名中国雇员和家仆已辞去职务。尽管日本人提出加薪或以其他方式改善待遇，这些中国人仍自愿离职。

据报道，由于抵制运动，相关的日本公司和家庭被迫雇佣白俄人。
在这些广为宣传的案例中，最引人注目的一个是关于王阿玉（Wang Ah-yu，音译），他在一个日本家庭担任黄包车夫超过20年，最终依照“良心的指引”离开了服务岗位。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, AUGUST 1, 1937

Groups Rally
To Support
Of Defenders

Shanghai Feverishly Or-
ganizing For Emer-
gency Service

Rallying to the aid of their coun-
try, several other organizations in
Shanghai announced yesterday plans
to co-operate with the National
Government in fighting the Japan-
ese invaders.

Nearly every organized group in
the city, from the taipans to the
$30-a-month office workers, are
mapping plans to help the Chinese
armies. The women also are or-
ganizing for war work, with activi-
ties centered about the Chinese
Women's Club, which will hold an
emergency meeting Monday. Even
children are being organised with
several Boy Scout units in Shanghai
being called out in the mobilisa-
tion of 500,000 scouts over 15 order-
ed by Nanking.

Answering the call of the National
Government, the National Y.M.C.A.
of China has established a hospital
in Paoting to care for wounded
soldiers.

Seventy-seven injured men were
cared for in the hospital on the first
day of operation, July 27.

Y.M.C.A. Launches Drive

A drive to raise $60,000 for war
work, the first phase of which is
the care of wounded soldiers, is
being launched by the Y.M.C.A.

Headquarters of the Emergency
Service for Soldiers Committee
have been established at the Na-
tional Committee Y.M.C.A., 131
Museum Road.

The Y.M.C.A. is not recruiting
volunteer workers yet as it has suf-
ficient workers at present in the
war area. Mr. D. W. Edwards,
regional Secretary for North China
of the Y.M.C.A., is directing the
work at present.

Mr. Chester Chan, General Secret-
ary of the Tientsin Y.M.C.A., has
also been sent up to Tientsin es-
pecially to supervise the war work.
The Shanghai Christian Federa-
tion, which includes representatives
of nearly all of the Christian bodies
in Shanghai met Friday to make
plans for emergency service.

that it will co-operate with the
Y.M.C.A. in its work on the north-
ern front so as not to conflict with
the association.

Meanwhile, the federation will
launch a drive to raise money to
carry on these activities.

The hospital at Paoting of the
Y.M.C.A. is the first hospital for
wounded soldiers established in the
North. The Red Cross Society of
China is also making plans now to
organize a first aid unit to send
to North China.

A special emergency meeting to
map plans for war work
will be held by the Chinese Women's
Club at its clubhouse tomorrow at
4.30 p.m. The members are asked
to bring suggestions on what the
club can do.

The main program of war work,
however, is centered about the
All-Shanghai Armed Resistance As-
sociation, which has launched a
financial drive to aid Chinese
troops on the Northern front.

Donations are being received at
some 404 local banks and newspa-
pers.

At least 6,000 sets of short-sleev-
ed shirts and shorts are in demand
for the wounded Chinese soldiers
on the Northern Front, according
to an interview with officials of the
All-Shanghai Armed-Resistance As-
sociation.

Each set costs around $1.10. The
association made a plea to the
Chinese community in Shanghai for
donations either in the form of
clothing material in order to meet
the demand. These donations will
be received at the Red Cross So-
ciety of China, 363 Avenue Haig.

For fear that anti-Japanese de-
monstrations in Shanghai may lead
to mob activities or international
complications, local organisations
and guilds have been warned by
the Bureau of Social Affairs of
the City Government of Greater
Shanghai not to hold unauthorised
meetings or parades in view of the
national crisis.

《字林西报》，1937年8月1日，星期日

各界集结
支援
守军

上海正狂热地组织
紧急服务

为援助祖国，上海其他几个组织昨日宣布计划，与国民政府合作抗击日本侵略者。

本市几乎每一个有组织的团体，从大班到月薪30美元的职员，都在制定协助中国军队的计划。妇女们也在组织战时工作，活动以中华妇女俱乐部为中心，该俱乐部将于周一召开紧急会议。甚至儿童也被组织起来，南京下令动员50万名15岁以上的童子军，上海的几个童子军团已被征召参与此次动员。

中华基督教青年会全国协会响应国民政府的号召，已在保定设立了一家医院，用于照料受伤士兵。

7月27日，即医院运营的第一天，共有77名伤员在该院得到救治。

青年会发起募捐运动

基督教青年会正发起一项为战时工作筹集6万美元的运动，其第一阶段工作是照料受伤士兵。

军人紧急服务委员会的总部已设在博物馆路131号的中华基督教青年会全国协会内。

基督教青年会目前尚未招募志愿工作人员，因为战区现有人员已足够。基督教青年会华北区干事D. W. Edwards先生目前正主持这项工作。

天津基督教青年会总干事Chester Chan先生也已专程派往天津，负责监督战时工作。上海基督教联合会（包括上海几乎所有基督教团体的代表）于周五开会，制定紧急服务计划。

该联合会表示，将在北方前线的工作中与基督教青年会合作，以免与该协会的工作发生冲突。

与此同时，联合会将发起一场募捐运动，以维持这些活动的开展。

基督教青年会在保定的医院是北方建立的第一所伤兵医院。中国红十字会目前也正计划组织一支急救队，派往华北。

中华妇女俱乐部将于明天下午4时30分在其会所举行特别紧急会议，制定战时工作计划。会员们被要求带来关于俱乐部能做些什么的建议。

然而，战时工作的主要项目集中在“全上海武装抗敌协会”，该协会已发起一场财务募捐运动，以援助北方前线的中国军队。

捐款正在约404家本地银行和报社接收。

据采访“全上海武装抗敌协会”官员得知，北方前线的中国伤兵至少需要6000套短袖衬衫和短裤。

每套成本约为1.10美元。该协会向上海华人社区呼吁，捐赠衣物材料以满足需求。这些捐赠将在海格路363号的中国红十字会接收。

出于担心上海的反日游行可能导致暴民活动或国际纠纷，大上海市政府社会局已警告当地组织和公会，鉴于国家危机，不得举行未经授权的集会或游行。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JULY 30, 1937
23329

Writer Sees
Need For Pact
With Soviets

U.S.S.R. Said Directly
Concerned In Sino-
Japan Conflict

By PERCY CHEN

Impending hostilities between China and Japan have disclosed that in Far Eastern Questions there are only three nations immediately interested and concerned. They are China herself, Soviet Russia and Japan.

Far Eastern Questions are those which concern the economic and political relations of these three countries. They are questions of the Asian mainland. And no matter how important the colony of Hong-kong may be to the defense scheme of Britain's possessions in the South Pacific, still the present state of British armament cannot permit her to interfere in the momentous events that are on the eve of taking place between China and Japan. That China has the goodwill of England is not left in doubt—after reading the expressions of the English Press both at home and abroad.

In the case of the U.S.A. she may be interested in questions of the Pacific Ocean. But these are not of the same fundamental character as those of the Asian Mainland which we Chinese understand as Far Eastern Problems. The questions involved in the Pacific Ocean, primarily questions of trade routes, are of such a nature that they can be said to change with the appearance of every new situation. For example, the interests of the U.S.A. today remain in the West Pacific inasmuch as the Philippine Islands have not achieved their full independence. But just as soon as Philippine independence is an accomplished fact, even this thin interest of the U.S.A. will disappear from the West Pacific Ocean.

Probably True

The latest developments have shown that my thesis concerning Britain's real power in the Far East is probably true. Britain has not the necessary strength in ships, men, and planes to influence events in China. It is well known that during the last Imperialist War Britain had to rely upon the Japanese navy and land forces for the protection of her possessions East of Colombo. And in the present world situation Britain's military and naval strength in Europe and in the Mediterranean being what it is, she is unable to send any considerable force to the Far East.

Had a rapprochement been achieved, the present critical situation might have been avoided or at least postponed for some time. We have more to gain than to lose by a postponement of the conflict. But this is well known to the Japanese militarists, who inflict war upon us because they fear the development of a strong China united under the leadership of the Kuomintang Government with general Chiang Kai-shek at its head.

Last December, in these pages, I offered four conditions for a rapprochement between Soviet Russia and China. They were:

1. The agreement must be for the maintenance of peace in the Far East.
2. The agreement must be open and invested with the sanction of the League of Nations.
3. It must be on the basis of equality, including the respect of the internal structure of each country.
4. The agreement must be concluded between the two governments.

A Stabilising Force

Had such a rapprochement taken place during the last six months, it is probable that the peace of the Far East would not have been in so precarious a situation, if not actually broken by the thunder of warfare between China and Japan. The stabilising strength of any agreement between China and Soviet Russia would have deterred Japan from taking steps to provoke hostilities, as she did at Lukouchiao against China and as she did on the Amur a few weeks ago against Soviet Russia.

As we now know, the provocation against Russia at the Amur island "Bolshoi" was to test the temper of the Russian Government. Japan found that the Russians were not to be drawn into a fight over such a small affair and concluded, wrongly no doubt, that Russia is weak or does not want to fight. Litvinoff' statement however "that any attack by Japan on the territory of Soviet Russia will call forth violent resistance and death to the invaders" indicates that the Russians are both ready and prepared for eventualities.

Such an agreement would therefore have worked in favor of peace and not against it. It is not too late for China and Soviet Russia to reach an agreement between themselves setting their intentions vis-a-vis each other on record and thus accept the guaranteeing of each other's security, in so far as it lies in the power of each other power to do so, to be the principle underlying their fundamental relations. This would not be an treaty of alliance or even of mutual assistance, but it would clear the air between the two countries and release Chinese troops, that might be otherwise engaged in protecting frontiers, for use against the invading forces of the Japanese.

Decline Of League Seen

The decline and the final death of the League of Nations as a political organ for world peace is now at hand. The second point therefore falls out of the picture. But the foreign powers who are interested in World Peace and in confining the conflict if possible to the Far East and not allow it to develop into a world war would look upon such an agreement between China and Soviet Russia with favor.

Such an agreement would lessen the responsibilities of the Soviet Government on the outlying frontiers between Soviet Russia and China, thereby freeing their troops for guaranteeing the status quo existing in Europe and particularly in Eastern Europe.

The complete unity that now prevails throughout China, in which all classes and all parties are united for the sacred war against the Japanese armies means that the third condition has already been fulfilled. And an agreement between China and Soviet Russia would not mean that China was going to adopt the Communist faith any more than does the French Mutual Assistance pact with Soviet Russia mean that the French have gone Communist.

There is no reason to mention the last condition, since the Kuomintang Government under the leadership of Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek is at the head of the entire country and as such is in friendly intercourse with the Soviet Russian Government.

Even at this last eleventh hour a rapprochement between China and Soviet Russia may still be the antidote to the poison of destruction and bitter warfare in which the war machine of Japanese Imperialism is trying to involve the Far East. And such a war, unless such an antidote is applied, cannot but develop into a second Imperialist World War.

《字林西报》，1937年7月30日，星期五
23329

作者认为
需与苏联
缔结协定

据称苏联直接
关切中日冲突

作者：陈依范 (Percy Chen)

中日之间迫在眉睫的敌对行动表明，在远东问题上，只有三个国家直接感兴趣并受到牵涉。它们是中国本身、苏维埃俄国和日本。

远东问题是指涉及这三个国家经济和政治关系的问题。它们是亚洲大陆的问题。无论香港殖民地对于英国在南太平洋属地的防御方案多么重要，英国目前的军备状况仍不允许其干涉中日之间即将发生的重大事件。阅读了英国国内外报刊的言论后，中国拥有英国的善意这一点毫无疑问。

就美国而言，它可能对太平洋问题感兴趣。但这些问题的性质与我们中国人理解为远东问题的亚洲大陆根本性问题不同。涉及太平洋的问题，主要是贸易路线问题，其性质可以说随着每一种新局势的出现而变化。例如，由于菲律宾群岛尚未获得完全独立，美国今天的利益仍留在西太平洋。但一旦菲律宾独立成为既成事实，即使美国在西太平洋的这一微薄利益也将消失。

可能是真的

最新事态发展表明，我关于英国在远东真正实力的论点可能是正确的。英国没有必要的舰船、人员和飞机力量来影响中国的事态。众所周知，在上次帝国主义战争期间，英国不得不依靠日本海军和陆军来保护其科伦坡以东的属地。而在当前的世界局势下，英国在欧洲和地中海的军事和海军力量既然如此，她便无法向远东派遣任何可观的部队。

如果实现了和解，目前的危急局势或许可以避免，或者至少推迟一段时间。推迟冲突对我们利大于弊。但这一点日本军国主义者也很清楚，他们之所以向我们发动战争，是因为他们害怕在蒋介石将军领导下的国民党政府领导下出现一个统一强大的中国。

去年十二月，我在本版提出了苏维埃俄国与中国实现和解的四个条件。它们是：

1. 协定必须是为了维护远东和平。
2. 协定必须是公开的，并获得国际联盟的认可。
3. 必须建立在平等的基础上，包括尊重各国的内部结构。
4. 协定必须在两国政府之间缔结。

一种稳定力量

如果在过去六个月里实现了这样的和解，远东的和平可能不会处于如此岌岌可危的境地，即便没有被中日之间的战争雷霆实际打破。中苏之间任何协定的稳定力量都会阻止日本采取步骤挑衅敌对行动，就像她此前在卢沟桥对中国所做的那样，以及几周前在阿穆尔河（黑龙江）对苏维埃俄国所做的那样。

正如我们现在所知，在阿穆尔河岛屿“博利绍伊”岛（Bolshoi）对俄国的挑衅是为了试探俄国政府的脾气。日本发现俄国人不会被卷入这样一件小事的争斗中，并得出结论（无疑是不正确的），即俄国软弱或不想打仗。然而，李维诺夫声明“日本对苏维埃俄国领土的任何攻击都将招致猛烈抵抗，入侵者将被消灭”，这表明俄国人已经为各种可能发生的情况做好了准备。

因此，这样的协定将有利于和平，而不是不利于和平。中国和苏维埃俄国现在达成协议，记录彼此对对方的意图，从而接受相互保证安全（在各自能力范围内），以此作为双方基本关系的基础，这还为时不晚。这不会是一个同盟条约，甚至不是互助条约，但它将澄清两国之间的关系，并释放原本可能用于保卫边境的中国军队，使其能够用于对抗日本的入侵部队。

国联的衰落可见

国际联盟作为世界和平政治机构的衰落和最终消亡现已近在眼前。因此，第二点已不再适用。但是，那些关心世界和平、希望尽可能将冲突限制在远东而不让其发展为世界大战的外国列强，将会看好中国与苏维埃俄国之间的这种协定。

这样的协定将减轻苏维埃政府在苏俄与中国偏远边境上的责任，从而腾出部队来保证欧洲，特别是东欧现有的现状。

目前遍及中国的完全统一，即所有阶级和所有政党团结起来进行反对日军的神圣战争，意味着第三个条件已经得到满足。中国与苏维埃俄国之间的协定并不意味着中国将要采用共产主义信仰，正如法国与苏维埃俄国的互助协定并不意味着法国人已经变成共产主义者一样。

没有必要提及最后一个条件，因为在蒋介石委员长领导下的国民党政府统领全国，并因此与苏维埃俄国政府保持着友好交往。

即使在这最后时刻，中国与苏维埃俄国之间的和解仍然可能是解毒剂，以对抗日本帝国主义战争机器试图让远东陷入的毁灭和残酷战争的毒害。除非施用这种解毒剂，否则这场战争不可避免地会发展为第二次帝国主义世界大战。

Ministry Of Finance
Checks Manipulators
In Government Bonds
7994
5

Minimum Price Level On
All Issues Fixed By
Government

BROKERS CALL
SPECIAL MEETING

New System Of Account-
ing Enforced Under
Ministry Ruling

In an effort to prevent speculators
from using the North China crisis
to manipulate the market, the Min-
istry of Finance, in an order yes-
terday, has set the minimum price
for the various issues of Government
bonds on the Chinese Stock and
Bond Exchange.

The action yesterday followed
the reopening of the market which
had been closed since Wednesday
to allow for the settlement of ac-
counts and enable the brokers to
learn the new system of account-
ing.

As a result of currency of rumors
on the exchange yesterday morning
and the general uneasiness among
the operators, quotations for all is-
sues of bonds dropped to the
minimum set by the Ministry. The
decline amounted from 30 cents to
$2 as compared with the closing
rates Tuesday.

In its order to the Exchange of-
ficials yesterday, the Ministry point-
ed out that there has always been
confidence in Government bonds,
which have been strengthened dur-
ing the past several years as a
result of the measures taken by
the government.

The recent decline, which threat-
ens to create turmoil in the coun-
try's financial set-up, as chiefly
the result of speculative activities
of operators who attempted to use
the North China crisis as an easy
road to profit. To prevent such
attempts, a minimum scale for
bond prices will be established the
order announced. Transactions under
the limit set by the Ministry will
be declared void and brokers were
warned not to do any trading out-
side the market.

The scales set by the Ministry
are: Issue "O," and "T," $7.80; Is-
sue "C" $7.80; Issue "B" $7.50;
Issue "A" $6.80.

Following the receipt of the Min-
istry's order, brokers on the ex-
change called a meeting at 11
o'clock to discuss the situation.
While the operators present
unanimously pledged their support
of the Ministry's effort to avert a
serious price drop, it was pointed
out that the order might seriously
curtail trading. Several brokers
were anxious to confer with the
members of the Board of the Ex-
change regarding their new sys-
tem.

Trading on the market yesterday
was limited to bonds of August de-

政府规定所有发行债券的最低价格水平

经纪人召开特别会议

根据财政部令强制执行新会计制度

为防止投机者利用华北危机操纵市场，财政部于昨日发布命令，规定了在中国证券市场上交易的各类政府公债的最低价格。

昨日的举措紧随市场重新开放之后。该市场自上周三起关闭，以便进行账目结算，并使经纪人熟悉新的会计制度。

由于昨日上午交易所内谣言流传，加之经营者普遍感到不安，所有债券的报价均跌至财政部规定的最低限度。与周二收盘价相比，跌幅在30美分至2美元之间。

财政部在昨日致交易所官员的命令中指出，公众对政府公债一直抱有信心，而过去几年政府采取的措施进一步加强了这种信心。

最近的下跌主要是一些经营者试图利用华北危机作为牟取暴利的捷径，进行投机活动所致，这威胁到要在国家金融体系中造成混乱。为防止此类企图，命令宣布将建立债券价格的最低标准。低于财政部规定限额的交易将被宣布无效，并警告经纪人不得在场外进行任何交易。

财政部规定的价格标准如下：“O”类和“T”类发行券，7.80美元；“C”类发行券，7.80美元；“B”类发行券，7.50美元；“A”类发行券，6.80美元。

收到财政部命令后，交易所经纪人在11点钟召开会议讨论局势。虽然与会经营者一致承诺支持财政部为避免价格严重下跌所作的努力，但有人指出，该命令可能会严重限制交易。几位经纪人急于就新制度与交易所理事会成员进行磋商。

昨日的市场交易仅限于八月交割的债券。尽管有许多九月发行券的卖盘，但买家倾向于观望，因此未达成任何交易。

与此同时，交易所官员昨日也采取行动，制止市场上的投机行为。保证金要求从400美元增加至600美元。

“B”类——9.55美元

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, AUGUST 3, 1937

A Quaint Argument

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—You are logical and by no means too severe in pointing out the "misconceptions" of Japanese efforts to size up the situation. It seems to me that you might also take note of "misconceptions" in certain British views. In "Oriental Affairs", a British-edited paper the crisis is dealt with in an article which after referring to the lack of good will on either side and the "strong under-current of tension" existing for many months delivers the following truly astonishing rebuke to the Chinese:

The Japanese were exasperated at their failure to make any progress in their programme for "economic cooperation," and Nanking's obstruction by insisting upon the prior settlement of political issues.

Perhaps this might pass from a Japanese but from nowhere else. In recent months I believe Great Britain and Japan have experienced difficulties in agreeing upon economic co-operation. Does that justify the argument that assuming one or other is "exasperated" by the delay there should be a coming and going of troops on the other soil so that if the inevitable clash comes military chastisement may be inflicted on the sinner? You yourself have more suitably referred to this question of co-operation by observing:

The main difference between the Chinese and Japanese Governments has, in the meantime, been ignored. Both are ready for economic co-operation, but China desires to have the political situation in North China defined before precise steps are taken to fulfil that common need. Japan does not see the necessity for this clarification but would proceed at once to enter into business agreements without the intrusion of political issues. There may be good ground for either point of view, but it seems to the detached observer that Japan is not doing herself justice if she thinks that the Gordian knot can be cut by the sword.

I cannot believe that "Oriental Affairs" in the article referred to is presenting a point of view which any decent British resident in China will endorse even though I am a
TREATYPORTER.
Shanghai, Aug. 2.

（批：UM）

一种奇特的论点

致《字林西报》编辑先生：

先生，您在指出日本方面对局势判断的“误解”时，逻辑严密且绝非过于严厉。在我看来，您或许也可以注意到某些英国观点中的“误解”。在英国编辑的刊物《东方事务》（Oriental Affairs）中，有一篇文章在提及双方缺乏善意以及数月来存在的“强烈的紧张暗流”后，对中国人发出了以下真正令人震惊的指责：

日本人因其在“经济合作”计划中未能取得任何进展而感到恼怒，而南京坚持要求先解决政治问题，从而构成了阻碍。

这种说法也许出自日本人之口尚可理解，但绝不应出自其他任何地方。我相信，近几个月来，英国和日本在经济合作问题上也难以达成一致。这是否足以证明这样的论点是合理的：假设其中一方因延误而“恼怒”，就应在另一方的土地上调动军队，以便当不可避免的冲突发生时，可以对“罪人”施加军事惩罚？您本人更恰当地提到了这个合作问题，您观察到：

与此同时，中日两国政府之间的主要分歧被忽视了。双方都愿意进行经济合作，但中国希望在采取具体步骤满足这一共同需求之前，先明确华北的政治局势。日本则认为没有澄清的必要，希望在不涉及政治问题的情况下立即进入商业协定。两种观点可能都有其合理之处，但在旁观者看来，如果日本认为可以用剑斩断戈耳狄俄斯之结（Gordian knot），那她并没有公正地对待自己。

我无法相信，《东方事务》在上述文章中提出的观点会得到任何在华体面英国居民的认可，尽管我是一名
条约港居民（TREATYPORTER）。
上海，8月2日。

（批：UM）

Mme. Chiang Sees Date
Final Victory To
Vindicate Honor

China Said Forced To Make Sacrifice Now To Erase Humiliation
WOMEN URGED TO UNITE FOR ACTION
Important Feminine Role In Struggle Pointed Out

NANKING, Aug. 1.—(Central).—As China is forced to make the supreme sacrifice for the sake of her national honor, Madame Chiang Kai-shek, in a speech today, predicted that “a final victory, no matter how belated it may be in coming, will erase forever the humiliation days that have for so long crowded our calendar and remove the sorrow that has for years past bent our heads and bowed our hearts.”

Speaking before a group of delegates of women’s organizations at 4:15 o’clock this afternoon, Mme. Chiang urged them to form a united body to comfort and support the nation’s defenders. The speech follows:

“Today we meet with the nation facing the gravest crisis in its history. It is with great sorrow that we find it necessary to come together under the shadow of war, for war is a terrible thing. It means that we must sacrifice a large number of our soldiers; masses of our innocent people; much of the nation’s wealth and resources, and see ruthlessly destroyed a considerable amount of reconstruction that we have been working upon so successfully for the past ten years. But sometimes it is necessary that we make the supreme sacrifice for the sake of our national honor. Now that our Government clearly has demonstrated that we have borne all suffering that a self-respecting people can possibly bear, we must unhesitatingly and with courage throw the last ounce of strength and energy into an effort to secure national survival. There is nothing left for us to do but to obey the orders of the Government and fortify others to do likewise.

Women Have Big Roll

“Today, every one of us Chinese must fight according to our ability. In order to preserve national unity and defend ourselves against aggression. We women are citizens just as much as are our men. Our positions, our capabilities and our line of usefulness may be different but each must do that which best can be done to strengthen our forces and rescue our nation from peril always.

“Wherever there is work for our hands to do, we must strive to do it. Today in Spain women are standing in the fighting lines with their men; and during the Great War in every country they gave of their best to aid in the realization of victory. No woman of China is one whit less patriotic or less courageous or less capable of physical endurance than our sisters of other lands, and that we shall show the world. Therefore I know that I needn’t urge you to be patriotic because the fact that you are here is proof sufficient that high patriotism is inspiring you.

“The purpose of our meeting today here is to unite and so organize ourselves that we shall not waste one ounce of energy, time or money in an effort to make our work as effective as possible. As a rule to organize for such a purpose we should have to go through much formality but necessity is the mother of invention. During war time we want to get the best results in the shortest time possible. I have therefore already delegated certain persons to draft a few simple working rules of organization and to suggest a few names of people who may head and direct different avenues of work. I hope you will accept what we have drafted and remember only that we are not working for name or fame but for the very life of our country itself.

Women Carry On At Rear

“I hope each one of you will take very enthusiastic part in the work and throw yourselves fully into it. While during war time the men are the fighters it is the women who bear the brunt of carrying on at the rear. We must encourage the men and let them know that we are in our own way holding on and not letting down; that we are just as ready to give up everything, even our lives, to support our fighters at the front.

“I know that various women’s institutions have started to organize to do the very same work that we are proposing to do. It is my hope we shall all unite under one organization so that what we do may be done effectively for indeed unity is strength.

“The fighting morale of our men at the front depends on how much support the rear can give. We must never forget that. And we must remember always a final national victory, no matter how belated it may be in coming, will erase forever the humiliation days that have for so long crowded our calendar and remove the sorrow that has for years past bent our heads and bowed our hearts.”

蒋夫人预见最终胜利
以雪国耻

称中国目前被迫做出牺牲以洗刷耻辱
呼吁妇女团结行动
指出女性在斗争中的重要角色

南京，8月1日电（中央社）。——蒋介石夫人在今日的演讲中预言：“最终的胜利，无论来得多么迟，将永远抹去长期以来充斥我们日历的屈辱日子，消除多年来使我们低头丧心的悲痛。”此时，中国正为了国家荣誉被迫做出最大的牺牲。

今天下午4点15分，蒋夫人在一群妇女组织代表面前发表讲话，敦促她们组成一个统一的团体，以慰问和支持国家的保卫者。演讲全文如下：

“今天，我们相聚之时，国家正面临其历史上最严重的危机。我们怀着巨大的悲痛发现，有必要在战争的阴影下聚集在一起，因为战争是一件可怕的事情。这意味着我们必须牺牲大量的士兵；无数无辜的百姓；大量的国家财富和资源，并眼睁睁看着我们在过去十年中如此成功地进行的大量建设成果被无情摧毁。但有时，为了国家荣誉，我们必须做出最大的牺牲。既然我们的政府已经清楚地表明，我们已经承受了一个自尊的民族所能承受的所有苦难，我们就必须毫不犹豫、勇敢地投入最后一点力量和精力，以确保国家的生存。我们除了服从政府命令并鼓励他人同样去做之外，已别无他法。

妇女肩负重任

“今天，我们每个中国人都必须根据自身能力进行战斗，以维护国家统一并抵御侵略。我们女性与男性一样，都是公民。我们的地位、能力和有用之处可能不同，但每个人都必须尽其所能，以加强我们的力量，始终将国家从危险中拯救出来。

“只要有我们需要动手做的工作，我们就必须努力去做。今天在西班牙，妇女们与男子并肩站在战斗行列中；而在大战期间，各国的妇女都贡献出自己最好的力量以帮助实现胜利。中国妇女在爱国精神、勇气或身体耐力方面，丝毫不逊于其他国家的姐妹，我们将向世界展示这一点。因此，我知道我不必敦促你们爱国，因为你们来到这里的事实本身就足以证明崇高的爱国主义精神在激励着你们。

“我们今天在此聚会的目的是团结起来并组织好自己，以便在努力使我们的工作尽可能有效时，不浪费一盎司的精力、时间或金钱。通常，为此目的进行组织需要经过许多繁文缛节，但需要是发明之母。在战时，我们希望在最短的时间内获得最好的结果。因此，我已经委托某些人起草几条简单的组织工作规则，并建议一些可以领导和指导不同工作领域的人员名单。我希望你们接受我们起草的内容，并记住，我们工作不是为了名利，而是为了我们国家本身的生命。

妇女在后方坚持工作

“我希望你们每个人都热情参与这项工作，并全身心投入其中。虽然在战时男子是战士，但妇女承担着在后方维持运转的主要重担。我们必须鼓励男子，让他们知道我们在以自己的方式坚持着，没有松懈；我们同样准备放弃一切，甚至我们的生命，以支持前线的战士。

“我知道各种妇女机构已经开始组织起来，开展与我们提议做的完全相同的工作。我希望我们都能在一个组织下团结起来，以便我们的工作能有效地完成，因为团结就是力量。

“前线男儿的战斗士气取决于后方能提供多少支持。我们绝不能忘记这一点。我们必须永远记住，最终的民族胜利，无论来得多么迟，将永远抹去长期以来充斥我们日历的屈辱日子，消除多年来使我们低头丧心的悲痛。”
