THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JULY 27, 1937

City Excited By News
Of Renewed Fightings

Chinese Bond Market Takes Drop At First Report;
Vernaculars Issue Extras; Patriotic Bodies
Busy Preparing Aid To Troops

After some four days of watchful waiting, Shanghai residents were again plunged into a state of intense excitement and tension yesterday as reports, authentic and otherwise, concerning the resumption of hostilities in North China and the activities of Japanese troops made their rapid rounds through the city.

First news yesterday morning of fighting at Lanfang sent quotations for Government bonds down by as much as $3.60 or within 40 cents of the maximum fluctuation allowed on the Chinese Stock and Bond Market during one session.

Hardest hit by the report of North China fighting was Consolidated Bonds "A" which dropped by $8 when the trading opened. Although the quotation later recovered for a brief period, the closing price registered another 60-cent drop for that issue. The decrease for other issue ranged from $1.70 upwards.

Plane Trip Uncertain

The fighting also placed travel facilities from here to Peiping in a state of uncertainty. Officials of the China National Aviation Corporation were unable to say yesterday whether their Peiping plane leaving here this morning will reach its destination. The northbound ship of the company landed in Tientsin and did not proceed to the Old Capital. Train service from here to Peiping was also only reaching Tientsin.

Interest and excitement of the North China fighting among the local residents were heightened by the extras published yesterday by several local Chinese newspapers which carried the latest developments of the hostilities. The China Times brought out an extra at 11 o'clock with news of fighting outside of Peiping and the attempt of the Japanese to shell Chiangtimen. In the morning the Japanese air raid at Lanfang was described by an extra of the China Evening News.

Other local vernacular papers brought out bulletins which were posted on the walls in the downtown areas. Large crowds gathered to read the hand-written notices and discussed the situation.

Red Cross Officials Meet

Officials of the Chinese Red Cross General Association yesterday gathered to discuss measures for aiding its Peiping and Tientsin branch associations in caring for the wounded. It is learned that several philanthropic organizations, including the Japanese Red Aid Corps were cooperating in rendering first-aid work and in sending medical supplies to North China.

Representatives of local public organisations and well-known local doctors will meet under the auspices of the Red Cross Association Wednesday afternoon to discuss a program concerning the training of first aid personal and the various practical phases of Red Cross work.

Steps are being taken by local bodies against export to foreign countries of commodities which have special value in times of emergency, such as metal, rice, and kerosene.

The Special District Citizens' Association yesterday instructed the City Chamber of Commerce to take special precaution against the export of refuse metal, which might be converted into ammunition.

It is learned that the Japanese and Korean jonins have been active in gathering metal refuse from retail shops in Shanghai, the owners of which are ignorant of its value.

《上海泰晤士报》，1937年7月27日，星期二

战事重开消息
令全市激动

初报传来公债市场下跌；
中文报纸发行号外；爱国团体
忙于筹备援军

经过约四天的观望等待后，随着有关华北战事重开及日军活动的真假消息迅速传遍全市，上海居民昨日再次陷入极度兴奋和紧张的状态。

昨日早晨关于廊坊战斗的第一条消息导致政府债券报价下跌高达3.60美元，接近中国股票和债券市场在一个交易时段内允许的最大波动幅度（差40美分）。

受华北战事报道打击最重的是统一公债“A”券，开盘时下跌8美元。虽然报价随后短暂回升，但该券收盘价又下跌了60美分。其他券种的跌幅从1.70美元起不等。

飞机行程不确定

战斗也使从这里到北平的旅行设施处于不确定状态。中国航空公司官员昨日无法表示今晨从这里起飞的北平航班是否能抵达目的地。该公司的北上飞机降落在天津，未继续前往旧都。从这里到北平的火车服务也只到达天津。

几家本地中文报纸昨日发布的号外刊登了敌对行动的最新进展，加剧了当地居民对华北战事的关注和兴奋。《时事新报》在11点推出号外，报道了北平外的战斗以及日军炮击彰仪门的企图。上午，《上海晚报》的号外描述了日军在廊坊的空袭。

其他本地中文报纸发布了公告，张贴在市中心区域的墙壁上。大量人群聚集阅读手写告示并讨论局势。

红十字会官员会晤

中国红十字会总会官员昨日集会，讨论援助其北平和天津分会照顾伤员的措施。据悉，包括日本赤十字救护队在内的几个慈善组织正在合作开展急救工作，并向华北运送医疗物资。

在当地公共组织的代表和知名本地医生将在红十字会的主持下于周三下午开会，讨论有关培训急救人员以及红十字会工作各个实际方面的计划。

本地团体正采取措施，禁止向国外出口在紧急时期具有特殊价值的商品，如金属、大米和煤油。

特区市民协会昨日指示市商会特别注意防止废金属出口，因为这些废金属可能被制成弹药。

据悉，日本人和朝鲜人居留民一直在积极从上海的零售店收集废金属，店主们并不了解其价值。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, JULY 27, 1937

WAR SITUATION AT A GLANCE

CHINESE and Japanese troops clashed at Langfang on
Sunday night. The Chinese were driven out of the city
yesterday morning, after an aerial bombardment.

General Sung Cheh-yuan, chairman of the Hopei-Chahar
Political Council, has ordered the 29th Army to resist all
attacks.

The Japanese have presented an ultimatum to General
Sung, setting noon to-day for the withdrawal of the Chinese
troops in the Wangping area, and noon to-morrow for the
withdrawal of all men of the 29th Army beyond the Yungting
River.

Serious fighting broke out near Peiping last night, and
was continuing at the time of going to press.

Nothing has yet been heard of the Japanese marine missing
in Shanghai, and meanwhile the Japanese suspect an insult
to their flag at a farm in Kiangwan.

Japanese reinforcements are arriving hourly in Tientsin,
many of them being moved immediately towards the fighting
zone.

Excitement reigns in Tokyo and Nanking. The Japanese
Diet is due to meet to-day.

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, JULY 23, 1937
23181

500 PUBLIC BODIES
ORGANIZE
Armed Resistance Against
Japan Wanted
GEN. CHIANG'S STAND
SUPPORTED

The association recently organized by more than 500 local public bodies for supporting armed resistance against Japan was formally inaugurated at a ceremony held in the auditorium of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Soochow Road, yesterday morning.

Many prominent local leaders, expressing their conviction that armed resistance is the only way out for China to save her from ultimate extinction, sponsored the organization. The Chinese Chamber of Commerce, the Civic Association, the Labour Union, the Chinese Women's Association, the University Professors' Federation and the Chinese Citizens' Federations are among those who have joined the new body.

The inaugural ceremony was attended by more than 1,000 persons representing all walks of life. Mr. Wang Hsiao-lai, Chairman of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, who presided, called the attention of the entire nation to the gravity of the present North China situation.

Resolutions Passed

"In the face of threatening foreign aggression," he asserted, "the whole nation should stand closer together to fight as one man against the invaders. To achieve ultimate victory, we must concentrate our national power and be ready to sacrifice our lives for the defence of our country."

Mr. Wang's speech was followed by a report rendered by Mr. Tao Po-chuen who also stressed the necessity of armed resistance at this juncture of national crisis.

A number of resolutions were adopted at the meeting, outstanding among which are mobilisation of the entire populace of this municipality in a war with Japan in case of necessity; strict vigilance on the activities of Chinese traitors; launching of a financial drive and supporting General Chiang Kai-shek's stand towards the present North China crisis.

The primary purpose of the new committee is to support Chinese defenders against foreign invasion and to protect China's territory in accordance with the plans already laid down by the Central Government.

The Committee Members

The association is composed of an executive committee of 15 members, a supervisory committee of 21 members and a standing committee of from 35 to 45 members. Under the standing committee is a secretariat to handle the routines of the organ.

Messrs. Wang Hsiao Lai, Tu Yueh-seng, Lu Ching-shih, Pan Kung-li, Feng Yu-shan, Chow Fu-chuan, Chow Hsueh-hsiang, H. Y. Tso, Li Sui-yuan, Han Fu-chu, and Wang Shu-ming were elected to the executive committee.

许多本地知名领袖发起成立了该组织，他们坚信武装抵抗是中国避免最终灭亡的唯一出路。加入该新团体的包括上海总商会、市民联合会、工会、中国妇女协会、大学教授联合会以及中华公民联合会等。

王晓籁先生发言后，陶百川先生作了报告，他也强调了在国家危机关头进行武装抵抗的必要性。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JULY 23, 1937

Salvationists
Praise Stand
Of Gen. Chiang

NANKING, July 22.—(Kuomin).—
General Chiang's powerful state-
ment has called forth a telegram
of support from the seven leaders
of the so-called "All-China Nation-
al Salvation Association" (Shen
Chun-ju, Tsou Tao-fen, Chang
Nai-chi, Li Kung-po, Sha Chien-li,
Wang Chao-shih and Miss Shih
Liang) who are under detention at
Soochow on charges of endangering
the Republic. Their telegram states:
"We have been informed by our
relatives that Your Excellency has
declared to the nation your deter-
mination to make the final sacrifice
in order to seek peace.
"You have declared that the final
limit will depend on whether or not
the Lukouchiao Incident can be
amicably settled. The conditions of
settlement will also be in conformity
with the general principle of non-
impairment of territorial and sov-
ereign rights and non-aggression.
Your ideas are correct and your
words dignified.
"We are greatly inspired by your
statement. We firmly believe that
your vigorous call will further unify
the nation and enhance the co-
operation between the Government
and the people, so that a concerted
effort may be made for coping with
the unprecedented national emer-
gency under your able direction.
"Although imprisoned, we are no
less anxious for the welfare of the
state. The invasion is becoming
daily more serious, and our anxiety
is increasing. While we cannot
participate in the work of national
salvation, we hope that your efforts
will be successful."

“阁下宣布，最后的界限取决于卢沟桥事件能否和平解决。解决条件也将符合不损害领土主权和不侵略的一般原则。阁下的见解正确，言辞庄重。
“我们深受阁下声明的鼓舞。我们坚信，阁下的有力号召将进一步统一全国，加强政府与人民之间的合作，从而在阁下的英明领导下，齐心协力应对前所未有的国家紧急状态。
“虽然身陷囹圄，我们对国家福祉的关切并未减少。侵略日益严重，我们的焦虑也与日俱增。虽然我们无法参与救国工作，但我们希望阁下的努力能够成功。”

Feng Appeals

People Should Concentrate Energy For

INTERVIEW GIVEN

29th Army Lauded And

KULING, July 22.—(Central).—
Every Chinese citizen should throw
in every ounce of his or her energy
in assisting China's survival in the
present national predicament under
the leadership of the Central Gov-
ernment.
This opinion was expressed by
Gen. Feng Yu-hsiang, Vice-chair-
man of the Military Affairs Com-
mission, in an interview with the
Central News Agency correspondent
today. The future of the North
China situation, Gen. Feng declared,
depends entirely upon 'the attitude
of Japan.'
"China," he asserted, "is a peace-
loving nation, but she will not stand
for alien aggression. 'The whole
nation will safeguard her independ-
ence and liberty at any cost."
Praises Hopei Officials
The "Christian General" paid a
glowing tribute to the officials and
people in North China for their
strenuous efforts in maintaining
peace under extremely unfavorable
circumstances, and believed that
they will continue their efforts for
national existence.
High praise was lavished by Feng
upon the heroic defenders of Lu-
kouchiao.
Gen. Feng revealed that immedia-
tely after the receipt of reports of
the incident, he wired to the 29th
Army, urging them to continue their
resistance against Japanese aggres-
sion and to protect China's terri-
torial and sovereign integrity.
Commenting on the incident, Gen.
Feng said that it was not accidental,
but arose from the challenging at-
titude of the Japanese military, who
have been emboldened by their
occupation of the four Northeastern
provinces without resistance on the
part of the Chinese troops.
China Stood Unmoved
Still blinded by their desire for
military expansion, they planned a
repetition of the Mukden incident
in North China, not realizing, how-
ever, that the Chinese people have
awakened to the dangers confront-
ing the nation and were determined
to defend the nation at all costs.

现在实现

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, July 21, 1937

Economic Background
Of Northern Crisis

BEHIND the obvious facts
of military clash in
North China lies an eco-
nomic background—specifi-
cally, Japan's iron and steel
famine, rendering Hopei's
iron deposits (and the
Chinese adverse attitude)
of acute importance—de-
clares an economic author-
ity in an intensely inter-
esting and timely article ap-
pearing on the Editorial
Page today.
Turn to Page 10 for a
concise but convincing
statement of what the
economic background of
the North China crisis con-
sists.

Seek The Economic Motive
AN ACUTE FRENCH SAYING runs "Cher-
chez la femme"—seek the woman.
When there is trouble between nations one
might amend this saying to read a French
equivalent of "Seek the economic motive."
We have heard a great deal of discussion
of the military aspects of the North China
crisis; today, of this page, The Shanghai
Evening Post presents a shrewd, well-reasoned
and well-supported economic background
analysis which no intelligent student of Far
Eastern matters should miss.
The qualifications of the author may best
be judged by what he says. We believe it will
be agreed that he knows what he's talking
about.
Iron, he says, has increasingly become the
central obsession of Japan's military econo-
mists, and their preoccupation has become
intense since late 1936 when an acute iron and
steel shortage threatened both her rearmament
plans and possible future war requirements.
As official building plans were curtailed and
renewal work on both Japanese and Man-
churian railways was delayed, Hopei's iron de-
posits suddenly loomed into special importance
instead of taking their part in a long-range
program—while at the same time, the Chinese
attitude became a matter of increasing
anxiety.
The article should be read in full (it is
brief) and we have no desire to attempt to
rewrite it. Anyone who judges a military
situation through its own obvious external
factors, however, errs in the increasingly
economically-minded world of today. Likewise
a purely military settlement of a situation
economically based must be distrusted and
doing nothing save establish a temporary basis
of power through which economic forces may
be channelized.
Viewed through the economic eye-glass,
North China seems increasingly a crucial point
for the Central Government to stand firm.
Japan's need for North China may at the same
time be seen to consist of more than a mere
thirst for new territory—yet at the same
time it becomes doubly imperative that Japan
reach a basis of friendly collaboration with
China rather than strive to play the part of
politico-economic exploiter by force.

华北危机
的经济背景

在华北军事冲突的明显事实背后，存在着一个经济背景——具体而言，是日本面临的钢铁饥荒，这使得河北的铁矿资源（以及中国的敌对态度）变得极为重要——一位经济权威人士在今天刊登于社论版的一篇极具趣味且及时的文章中如是宣称。

请翻至第10页，阅读关于华北危机经济背景构成的简明而令人信服的陈述。

探寻经济动机

有一句尖锐的法国谚语说：“Cherchez la femme”（寻找女人）。当国家之间出现纠纷时，人们或许可以将这句谚语修改为法语中对应的“寻找经济动机”。

我们已听到大量关于华北危机军事层面的讨论；今天，本报在这一版面上呈现了一篇敏锐、推理严密且有充分依据的经济背景分析，任何关注远东事务的明智读者都不应错过。

作者的资格最好通过其言论来判断。我们相信大家会同意，他对自己所谈论的内容了如指掌。

他说，铁已日益成为日本军事经济学家的核心执念，而自1936年末以来，这种专注变得尤为强烈，当时严重的钢铁短缺威胁到了日本的重整军备计划及未来可能的战争需求。随着官方建筑计划的缩减以及日本和满洲铁路翻新工作的延误，河北的铁矿突然显得尤为重要，不再仅仅是长期计划中的一部分——与此同时，中国的态度也成为一个日益令人焦虑的问题。

这篇文章篇幅简短，应全文阅读，我们无意尝试重写它。然而，在当今这个日益注重经济的世界里，任何人如果仅通过其明显的外部因素来判断军事局势，都是错误的。同样，对于基于经济基础的局势，纯粹的军事解决方式必须受到质疑，因为它除了建立一个可通过之引导经济力量的临时权力基础外，别无他用。

透过经济透镜来看，华北似乎日益成为中央政府坚守立场的关键点。日本对华北的需求，同时也可被视为不仅仅是对新领土的渴望——但与此同时，日本与中国达成友好合作基础，而非试图以武力扮演政治经济剥削者的角色，变得加倍紧迫。

Chinese Authorities Stop
Foreign Visas To North

Temporary Suspension In View Of Critical Status
Of North China; Ban On Flour Shipments Is
Ordered; Mr. Hsu Leaves For Japan

The temporary suspension of travelling visas to foreigners wishing to go to Peitaiho, Tientsin, Peiping and other areas near the scene of the latest Sino-Japanese hostilities was announced at the Passport Examination Office of the Shanghai City Government yesterday morning. Owing to the grave situation in the north, it is deemed unsafe for foreigners to travel in the region until conditions return to normal.

This action comes to many residents as a disappointment since Peitaiho is one of the best summer resorts on the China coast, while tourists regard Tientsin and Peiping as "must" places to visit. Tsingtao, however, perhaps the most popular resort for overheated Shanghailanders, is still open to tourist trade.

Control Of Shipments
Tight control over business deals which might work to the benefit of the Japanese in the event of hostilities in earnest, is being instituted by Chinese authorities. A ban against shipments of flour from Shanghai to Tientsin, Foochow and Amoy was reported yesterday. On Friday the Shanghai Customs authorities stopped some 200,000 bags of flour which had been consigned to Tientsin buyers. A consignment of 35,000 bags aboard the s.s. Chong Lee was unloaded at a Pootung wharf when a Customs cruiser stopped the ship outside Woosung and ordered it to return.

Ambassador Returns
"I shall devote my utmost to liquidate the present crisis between China and Japan on the basis of justice and sincerity after I return to Tokyo post," declared Mr. Hsu Shih-ying, Chinese Ambassador to Japan, in a written statement to the press when he boarded the President Cleveland on Friday night to resume his duties in Japan.

Mr. Hsu, who originally decided to resign from his post on account of ill-health, changed his mind in order to serve the country in view of the present tension in North China.

In his statement, he expressed the hope that Prince Konoye and Mr. Koki Hirota, who have repeatedly announced in the past their professed desire for the readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations, will continue to devote their energy along this line and work for peace in East Asia.

While he will not humiliate the country in carrying out his duties in Tokyo, the statement further stated, he hoped that the people in the country will rally under the Government to face any emergency.

Given Big Send-Off
Mr. Hsu was seen off by a large number of local officials and business leaders last night. Among them were Mr. Wang Shao-tsai, representing Acting Mayor O. K. Yui, Colonel Wang Tse-nan, representing General Yang Hu, Garrison Commander of the Shanghai-Woosung area, Mr. Chen Ming, deputy director of the Shanghai Office of the Waichiaopu, Messrs. Yu Ya-ching, Wang Hsiao-lai, and Tu Yuch-sen.

He was profusely entertained yesterday. At noon, local charity groups gave a luncheon in his honour at the Buddhist Kung Teh Ling restaurant. In the afternoon, various other local bodies entertained the Chinese Envoy at the Pootung Guilds Association.

At the latter function, Mr. Wang Hsiao-lai, Chairman of the Shanghai Chamber of Commerce, in the course of a speech commended Mr. Hsu for his courage to serve the country during the present tension in North China by returning to his Tokyo post despite his ill-health. He also wished Mr. Hsu success in his mission when he returns to Japan.

中国当局停止
向北方发放外籍人士签证

鉴于华北危急局势暂时停发；下令禁止面粉装运；许先生启程赴日

上海市政府护照查验处昨日上午宣布，暂时停止向希望前往北戴河、天津、北平及其他最新中日敌对行动发生地附近地区的外国人发放旅行签证。由于北方局势严峻，在局势恢复正常之前，外国人前往该地区旅行被认为是不安全的。

这一举动令许多居民感到失望，因为北戴河是中国沿海最好的避暑胜地之一，而游客将天津和北平视为“必去”之地。然而，青岛或许是过热难耐的上海外侨最受欢迎的度假地，目前仍对旅游业开放。

管制装运

中国当局正在实施严格控制，以防在真正发生敌对行动时，某些商业交易可能使日本受益。据报道，昨日已禁止从上海向天津、福州和厦门装运面粉。周五，上海海关当局扣留了约20万袋已发给天津买家的面粉。一批3.5万袋的面粉装载于“崇礼”号轮船上，当一艘海关巡艇在吴淞口外拦截该船并命令其返回时，这批货物在浦东码头被卸下。

大使返任

“我回到东京职位后，将在正义和真诚的基础上，竭尽全力消除当前中日之间的危机。”中国驻日大使许世英先生在周五晚间登上“克利夫兰总统”号轮船以恢复其在日本的职务时，在向媒体发表的书面声明中如是宣称。

许先生最初因健康原因决定辞职，但鉴于目前华北的紧张局势，他改变主意以报效国家。

他在声明中表示，希望近卫公爵和广田弘毅先生——他们过去曾多次宣布希望调整中日关系——能继续在此方向上投入精力，并为东亚和平而努力。

声明进一步指出，虽然他在东京履行职责时不会使国家蒙羞，但他希望国内民众能在政府领导下团结起来，应对任何紧急情况。

盛大送行

昨晚，众多地方官员和商业领袖为许先生送行。其中包括代表代理市长俞鸿钧的王绍斋先生、代表上海-吴淞地区卫戍司令杨虎将军的王泽南上校、外交部上海办事处副主任陈明先生，以及虞洽卿、王晓籁和杜月笙先生。

昨日他受到了盛情款待。中午，当地慈善团体在佛教功德林饭店为他举行了午宴。下午，其他各地方团体在浦东同乡会招待了这位中国特使。

在后一场活动中，上海总商会会长王晓籁先生在演讲中赞扬许先生不顾健康状况，在当前华北紧张局势下返回东京职位报效国家的勇气。他还祝愿许先生返回日本后使命成功。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JULY 14, 1937

Extra Precautions Locally
To Prevent Incidents

Japanese Community Warned To Keep Calm And
Avoid Excitement Over Exaggerated Reports;
Extra Police Patrols On Streets

Japanese residents here were warned on Monday by their authorities to exercise "all possible caution" until the settlement of the North China incident.
Special instructions were issued in this connection to the Japanese Consular Police by Chief Shuhei Tajima.
Municipal police stations in the Hongkew and Yangtzepoo districts have been instructed, according to local Japanese newspapers, to take every possible precaution against the recurrence of anti-Japanese terrorism.
S.M.P. patrols on duty, the press said, were to be reinforced at 7 o'clock last night.
The Shanghai "Mainichi" editorially asked the local Japanese community yesterday to place "unquestioning reliance" upon the Japanese authorities.
The daily also warned its readers to place no credence on the "exaggerated or garbled" reports on the North China situation in foreign and Chinese newspapers.
"Always Accurate"
"It must always be kept in mind," the journal declared, "that reports issued by the Japanese authorities through the Japanese press are always accurate.
"Local Japanese residents must, therefore, base their judgment of the situation on Japanese official and press reports."
Groundless news published in the Chinese press, the daily asserted, "led to the suspension of trading in Government bonds on Monday and caused exchange fluctuations unparalleled since the Sian incident."
Local Japanese consular, naval and military officials, the daily said, met on Monday to discuss the possible local repercussions of any new grave developments in the north.

Destroyers Arrive
Augmenting the Japanese naval power in Shanghai, two destroyers arrived here at 12.00 p.m. yesterday.
They were the Fuyo and the Karukaya belonging to the Fifth Torpedo Boat Flotilla of the Third Fleet, which is stationed in Chinese waters.
The Fuyo left for Tsingtao at 7 o'clock last night.
Latent anti-Japanese feeling, heightened by the events in North

China, was ascribed by the local Japanese press as the cause for a mob attack on the home of M. Hidesaburo Aoyagi, 250, Yochow Road, at about 11.30 o'clock on Monday night. Material damage estimated at $30 was caused, the papers said.
The trouble arose from a dispute over a ricsha fare, the reports stated. About 30 Chinese gathered to watch the altercation, and rushed into Mr. Aoyagi's home, the dailies alleged.
Municipal police from the Wavside station dispersed the attackers. No injuries were reported the papers added.—Domei.

周一，当地日本当局警告在沪日侨，在华北事件解决之前，务必“尽一切可能谨慎行事”。
首席警官田岛周平就此向日警署发布了特别指令。
据当地日文报纸报道，虹口和杨浦区段的工部局警察分局已接到指示，要采取一切可能的预防措施，防止反日恐怖活动再次发生。
报界称，值勤的工部局警务处（S.M.P.）巡逻队已于昨晚7点得到加强。
《上海每日新闻》昨日在社论中要求当地日侨社区对日本当局给予“毫无保留的信任”。
该日报还警告读者，不要相信外国和中国报纸上关于华北局势的“夸大或歪曲”的报道。
“始终准确”
该报刊称：“必须始终牢记，日本当局通过日本媒体发布的报道始终是准确的。
“因此，当地日侨必须根据日本官方和媒体的报道来判断局势。”
该日报断言，中文报纸发布的无根据新闻，“导致周一公债交易暂停，并引发了自西安事变以来前所未有的汇率波动”。
该日报称，当地日本领事、海军和军事官员周一开会，讨论了北方任何新的严重事态发展可能在本地引起的反响。

驱逐舰抵达

为增强日本在上海的海军力量，两艘驱逐舰于昨天中午12点抵达此地。
它们是隶属于驻扎在中国水域的第三舰队第五鱼雷艇队的“芙蓉”号和“樫野”号。
“芙蓉”号于昨晚7点启程前往青岛。
当地日文报纸将潜伏的反日情绪（因华北事件而加剧）归因为周一晚上11点半左右，一群暴徒袭击了位于姚主教路250号的青柳秀三郎先生住宅的原因。报纸称，造成的物质损失估计为30美元。
报道指出，麻烦起因于人力车车费纠纷。日报声称，约有30名中国人聚集围观争执，并冲进了青柳先生的家中。
来自西区警察分局的工部局警察驱散了袭击者。报纸补充说，据报道无人受伤。——同盟社。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JULY 13, 1937
23007
5994

Japanese Ask Chinese For
Protection Locally

Nippon Consul-General To Seek Guarantees For
Steps To Be Taken To Safeguard Lives And
Property; Local Bodies Exhort 29th Army

Calling on Mr. O. K. Yui, Acting Mayor of Greater Shanghai, to-day, Mr. Suemasa Okamoto, Japanese Consul-General here, will press for guarantees of adequate steps for the protection of Japanese lives and property in Shanghai.

This followed a 1½-hour conference at the Consulate-General yesterday morning attended by high Japanese, Army, Navy and diplomatic officials.

Information regarding the situation in North China and possible local repercussions was exchanged by the conferees.

Attending were: Major-General Seiichi Kita, military attache to the Embassy; Rear - Admiral Tadao Honda, naval attache; Colonel Sanetaka Kusumoto, assistant military attache; Mr. Akiyoshi Tajiri, First Secretary of the Embassy; and others.—Domei.

Local Reaction

Highly indignant over the renewal of Japanese attacks on Lukouchiao various local bodies have telegraphed to the 29th Army, urging resistance against the aggressors, to the last man.

The telegrams all commended the stiff stance adopted by the Army and exhorted it to continue their resistance with renewed vigour. The firm defence of Chinese soil was also urged upon the troops.

Among senders of these dispatches are the China Cultural Reconstruction Association, the National Postal Service Labour Union, and other cultural and labour organizations.

The "Ta Kung Pao," an independent local daily, yesterday received $100 from the Students National Salvation Association to be forwarded to the 29th Army as "comfort" purposes.

In an accompanying letter, the Association pledged its support to the Army in collaboration with the Central Government and the people of the whole country.—Central News.

Message To Troops

A telegram of encouragement to the 29th Army, for its "great services to our country, in the defence of the Marco Polo Bridge," was sent on Sunday by the Chinese Cultural Reconstruction Society, the Japanese papers reported yesterday.

Addressed to the officers of the Army, through General Chin Teh-chun, Mayor of Peiping, the telegram read:

"We all tender our profound gratitude to the officers of the 29th Army who had rendered a great service to our country by their defence of Marco Polo Bridge at the risk of their lives.

"Hoping that the Central Government will soon decide to protect the territorial integrity of China by continuing the military operations, the Society hereby pledges to join all other Chinese in backing the Government."

The meeting, attended by 81 officials of the Society and representatives of other bodies, was held, according to the Japanese press, at the Reception Hall of the Shanghai City Government, in Kiangwan.—Domei.

（批：DBR）

《字林西报》，1937年7月13日，星期二

日本人要求中方提供本地保护

日本总领事将寻求保障，以采取必要措施 safeguard 生命和财产；本地团体敦促第二十九军

日本驻沪总领事冈本季正（Suemasa Okamoto）今日拜访大上海代理市长俞鸿钧（O. K. Yui）先生，将强烈要求保证采取充分措施，以保护在上海的日本人的生命和财产。

此举继昨天上午在总领事馆举行的一场历时一个半小时的会议之后，出席会议的有日本军方、海军和外交界的高级官员。

与会者交换了关于华北局势及可能在本地引发反响的情报。

出席者包括：日本驻华大使馆武官北岛骥子雄（Seiichi Kita）少将；海军武官本多忠雄（Tadao Honda）少将；助理武官楠本实隆（Sanetaka Kusumoto）上校；大使馆一等秘书田尻爱义（Akiyoshi Tajiri）先生等。——同盟社

本地反应

鉴于日军再次进攻卢沟桥，各本地团体深感愤慨，纷纷致电第二十九军， urging 抵抗侵略者，直至最后一人。

这些电文均赞扬军队采取的强硬立场，并勉励其以更旺盛的斗志继续抵抗。同时也 urged 部队坚决保卫中国领土。

发送这些电文的团体包括中国文化重建协会、全国邮政工会以及其他文化和劳工组织。

本地独立日报《大公报》昨日收到学生救国会汇款100美元，将转交第二十九军作为“慰劳”之用。

在随附的信函中，该会承诺将与中央政府及全国人民合作，支持军队。——中央通讯社

致部队讯息

据日本报纸昨日报道，中国文化重建学会于周日向第二十九军发出了一封鼓励电报，表彰其“在保卫卢沟桥方面对国家做出的巨大贡献”。

该电报通过北平市长秦德纯（Chin Teh-chun）将军转达给该军军官，内容如下：

“我们对第二十九军全体军官致以深切谢意，他们冒着生命危险保卫卢沟桥，为国家立下了大功。

“希望中央政府早日决定通过继续军事行动来保卫中国领土完整，本会特此承诺与所有中国人一道支持政府。”

据日本媒体报道，这次会议在上海江湾上海市政府接待大厅举行，出席者包括该会81名官员及其他团体的代表。——同盟社

（批：DBR）

上海各公共团体将于明日在区商会举行会议，目的是“慰劳”正在北方与日军进行严重武装冲突的第二十九路军。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, JULY 13, 1937
23016
Shanghai Keeps Calm In
Spite Of Wild Rumors;
Communications Suffer

Public Indignation Against Japanese Soars
And Chinese Urge Resistance; Trains Off
Schedule, Planes Getting Through

With reports from strife-torn North China shuttling incessantly between optimism and pessimism. Shanghai was yesterday a happy hunting ground for rumor-mongers of both the professional and amateur varieties.

The town was literally seething with "reliable reports gained from confidential sources," which made their rapid rounds in stock and bond and commodity markets, offices, homes and every place where people foregather.

Despite these wide rumors, local residents remained calm but tense. They were eager, however, to hear the "latest reports" from the North.

Trading Suspended

As a result of the many unfounded "confidential reports" and the activities of the speculators, Government bonds slipped $4 on the Chinese Bond Market yesterday morning. This drastic drop prompted the market officials to suspend trading and issue notices asking the operators to make good their margins.

The tumble in bond quotations occurred almost immediately after the opening of the morning session yesterday. The general uneasiness among operators as a result of resumption of hostilities at Lukouchiao was reflected in the bidding at the first bell when bonds of Groups "A," "B," "C," "D" and "E" for both nose-dived by the maximum $4 difference allowed on the market during one session. This drop prompted market officials to take the customary procedure of declaring the trading closed. Because of the heat, the bond market has not been in session in the afternoon.

On the Chinese Flour Exchange, trading was also at a standstill yesterday. This was partly because of the low prices brought about by speculators, although lack of demand due to the unsettled condition in the North also contributed to the stoppage in trading.

Northern Merchants Cautious

North China merchants, who ordinarily buy a large quantity of cereal and flour on the local markets, were yesterday adopting a cautious policy and refraining from making any commitments. Their withdrawal from active trading, Chinese reports said, was also responsible for the dearth of demands yesterday.

Meantime, airplane and rail traffic schedules between Shanghai and Peiping remained uncertain yesterday. Despite reports from the North that traffic on the Peiping-Tientsin railway has been resumed, travel agencies and railroad offices were yesterday still not selling any through tickets from Shanghai to the Old Capital.

Reports received at the North Station here said last night that the first Shanghai-bound train from Peiping left that city at 8 o'clock last night. It is expected to arrive here this morning.

around 3 o'clock yesterday afternoon. Company officials said yesterday that they have not received any confirmation regarding reports that the Japanese military authorities had demanded the use of the C.N.A.C. field in Tientsin for landing military planes.

Eurasia Service Running

The Peiping-Hongkong service of the Eurasia Aviation Corporation was being maintained yesterday, after a temporary suspension last Friday. The Hongkong-bound plane, company officials announced, will leave Peiping on its scheduled time this morning. Reports received here yesterday stated that a Eurasia plane bound from Hongkong to Peiping landed on Friday at Taiyuan as a result of the outbreak of fighting. This plane resumed its flight to Peiping yesterday, reaching the Old Capital at 11.13 a.m.

The tense situation in North China also brought about a heavy increase of telegrams from Shanghai to cities near the trouble centers. As a result messages to the Northern cities, according to reports of the local Telegraph Office, were delayed as a result of the lack of facilities to handle the sudden increase.

Conflicting reports on the North China situation which could not be confirmed took many varied forms yesterday. One of these said the local Japanese residents have completed arrangements for evacuating the city. Also gaining wide currency yesterday were the unconfirmed reports from Chinese sources claiming that Lieut.-Gen. K. Tashiro, who was replaced as General Officer in Command of Japanese forces in North China, died Sunday evening at Tientsin from a heart ailment.

Some 300 Japanese bluejackets of the Special Naval Landing Party made a trip yesterday morning to Chapel. They visited Kiangwan and Tungchi Road in their army trucks.

Japanese Get Instructions

Japanese banks and cotton mills in Shanghai yesterday were instructed by their home offices to be prepared to take emergency measures in case the present Sino-Japanese crisis should become aggravated.

The financial institutions were directed to be cautious in their commitments, while the textile firms received orders to draw up plans for the evacuation of women and children among the families of their staffs.

Shanghai Urges Resistance

Highly indignant over the renewal of Japanese aggression, various local bodies have cabled messages to the authorities to the last man.

The Ta' Kung Pao, an independent local daily, yesterday received $100 from the Students National Salvation Association to be forwarded to the 29th Army as "comfort" purposes.

In an accompanying letter, the Association pledged its support to the Army in collaboration with the Central Government and the people of the whole country.

Indignation Runs High

NANKING, July 13.—(Central). —Public indignation has been aroused here over the violation of the demobilization pledge by the Japanese military and their renewed attack on Lukouchiar on Saturday and Sunday night.

"Extras", printing the lightning developments in the North, are selling like hot cakes and throngs of eager news seekers swarm the front of local newspaper offices for the latest reports on the tense situation.

Stores which install radio receivers also attract big crowds who listen to the latest broadcast on the "war."

Many messages supporting the stand of the 29th Route Army have been sent by various local bodies to the "front", while a campaign has been launched to raise "comfort" funds for the defenders in the North.

"Pacific Means" Said Futile

Futility in the employment of "pacific means" to settle the Lukouchiao incident was pointed out by the local Hsin Min Pao editorial yesterday.

Such "pacific means" adopted by the Chinese Government toward Japanese aggression, the paper opined, will not thoroughly settle the trouble nor will it attain true peace.

Since the Mukden incident of 1931, the Chinese Government, the paper recalled, has been trying to settle disputes between China and Japan through "pacific means", but the efforts have been fruitless in improving the relations between the two countries or in consolidating peace in the Orient.

Recalling the Fengtai incident of last year, the journal said, the evacuation of the 29th Army from the strategic railway junction planted the seed of the recent Lukouchiao case.

Fail To Evacuate

In the hope of "peaceful settlement" of the latter incident, the Chinese authorities withdrew the troops of the 29th Army from Lukouchiao replacing them with the Peace Preservation Corps under the command of Gen. Shih Yu-sun. But in violation of the agreement reached in the negotiations with the Chinese authorities, the Japanese troops failed to evacuate from the scene of conflicts, thus aggravating the situation.

Continuing to apply this "pacific" formula for the settlement of the latest incident, the paper predicted, the Chinese authorities will be compelled to allow Japan to station troops in Wanping, and the Yungting River area or to mark out these places as a buffer zone to be garrisoned by Peace Preservation Corps.

（批：DR）

《大美晚报》，1937年7月13日，星期二
23016
尽管谣言四起，上海保持冷静；通讯受阻

公众对日愤慨高涨，国人 urged 抵抗；火车晚点，飞机勉强通行

随着来自战乱不断的华北的报道在乐观与悲观之间不断摇摆，上海昨日成了职业和业余造谣者的乐园。

城里简直沸腾着各种“从机密渠道获得的可靠报告”，这些消息在股票、债券和商品市场、办公室、家庭以及人们聚集的任何地方迅速传播。

尽管谣言满天飞，本地居民仍保持冷静但紧张。然而，他们渴望听到来自北方的“最新报道”。

交易暂停

由于许多毫无根据的“机密报告”以及投机者的活动，昨日早晨中国债券市场上的公债下跌了4元。这一剧烈下跌促使市场管理人员暂停交易，并发布通知，要求操作员补足保证金。

债券报价的暴跌几乎发生在昨日早盘开市后立即发生。由于卢沟桥战事重开，操作员普遍感到不安，这在第一声钟响时的竞价中得到了反映，A、B、C、D和E组债券均出现了单次交易允许的最大4元差价的暴跌。这一下跌促使市场管理人员采取惯例程序，宣布休市。由于天气炎热，债券市场下午未开市。

在上海面粉交易所，昨日交易也处于停滞状态。这部分是因为投机者导致的低价，尽管北方局势动荡导致需求缺乏也是造成交易停止的原因之一。

北方商人谨慎

通常在本地市场购买大量谷物和面粉的华北商人，昨日采取了谨慎政策，避免做出任何承诺。中文报道称，他们退出活跃交易也是造成昨日需求匮乏的原因。

与此同时，昨日上海与北平之间的飞机和铁路交通时刻表仍不确定。尽管有来自北方的报道说平津铁路的交通已恢复，但旅行社和铁路局昨日仍未出售从上海到旧都（北平）的联程票。

据本站（北站）昨晚收到的报告称，第一列从北平开往上海的火车于昨晚8点离开该市。预计将于今天上午抵达此处。

昨天下午3点左右。公司官员昨日表示，他们尚未收到任何确认，证实有关日本军方要求使用天津的中国航空公司（C.N.A.C.）机场降落军用飞机的报道。

欧亚航空服务运行

欧亚航空公司的北平-香港航线在上周五暂时停飞后，昨日维持运行。公司官员宣布，飞往香港的飞机将于今天上午按预定时间从北平起飞。昨日在此收到的报告称，一架从香港飞往北平的欧亚飞机因战斗爆发于周五降落在太原。该飞机昨日恢复飞往北平，于上午11点13分抵达旧都。

华北的紧张局势也导致从上海发往靠近冲突中心城市的电报大量增加。因此，据本地电报局报告，由于缺乏处理突然增加量的设施，发往北方城市的信息被延误。

昨日，关于华北局势无法证实的相互矛盾的报道以多种形式出现。其中一种说法称，本地日本居民已完成撤离城市的安排。昨日广泛流传的还有来自中方来源的未经证实的报道，声称被撤换的日本华北驻屯军司令官田代皖一郎（K. Tashiro）中将，因心脏病于周日晚在天津去世。

约300名日本特别海军陆战队水兵昨日上午前往闸北（Chapel，原文疑为Chapei之误，结合上下文及历史事实应为闸北）。他们乘坐军用卡车访问了江湾和同济路。

日本人接到指示

昨日，在上海的日本银行和棉纺厂接到国内总行的指示，准备在当前中日危机加剧的情况下采取紧急措施。

金融机构被指示在承诺业务时要谨慎，而纺织公司则接到命令，制定计划，疏散其职员家属中的妇女和儿童。

上海 urged 抵抗

鉴于日军再次侵略，各本地团体深感愤慨，纷纷致电当局，呼吁抵抗至最后一人。

本地独立日报《大公报》昨日收到学生救国会汇款100美元，将转交第二十九军作为“慰劳”之用。

在随附的信函中，该会承诺将与中央政府及全国人民合作，支持军队。

愤慨情绪高涨

南京，7月13日。（中央社）——日军违反复员承诺，并于周六和周日夜间再次进攻卢沟桥，在此激起本地公众的愤慨。

刊登北方闪电般事态发展的“号外”销售火爆，成群结队的急切新闻 seekers 涌向本地报社门前，获取关于紧张局势的最新报道。

安装无线电接收器的商店也吸引了大量人群，收听关于“战争”的最新广播。

各本地团体已向“前线”发送了许多支持第二十九路军立场的信息，同时发起了一场为北方保卫者筹集“慰劳”资金的运动。

称“和平手段”无效

本地《新民报》社论昨日指出，运用“和平手段”解决卢沟桥事件是徒劳的。

该报认为，中国政府对日本侵略采取的这种“和平手段”，既不能彻底解决麻烦，也不能实现真正的和平。

该报回顾称，自1931年沈阳事变以来，中国政府一直试图通过“和平手段”解决中日争端，但这些努力在改善两国关系或巩固东方和平方面均无果而终。

该报回顾去年的丰台事件时说，第二十九军从战略铁路枢纽撤军，埋下了近期卢沟桥事件的种子。

未能撤离

为了“和平解决”后者事件，中国当局从卢沟桥撤出了第二十九军的部队，取而代之的是由石友三（Shih Yu-sun）将军指挥的保安队。但是，日军违反了与中国当局谈判达成的协议，未能从冲突现场撤离，从而加剧了局势。

该报预测，如果继续套用这种解决最新事件的“和平”公式，中国当局将被迫允许日本在宛平和永定河地区驻军，或将这些地方划定为由保安队驻守的缓冲区。

（批：DR）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 8, 1937    28913

Battle, Started At 10
Last Night, Resumes
At Noon After Truce

CHINESE SENTRIES
OPENED FIRE SAY
JAPANESE REPORTS

Nipponese Report Two Officers Slain And 25
Chinese Dead; Figures Disputed; Chinese
Say Own Casualties “More Than 200”

Two Forces Battle West Of Fengtai

(Domet)
PEIPING, July 8.—Thundering gunfire, clearly audible here, at 11:40 o’clock this morning heralded the resumption of the most sanguinary Sino-Japanese conflict since the Jehol campaign of 1933.

Twenty minutes before a two-hour truce was to expire, the echo of exploding shells 20 miles away cast a pall of gloom over agitated Peiping.

The fighting was apparently resumed as Chinese and Japanese negotiators, racing against time to prevent a renewal of hostilities, failed to reach an accord at a conference held in the walled city of Yuanping, on the Peiping-Hankow Railway.

The Japanese military authorities are demanding the immediate withdrawal of all Chinese troops from the vicinity of Lukouchiao.

A one-hour interval was agreed upon at 10 o’clock and extended until noon.

Heavy damage was inflicted on Japanese forces by the artillery of an independent cavalry brigade, garrisoned in Changhsintien, which rushed north following a brush between Chinese and Japanese troops last night.

The known toll of this morning’s fighting was:
27 DEAD, 11 WOUNDED
Japanese: dead—one officer and one non-commissioned officer;
wounded—one officer and about ten soldiers.
Chinese: dead—about 25 officers and men.

These figures, however, were disputed by officials of the Hopei-Chahar Political Council, who placed Chinese casualties at “more than 200”.

Japanese reinforcements, being rushed on trucks from Tungchow to the Embassy here, were prevented from entering

BACKGROUND

The fighting that has broken out between Chinese and Japanese troops south of Peiping is by no means unheralded, though very little of the undercurrents has been reported in Shanghai. Peiping has for some time been tense and expectant, and at various times martial law has been declared at night, though few were aware of it outside the authorities and foreign consular officers. There has been increasing friction as a result of the determined rounding-up of scores of agitators and plotters, Chinese and Koreans, by the 29th route army, though outwardly everything has been fairly calm.

The large number of Chinese troops in the vicinity is said to have been the only reason an outbreak has not occurred before. The 29th army is General Sung Cheh-yuan’s troops, he being chairman of the Hopei-Chahar Political Council, and while he has not been openly defiant of Japanese aggression, he has been firm in determination to maintain the integrity of Chinese territory. His troops have been so on the alert recently that any move similar to that by the Japanese that started the Mukden incident in 1931 would be difficult.

LOCAL WOMAN ASKS FATHER
For Help

An appeal to save his daughter from the hands of her cruel husband was received yesterday by the local Japanese Consular Police from Mr. Bunkichi Itamoto, 59, of Nagasaki Prefecture. The unfortunate woman was his 31-year-old daughter Fumiko, who ran away from her father’s home five years ago. The woman’s appeal to her father claimed that she is being imprisoned by her husband at their home at 125 Yangtzepoo Road, on fear of death if she tries to escape. Some time ago, the appeal said, the woman escaped to Tsingtao, but was found by him and brought back to Shanghai. Now he refuses to release her until she pays $80,—the cost of her trip to Tsingtao.

* * *

Bethel Mission Bible
Sessions Attended

In spite of the heat large throngs of delegates and guests are attending the bible meet conference of the Bethel Mission now being held at its mission headquarters in Nantao. The daily program starts with a “Morning Watch,” a time for prayer and bible study, and singing class and an hour led by the Reverend Andrew Gih comprise other items in the mornings. A platform meeting at 4.30 is the afternoon program while in the evenings illustrated reports of Bethel Evangelistic Bands from various parts of China and the Philippines are

...plained, is necessary as the investigations are still going on and the trial is proceeding. The seven accused were arrested in Shanghai on November 22.

No date for the resumption of the trial has yet been announced.

Card-Sharper Nabbed
After Blood Alley
Snatch From Yokel

A country yokel from Changsoh named Tao Haimin, 24, who has been in Shanghai for a short period, passed Blood Alley at about 1 o’clock yesterday afternoon and seeing a card game in full swing he took out his worldly possession of $6 and tried to test his luck. At this stage one of the accomplices of the card player snatched the money from the man and took to his heels.

The yokel was bewildered at first, and was hurt in turn and then saw red because $6 was all he had in the world. Mustering all his courage he gave chase to one of the men and held him for dear life until the arrival of a police officer. At the Second Special District Court this morning Mao Chang-ken, one of the card sharpers, told the judge that the man lost his money in the game and he was not robbed. 《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年7月8日，星期四 28913

战斗于昨晚10时爆发
休战后于中午恢复

据日方报告
中国哨兵开火

日方报告两名军官被杀及25名中国人死亡；数字存疑；中方称己方伤亡“超过200人”

两军在丰台以西交战

（多梅特）
北平，7月8日电。——今天上午11时40分，此处清晰可闻的隆隆枪声，预示着自1933年热河战役以来最惨烈的中日冲突再度爆发。

在两小时停战协定即将到期前二十分钟，远处二十英里外传来的炮弹爆炸声，给动荡不安的北平笼罩上一层阴郁的气氛。

随着中日谈判代表在北平至汉口铁路线上的宛平县城举行的会议上未能达成协议，尽管他们争分夺秒试图防止敌对行动重演，战斗显然已经恢复。

日本军方当局要求所有中国军队立即从卢沟桥附近撤出。

双方于10时商定了一小时间隔，并延长至中午。

驻守长辛店的一个独立骑兵旅的火炮对日军造成了严重破坏，该部队在昨晚中日军队发生小规模冲突后迅速北上。

今晨战斗的已知伤亡情况为：
27人死亡，11人受伤
日军：死亡——一名军官和一名士官；
受伤——一名军官和约十名士兵。
中方：死亡——约25名官兵。

然而，这些数字受到冀察政务委员会官员的质疑，他们称中方伤亡人数为“超过200人”。

从通州乘卡车紧急赶往此处使馆区的日本增援部队，被阻止进入

背景

北平以南中日军队之间爆发的战斗绝非毫无预兆，尽管上海方面很少报道其潜在动向。北平在一段时间内一直处于紧张和期待状态，夜间曾多次宣布戒严，尽管除当局和外国领事官员外，鲜有人知晓。由于第二十九路军坚决逮捕了数十名中国和朝鲜煽动者及阴谋策划者，摩擦日益加剧，尽管表面上局势相当平静。

据说，该地区大量中国军队的存在是此前未爆发冲突的唯一原因。第二十九军是宋哲元将军的部队，他兼任冀察政务委员会委员长，虽然他没有公开违抗日方的侵略，但在维护中国领土完整方面决心坚定。他的部队最近高度警戒，使得类似1931年引发沈阳事变的日军行动难以实施。

本地女子向父亲
求助

昨日，当地日本领事警察收到来自长崎县59岁的饭本文吉（Bunkichi Itamoto，音译）先生的请求，希望将其女儿从残酷丈夫手中救出。这名不幸的女子是他31岁的女儿富美子（Fumiko，音译），五年前从父亲家中出走。该女子向父亲的求助信中称，她被丈夫囚禁在杨树浦路125号的家中，若试图逃跑将面临死亡威胁。求助信称，不久前该女子曾逃往青岛，但被其夫找到并带回上海。现在他拒绝释放她，除非她支付80美元，即她前往青岛的旅费。

* * *

伯特利教会圣经
聚会出席情况

尽管天气炎热，大批代表和嘉宾仍出席了目前正在南市伯特利教会总部举行的圣经会议。每日日程以“晨更”开始，这是一段祈祷和研读圣经的时间，此外上午的项目还包括歌唱课以及由季安德鲁牧师（Reverend Andrew Gih）主持的一小时活动。下午4时30分举行平台聚会，而晚间则播放来自中国各地和菲律宾的伯特利布道团的图文报告

……解释是必要的，因为调查仍在进行，审判也在继续。七名被告于11月22日在上海被捕。

尚未宣布恢复审判的日期。

牌局骗子在血巷
从乡下人手中抢夺后
被捕

来自常熟、名为陶海民（Tao Haimin，音译）的24岁乡下人，来沪不久，昨天下午1点左右经过血巷（Blood Alley），看到一场牌局正在进行，便拿出全部身家6美元，试图碰碰运气。此时，牌局参与者的一名同伙从该男子手中抢走钱款并拔腿就跑。

这名乡下人起初感到困惑，随后受到伤害，继而怒火中烧，因为6美元是他所有的积蓄。他鼓起全部勇气追赶其中一人，并死死抓住他不放，直到警察赶到。今天上午在第二特区法院，牌局骗子之一毛长根（Mao Chang-ken，音译）告诉法官，该男子是在游戏中输掉了钱，并未遭到抢劫。然而，他的过往记录显示，被告是一名曾服过刑的前科骗子，当他的故事被

page_data.en:
Japanese And Chinese Soldiers
Battling Outside Peiping; Clash
"Most Sanguinary Since Jehol"

White Flag Hoisted Over Lukouchiao Viewed
As Disassociation Of Gen. Feng Chih-an's
37th Division From 29th R. A. Action

Peiping-Tientsin Telephone Is Cut

(Concluded from Page 1)
ping, was allegedly subjected to rifle and machine-gun fire
from a Chinese pill box located near Liuwangmiao.

NORTH OF LUKOUCHIAO
This is about 1,000 meters north of Lukouchiao, a small
town to the west of Yuanping. A railway line runs east from
Yuanping to Fengtai joining the Peiping-Hankow and the
Peiping-Mukden Railways.
Following the alleged Chinese attack, the Japanese unit
immediately suspended operations. A message was sent to
headquarters in Peiping and instructions requested.
Lieut.-Col. Tetsu Morita, headquarters officer, immediately
proceeded to the scene of the clash, accompanied by Mr. Wang
I.eng-chi, magistrate of Yuanping Hsien, and Mr. Lin Heng-
yu of the foreign affairs commission of the Hopei-Chahar
Political Council, the announcement said.

JAPANESE, CHINESE CONFER
Captain Tadasuke Teradaira, Chinese language expert;
Lieut.-Colonel Ryozo Sakurai, Japanese advisor to the
Twenty-Ninth Army and a Chinese staff officer also left Pei-
ping for the scene of the incident.
Before these officers arrived, however, a combat had
broken out at about 5:30 o'clock, the Japanese authorities said.
This was precipitated, according to the communique, when
Chinese forces, reinforced by artillery units from Changhsin-
tien, important station on the Peiping-Hankow railway,
allegedly opened fire on the Japanese troops.

FIRE RETURNED
"Our forces were compelled to return the fire," the com-
munique said.
Machine-guns, trench mortars and light artillery were
used in the subsequent fight.
Strengthened by the arrival of one battalion of infantry
from Fengtai, the Japanese forces made an assault dislodging
the Chinese from their positions.
Fleeing across the Yuanting River in the direction of
the barracks adjoining the walled city of Lukouchiao, the
Chinese were subjected to a heavy Japanese fire. Many fell
in their flight and scores of bodies were seen floating on the
river afterwards, Japanese military reports said.

White Flag
Meantime, a white flag was
hoisted atop a watch tower on the
Lukouchiao town wall. This was
interpreted by the Japanese to
signify that General Feng Chih-
an, commander of the Thirty-
Seventh Division, did not want to
become involved in the fighting
outside the walls.
As a precaution, however, the
Japanese forces occupied the town
and proceeded to disarm the Chi-
nese garrison, an announcement
by the headquarters of the Japan-
ese garrison in North China, in
Tientsin said.
General Feng, the Japanese
military authorities in Peiping
stated, has disclaimed responsibil-
ity for the conflict stating that
the Chinese forces involved were
not under his command.

Reports Conflict
Information available in Pei-
ping regarding the identity of the
Chinese troops involved was con-
flicting. Some sources stated that
they were part of the 219th regi-
ment, other that they belonged to
the 220th regiment of the 110th
brigade.

Colonel Yoji Wachi, chief of the
special service branch of the
Japanese North China Army
headquarters, hurried to Peiping
early this morning to confer with
Japanese army officers there.
This followed the breakdown of
telephone communication between
Peiping and Tientsin.

Emergency Session
Major-General Torashiro Kawa-
be, Japanese brigade commander
in Peiping; Col. Renya Mutaguchi,
infantry commandant; Colonel
Ma'sui, chief of the special service
branch in Peiping, and others
went into emergency conference
soon after the receipt of first re-
ports of the clash.
While the rattle of rifle and
machine-gun fire and the boom
of field and trench guns could be
heard in Peiping, the city remained
calm.
Chinese troops at the Nanyuan
and Shihliyuan barracks have not
been mobilized.

Previous Trouble
An incident was narrowly avert-
ed recently through the espion-
age system of the 29th Route
Army, according to reports from
the former capital, when seven
armored cars manned by Japan-
ese soldiers began an early-
morning cruise about the city for
two hours or so.
It was stated that about 200
Koreans had been placed at
various strategic points through-
out the city and instructed to
create disturbances, with the
Japanese soldiers aiding them if
necessary. The 29th Route Army
however, picked up numerous

Koreans and alleged Chinese trai-
tors during the truck parade and
hurled many into prison after
questioning, it is said.

Conferences Held
This state of affairs, with con-
tinual arrests of suspected Ko-
reans and Chinese and an atmos-
phere of tenseness and uncer-
tainty, went on for some time.
High Chinese officials held con-
ferences to discuss measures of
defense and to co-operate in the
maintenance of peace and order
in the two provinces and two
special municipalities under the
jurisdiction of the Hopei-
Chahar Political Council, reports
said. Although it was stated at
General Sung Cheh-yuan's ab-
sence from Peiping was due to
private matters, it was believed
that he had actually gone to
Shantung to confer with Han Fu-
chu, provincial chairman.
Hundreds of residents of Tung-
chow were also said to be leaving
the capital and adding to the
worries of Yin Ju-keng, head of
the East Hopei regime, who tried
to stop the exodus, due mainly
to wild rumors, by an inspection
of all busses passing in and out
of Tungchow. Yin was also
meanwhile organizing the "Japan-
ese-Manchukuo-Mongolian allied
forces" to strengthen his defenses,
for which project he was said to
be attempting to secure $600,000
from the Kwantung Army and
the Japanese Garrison forces in
North China.

Japanese To Maneuver
The second summer review of
the Japanese garrison forces in
North China will soon be held,
according to a special dispatch
from Tientsin.
Preparatory to the inspection, it
is reported, Japanese troops sta-
tioned at Tungchutzu and Hai-
kwangssu barracks will be ordered
to Nantassu near Tientsin for
joint maneuvers and camping.
Meanwhile, it is reported that
the Japanese Residents' Corpora-
tion in Tientsin yesterday com-
pleted the plans for an expansion
of its own organization. Under
the new arrangements, there will
be five departments and 18 sec-
tions, and Japanese living outside
their Concession will come under
the jurisdiction of the Corpora-
tion, with which their business
enterprises should be registered.

Nanking Orders Localization
(Domei)
NANKING, July 8.—Instructions
to "localize" the clash between
Japanese and Chinese troops west
of Fengtai were dispatched to
General Chang Chih-chung, com-
mander of the 38th Division gar-

risoned near Peiping, by the
foreign affairs Commission here
this morning.
A sketchy report of the Luka-
chiao fighting was understood to
have been received by the Com-
mission.
This dispatch alleged that the
Japanese had opened fire on the
Chinese outpost, "compelling" the
latter to return the fire.
A similar message was sent to
General Chiang Kai-shek, chair-
man of the Commission, at Nanking.

Tokyo Takes Grave View
(Domei)
TOKYO, July 8.—Emergency
conferences were called early this
morning in the War Office to con-
sider the serious Sino-Japanese
incident near Peiping.
Declining to comment on the
situation pending the receipt of
official reports, high Army officials,
however, said they could not but
take a "very grave" view of the
affair.
The fragmentary press reports
received here this morning, it was
said, indicated that the respon-
sibility for the breach of peace in
North China rested upon the
shoulders of Chinese troops.

中日士兵
在北平郊外激战；冲突
“自热河事件以来最为惨烈”

卢沟桥升起白旗被视为
冯治安将军第37师
与第29军行动脱钩之举

北平至天津电话线被切断

（接第1版）
平，据称遭到位于刘王庙附近的一个中国碉堡的步枪和机枪射击。

卢沟桥以北
此处位于元平以西的小镇卢沟桥以北约1,000米处。一条铁路线从元平向东延伸至丰台，连接北平-汉口铁路和北平-沈阳铁路。
据称在中国军队发动攻击后，日军部队立即停止行动。向北平总部发送了消息并请求指示。
公告称，总部军官森田铁中校（Tetsu Morita，音译）立即前往冲突现场，随行人员包括元平县县长王英池先生（Wang I.eng-chi，音译）以及冀察政务委员会外交委员会的林恒宇先生（Lin Heng-yu，音译）。

中日双方会谈
中文专家寺平忠助上尉（Tadasuke Teradaira，音译）、日本驻第二十九军顾问樱井良三郎中校（Ryozo Sakurai，音译）以及一名中国参谋军官也离开北平前往事发地点。
然而，日本当局称，在这些军官抵达之前，战斗已于大约5点30分爆发。
根据公报，此次冲突的起因是，据称由中国军队在得到北平-汉口铁路重要车站长辛店炮兵部队的增援后，向日军开火。

还击
公报称：“我军被迫还击。”
随后的战斗中使用了机枪、战壕迫击炮和轻型火炮。
随着一个步兵营从丰台抵达加强兵力，日军发起突击，将中国军队从其阵地上驱逐。
中国军队逃过永定河，朝卢沟桥城墙 adjacent 的兵营方向撤退，途中遭到日军猛烈火力射击。日军军事报告称，许多人在逃亡中倒下，事后看到数十具尸体漂浮在河面上。

白旗
与此同时，一面白旗在卢沟桥镇城墙的瞭望塔上升起。日方将此解读为第37师师长冯治安将军不希望卷入城墙外的战斗。
然而，作为预防措施，驻华北日军天津总部发布公告说，日军占领了该镇，并开始解除中国守军的武装。
北平日军军事当局称，冯将军已声明不对此次冲突负责，并表示涉事中国军队不在其指挥之下。

报道相互矛盾
北平方面关于涉事中国军队身份的信息相互矛盾。一些消息来源称他们是第219团的一部分，另一些则称他们属于第110旅的第220团。

日本华北军总部特务机关长和知鹰二大佐（Yoji Wachi，音译）今晨匆忙赶往北平，与那里的日本陆军军官进行会谈。
此举发生在北平与天津之间电话通信中断之后。

紧急会议
日本驻北平旅团长河边虎四郎少将（Torashiro Kawabe，音译）、步兵指挥官牟田口廉也大佐（Renya Mutaguchi，音译）、北平特务机关长松井大佐（Ma'sui，音译）及其他人员在收到冲突的首批报告后不久，即进入紧急会议状态。
虽然北平城内能听到步枪和机枪的哒哒声以及野战炮和战壕炮的轰鸣声，但城市保持平静。
南苑和石里园兵营的中国军队尚未动员。

此前的麻烦
据前首都的报道，最近通过第29路军的间谍系统避免了一起事件，当时七辆由日本士兵驾驶的装甲车在清晨开始在城市周围巡航约两小时。
据说约有200名朝鲜人被部署在全市各个战略要点，并受命制造骚乱，必要时由日本士兵协助。然而，第29路军在卡车游行期间抓获了许多朝鲜人和所谓的中国叛徒，并在审讯后将许多人投入监狱。

举行会议
这种局势，伴随着对疑似朝鲜人和中国人的持续逮捕，以及紧张和不确定的气氛，持续了一段时间。
据报道，中国高级官员举行会议，讨论防御措施，并在冀察政务委员会管辖下的两省两市合作维持和平与秩序。虽然声称宋哲元将军离开北平是由于私人事务，但人们相信他实际上是去山东与省主席韩复榘会谈。
据说通州数百名居民也在离开首都，这加剧了冀东政权头目殷汝耕的担忧，他试图通过检查所有进出通州的公共汽车来阻止主要因荒谬谣言引起的逃亡潮。与此同时，殷还在组建“日满蒙联军”以加强其防御，据说为此项目他正试图从关东军和日本驻华北驻屯军那里获得60万美元。

日军将进行演习
据天津特别电讯，驻华北日军夏季第二次检阅即将举行。
据报道，为准备检阅，驻扎在通州和海光寺兵营的日军将被命令前往天津附近的南大寺进行联合演习和宿营。
同时，据报道，天津日本居留民团昨日完成了扩大其自身组织的计划。根据新安排，将设立五个部和十八个科，居住在租界以外的日本人将受该团管辖，其商业企业应在该团注册。

南京下令就地解决
（同盟社）
南京，7月8日。——外交部今晨向驻扎在北平附近的第38师师长张自忠将军发出指令，要求将丰台以西的中日军队冲突“就地解决”。
据悉，外交部已收到关于卢沟桥战斗的简略报告。
这份电文声称，日军向中国哨所开火，“迫使”中方还击。
类似的信息也发送给了在南京的外交委员会委员长蒋介石将军。

东京视事态严重
（同盟社）
东京，7月8日。——陆军省今晨召开紧急会议，审议北平附近严重的中日事件。
高层陆军官员拒绝在收到官方报告前对局势发表评论，但他们表示，不得不对此事持“非常严重”的看法。
据说，今晨在此收到的零星新闻报道表明，破坏华北和平的责任在于中国军队一方。

Scene of the latest Sino-Japanese armed clash, Liuwangmiao (rendered as Lungwang-miao or "Dragon God's Temple" in Chinese maps) is located on the northern bank of the Yungting River about 1000 meters from Lukouchiao, the walled city along the Peiping-Hankow Railway. Both places are within the vicinity of Fengtai, the important railway juncture south of Peiping. Chinese troops were formally stationed at Fengtai proper but withdrawn towards Lokouchiao and the vicinity owing to Japanese opposition following an armed clash at the railway juncture some months ago. The first clash took place near Liuwangmiao at 10 o'clock last night when Japanese troops conducting a night maneuver were attacked by machine-gun fire from a Chinese pill box as reported by the Japanese sources. Fighting continued and Chinese troops were finally driven south towards the walled city across Yungting River to Lukouchiao barracks. The fighting is in the vicinity of the famous Marco Polo Bridge across the river, familiar to many foreign visitors to Peiping.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 8, 1937

Japanese Paper
Warns Chinese

China Urged To “Come
To Senses”; Envoy
Reports Rapped

Contending that China, “with pride gone to her head,” was riding for a fall “unless she comes to her senses,” the Shanghai Mainichi warns that “a great commotion” was in the offing unless the Chinese attitude were remedied.

The Chinese Press, the daily said, “is giving full vent to its conjectures about purported sub-rosa adventures” in connection with the impending visit of Ambassador Shigeru Kawagoe to North China.

Looking Askance

Its Chinese contemporaries, the Mainichi went on, are looking askance at the visit of Mr. Kawagoe to Tsingtao where he is to confer with Mr. Shojiro Ohtaka, Consul-General, and Major Nakao Yahagi, resident military officer, and his subsequent trip to Tientsin where he is to meet with Lieut.-Gen. Kanichiro Tashiro, commander of the Japanese forces in North China; Mr. Tateki Horiuchi, consul-General, and Mr. Denjiro Kato, secretary of the Embassy at Peiping.

“They seem to think that he will concoct something sinister at these meetings,” the Japanese journal remarked.

Natural Trip

“It is true that Ambassador Kawagoe seldom goes north, but European and American envoys are making such trips frequently. Moreover, it is only natural that, since a new cabinet has been formed in Japan, Mr. Kawagoe should inform those officials of the wishes of the home authorities. Moreover, his presence in Nanking would be of no avail as most Chinese officials have already left for Kuling.

“We have noted with surprise that the Chinese press has seen in Mr. Kawagoe’s sincere statement upon his return to China an attempt to gloss over the views he expressed while on his way here. According to the Chinese press, Mr. Kawagoe’s expressions stirred ill-feeling in China and revealed that ‘innermost intentions’ of the Japanese government in spite of ‘their verbose coating.’”

Speaks For Nanking

“In voicing such views, the Chinese press is speaking for the Chinese government. It is contended that it is Japan that should revise her attitude towards China as China is always ready to be friendly with Japan.

“It goes without saying that this represents a perversion of the last degree. In our opinion, China has not the slightest wish to see Sino-Japanese relations readjusted.”

Pride Before Fall

“The saying that ‘Pride goes before a fall’ should serve as a maxim for the Chinese people today. It is China, and not Japan, that is feeling proud to the point of dizziness.

“It is true, as Gen. Ho Yin-ching said the other day, that China is now progressing upwards like Japan at the time of the Meiji Restoration. Reconstruction is going apace as is the centralization of military power.

Only Half-way

“But China is only half-way in her task of national reconstruction. And yet we can already see her vainly pointing at her achievements. Could there be anything more dangerous!

“History shows that it is not easy to transform a nation. Japan had to witness a number of bloody events before the transition from feudalism to capitalism was completed.”

日本报纸
警告中国

敦促中国“清醒过来”；大使报告遭驳斥

《上海每日新闻》声称，中国“骄傲自满”，除非“清醒过来”，否则必将遭遇挫折，并警告说，除非纠正中国的态度，否则“一场大动荡”即将发生。

该日报称，中国报纸“正尽情宣泄其对于川越茂大使即将访问华北之际所谓秘密行动的猜测”。

侧目而视

《每日新闻》接着指出，其中文同行对川越先生访问青岛一事侧目而视，他将在青岛与总领事大高正二郎先生及驻在武官矢萩中佐会谈，随后前往天津，会见日本华北驻屯军司令官田代勘一郎中将、总领事堀内干城先生以及北平大使馆秘书加藤传次郎先生。

这家日本报刊评论道：“他们似乎认为，川越将在这些会晤中策划某种险恶阴谋。”

正常之行

“诚然，川越大使很少北上，但欧美使节却经常进行此类旅行。此外，既然日本已组建新内阁，川越先生向上述官员通报国内当局的意愿，乃是顺理成章之事。况且，由于大多数中国官员已前往牯岭，他留在南京也无济于事。

“我们惊讶地注意到，中国报纸将川越先生返华后的诚恳声明，视为试图掩饰他在来华途中所表达的观点。据中国报纸称，川越先生的言论在中国激起了反感，并揭示了日本政府‘尽管言辞冗长粉饰’下的‘最深层次意图’。”

代表南京发言

“中国报纸在发表此类观点时，是在代表中国政府发言。其论点是，应该由日本改变对华态度，因为中国始终愿意与日本友好相处。

“毋庸讳言，这代表了极度的歪曲。在我们看来，中国丝毫无意看到中日关系得到调整。”

骄兵必败

“‘骄兵必败’这句谚语应成为当今中国人民的座右铭。感到骄傲至头晕目眩的是中国，而非日本。

“正如贺耀组将军日前所言，中国目前正像明治维新时期的日本一样向上发展。重建工作正在迅速推进，军事权力的集中也是如此。

仅完成一半

“但是，中国的国家重建任务仅完成了一半。然而，我们已经可以看到她在徒劳地炫耀自己的成就。还有什么比这更危险的呢！

“历史表明，改造一个国家并非易事。日本在完成从封建主义向资本主义的过渡之前，不得不目睹许多血腥事件。”

(Reuter’s Agency) 

HANKOW, Aug. 9.—A general feeling of relief has 
Ldaceceetad upon Hankow following the evacuation of the 
‘Japanese Concession here by Japanese armed forces as well 
as residents. 

The last detachment of Japanese blue jackets left ves- 
terday, completing the withdrawal, which was carried out 
smoothly and without a hitch. 

A force of 60 Chinese police have now entered the Con- 
cession, in accordance with the request made by Japanese 
Congular officials, to safeguard Japanese interests and property. 

The transfer of administration is only a temporary mea- 
sure which, it is presumed, will be removed when the North 
China “incident” has been settled. 

ONLY ONE ENTRANCE 

For the time being there will be only one entrance to the 
Concession, and it will be open daily only from six in the 
morning until seven in the evening. All persons enter- 
ing or leaving are liable to be searched. 

The Japanese area presented a desolate and somewhat 
pathetic picture when Reuter’s correspondent toured the place. 

There were signs everywhere of hurried departure, such 
an half-finished meals on tables, open and bare cupboards, and 
floors strewn with refuse. Many Japanese did not even bother 
‘to lock up the doors of their houses. 
' Meanwhile, foreigners living in outlying districts are re-| 
turning to their homes, which they had previously evacuated.

easily avoided if both the Chinese and

of foolish rumours which has tended to 
increase the nervousness on both sides

benefit thereby. We feel that there

point given to the public. If that were 
done, Shanghai would be spared a great 
deal of anxiety and upset, the cost of 
which falls.so heavily on the poorer class 
of Chinese. A plan to establish a number 
of refugee camps in Shanghai has been 
already decided upon and _ to-morrow 
there will be a big meeting of Chinese 
organizations to discuss the latest

whatever measures may be deemed necess- 
ary. But the point we would unfailingly 

yi emphasize is that it is up to the public
